title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text: 廣東鄕試錄〔隆慶四年〕
punctuated: 廣東鄕試錄〔隆慶四年〕
translation_en: Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination〔Fourth year of the Longqing reign (1570)〕

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
隆慶庚午爲
皇上御極之四年天下鄉試士凡
再舉矣廣東遠在海隅御史
趙焞蓋自
闕下受
明命萬里馳至而監臨之秦等文
===
學官則以前御史楊標禮聘
繼至也闈館旣飭掫枅載嚴
百執事莫不懍懍受御史策
以襄翼
盛典司提調則右布政使莊應
禎右參政桂嘉孝司監試則
按察使佘敬中副使江一麟
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

隆慶庚午，爲皇上御極之四年，天下鄉試士凡再舉矣。廣東遠在海隅，御史趙焞蓋自闕下受明命，萬里馳至而監臨之。秦等文學官，則以前御史楊標禮聘，繼至也。闈館旣飭，掫枅載嚴，百執事莫不懍懍受御史策，以襄翼盛典。司提調，則右布政使莊應禎、右參政桂嘉孝；司監試，則按察使佘敬中、副使江一麟，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The gengwu year of Longqing was the fourth year since His Majesty ascended the throne. By then, the Provincial Examination for scholars throughout the realm had been held twice. Guangdong lies far away in a coastal corner of the realm. The Censor Zhao Tun received the imperial command at court and hastened ten thousand li to serve as Supervising Official. Qin and the other educational officials subsequently arrived, having been formally invited by the former Censor Yang Biao. Once the examination compound had been put in order and its guard arrangements [?] made strict, all the functionaries reverently received the Censor’s instructions to assist in this grand ceremony. Serving as Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhuang Yingzhen and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Gui Jiaxiao; supervising the examination were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner She Jingzhong and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Jiang Yilin …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以泰與敎諭萬濟川爲考試
官學正林大觀廖雲鵬敎諭
唐汝禮王世道鄭誨陳然陳
文彬爲同考試官如期進提
學僉事余立所選士二千二
百有奇鎖院三試之得七十
五人錄之遵
===
制也錄且
獻御史謂泰當以職事序首簡謹
拜手言曰職方氏紀南粵爲
揚粤蓋內之也所從來遠矣
夫揚粵負嶺帶海界諸夏以
控制百蠻豈非天下一巨區
乎無論聲曁唐虞功冒成周
punctuated:
以泰與敎諭萬濟川爲考試官，學正林大觀、廖雲鵬，敎諭唐汝禮、王世道、鄭誨、陳然、陳文彬爲同考試官。如期進提學僉事余立所選士二千二百有奇，鎖院三試之，得七十五人，錄之，遵制也。
錄且獻，御史謂泰當以職事序首簡。謹拜手言曰：「職方氏紀南粵爲揚粤，蓋內之也，所從來遠矣。夫揚粵負嶺帶海，界諸夏以控制百蠻，豈非天下一巨區乎？無論聲曁唐虞，功冒成周，」
translation_en:
…Tai and Wan Jichuan, an Instructor, were appointed Examiners; Lin Daguan and Liao Yunpeng, School Directors, and Tang Ruli, Wang Shidao, Zheng Hui, Chen Ran, and Chen Wenbin, Instructors, were appointed Associate Examiners. At the appointed time, the more than 2,200 candidates selected by Yu Li, Education Intendant and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, were admitted. The examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions. Seventy-five men were selected and their names recorded, in accordance with the imperial regulations.
When the record was about to be submitted to the throne, the Censor told me, Tai, that my official duties required me to write a preface for its opening pages. I respectfully bowed with clasped hands and said: “The account of the Director of Territorial Administration records Nanyue as Yang-Yue [?], thereby presumably including it within the realm. This inclusion has a long history. Yang-Yue has the mountain range at its back and the sea along its flank; it forms the frontier of the Chinese states and commands the many non-Chinese peoples. Is it not one of the great regions of the realm? Leaving aside its renown reaching back to the ages of Tang and Yu, and its achievements extending to the flourishing Zhou …”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
卽楚相傳書以往秦郡其地
而漢藩其王脩貢入侍駸駸
章甫國矣南海衣冠之氣晉
人有能望而測之者彼誠謂
山海靈秀蟠鬱廣旴不當獨
鍾異物必得異才應之顧風
氣之開也以漸而其盛也以
===
時方唐宋盛時張余諸賢相
望崛起功被一世譽流無窮
業已彬彬視鄒魯間至於鴻
筆之士鼎甲之臣則莫盛於
我
祖宗朝〔泰〕以其時考之尤宜增盛
於
punctuated: 卽楚相傳書以往，秦郡其地，而漢藩其王，脩貢入侍，駸駸章甫國矣。南海衣冠之氣，晉人有能望而測之者。彼誠謂山海靈秀，蟠鬱廣旴，不當獨鍾異物，必得異才應之。顧風氣之開也以漸，而其盛也以時。方唐宋盛時，張余諸賢相望崛起，功被一世，譽流無窮，業已彬彬視鄒魯間。至於鴻筆之士、鼎甲之臣，則莫盛於我祖宗朝。〔泰〕以其時考之，尤宜增盛於
translation_en: …From the time when a minister of Chu transmitted a letter onward [?], Qin made this territory a commandery, and Han made its king a vassal. Presenting tribute and attending at court, it steadily became a land of ceremonial caps and cultivated manners. Among the people of Jin were those able to discern and interpret the aura of cultured gentlemen over Nanhai. They truly held that the spiritual excellence of its mountains and seas, concentrated across its broad expanse [?], ought not to find expression solely in extraordinary things: extraordinary talents must necessarily arise in response. Yet the opening of its cultural climate proceeded gradually, and its flourishing awaited the proper time. During the flourishing ages of Tang and Song, worthies such as Zhang and Yu arose one after another, their achievements benefiting their age and their renown enduring without end. In cultural refinement, the region already rivaled Zou and Lu. As for men of magnificent literary gifts and officials who had placed in the top three in the Palace Examination, however, no age surpassed the reigns of our imperial ancestors. Judging by the timing, I, 〔Tai〕, hold that this flourishing should increase still further in…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今日何也應期故也蓋自我
皇祖以及
先帝興敎育士垂二百年培養以
待
皇上者至深厚矣我
皇上又以崇儒重道敦本尚實風
之如
===
登極初詔首罷珍異之役表用巖
穴之遺蓋粹乎
帝王盛節賤遠物而寶賢才海邦
黎獻聞風希聲塗歌而邑頌
之矣頃屬窮島巨寇稱釁葦
澤兵連十郡士至無所息踵
我
punctuated: 今日，何也？應期故也。蓋自我皇祖以及先帝，興敎育士垂二百年，培養以待皇上者至深厚矣。我皇上又以崇儒重道、敦本尚實風之。如登極初詔，首罷珍異之役，表用巖穴之遺，蓋粹乎帝王盛節，賤遠物而寶賢才。海邦黎獻聞風希聲，塗歌而邑頌之矣。頃屬窮島巨寇稱釁葦澤，兵連十郡，士至無所息踵。我
translation_en:
…today. Why is this so? Because the appointed time has arrived. From our imperial ancestor down to the late emperor, education has been promoted and scholars nurtured for nearly two hundred years. The cultivation undertaken in preparation for His Majesty has been most profound and generous. His Majesty has further inspired them by honoring Confucian learning, esteeming the Way, strengthening fundamentals, and valuing substance. For example, in his first edict upon ascending the throne, he first abolished the services imposed to procure rare and exotic objects, and publicly honored and appointed overlooked worthies living in seclusion. These were indeed pure expressions of the highest imperial virtue: setting little value on goods from distant lands while treasuring worthy and talented men. The worthy men of this coastal region heard of his example and aspired to follow his influence, singing his praises along the roads and acclaiming him in their towns.
Recently, however, powerful bandits from remote islands stirred up trouble in the reed marshes [?]. Warfare spread across ten prefectures, until scholars had nowhere even to rest their heels. Our…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上南顧憂之爲發
內帑金數萬
詔遣重臣視師平之有司者始得
投戈而講藝焉諸懷鉛剌經
之士遂晏然脫荊棘而就試
于有司此我
皇上之有大造於粵也夫培養厚
===
則掄用有餘資
詔令一則觀聽無異嚮而又出之
鋒刃之衝置諸樽俎之序則
其戴
恩而思報也益奮奮不可遏秦是
以不假洞靈之測而知得士
之必盛於
punctuated:
皇上南顧憂之，爲發內帑金數萬，詔遣重臣視師平之。有司者始得投戈而講藝焉，諸懷鉛剌經之士遂晏然脫荊棘而就試于有司。此我皇上之有大造於粵也。
夫培養厚，則掄用有餘資；詔令一，則觀聽無異嚮。而又出之鋒刃之衝，置諸樽俎之序，則其戴恩而思報也益奮，奮不可遏。秦是以不假洞靈之測，而知得士之必盛於
translation_en:
…His Majesty looked southward with concern over this and released tens of thousands in gold from the imperial treasury. By imperial decree, he dispatched a high minister to oversee the military campaign and pacify the rebels. Only then could the responsible officials lay down their weapons and attend to literary learning. The scholars who carried writing leads and studied the Classics [?] could at last emerge peacefully from the thorny troubles and present themselves for examination before the authorities. Such is the great beneficence His Majesty has bestowed upon Guangdong.
When cultivation is generous, there is an ample supply of talent for selection and employment; when imperial commands are consistent, those who see and hear them follow a common direction. Moreover, having been brought out of the clash of blades and placed within the orderly setting of ritual vessels and offerings, these scholars become all the more ardent in cherishing imperial favor and seeking to repay it—their ardor cannot be restrained. Thus Qin [?], without resorting to spirit divination, knows that the recruitment of worthy men will surely flourish in…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今夫得士非以文也而文則其
先資之信也今披睹其文類
多明理習事通經術潛乎天
人之際而鏡於得失之林述
性而弗矯其眞譚藝而弗詭
於道圖事揆策而皆度於衷
泰始擊節賞之已而不可勝
===
錄則撫卷三歎曰士盛哉古
敷言試功若考德行道藝以
獻賢能何以加此哉雖然泰
又有聞議賢而下之臣之忠
也使士飾其說以自媒而錄
士者又止賢其說而不計其
實則失所爲議賢之道不忠
punctuated:
今。夫得士非以文也，而文則其先資之信也。今披睹其文，類多明理習事，通經術，潛乎天人之際，而鏡於得失之林；述性而弗矯其眞，譚藝而弗詭於道，圖事揆策而皆度於衷。泰始擊節賞之，已而不可勝錄，則撫卷三歎曰：「士盛哉！古敷言試功，若考德行道藝以獻賢能，何以加此哉！」
雖然，泰又有聞：議賢而下之，臣之忠也。使士飾其說以自媒，而錄士者又止賢其說而不計其實，則失所爲議賢之道，不忠……
translation_en:
…today. Men of worth are not obtained through literary composition alone; yet their writing supplies preliminary evidence of their qualifications. Reading their compositions now, I find that most understand principles, are versed in practical affairs, and comprehend classical learning. They delve into the relations between Heaven and humanity and discern the many forms of success and failure. They expound human nature without distorting its authenticity, discuss the arts without departing from the Way, and plan affairs and weigh policies in accordance with what is right. At first I, Tai, beat time in admiration; then, finding more worthy passages than could be recorded, I laid my hand upon the scrolls and sighed repeatedly in admiration: “How abundant are men of worth! The ancients examined men’s statements and tested their achievements, or assessed their virtue, conduct, learning in the Way, and arts in order to recommend the worthy and capable. How could they surpass this?”
Nevertheless, I, Tai, have also heard that recognizing worthy men and placing oneself below them is the loyalty of a minister. If scholars embellish their statements to promote themselves, and those who select them esteem only their statements without considering their actual substance, then they lose the proper way of assessing worthy men. Such disloyalty…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孰甚焉昔者伊尹就聘數語
傅說對揚三篇皆先資也卒
之堯舜君民霖雨天下即畎
畝巖穴所自信者以成其信
次則杖策鄴下屏語隆中曾
不移時而定天下大計及其
功烈所就如合左券然由是
===
觀之古人之自獻皆量其能
而後言也辟諸田獵射御貫
則能獲禽不則厭覆是懼何
暇思獲泰不佞敢以忠道自
責而以量入之道望諸士諸
士其爲伊傅乎爲禹亮乎毋
徒沾沾豪舉爲也是役也先
punctuated:
孰甚焉？昔者伊尹就聘數語，傅說對揚三篇，皆先資也。卒之堯舜君民，霖雨天下，即畎畝巖穴所自信者，以成其信。次則杖策鄴下，屏語隆中，曾不移時而定天下大計，及其功烈所就，如合左券然。由是觀之，古人之自獻，皆量其能而後言也。辟諸田獵，射御貫則能獲禽，不則厭覆是懼，何暇思獲？泰不佞，敢以忠道自責，而以量入之道望諸士。諸士其爲伊傅乎？爲禹亮乎？毋徒沾沾豪舉爲也。
是役也，先
translation_en:
…what could be worse? In former times, the few words Yi Yin spoke upon accepting his appointment and the three chapters in which Fu Yue responded to and extolled his sovereign’s charge all served as preliminary credentials [?]. In the end, they brought their rulers and people to the standard of Yao and Shun and became life-giving rain for all under Heaven. Thus they fulfilled the promise of what they had trusted themselves capable of while still among the fields and rocky caves. Next came Deng Yu, staff in hand, at Ye, and Zhuge Liang, speaking privately at Longzhong: in scarcely any time they settled the grand strategy for the realm. When their achievements were realized, these matched their words like the matching halves of a contract tally.
Viewed in this light, the ancients who offered themselves for service all assessed their abilities before speaking. It is like hunting: proficiency in archery and charioteering enables one to take game; without it, one fears being crushed or overturned—what leisure is there to think of taking game? I, Tai, lacking in talent, venture to hold myself accountable to the way of loyal service and to expect these scholars likewise to measure their capacities. Will you scholars become men like Yi Yin and Fu Yue, or Deng Yu and Zhuge Liang? Do not merely congratulate yourselves on grand gestures.
In this undertaking, the former…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
總督兩廣左都御史兼兵部
左侍郎劉燾夙著勳猷士有
寧宇今提督兩廣巡撫廣東
兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史
李遷奮武揆文譽髦斯士先
巡撫廣東右副都御史熊汝
達飭度綏化士民用章先提
===
督南贛右僉都御史張翀今
提督南贛右僉都御史殷從
儉約法樹防澤流教遠右參
議史嗣元按察使分巡伸威
道張子弘副使許宗鎰史朝
宜僉事楊芷羅向辰防範於
外綜翊惟周右參將羅繼祖
punctuated: 總督兩廣左都御史兼兵部左侍郎劉燾，夙著勳猷，士有寧宇。今提督兩廣巡撫廣東兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史李遷，奮武揆文，譽髦斯士。先巡撫廣東右副都御史熊汝達，飭度綏化，士民用章。先提督南贛右僉都御史張翀、今提督南贛右僉都御史殷從儉，約法樹防，澤流教遠。右參議史嗣元、按察使分巡伸威道張子弘、副使許宗鎰、史朝宜、僉事楊芷、羅向辰，防範於外，綜翊惟周。右參將羅繼祖
translation_en:
…Liu Tao, Supreme Commander of Guangdong and Guangxi, Censor-in-Chief of the Left, and concurrently Vice Minister of War of the Left, had long distinguished himself through meritorious achievements and plans, providing the scholars with a peaceful home. Li Qian, the present superintendent of Guangdong and Guangxi and Grand Coordinator of Guangdong, Vice Minister of War of the Left and concurrently Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right, promoted military strength and directed civil affairs, fostering these outstanding scholars. Xiong Ruda, the former Grand Coordinator of Guangdong and Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right, put regulations in order and fostered peaceful moral transformation, through which scholars and commoners flourished. Zhang Chong, the former superintendent of Nan-Gan and Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right, and Yin Congjian, the present superintendent of Nan-Gan and Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right, simplified the laws and established safeguards; their beneficence spread and their instruction reached far.
Shi Siyuan, Administration Commissioner’s Assistant of the Right; Zhang Zihong, Surveillance Commissioner assigned to inspect the Shenwei Circuit [?]; Xu Zongyi and Shi Chaoyi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Yang Zhi and Luo Xiangchen, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, maintained safeguards outside and provided comprehensive coordination and support. Luo Jizu, Regional Commander of the Right…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遊擊將軍李誠立署都指揮
僉事來熙晏秋元捍禦於外
保綏孔固副使施堯臣左參
議黎德充以入
賀行左參政姚世熙僉事張士
純以遷秩行皆先後賛襄與
有勞焉故事得竝書書之
===
直隸太平府儒學敎授鄒秦
謹序
punctuated:
遊擊將軍李誠立、署都指揮僉事來熙、晏秋元，捍禦於外，保綏孔固。副使施堯臣、左參議黎德充以入賀行，左參政姚世熙、僉事張士純以遷秩行，皆先後賛襄，與有勞焉。故事，得竝書，書之。
直隸太平府儒學敎授鄒秦謹序。
translation_en:
…Mobile Corps Commander Li Chengli and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Lai Xi and Yan Qiuyuan defended against external threats, ensuring firm protection and security. Deputy Surveillance Commissioner Shi Yaochen and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Dechong departed to offer congratulations at court; Left Administration Vice Commissioner Yao Shixi and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Shichun departed upon promotion. All had, at various times, assisted in this undertaking and shared in its meritorious service. Precedent permits their names to be recorded together, and so I record them here.
This preface was respectfully written by Zou Qin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Taiping Prefecture in the directly administered territory.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史趙　焞〔子明山東平原縣人乙丑進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使莊應禎〔希周福建惠安縣人丁未進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司右參政桂嘉孝〔純甫四川成都縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使佘敬中〔子星直隸銅陵縣人己未進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司副使江一麟〔仲文直隸婺源縣人癸丑進士〕
===
考試官
直隸太平府儒學教授鄒　泰〔景孟直隸濬縣人癸卯貢士〕
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭萬濟川〔汝舟江西南昌縣人己酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隸鳳陽府亳州儒學學正林大觀〔朝敷福建莆田縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府潁州儒學學正廖雲鵬〔子翀福建侯官縣籍江西新淦縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣儒學教諭唐汝禮〔思敬浙江蘭谿縣人甲子貢士〕
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭王世道〔時鳴江西萬年縣人壬子貢士〕
湖廣荆州府夷陵州遠安縣儒學教諭鄭　誨〔忠卿江西浮梁縣人戊午貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年廣東鄉試

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史趙　焞〔子明，山東平原縣人，乙丑進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使莊應禎〔希周，福建惠安縣人，丁未進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司右參政桂嘉孝〔純甫，四川成都縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使佘敬中〔子星，直隸銅陵縣人，己未進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司副使江一麟〔仲文，直隸婺源縣人，癸丑進士〕。

考試官：
直隸太平府儒學教授鄒　泰〔景孟，直隸濬縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭萬濟川〔汝舟，江西南昌縣人，己酉貢士〕。

同考試官：
直隸鳳陽府亳州儒學學正林大觀〔朝敷，福建莆田縣人，壬子貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府潁州儒學學正廖雲鵬〔子翀，福建侯官縣籍，江西新淦縣人，壬子貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣儒學教諭唐汝禮〔思敬，浙江蘭谿縣人，甲子貢士〕。
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭王世道〔時鳴，江西萬年縣人，壬子貢士〕。
湖廣荆州府夷陵州遠安縣儒學教諭鄭　誨〔忠卿，江西浮梁縣人，戊午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Longqing (1570)

Supervising Official
Zhao Tun, Investigating Censor assigned to巡 inspect Guangdong, had the courtesy name Ziming and was from Pingyuan County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the yichou year.

Proctors
Zhuang Yingzhen, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Xizhou and was from Hui’an County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.
Gui Jiaxiao, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Chunfu and was from Chengdu County, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
She Jingzhong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Zixing and was from Tongling County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.
Jiang Yilin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Zhongwen and was from Wuyuan County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examiners
Zou Tai, Professor of the Confucian School of Taiping Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Jingmeng and was from Xun County, Zhili. He became a tribute scholar (gongshi) in the guimao year.
Wan Jichuan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Ruzhou and was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the jiyou year.

Associate Examiners
Lin Daguan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Bozhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Chaofu and was from Putian County, Fujian. He became a tribute scholar in the renzi year.
Liao Yunpeng, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yingzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zichong. His registered domicile was Houguan County, Fujian, and his native place was Xingan County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the renzi year.
Tang Ruli, Instructor of the Confucian School of Lingbi County, Suzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Sijing and was from Lanxi County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute scholar in the jiazi year.
Wang Shidao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Shiming and was from Wannian County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the renzi year.
Zheng Hui, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yuan’an County, Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Zhongqing and was from Fuliang County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the wuwu year.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭陳然〔少白湖廣沅陵縣人戊午貢士〕
浙江嘉興府嘉善縣儒學教諭陳文彬〔仲質廣西陸川縣人甲子貢士〕
印卷官
廣東等處承宣布政使司理問所副理問羅廷芳〔汝桂湖廣安鄉縣人監生〕
廣東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷程玠〔國信直隸休寧縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
南雄府知府林應節〔時卿福建莆田縣人己未進士〕
潮州府知府侯必登〔叔良雲南廣南衛籍直隸上元縣人己未進士〕
肇慶府知府熊俸〔德南江西星子縣人丙辰進士〕
===
高州府知府吳國倫〔明卿湖廣興國州人庚戌進士〕
瓊州府知府周思久〔子徵湖廣麻城縣人癸丑進士〕
受卷官
韶州府同知熊曉〔達夫福建甌寧縣人壬子貢士〕
南雄府推官殷濡〔子霖直隸常熟縣人戊辰進士〕
惠州府長寧縣知縣趙鉞〔可度福建長汀縣人丙午貢士〕
肇慶府德慶州瀧水縣知縣譚文達〔時義廣西賓州人乙卯貢士〕
彌封官
廉州府同知江萬仞〔若度福建晉江縣人癸丑進士〕
punctuated:
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭陳然〔少白，湖廣沅陵縣人，戊午貢士〕。
浙江嘉興府嘉善縣儒學教諭陳文彬〔仲質，廣西陸川縣人，甲子貢士〕。

印卷官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司理問所副理問羅廷芳〔汝桂，湖廣安鄉縣人，監生〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷程玠〔國信，直隸休寧縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：
南雄府知府林應節〔時卿，福建莆田縣人，己未進士〕。
潮州府知府侯必登〔叔良，雲南廣南衛籍，直隸上元縣人，己未進士〕。
肇慶府知府熊俸〔德南，江西星子縣人，丙辰進士〕。
高州府知府吳國倫〔明卿，湖廣興國州人，庚戌進士〕。
瓊州府知府周思久〔子徵，湖廣麻城縣人，癸丑進士〕。

受卷官：
韶州府同知熊曉〔達夫，福建甌寧縣人，壬子貢士〕。
南雄府推官殷濡〔子霖，直隸常熟縣人，戊辰進士〕。
惠州府長寧縣知縣趙鉞〔可度，福建長汀縣人，丙午貢士〕。
肇慶府德慶州瀧水縣知縣譚文達〔時義，廣西賓州人，乙卯貢士〕。

彌封官：
廉州府同知江萬仞〔若度，福建晉江縣人，癸丑進士〕。
translation_en:
Chen Ran, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Shaobai; he was a native of Yuanling County, Huguang, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuwu year.
Chen Wenbin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Zhongzhi; he was a native of Luchuan County, Guangxi, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year.

Officials for Printing Examination Papers:
Luo Tingfang, Vice Judicial Commissioner in the Judicial Commission of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Rugui; he was a native of Anxiang County, Huguang, and a student of the Imperial Academy.
Cheng Jie, Registrar in the Registry of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Guoxin; he was a native of Xiuning County, Zhili, and a student of the Imperial Academy.

Officials for Collecting and Keeping Examination Papers:
Lin Yingjie, Prefect of Nanxiong. His courtesy name was Shiqing; he was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiwei year.
Hou Bideng, Prefect of Chaozhou. His courtesy name was Shuliang; he was registered in Guangnan Guard, Yunnan, and was a native of Shangyuan County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiwei year.
Xiong Feng, Prefect of Zhaoqing. His courtesy name was Denan; he was a native of Xingzi County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year.
Wu Guolun, Prefect of Gaozhou. His courtesy name was Mingqing; he was a native of Xingguo Subprefecture, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the gengxu year.
Zhou Sijiu, Prefect of Qiongzhou. His courtesy name was Zizheng; he was a native of Macheng County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guichou year.

Officials for Receiving Examination Papers:
Xiong Xiao, Vice Prefect of Shaozhou. His courtesy name was Dafu; he was a native of Ouning County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renzi year.
Yin Ru, Prefectural Judge of Nanxiong. His courtesy name was Zilin; he was a native of Changshu County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuchen year.
Zhao Yue, Magistrate of Changning County, Huizhou Prefecture. His courtesy name was Kedu; he was a native of Changting County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingwu year.
Tan Wenda, Magistrate of Longshui County, Deqing Subprefecture, Zhaoqing Prefecture. His courtesy name was Shiyi; he was a native of Binzhou Subprefecture, Guangxi, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the yimao year.

Officials for Sealing Candidates’ Identifying Information:
Jiang Wanren, Vice Prefect of Lianzhou. His courtesy name was Ruodu; he was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guichou year.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣州府連州知州徐美〔中夫福建邵武縣人壬子貢士〕
廣州府增城縣知縣張孔脩〔德成福建福寧州籍浙江餘姚縣人己酉貢士〕
謄錄官
潮州府同知陳學麟〔尚魯福建懷安縣人戊午貢士〕
潮州府推官來經濟〔濟時浙江蕭山縣人戊辰進士〕
廣州府南海縣知縣蕭騰鳳〔明仲福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
廣州府東莞縣知縣張鏜〔汝柪江西永豐縣人戊辰進士〕
肇慶府四會縣知縣劉順之〔體信廣西馬平縣籍湖廣善化縣人壬子貢士〕
對讀官
===
廣州府推官王任重〔尹卿福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
肇慶府推官李時春〔元卿福建候官縣人乙卯貢士〕
惠州府博羅縣知縣顏容舒〔日莊福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
潮州府海陽縣知縣秦舜翰〔國宗福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
潮州府潮陽縣知縣黃一龍〔雲卿福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
巡綽官
廣州左衛指揮使趙陞〔惟遷直隸滁州人〕
廣州右衛指揮同知王暹〔于明直隸無為州人〕
廣州右衛指揮僉事李田龍〔文見湖廣桂東縣人〕
punctuated:

肇慶府推官李時春〔元卿，福建候官縣人，乙卯貢士〕。

Huang Yilong, District Magistrate of Chaoyang County in Chaozhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yunqing. He was from Jinjiang County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Patrol Officials:

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣州後衛指揮僉事楊堯佐〔憲伯直隸和州人〕
搜檢官
廣州左衛指揮使胡潮〔信吾湖廣衡陽縣人〕
廣州右衛指揮使楊永勳〔紹先直隸臨淮縣人〕

廣州前衛指揮僉事黎軾〔元敬湖廣沔陽州人〕

供給官
===

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰性相近也習相遠也
所求乎子以事父未能也所求乎臣以事
君未能也
中天下而立定四海之民
易
聖人以順動則刑罰清而民服
天地節而四時成節以制度不傷財不害
===
民
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深也
故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成天下
之務唯神也故不疾而速不行而至
震東方也
書
九德咸事俊乂在官百僚師師百工惟時
撫于五辰庶績其凝
導岍及岐至于荊山逾于河壺口雷首至
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「性相近也，習相遠也。」

所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也。

中天下而立，定四海之民。

易

聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。

天地節而四時成；節以制度，不傷財，不害民。

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。

震，東方也。

書

九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

導岍及岐，至于荊山，逾于河；壺口、雷首，至
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “By nature, people are close to one another; through acquired habits, they grow far apart.”

“What I require of a son, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my father; what I require of a minister, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my ruler.”

“To stand at the center of all under Heaven and bring settled order to the people within the Four Seas.”

Book of Changes

“When the sage acts in accordance with what is right, punishments are just and clear, and the people submit.”

“Heaven and Earth observe their bounds, and the four seasons are thereby formed. Restraint through institutions and regulations neither wastes resources nor harms the people.”

“The Changes is the means by which the sages fathom the depths and investigate the first stirrings of things. Only through profundity can they comprehend the intentions of all under Heaven; only through discerning the first stirrings can they accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; only through spiritual efficacy can they be swift without haste and arrive without traveling.”

“Zhen is the east.”

Book of Documents

“When all nine virtues are put into practice, men of outstanding ability hold office, the many officials learn from one another, and all officers attend to their duties at the proper times. In accord with the five heavenly time markers, their many achievements will be firmly established.”

“Tracing the mountains from Qian and Qi, reaching Mount Jingshan, and crossing the Yellow River; from Hukou and Leishou, reaching …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于太岳厎柱析城至于王屋太行恒山
至于碣石入于海
無偏無黨王道蕩蕩
一人有慶兆民賴之
詩
彼君子兮不素餐兮
南山有桑北山有楊樂只君子邦家之光
樂只君子萬壽無疆南山有杞北山有
李樂只君子民之父母樂只君子德音
不已
恒之秬秠是穫是畝恒之縻芑是任是負
方命厥后奄有九有
春秋
晉人敗狄于箕僖公三十有三年晉欒書
帥師救鄭成公六年
春王三月甲寅齊人伐衛莊公二十有八
年齊師宋師曹師城邢僖公元年
晉人宋人衛人曹人伐鄭宣公十年
punctuated:
于太岳、厎柱、析城，至于王屋、太行、恒山，至于碣石，入于海。
無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩。
一人有慶，兆民賴之。

詩
彼君子兮，不素餐兮。
南山有桑，北山有楊。樂只君子，邦家之光。樂只君子，萬壽無疆。南山有杞，北山有李。樂只君子，民之父母。樂只君子，德音不已。
恒之秬秠，是穫是畝；恒之縻芑，是任是負。
方命厥后，奄有九有。

春秋
晉人敗狄于箕。僖公三十有三年。晉欒書帥師救鄭。成公六年。
春，王三月，甲寅，齊人伐衛。莊公二十有八年。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。僖公元年。
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人伐鄭。宣公十年。
translation_en:
…to Taiyue, Dizhu, and Xicheng, reaching Wangwu, Taihang, and Hengshan; then reaching Jieshi and entering the sea.
Without partiality or faction, the kingly way is broad and open.
When the One Man enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them.

Book of Odes
That gentleman does not eat without earning his food!
On the southern mountain grow mulberries; on the northern mountain grow poplars. Joyful is the gentleman, the glory of the state and its ruling house. Joyful is the gentleman: may he live ten thousand years without end! On the southern mountain grow medlars; on the northern mountain grow plums. Joyful is the gentleman, father and mother of the people. Joyful is the gentleman: may his virtuous reputation never cease!
They planted black millet and double-grained millet, harvesting it and piling it in the fields; they planted red millet [?] and white millet, carrying it in their arms and on their backs.
Heaven then appointed its ruler, who came to possess all the Nine Regions.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The men of Jin defeated the Di at Ji. Thirty-third year of Duke Xi. Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. Sixth year of Duke Cheng.
In spring, in the third month of the royal calendar, on the jiayin day, the men of Qi attacked Wei. Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang. The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built fortifications at Xing. First year of Duke Xi.
The men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao attacked Zheng. Tenth year of Duke Xuan.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
八月戊辰同盟于馬陵〔成公七年〕
禮記
事君以自顯也
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節
使民有父之尊有母之親如此而后可以
爲民父母矣
氣如白虹天也
第貳塲
論
===
人主制馭臣民之柄
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘〕
〔露三年〕
擬唐加裴度同平章事誥〔長慶四年〕
擬宋遣使分賑諸州羣臣謝表〔建隆元年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
轉解官物
punctuated:
八月戊辰，同盟于馬陵〔成公七年〕。
禮記
事君以自顯也。
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。
使民有父之尊，有母之親，如此而后可以爲民父母矣。
氣如白虹，天也。
第貳塲
論
人主制馭臣民之柄。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘〕〔露三年〕。
擬唐加裴度同平章事誥〔長慶四年〕。
擬宋遣使分賑諸州羣臣謝表〔建隆元年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
轉解官物。
translation_en:
In the eighth month, on the wuchen day, they concluded a joint covenant at Maling. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng〕

Record of Rites
“To serve one’s lord is to make oneself illustrious.”
“Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares their measured order.”
“Give the people someone whom they respect as a father and cherish as a mother; only then can one become a father and mother to the people.”
“Vital energy like a white rainbow: this pertains to Heaven.”

Second Session
Discourse
The ruler’s authority to control and govern his officials and people.

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor summoning the scholars to discuss the agreements and differences among the Five Classics at the Shiqu Pavilion. 〔Third year of Ganlu〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor appointing Pei Du as Joint Manager of Affairs, Secretariat–Chancellery. 〔Fourth year of Changqing〕
Compose a memorial in the voice of the assembled Song officials giving thanks for the dispatch of envoys to distribute famine relief throughout the prefectures. 〔First year of Jianlong〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Issuing service certificates to officials and clerks.
Forwarding government goods.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
脩理倉庫
第參塲
策〔五道〕
問書稱元良詩詠燕翼自古帝王所以爲
宗社萬世計至深遠也三代之盛不可
尚已然典則風愆與夫謨烈之垂班班
可考則盛治固有本矣我
===
太祖高皇帝誕膺
天命肇造區宇深惟
國本之重爰作
昭鑒錄以爲萬世
聖子
神孫法其大旨可得聞與嗣我
成祖文皇帝則有
聖學心法
宣宗章皇帝則有
punctuated:
禁止迎送。
優恤軍屬。
脩理倉庫。
第參塲
策〔五道〕
問：書稱元良，詩詠燕翼，自古帝王所以爲宗社萬世計，至深遠也。三代之盛，不可尚已；然典則風愆，與夫謨烈之垂，班班可考，則盛治固有本矣。我太祖高皇帝誕膺天命，肇造區宇，深惟國本之重，爰作《昭鑒錄》，以爲萬世聖子神孫法。其大旨可得聞與？嗣我成祖文皇帝則有《聖學心法》，宣宗章皇帝則有
translation_en:
Prohibiting ceremonial welcomes and send-offs.
Providing preferential relief for military dependents.
Repairing granaries and storehouses.
Third Session
Policy questions 〔five questions〕
Question: The Book of Documents speaks of the supremely good heir, and the Book of Odes celebrates providing security for one’s descendants. Since antiquity, the means by which emperors and kings have planned for the imperial ancestral temples and altars of state through ten thousand generations have been profound and far-reaching indeed. The flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties could not be surpassed. Yet their canonical rules, admonitions against faults, and the plans and achievements they handed down can all be clearly examined. Thus flourishing government assuredly has its foundations.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao grandly received Heaven’s Mandate and first established the realm. Deeply considering the importance of the foundation of the state, he composed the Record of Illustrious Exemplars (Zhaojian lu) as a model for his sagely sons and divine grandsons through ten thousand generations. May we hear its principal purport? Subsequently, our Emperor Chengzu Wen had the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang had …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
御製帝訓
憲宗純皇帝則有
文華大訓三書之㫖不知於
昭鑒錄同與否與我
皇上盛德格
天
前星炳耀
東宮正位
睿知夙啓行且進講
===
宮筵述
祖宗之訓以資啓沃副
聖心其務奚先諸士咸懷忠愛之忱願悉陳之
將轉聞于
上
問帝王慎乃儉德非獨爲天下節財其爲
慮蓋遠也稽之唐虞夏商周如史臣所
紀典謨訓誥所載數聖人儉德先後一
揆至漢唐晉宋諸君有衣弋绨履革舄
punctuated:
《御製帝訓》，憲宗純皇帝則有《文華大訓》。三書之㫖，不知於《昭鑒錄》同與否與？我皇上盛德格天，前星炳耀，東宮正位，睿知夙啓，行且進講宮筵，述祖宗之訓，以資啓沃，副聖心，其務奚先？諸士咸懷忠愛之忱，願悉陳之，將轉聞于上。
問：帝王慎乃儉德，非獨爲天下節財，其爲慮蓋遠也。稽之唐虞夏商周，如史臣所紀、典謨訓誥所載，數聖人儉德，先後一揆。至漢唐晉宋諸君，有衣弋绨、履革舄
translation_en:
…the Imperially Composed Instructions for Emperors (Yuzhi dixun), while Emperor Xianzong Chun had the Great Instructions of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua daxun). Are the essential teachings of these three books the same as those of the Record of Illustrious Lessons (Zhaojian lu), or different? Our reigning emperor’s abundant virtue reaches Heaven. The star of the heir apparent shines brilliantly; the crown prince has duly assumed his position in the Eastern Palace, and his sagely understanding has awakened early. Lectures will soon be presented at the palace lecture mat, expounding the ancestral emperors’ instructions to nurture his understanding and fulfill His Majesty’s wishes. What should take priority in this undertaking? All you candidates cherish sincere loyalty and devotion. Please set forth your views fully, so that they may be conveyed to His Majesty.
Question: When emperors and kings diligently cultivate the virtue of frugality, they do so not merely to conserve the realm’s resources; their concerns surely extend much further. Examining the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, we find that, as recorded by court historians and preserved in the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, these sages’ virtue of frugality followed a single standard throughout successive ages. Among the rulers of Han, Tang, Jin, and Song, there were those who wore dark silk garments [?] and leather shoes…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有詔恐妨農事害女紅者有身衣大練
色無重綵有身御澣服食無兼珎者有
焚裘焚錦於前殿者有碎七寶器有以
節儉試進士以民力戒嬪御者類以儉
名也孰優劣與洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
承帝王之統
敦儉德以為天下先開
國之初屢卻珎獻鉅若金玉飾馬鞍鏤金牀
===
水晶漏細若香米蘄簟蒲萄酒不但毀
絕不受且
下令以為戒而又
諭省臣以惜民力法子孫至意此豈與古帝王
有異較耶迨我
皇上中天撫運法
祖愛民
登極一詔行之信如四時諸生羣伏誦之矣如
裁省光祿供億清汰
punctuated: 有詔恐妨農事、害女紅者，有身衣大練、色無重綵，有身御澣服、食無兼珎者，有焚裘焚錦於前殿者，有碎七寶器，有以節儉試進士、以民力戒嬪御者，類以儉名也。孰優劣與？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，承帝王之統，敦儉德以為天下先。開國之初，屢卻珎獻，鉅若金玉飾馬鞍、鏤金牀、水晶漏，細若香米、蘄簟、蒲萄酒，不但毀絕不受，且下令以為戒，而又諭省臣以惜民力、法子孫至意。此豈與古帝王有異較耶？迨我皇上中天撫運，法祖愛民，登極一詔，行之信如四時，諸生羣伏誦之矣。如裁省光祿供億、清汰
translation_en:
…there were those whose edicts expressed concern lest farming be impeded and women’s textile work harmed; those who themselves wore coarse silk, without layers of rich colors; those who wore washed garments and ate without an array of delicacies; those who burned furs and brocades in the front hall; those who smashed vessels made of the seven treasures; and those who examined candidates for metropolitan graduate status on frugality and admonished their consorts to spare the people’s labor. All alike were renowned for frugality. Which were superior, and which inferior?

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao inherited the succession of emperors and kings and cultivated the virtue of frugality, setting an example for all under Heaven. At the founding of the dynasty, he repeatedly rejected precious offerings: large objects such as saddles adorned with gold and jade, beds with chased gold ornament, and crystal clepsydras, as well as lesser items such as fragrant rice, bamboo mats from Qi, and grape wine. He not only had such things destroyed or prohibited and refused to accept them, but also issued orders warning against them. Moreover, he instructed the Secretariat officials in his profound intention to spare the people’s labor and set a model for his descendants. Could this be judged by any different standard from that applied to the emperors and kings of antiquity?

Now our reigning Emperor, occupying the center of Heaven and presiding over the course of destiny, follows his ancestor and cherishes the people. His accession edict has been carried out with the reliability of the four seasons; you students have all reverently recited it. Among its measures are reductions in the provisions supplied by the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the elimination of…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
內府諸需至於珠寶香蠟之役一切罷之以
蘇民困且
諭部臣曰朕加意節省用自有餘猗歟此即典
謨訓誥文也
媲美唐虞同符
聖祖
社稷生靈抑何幸耶諸生博古憲
今其將殫述而榆揚之毋忽
問書曰在知人在安民知人固所以安民
===
也又曰知人則哲惟帝其難之則人才
難得亦難知矣然晏元獻之判西京也
與范希文論人一問答而萃四相張忠
定之守金陵也一諮詢而得二子皆當
時之儁則人才之得亦不難與房杜微
時曾靡尺寸之豎而司銓衡者預以公
輔期之盧駱王楊文藝燁燁一時而占
器識者已逆覩其後焉則知人之鑑顧
亦易與彼慨人之難知至有江海浮雲
punctuated:
內府諸需，至於珠寶香蠟之役，一切罷之，以蘇民困。且諭部臣曰：「朕加意節省，用自有餘。」猗歟！此即典謨訓誥文也。媲美唐虞，同符聖祖，社稷生靈抑何幸耶！諸生博古憲今，其將殫述而榆揚之，毋忽。
問：書曰：「在知人，在安民。」知人固所以安民也。又曰：「知人則哲，惟帝其難之。」則人才難得，亦難知矣。然晏元獻之判西京也，與范希文論人，一問答而萃四相；張忠定之守金陵也，一諮詢而得二子，皆當時之儁，則人才之得亦不難與？房杜微時，曾靡尺寸之豎，而司銓衡者預以公輔期之；盧駱王楊文藝燁燁一時，而占器識者已逆覩其後焉。則知人之鑑，顧亦易與？彼慨人之難知，至有江海浮雲
translation_en:
…all requirements of the Inner Palace, including the requisitioning of pearls, jewels, incense, and wax: he abolished them all to relieve the people's distress. He also instructed the ministers: “I shall give particular attention to economy, and there will naturally be enough for expenditure.” Ah! These are words worthy of the Canon, Counsel, Instruction, and Announcement sections of the Book of Documents. Matching the excellence of Tang and Yu and according with the sagely ancestor, what good fortune this is for the altars of soil and grain and for all the people! You students, widely versed in antiquity and taking the present as your model, should expound these matters fully and extol them [?]. Do not neglect this.
Question: The Book of Documents says: “It lies in knowing men and in bringing peace to the people.” Knowing men is indeed the means of bringing peace to the people. It also says: “To know men is wisdom; even the emperor found this difficult.” Thus talented men are difficult both to obtain and to recognize. Yet when Yan Yuanxian administered the Western Capital, he discussed men with Fan Xiwen, and a single exchange of question and answer brought together four future chief councilors. When Zhang Zhongding governed Jinling, a single consultation secured two men, both outstanding talents of their day. Does this mean that obtaining talented men is not difficult after all? When Fang and Du were still obscure and had not yet accomplished even the slightest meritorious deed, those responsible for selecting officials already expected them to become the highest ministers of state. Lu, Luo, Wang, and Yang shone brilliantly in the literary arts in their day, yet those who assessed their capacity and judgment had already foreseen their later fortunes. Is discerning men, then, actually easy? Those who lament the difficulty of knowing men have even used comparisons involving rivers, seas, and floating clouds…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之喻抑又何也方今
聖明御極思得才賢以乂安斯民意甚殷也天
下士懷瑾握瑜雲蒸風會然用輒乏才
至厪
當宁知人之慮何與夫知之真而後用之不謬
不知知人果有其術與古有所謂五視
九徵之法亦可采而行之與大學衍義
所以辨人才者悉矣可得聞其要與為
政在人誠切務也故以質之多士
===
問人有恒言聖本生知無事于學乃孔子
大聖人也其自謂曰我非生而知之者
好古敏以求之者也又曰我學不厭豈
孔子之上復有所謂生知者乎抑其學
固與人異也夫學之益人自昔然矣故
佩豭之子解利劒而升堂築埋之兒聞
斷機而學孔不謁執政者固曾欲更經
利舉之人冠冕南州者其進在驚汗浹
背之後藉令此四子者安其故習罔典
punctuated:
之喻，抑又何也？方今聖明御極，思得才賢以乂安斯民，意甚殷也。天下士懷瑾握瑜，雲蒸風會，然用輒乏才，至厪當宁知人之慮，何與？夫知之真而後用之不謬，不知知人果有其術與？古有所謂五視九徵之法，亦可采而行之與？《大學衍義》所以辨人才者悉矣，可得聞其要與？為政在人，誠切務也，故以質之多士。

問：人有恒言，聖本生知，無事于學。乃孔子，大聖人也，其自謂曰：「我非生而知之者，好古，敏以求之者也。」又曰：「我學不厭。」豈孔子之上復有所謂生知者乎？抑其學固與人異也？夫學之益人，自昔然矣。故佩豭之子解利劒而升堂，築埋之兒聞斷機而學孔。不謁執政者，固曾欲更經利舉之人；冠冕南州者，其進在驚汗浹背之後。藉令此四子者安其故習，罔典
translation_en:
…such metaphors—why, then, was this so? Today our sagely and enlightened sovereign occupies the throne, earnestly wishing to obtain talented and worthy men to govern and bring peace to the people. Throughout the realm, scholars cherish jade-like virtues, gathering like rising clouds and converging winds. Yet whenever men are needed for service, talent proves lacking, even troubling the sovereign with the problem of discerning men. Why is this? Only after knowing men truly can one employ them without error. Is there indeed a method for discerning men? Could the ancient methods known as the Five Observations and Nine Tests also be adopted and put into practice? The Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) treats the discernment of talent comprehensively. May we hear its essentials? Government depends upon men: this is indeed an urgent concern. We therefore put these questions to you assembled scholars.

Question: People commonly say that sages are born knowing and have no need to learn. Yet Confucius, a great sage, said of himself: “I am not one who was born knowing; I love antiquity and diligently seek knowledge.” He also said: “I never tire of learning.” Could there be others above Confucius who truly possessed innate knowledge? Or was his learning inherently different from that of other people? Learning has benefited people since ancient times. Thus the young man who wore a boar ornament unfastened his sharp sword and ascended the hall; the child who played at burial [?], hearing the lesson of cutting the cloth on the loom, studied Confucius. The man who would not pay visits to those holding power had once wished to change his study of the Classics to gain an advantage in the examinations [?]; the man foremost in the southern region made his progress only after a shock left his back drenched in sweat. Suppose these four men had remained content with their former habits and paid no heed …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于學其終身所能至此否耶又有自
謂做人不倚師友載籍者有所見一定
不須窮索人稱其為天資出人非假學
力者皆若於生知似矣而一則不免於
禪學之疑一則坐蒙乎晚出之詬此又
何耶夫學人也不學而知天也天人之
際非知道者孰能一之二三子儻有達
於此者乎其以所自有者商之毋勦昔
人已吐之語
===
問寇賊姦宄蠻夷猾夏古盛世亦不免者
東粵之寇有猺黎倭醜及巢浪諸種類
不一彌竟山海出沒不時其所從來舊
矣畫計者曰勦與撫大都不越此兩者
然鐃歌甫畢而羽檄復馳納款未幾而
嘯聚旋熾豈制禦之術此兩者猶不足
以盡之而別有其說與或謂禦山寇易
禦海寇難蓋謂其雲帆風浪蹤跡飄忽
欲繫而殪之難也乃今舍其檣楫執梃
punctuated:
于學，其終身所能至此否耶？又有自謂做人不倚師友載籍者，有所見一定，不須窮索，人稱其為天資出人、非假學力者，皆若於生知似矣，而一則不免於禪學之疑，一則坐蒙乎晚出之詬，此又何耶？夫學，人也；不學而知，天也。天人之際，非知道者孰能一之？二三子儻有達於此者乎？其以所自有者商之，毋勦昔人已吐之語。

問：寇賊姦宄，蠻夷猾夏，古盛世亦不免者。東粵之寇，有猺、黎、倭醜及巢浪諸種，類不一，彌竟山海，出沒不時，其所從來舊矣。畫計者曰勦與撫，大都不越此兩者。然鐃歌甫畢，而羽檄復馳；納款未幾，而嘯聚旋熾。豈制禦之術，此兩者猶不足以盡之，而別有其說與？或謂禦山寇易，禦海寇難，蓋謂其雲帆風浪，蹤跡飄忽，欲繫而殪之難也。乃今舍其檣楫，執梃
translation_en:
…to learning, could they have attained such achievements in their lifetimes? There have also been those who claimed that, in conducting themselves as human beings, they did not rely on teachers, friends, or written works; and those whose understanding, once settled, required no further searching, whom people praised as possessing natural gifts surpassing others, without depending on the effort of study. Both seem to resemble those born with knowledge. Yet one could not escape suspicion of practicing Chan Buddhist learning, while the other incurred reproach for having appeared only belatedly [?]. Why should this be? Learning belongs to the human; knowing without learning belongs to Heaven. At the juncture of Heaven and humanity, who but someone who understands the Way can unite the two? Might any of you gentlemen have grasped this? Discuss it on the basis of your own understanding; do not plagiarize words already uttered by men of the past.

Question: Bandits and criminals, evildoers within and without, and non-Chinese peoples disturbing the Chinese realm—these were troubles that even the flourishing ages of antiquity could not avoid. Among the bandits of eastern Yue are the Yao, the Li, the vile Japanese raiders, and the various Chao and Lang groups [?]. They are of many kinds, spread throughout the mountains and seas, appearing and disappearing at unpredictable times. Their origins go far back. Those who devise plans speak of suppression and pacification; generally, their proposals do not go beyond these two measures. Yet scarcely have the victory songs ended before urgent military dispatches speed forth again; not long after submission has been offered, bands gather again and their violence swiftly intensifies. Could it be that these two measures do not exhaust the methods of controlling them, and that there is some other approach? Some say that defending against mountain bandits is easy, but defending against sea raiders is difficult. Presumably they mean that, with sails reaching to the clouds amid wind and waves, the raiders’ movements are elusive, making it difficult to capture and kill them. But now they abandon their masts and oars and take up clubs…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
刃而與山寇竝訌則山與海何别而計
又將安施耶又謂黎猺盤流卒難盡殲
當先拔其苞孽如治病先腹心而後手
足其說似矣然刋山通道之謀費重而
難舉土舍招主之設詭譎而難憑腹心
手足總之爲病則所以治之者又當孰
先後也夫士明於當世之務者然後可
與言經濟矧二三子生長海邦恫瘝乆
矣其以嘉謨相告當事者將采而行之
punctuated: 刃而與山寇竝訌，則山與海何别，而計又將安施耶？又謂黎猺盤流，卒難盡殲，當先拔其苞孽，如治病先腹心而後手足，其說似矣。然刋山通道之謀，費重而難舉；土舍招主之設，詭譎而難憑。腹心手足，總之爲病，則所以治之者，又當孰先後也？夫士明於當世之務者，然後可與言經濟。矧二三子生長海邦，恫瘝乆矣，其以嘉謨相告，當事者將采而行之。
translation_en:
…and blades, joining the mountain bandits in rebellion, what distinction remains between mountain and sea, and what strategy can now be applied? It is further argued that the Li and Yao, entrenched or roaming [?], are ultimately difficult to annihilate entirely; their deep-rooted sources of trouble should therefore be eradicated first, just as one treats illness first in the vital organs and then in the limbs. This argument seems plausible. Yet plans to cut through mountains and open roads are costly and difficult to undertake; arrangements involving the sons of native officials and leaders charged with securing submission [?] are beset by deceit and difficult to rely upon. Whether in the vital organs or the limbs, all are illnesses: which, then, should be treated first, and which afterward?
Only with scholars who understand the affairs of the present age can one discuss statecraft. Moreover, you gentlemen were born and raised in this coastal region and have long felt its suffering. Share your sound counsels with us; those responsible for these affairs will adopt and implement them.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰性相近也習相遠也
霍鎭東
同考試官教諭王批性字塲中作者率欠體
認是篇發明眞切蓋嘗究心性學者
考試官教諭萬批見理精深措辭醇雅
考試官教授鄒批體認精確
聖人原性之初而究其所由異焉夫性之相近
===
者其初也至有相遠則由於習耳而豈性之有
異乎夫子欲人自識其初言此若曰天下之論
性者惟因其所習之異遂以性爲相遠矣曷自
其初而觀之夫性也者帝降之衷盡夫人而各
正民秉之彝隨所賦而惟均雖其乗夫氣者有
清濁之不同矣然稟氣之初其天精未汩也蓋
不過統同中之小異耳雖其麗夫質者有厚薄
之不一矣然凝質之初其天粹未漓也蓋不過
合一中之少間耳但形生之後而命於天者不
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「性相近也，習相遠也。」

霍鎭東

同考試官教諭王批：「性字，塲中作者率欠體認。是篇發明眞切，蓋嘗究心性學者。」

考試官教諭萬批：「見理精深，措辭醇雅。」

考試官教授鄒批：「體認精確。」

聖人原性之初，而究其所由異焉。夫性之相近者，其初也；至有相遠，則由於習耳，而豈性之有異乎？夫子欲人自識其初，言此若曰：天下之論性者，惟因其所習之異，遂以性爲相遠矣。曷自其初而觀之？夫性也者，帝降之衷，盡夫人而各正；民秉之彝，隨所賦而惟均。雖其乗夫氣者，有清濁之不同矣，然稟氣之初，其天精未汩也，蓋不過統同中之小異耳。雖其麗夫質者，有厚薄之不一矣，然凝質之初，其天粹未漓也，蓋不過合一中之少間耳。但形生之後，而命於天者不
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “By nature, people are close to one another; through practice, they grow far apart.”

Huo Zhendong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Most candidates in this examination have failed to grasp adequately the meaning of ‘nature.’ This essay elucidates it truly and precisely. Its author must have devoted himself to the study of nature.”

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “His insight into principle is penetrating and profound; his diction is pure and elegant.”

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “His understanding is precise and sound.”

The Sage traces human nature to its beginnings and investigates how differences arise within it. That people are close to one another in nature describes their original condition. When they become far apart, this results only from practice: how could it mean that their natures differ? The Master wished people to recognize their own original condition. In saying this, he meant something like the following: Those in the world who discuss human nature take differences in acquired practices as grounds for concluding that people’s natures are far apart. Why not consider nature from its beginnings? Nature is the moral mean bestowed by the Lord on High, correct in every person without exception; it is the constant norm that the people possess, equally present in the endowment each receives. Although the vital energy through which it is borne differs in clarity and turbidity, at the moment this energy is first received, its heavenly essence has not yet been obscured. These are merely small differences within an underlying sameness. Although the physical constitutions to which it attaches differ in robustness and frailty, when those constitutions first take shape, their heavenly purity has not yet been diluted. These are merely slight variations within an underlying unity. Yet after bodily form comes into being, what is ordained by Heaven does not…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
金節
同考試官學正林批發揮聖人自責之意最
爲婉切宜錄之以式多士
考試官教諭萬批辭不繁而意自縝密
考試官教授鄒批簡潔可嘉
聖人責人以子臣之道而以之自責焉甚矣聖
人人道之極也而自責者不外乎子臣之倫道
之不遠人也可見矣昔中庸引夫子之言以明
道也若曰學以盡倫爲先倫以君親爲大丘竊
===
有志焉而未之逮也是故子之事父天之性也
吾固謂不可解於其心而求人以爲子之翼矣
然而吾之所以事父亦人之所以爲子也反之
於已其能如其所求乎蓋親之恩罔極而人子
之孝養爲無方苟一毫之未盡即子道之有虧
皇皇焉惟懼其忝爾所生此吾之所以明發有
懷也敢曰能之而姑以自恕哉臣之事君天之
制也吾固謂無所逃於其分而求人以爲臣之
共矣然而吾之所以事君亦人之所以爲臣也
punctuated:
金節

同考試官學正林批：發揮聖人自責之意，最爲婉切，宜錄之以式多士。
考試官教諭萬批：辭不繁而意自縝密。
考試官教授鄒批：簡潔可嘉。

聖人責人以子臣之道，而以之自責焉。甚矣，聖人人道之極也！而自責者不外乎子臣之倫，道之不遠人也可見矣。昔中庸引夫子之言以明道也，若曰：學以盡倫爲先，倫以君親爲大，丘竊有志焉而未之逮也。是故子之事父，天之性也。吾固謂不可解於其心，而求人以爲子之翼矣。然而吾之所以事父，亦人之所以爲子也。反之於已，其能如其所求乎？蓋親之恩罔極，而人子之孝養爲無方。苟一毫之未盡，即子道之有虧，皇皇焉惟懼其忝爾所生，此吾之所以明發有懷也。敢曰能之而姑以自恕哉？臣之事君，天之制也。吾固謂無所逃於其分，而求人以爲臣之共矣。然而吾之所以事君，亦人之所以爲臣也。
translation_en:
Jin Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor: His exposition of the sage’s intention in holding himself to account is especially tactful and apposite. This should be included as a model for the many scholars.
Comment by Examiner Wan, County School Instructor: The wording is concise, yet the thought is closely reasoned.
Comment by Examiner Zou, Prefectural School Instructor: Commendably succinct and clear.

The sage holds others accountable to the Way of the son and the minister, and holds himself accountable by the same standard. How consummate is the sage as the highest embodiment of the human Way! Yet the standards by which he holds himself accountable extend no further than the relationships of son and minister. From this we can see that the Way is not far from human beings. The Doctrine of the Mean quoted the Master’s words to elucidate the Way, as though he were saying: In learning, fulfilling one’s human relationships comes first; among those relationships, those with ruler and parents are paramount. I, Qiu, privately aspire to this, but have not yet attained it.

Thus, a son’s service to his father springs from Heaven-endowed nature. I have always maintained that this obligation cannot be relaxed in one’s heart, and have required of others the reverent conduct proper to a son. Yet the principles by which I serve my father are also those by which others act as sons. Turning the scrutiny upon myself, can I measure up to what I require of them? Parents’ kindness is boundless, and a son’s filial care admits of no fixed limits. If even the slightest part remains unfulfilled, the Way of the son is deficient. Anxiously, I fear only bringing shame upon those who gave me birth. This is why, when dawn breaks, my thoughts remain with them. Dare I claim to be capable of this and complacently excuse myself?

A minister’s service to his ruler is ordained by Heaven. I have always maintained that there is no escaping the duty inherent in one’s station, and have required of others the reverence proper to a minister. Yet the principles by which I serve my ruler are also those by which others act as ministers. …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
反之於已其能如其所求乎蓋君之尊如天而
人臣之忠愛為無已苟一毫之未盡即臣節之
未純皇皇焉惟恐其上負吾君此吾之所以夙
夜匪懈也敢曰能之而容以自諉哉是則子道
也臣道也不遠於人也而以此責人自責夫豈
遠人以為道哉雖然聖人亦非心以為能而故
為是退託也蓋臣子之心無窮雖忠孝之至亦
不過其當為之分耳自昔稱忠孝莫盛於舜與
周公然一則夔夔齋慄一則公孫碩膚與夫子
===
未能之心一也若自以為已足則豈聖人之心
哉
中天下而立定四海之民
徐賛化
同考試官教諭唐 批 格局正大辭氣明整可
以觀所養矣敬羡敬羡
考試官教諭萬 批 辭健氣渾迥異眾作
考試官教授鄒 批 醇正典雅
觀君子一統之治而道之大行可知矣夫君子
punctuated:
反之於已，其能如其所求乎？蓋君之尊如天，而人臣之忠愛為無已。苟一毫之未盡，即臣節之未純。皇皇焉，惟恐其上負吾君，此吾之所以夙夜匪懈也。敢曰能之，而容以自諉哉？是則子道也，臣道也，不遠於人也。而以此責人、自責，夫豈遠人以為道哉？雖然，聖人亦非心以為能，而故為是退託也。蓋臣子之心無窮，雖忠孝之至，亦不過其當為之分耳。自昔稱忠孝，莫盛於舜與周公。然一則夔夔齋慄，一則公孫碩膚，與夫子未能之心一也。若自以為已足，則豈聖人之心哉？

中天下而立，定四海之民。
徐賛化

同考試官教諭唐批：格局正大，辭氣明整，可以觀所養矣。敬羡！敬羡！
考試官教諭萬批：辭健氣渾，迥異眾作。
考試官教授鄒批：醇正典雅。

觀君子一統之治，而道之大行可知矣。夫君子
translation_en:
…Turning this back upon oneself, can one live up to what one demands of others? The ruler is as exalted as Heaven, and a minister’s loyal devotion knows no end. If even the slightest part remains unfulfilled, the minister’s integrity is not yet pure. Anxiously fearing only that I might fail my ruler above, I remain unremitting from dawn to night. Dare I claim to have succeeded and permit myself to evade responsibility? Thus the way of the son and the way of the minister are not remote from human beings. To hold others and oneself accountable by these standards—how could this be to seek the Way far from human beings? Nevertheless, the sage does not inwardly consider himself fully capable and deliberately make such disclaimers out of modesty. The devotion of a minister or son is inexhaustible: even the utmost loyalty and filial piety amount only to fulfilling one’s proper duty. Since antiquity, none have been more celebrated for loyalty and filial piety than Shun and the Duke of Zhou. Yet the one was reverent, solemn, and apprehensive; the other was humble and yielding, yet great in achievement. Their hearts were at one with the Master’s sense that he had not yet succeeded. If one considered oneself already adequate, how could that be the heart of a sage?

“Standing at the center of all under Heaven and bringing settled order to the people within the Four Seas.”
By Xu Zanhua.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The structure is upright and grand; the language and tone are clear and orderly. These reveal the author’s self-cultivation. Admirable! Admirable!”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “Vigorous language and a full, integrated spirit distinguish this decisively from the other compositions.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Pure and orthodox, classically refined.”

By observing the gentleman’s unified governance, one can recognize the widespread realization of the Way. Now, the gentleman…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以天下爲度者也中天下而定四海則一統之
治在是矣不可以見道之大行也哉昔孟子論
性而先之以此曰君子之欲行其道者心也而
所賴以得行其道者勢也廣土衆民勢固可資
而不猶有所限乎兹焉體元凝命而居中以君
臨乎萬邦嚮明出治而宅中以宰制乎六合中
國之要樞于是乎握也而乂安之澤有以弘敷
而不匱天下之根本于是乎植也而撫綏之仁
有以廣運而無方中天下而爲紀法之宗盡一
===
世而帲冒之而凡四海之待命於我者胥此焉
定其分矣中天下而爲綱常之主盡一世而甄
陶之而凡四海之取則於我者胥此焉定其性
矣斯蓋語其統御之大則極天所覆也極地所
載也而聯屬天下以成其身矣廣土云乎哉語
其德業之隆則覆之如天焉載之如地焉而以
萬物得所爲極致矣衆民云乎哉吁觀於君子
之所樂在此其視夫所欲者誠有間矣雖然所
謂君子之樂之者非徒以是爲榮也蓋一夫不
punctuated: 以天下爲度者也。中天下而定四海，則一統之治在是矣，不可以見道之大行也哉？昔孟子論性而先之以此，曰：君子之欲行其道者，心也；而所賴以得行其道者，勢也。廣土衆民，勢固可資，而不猶有所限乎？兹焉體元凝命，而居中以君臨乎萬邦；嚮明出治，而宅中以宰制乎六合。中國之要樞于是乎握也，而乂安之澤有以弘敷而不匱；天下之根本于是乎植也，而撫綏之仁有以廣運而無方。中天下而爲紀法之宗，盡一世而帲冒之，而凡四海之待命於我者，胥此焉定其分矣；中天下而爲綱常之主，盡一世而甄陶之，而凡四海之取則於我者，胥此焉定其性矣。斯蓋語其統御之大，則極天所覆也，極地所載也，而聯屬天下以成其身矣，廣土云乎哉？語其德業之隆，則覆之如天焉，載之如地焉，而以萬物得所爲極致矣，衆民云乎哉？吁！觀於君子之所樂在此，其視夫所欲者，誠有間矣。雖然，所謂君子之樂之者，非徒以是爲榮也。蓋一夫不
translation_en: …takes all under Heaven as his measure. Standing at the center of all under Heaven and bringing stability to the four seas: herein lies unified government. Does this not reveal the Way being widely put into practice? In discussing human nature, Mengzi prefaced his account with this, saying: What moves the gentleman to wish to put his Way into practice is his heart; what he relies upon to be able to do so is his position of power. Extensive territory and a numerous population certainly provide power upon which he can draw, yet does this not still have its limits? Here he embodies the primal principle and secures the Mandate, occupying the center to rule over the myriad states; facing the light, he issues his government’s commands, dwelling at the center to govern the six directions. Thus he grasps the vital pivot of the Central Kingdom, enabling the benefits of peace and order to spread widely without exhaustion. Thus he establishes the foundation of all under Heaven, enabling his benevolent care and pacification to extend everywhere without bounds. Standing at the center of all under Heaven as the fountainhead of regulations and laws, he shelters the entire age; all within the four seas who await his commands thereby have their respective stations settled. Standing at the center of all under Heaven as the master of the cardinal relationships and constant moral norms, he molds the entire age; all within the four seas who take their standards from him thereby have their moral natures settled. Thus, speaking of the vastness of his dominion, it reaches to the limits of all that Heaven covers and Earth bears, joining all under Heaven together to form a single body. Can this be described merely as extensive territory? Speaking of the grandeur of his virtue and achievements, he shelters all as Heaven does and supports all as Earth does, taking as his highest attainment that the myriad things should each find their proper place. Can this be described merely as a numerous population? Ah! When we see that the gentleman’s delight lies here, there is indeed a distinction between this and what he desires. Nevertheless, to say that the gentleman delights in this does not mean that he merely regards it as an honor. For if even one man fails to…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
獲猶曰時予之辜而道旣大行君子之心始慰
矣不然堯舜事業亦漠然無所與耳寧足以動
其心耶故大行窮居必處之一而後見君子所
性之蘊
易
聖人以順動則刑罰清而民服
徐賛化
同考試官敎諭陳批豫道不外順動此作就
豫上發揮精密典雅點民服尤有關鍵宜冠本房
===
考試官敎諭萬批發上下和樂意明雅
考試官敎授鄒批發揮道明悉
聖人以豫道治天下而大順之化成焉蓋順而
動豫道也聖人以此爲治而天下有不順應之
者乎此見豫之道大也且豫以和樂爲義而以
順動爲德推其極天地旣不能外之以運化矣
聖人之治天下何如哉蓋其心與理涵而本之
爲和順之積故其動與理俱而達之爲至順之
猷以總萬幾非一無所爲也然皆隨感而順應
punctuated:
獲，猶曰：「時予之辜。」而道旣大行，君子之心始慰矣。不然，堯舜事業亦漠然無所與耳，寧足以動其心耶？故大行窮居，必處之一，而後見君子所性之蘊。

易
聖人以順動則刑罰清而民服
徐賛化

同考試官敎諭陳批：豫道不外順動，此作就豫上發揮，精密典雅，點民服尤有關鍵，宜冠本房。
考試官敎諭萬批：發上下和樂意，明雅。
考試官敎授鄒批：發揮道明悉。

聖人以豫道治天下，而大順之化成焉。蓋順而動，豫道也。聖人以此爲治，而天下有不順應之者乎？此見豫之道大也。且豫以和樂爲義，而以順動爲德。推其極，天地旣不能外之以運化矣，聖人之治天下何如哉？蓋其心與理涵，而本之爲和順之積；故其動與理俱，而達之爲至順之猷。以總萬幾，非一無所爲也，然皆隨感而順應
translation_en:
…fails to find his proper place, he still says, “This is my fault.” Only when the Way prevails widely does the gentleman’s heart find comfort. Otherwise, even the achievements of Yao and Shun would leave him indifferent, as though they had nothing to do with him; how could they suffice to move his heart? Thus, whether his Way prevails widely or he lives in obscurity, he must approach both alike. Only then can the depths of the gentleman’s inherent nature be seen.

Book of Changes
“When the sage acts in accordance with what is right, punishments become clear and the people submit.”
Xu Zanhua

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The Way of Yu (Contentment) consists entirely in acting in accordance with what is right. This composition develops its argument from Yu with precision, refinement, and classical elegance. Its treatment of “the people submit” is especially pivotal. It should rank first in this examination section.

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: It develops the meaning of harmony and joy between those above and those below, with clarity and elegance.

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: Its exposition of the Way is clear and thorough.

The sage governs all under Heaven through the Way of Yu, and thereby brings about a transformation toward perfect accord. For acting in accordance with what is right is the Way of Yu. When the sage governs by this means, can anyone under Heaven fail to respond in accord? Here we see the greatness of the Way of Yu. Now, Yu signifies harmony and joy, and its virtue is action in accord with what is right. Taken to its fullest extent, even Heaven and Earth cannot operate and transform outside it. How, then, does the sage govern all under Heaven? His heart is steeped in principle, making this the foundation of accumulated harmony and accord. Thus his actions accompany principle, giving it expression in plans of utmost accord. In overseeing the myriad affairs of government, he does not simply do nothing; rather, in every case he responds in accord with whatever moves him…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之聖人之所爲固人心之所欲爲者也而一毫
私智不存焉以裁庶務非一無所事也然皆因
勢而利導之聖人之有事乃天下之所恃以無
事者也而一毫己意不與焉夫如是吾知順動
之德旣參諸天地而不違則和樂之情自通乎
上下而無間國有五刑將以弼敎也玆則敎已
孚於神道之設而民默順乎帝則焉刑不必施
而天下咸以聖人之心爲心矣是謂無爲而治
其治之所以益隆乎刑有五罰將以明法也玆
===
則法已昭於大道之公而民自格其非心焉罰
不必用而天下皆以聖人之德爲德矣是謂不
言而化其化之所以益神乎夫盡民而服之又
不假刑罰焉順之極也豫之至也而以順動得
之豫之爲義大矣哉嗟乎此堯舜事也精一執
中垂拱無爲而時雍於變堯舜不知焉殆與天
地之順動一道也至於禹則有不然者下車之
泣蓋傷之也而刑罰其可遽措乎雖然禹非不
能順動而民自爲心時也無害其爲服也人君
punctuated: 之。聖人之所爲，固人心之所欲爲者也，而一毫私智不存焉。以裁庶務，非一無所事也，然皆因勢而利導之。聖人之有事，乃天下之所恃以無事者也，而一毫己意不與焉。夫如是，吾知順動之德旣參諸天地而不違，則和樂之情自通乎上下而無間。國有五刑，將以弼敎也。玆則敎已孚於神道之設，而民默順乎帝則焉。刑不必施，而天下咸以聖人之心爲心矣。是謂無爲而治，其治之所以益隆乎！刑有五罰，將以明法也。玆則法已昭於大道之公，而民自格其非心焉。罰不必用，而天下皆以聖人之德爲德矣。是謂不言而化，其化之所以益神乎！夫盡民而服之，又不假刑罰焉，順之極也，豫之至也，而以順動得之。豫之爲義大矣哉！嗟乎！此堯舜事也。精一執中，垂拱無爲，而時雍於變，堯舜不知焉，殆與天地之順動一道也。至於禹，則有不然者。下車之泣，蓋傷之也，而刑罰其可遽措乎？雖然，禹非不能順動，而民自爲心，時也，無害其爲服也。人君
translation_en:
…to them. What the sage does is precisely what the hearts of the people wish to do, and not the slightest trace of private cleverness remains in it. In managing the many affairs of government, he is not wholly without tasks; rather, he always follows the circumstances and guides them to advantage. The sage’s undertaking of affairs is what all under Heaven rely upon for freedom from trouble, and not the slightest trace of personal will enters into it. Thus, I know that once his virtue of acting in accordance with the natural order accords with Heaven and Earth without deviation, feelings of harmony and joy naturally pass between those above and below without obstruction.

The state has the five punishments to support its teaching. Here, however, that teaching has already won trust through instruction grounded in the spiritual Way, and the people silently conform to the Supreme Lord’s standards. Punishments need not be imposed, and all under Heaven take the sage’s heart as their own. This is called governing through nonaction: is this not why his government becomes ever more flourishing? The penal system has five fines to make the law manifest. Here, however, the law is already clear through the impartiality of the Great Way, and the people themselves rectify their wrongful thoughts. Fines need not be used, and all under Heaven take the sage’s virtue as their own. This is called transforming without words: is this not why his transforming influence becomes ever more wondrous?

To bring all the people into willing submission without resorting to punishments or fines is the utmost of accord and the culmination of Yu, joyful harmony; it is attained by acting in accordance with the natural order. Great indeed is the meaning of Yu! Ah, these were the accomplishments of Yao and Shun. Through refinement and singleness of purpose they held fast to the Mean; with robes hanging down and hands folded, they practiced nonaction. Yet the people were transformed and brought into harmony, without Yao and Shun being conscious of it. This was surely one and the same Way as the movement of Heaven and Earth in accordance with the natural order.

With Yu, however, matters were somewhat different. His tears upon descending from his carriage expressed his sorrow over this; how, then, could punishments and fines immediately be set aside? Nevertheless, it was not that Yu could not act in accordance with the natural order. Rather, the people each pursued their own inclinations: this was a matter of the times and did not prevent their submission. The ruler…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
欲法堯舜其惟以順動乎
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深也
故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成天下
之務唯神也故不疾而速不行而至
梁俸
同考試官教諭陳批融會幾深本旨說入通
志成務一神所為意明徹可玩允宜高薦
考試官教諭萬批諸作幾深神類用套惟
積此獨脫去浮辭洞見本真殆邃於易學者
===
考試官教授鄒批歸功聖人得旨
大傳以易道歸聖人而因推其妙用焉甚矣易
非聖人不能作也易作而天下之妙用具是矣
人可不知所尚乎大傳之意若曰易之為道闡
於聖心者甚微而利於天下也甚大是故辭占
象變皆易也而以為聖人之道何哉蓋以吉凶
之理精入無形若是乎深矣聖人以心涵之而
繫之辭焉决之占焉所以洩此理之祕而究極
其深也深極而精有不顯乎老少之端變動莫
punctuated:
欲法堯舜，其惟以順動乎？

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。

梁俸

同考試官教諭陳批：融會幾深本旨，說入通志成務，一神所為，意明徹可玩，允宜高薦。

考試官教諭萬批：諸作幾深神，類用套，惟積此獨脫去浮辭，洞見本真，殆邃於易學者。

考試官教授鄒批：歸功聖人，得旨。

大傳以易道歸聖人，而因推其妙用焉。甚矣，易非聖人不能作也！易作而天下之妙用具，是矣，人可不知所尚乎？大傳之意若曰：易之為道，闡於聖心者甚微，而利於天下也甚大。是故辭占象變皆易也，而以為聖人之道，何哉？蓋以吉凶之理，精入無形，若是乎深矣。聖人以心涵之，而繫之辭焉，决之占焉，所以洩此理之祕，而究極其深也。深極而精有不顯乎？老少之端，變動莫
translation_en:
…If a ruler wishes to emulate Yao and Shun, must he not act in accordance with the natural order?

“The Changes is that by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient. Only through depth can they comprehend the intentions of all under Heaven; only through the incipient can they accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; only through the numinous can they be swift without haste and arrive without traveling.”

Liang Feng 梁俸

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He integrates the fundamental meanings of the incipient and the deep, bringing his exposition to bear on comprehending intentions and accomplishing affairs, both as operations of the numinous. His meaning is clear and penetrating, and rewards contemplation. He certainly deserves a high recommendation.”

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The other compositions mostly use stock formulas in discussing the incipient, the deep, and the numinous. This one alone [?] sheds empty rhetoric and penetrates to the essential truth. Its author must be deeply versed in the study of the Changes.”

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “By attributing the achievement to the sages, he grasps the purport.”

The Great Commentary attributes the Way of the Changes to the sages and proceeds to expound its wondrous operations. How true it is that none but sages could have composed the Changes! Once the Changes was composed, the wondrous operations of all under Heaven were fully embodied in it. This being so, can people fail to know what they should esteem? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as if to say: the Way of the Changes, as unfolded in the sages’ minds, is exceedingly subtle, yet its benefit to all under Heaven is exceedingly great. Thus, the statements, divinations, images, and transformations all belong to the Changes. Why, then, are they deemed the Way of the sages?

It is because the principles of good and ill fortune are so fine that they enter the realm of the formless: such is their depth. The sages embrace them in their minds, attach statements to them, and determine them through divination. By these means they disclose the secrets of these principles and plumb their depths to the utmost. Once their depths have been fully plumbed, how could their subtleties fail to become manifest? The beginnings of the old and young forms of yin and yang change and move without…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
測若是乎幾矣聖人以心契之而裁之變焉定
之象焉所以發此端之微而研窮其幾也幾研
而變有不著乎夫惟辭占一深也故能受命知
來示人以失得之報而天下無復有惑志矣惟
象變一幾也故能成文定象鼓人以趨避之方
而天下無復有廢務矣惟深與幾而無思無爲
一天下之至神也故機動於無端而化應於無
迹志之通也若或啓之務之成也若或翼之所
以妙於寂而通於感者又豈待疾而後速行而
===
後至也哉此其精變之用雖達之天下而幾深
之妙實闡於聖人惟聖人妙神道以設教故天
下自鼓舞以盡神易有聖人之道不其然乎雖
然易之作也聖人豈得已哉幾深之理弗彰則
天下無由以寡過因貳以濟民行其慮蓋深矣
故象變立卽不能忘象辭占立卽不能忘言尚
易者又執其象與言而求之聖人之意益遠矣
宋儒有言君子脩之吉小人悖之凶蓋得之言
象之外也其深於易者乎
punctuated: 測，若是乎幾矣！聖人以心契之，而裁之變焉，定之象焉，所以發此端之微而研窮其幾也。幾研而變有不著乎？夫惟辭占一深也，故能受命知來，示人以失得之報，而天下無復有惑志矣。惟象變一幾也，故能成文定象，鼓人以趨避之方，而天下無復有廢務矣。惟深與幾而無思無爲，一天下之至神也，故機動於無端，而化應於無迹。志之通也，若或啓之；務之成也，若或翼之。所以妙於寂而通於感者，又豈待疾而後速、行而後至也哉？此其精變之用雖達之天下，而幾深之妙實闡於聖人。惟聖人妙神道以設教，故天下自鼓舞以盡神。易有聖人之道，不其然乎？雖然，易之作也，聖人豈得已哉？幾深之理弗彰，則天下無由以寡過。因貳以濟民行，其慮蓋深矣。故象變立，卽不能忘象；辭占立，卽不能忘言。尚易者又執其象與言而求之，聖人之意益遠矣。宋儒有言：「君子脩之吉，小人悖之凶。」蓋得之言象之外也，其深於易者乎！
translation_en:
…beyond fathoming: how subtle are these incipient movements! The sage apprehends them in his mind, regulates them through the changes, and fixes them in the images, thereby revealing the subtlety of these beginnings and thoroughly investigating their incipient movements. Once these movements have been investigated, could the changes fail to become manifest? The statements and divinations share one profundity; thus they can receive an inquiry and disclose what is to come, showing people the consequences of loss and gain, so that no perplexity of purpose remains in the world. The images and changes share one subtlety of incipient movement; thus they can form patterns and establish images, prompting people with methods for pursuing what is favorable and avoiding what is harmful, so that no undertaking in the world remains neglected. Profundity and incipient movement, operating without thought or action, together constitute the utmost spiritual efficacy in the world. Thus their impulse stirs without any discernible beginning, and their transforming responses leave no trace. When purposes become clear, it is as though something were opening the way; when undertakings reach completion, it is as though something were lending assistance. Such wondrous stillness and responsiveness to stimulation—how could they require haste to be swift, or movement to arrive?

Although this operation of subtle understanding and change extends throughout the world, the wonder of incipient movement and profundity is in fact revealed through the sage. Only the sage draws wondrously upon the way of spiritual efficacy to establish instruction; thus all under Heaven are spontaneously stirred and inspired to realize that efficacy fully. Is it not indeed true that the Changes contains the way of the sage? Yet could the sage have refrained from composing the Changes? If the principles of incipient movement and profundity were not made manifest, people throughout the world would have no means of reducing their errors. By addressing their doubts, he aided the people in their conduct: profound indeed was his concern.

Thus, once images and changes have been established, one cannot forget the images; once statements and divinations have been established, one cannot forget the words. Yet if those who esteem the Changes cling to its images and words in seeking it, the sage’s intention grows ever more remote. A Confucian scholar of the Song said: “For the gentleman who cultivates it, good fortune; for the petty man who goes against it, misfortune.” This surely grasps what lies beyond words and images. Was he not one who understood the Changes profoundly?

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
九德咸事俊乂在官百僚師師百工惟時
撫于五辰庶績其凝
金節
同考試官學正林批
近作于九德俊乂百僚
百工講多纏繞子獨辭不費而理明亦佳作也
考試官敎諭萬批虞廷得人氣象宛然在
目可取可敬
考試官敎授鄒批清脫得旨
===
大臣論官人之效羣賢用而治功成也蓋治道
以人而立也羣賢悉效其用而治功其有不成
者哉皐陶陳謨至此若曰天下無不可用之賢
人君貴得善用之道誠於九德之人而翕受敷
施矣吾知德之在人雖有多寡而均為有常之
吉也舉咸自奮於明時而因才以任事人之抱
德雖有大小而均為俊乂之良也玆皆布列於
庶位而隨事以服官以斯人也任斯治也同道
以為朋則見其百僚之師師焉惟善是主孚契
punctuated:
書

九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

金節

同考試官學正林批：近作于九德、俊乂、百僚、百工，講多纏繞。子獨辭不費而理明，亦佳作也。

考試官敎諭萬批：虞廷得人氣象，宛然在目，可取可敬。

考試官敎授鄒批：清脫得旨。

大臣論官人之效，羣賢用而治功成也。蓋治道以人而立也，羣賢悉效其用，而治功其有不成者哉？皐陶陳謨至此，若曰：天下無不可用之賢，人君貴得善用之道。誠於九德之人而翕受敷施矣，吾知德之在人，雖有多寡，而均為有常之吉也。舉咸自奮於明時，而因才以任事；人之抱德，雖有大小，而均為俊乂之良也。玆皆布列於庶位，而隨事以服官。以斯人也，任斯治也。同道以為朋，則見其百僚之師師焉。惟善是主，孚契
translation_en:
Documents (Shu)

“When those possessing the nine virtues all undertake service, and men of outstanding talent hold office, the many officials learn from one another, and all officers attend to timely duties. In accord with the five celestial markers, all achievements will be firmly established.”

Jin Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor: Recent essays have often become tangled in their explanations of the nine virtues, outstanding men, the many officials, and all officers. Your wording alone is economical while your reasoning is clear. This too is a fine composition.

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: The scene of the court of Yu obtaining worthy men stands vividly before the eyes. Worthy of acceptance and respect.

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: Clear and unencumbered; it grasps the essential meaning.

The great minister discusses the results of appointing men to office: when the assembled worthies are employed, the work of government is accomplished. For the way of governing is established through people. When all the worthies fully exercise their abilities, how could the work of government fail to be accomplished? When Gao Yao reaches this point in presenting his counsels, it is as though he were saying: There are no worthy men in the world who cannot be employed; what matters for the ruler is to find the way to employ them well. If he truly receives men possessing the nine virtues together and distributes them in service, I know that, although the virtues people possess may be more or fewer, all are good men of constancy. They all exert themselves in an enlightened age and undertake responsibilities according to their talents. Although the virtue people cherish may be greater or smaller, all are excellent men of outstanding ability. They are now arrayed throughout the various posts and hold office according to the tasks to be performed. These are the men entrusted with this government. When they form fellowship through a shared Way, we see the many officials learning from one another. Taking goodness alone as their guiding principle, they are united in mutual trust…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于人已之交無睽志矣率職以自效則見其百
工之咸勤焉若時是務順播乎節宣之宜無曠
官矣夫衆賢悉致既有以豫敏政之本羣力畢
宣又足以臻廣業之休庶績之分理於邦家者
不齊也自是其人存則其政舉而治具燦然焉
之弘敷矣故勳之業於今其為烈乎庶績之分
布於天下者不一也自是有治人斯有治法而
衆功秩然焉之就緒矣煕載之治今玆其考成
乎吁治不自成而成於官之得人人不易得而
===
得於知之有道帝於知人之謨可不加之意哉
雖然官人要矣而君身尤為取人之本苟少肆
於功成之餘亦未有能盡其用者故君臣相遇
自古為難此臯陶陳謨必先之以允迪厥德而
無教逸欲之戒尤惓惓於庶績其凝之後也嘉
有虞之治者尚鑒玆哉
一人有慶兆民賴之
周篤棐
同考試官學正林批〔通篇氣格渾融而歸重〕
punctuated:
于人已之交，無睽志矣。率職以自效，則見其百工之咸勤焉；若時是務，順播乎節宣之宜，無曠官矣。夫衆賢悉致，既有以豫敏政之本；羣力畢宣，又足以臻廣業之休。庶績之分理於邦家者不齊也，自是其人存則其政舉，而治具燦然焉之弘敷矣。故勳之業，於今其為烈乎！庶績之分布於天下者不一也，自是有治人斯有治法，而衆功秩然焉之就緒矣。煕載之治，今玆其考成乎！吁！治不自成，而成於官之得人；人不易得，而得於知之有道。帝於知人之謨，可不加之意哉？雖然，官人要矣，而君身尤為取人之本。苟少肆於功成之餘，亦未有能盡其用者。故君臣相遇，自古為難。此臯陶陳謨，必先之以允迪厥德，而無教逸欲之戒，尤惓惓於庶績其凝之後也。嘉有虞之治者，尚鑒玆哉！
一人有慶，兆民賴之。
周篤棐
同考試官學正林批〔通篇氣格渾融，而歸重〕
translation_en:
…in relations between others and oneself, there will be no discord of purpose. When they discharge their duties to prove their worth, all the officials will be seen diligently at work. Attending to what the times require and appropriately regulating and distributing their efforts, they will leave no office neglected. Bringing together all the worthy thus provides in advance the foundation for effective government; fully employing their collective strength also suffices to achieve the excellence of far-reaching accomplishments. The many tasks separately administered within the state differ in kind. Henceforth, with the right men present, their policies will be carried out, and the instruments of government will be splendidly and extensively deployed. Will the work of established achievement [?] now become illustrious! The many tasks distributed throughout the realm are likewise diverse. Henceforth, with men capable of governing, there will be methods of government, and the various undertakings will proceed in orderly fashion. Will the government that makes all affairs flourish now have its accomplishments brought to completion!
Ah! Good government does not come about of itself: it comes about through securing the right men for office. Such men are not easily obtained; they are obtained through having the proper way to recognize them. Could the emperor fail to attend carefully to this counsel on recognizing men? Nevertheless, although appointing men to office is essential, the ruler’s own person is especially fundamental to selecting them. If he becomes even slightly indulgent after success has been achieved, he will still be unable to make full use of their abilities. Thus, from antiquity, it has been difficult for rulers and ministers to find one another. This is why Gao Yao, in presenting his counsels, necessarily began with “truly practicing his virtue,” and why his admonition against encouraging indolence and desire was especially earnest after the many achievements had been firmly established. Let those who admire the government of Youyu take this as their mirror!
“When the one man enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them.”
Zhou Dufei
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, School Director: 〔Throughout the piece, its force and style form a harmonious whole, while its principal emphasis rests on …〕

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一人有慶尤見卓識是文之可傳者
考試官教諭萬批規摸宏壯辭氣端重得
人君訓諸侯敬刑體
考試官教授鄒批瑩練
賢王言敬刑之福由君而及之民也夫民籍君
以自安也君慶於上而民以賴焉其刑之祥何
如哉穆王訓刑之意若曰人君以一人而臨兆
民有斂福敷錫之道焉而其機則司刑者致之
茲爾能敬刑以成德也將見惟予一人幸剛柔
===
之兼濟而民用不犯垂拱以迓乂安之休樂正
直之無為而化成有象恭已以享平康之盛天
地之和氣慶其有以導迎之也優游於清穆而
帝位其不疚矣國家之元氣慶其有以培植之
也伴奐於密勿而皇圖其永綏矣此蓋敬之所
成即慶之所集而汝之所為日勤於已者斯其
所以上效於君者也然豈專於予一人哉今此
兆民幸生明盛之世莫不獲有所庇以自適其
安全之願欣逢有道之長莫不得有所依以自
punctuated:
一人有慶，尤見卓識，是文之可傳者。
考試官教諭萬批：規摸宏壯，辭氣端重，得人君訓諸侯敬刑體。
考試官教授鄒批：瑩練。
賢王言敬刑之福由君而及之民也。夫民籍君以自安也，君慶於上，而民以賴焉，其刑之祥何如哉！穆王訓刑之意若曰：「人君以一人而臨兆民，有斂福敷錫之道焉，而其機則司刑者致之。茲爾能敬刑以成德也，將見惟予一人，幸剛柔之兼濟，而民用不犯，垂拱以迓乂安之休；樂正直之無為，而化成有象，恭已以享平康之盛。天地之和氣，慶其有以導迎之也，優游於清穆，而帝位其不疚矣；國家之元氣，慶其有以培植之也，伴奐於密勿，而皇圖其永綏矣。此蓋敬之所成，即慶之所集，而汝之所為日勤於已者，斯其所以上效於君者也。然豈專於予一人哉？今此兆民，幸生明盛之世，莫不獲有所庇，以自適其安全之願；欣逢有道之長，莫不得有所依，以自
translation_en:
…In its treatment of ‘the one man enjoys blessings,’ it particularly displays outstanding insight: this is what makes the essay worthy of transmission.
Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: Its conception is grand and expansive, its language and tone dignified and weighty. It captures the proper manner of a ruler admonishing the feudal lords to exercise reverent care in punishments.
Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: Polished and refined.
The worthy king explains that the blessings arising from reverent care in punishments pass from the ruler to the people. The people rely on their ruler for their own security. When the ruler enjoys blessings above and the people thereby find support, how auspicious are the effects of his punishments! The purport of King Mu’s instructions on punishments is as though he said: ‘The ruler, as one man presiding over the myriad people, has a way of gathering blessings and bestowing them widely; yet those who administer punishments are the ones who bring its workings to fruition. Now, if you can exercise reverent care in punishments and thereby perfect your virtue, you will see me, the one man, fortunate in the complementary operation of firmness and gentleness, so that the people commit no offenses. With hands folded and robes hanging down, I shall welcome the blessings of order and peace. I shall rejoice that uprightness achieves its effects without deliberate action and that moral transformation takes visible form; holding myself reverently, I shall enjoy flourishing peace and well-being. As for the harmonious energies of Heaven and Earth, I shall rejoice that there are means to guide and welcome them; at ease in purity and solemn harmony, I shall occupy the imperial throne without distress. As for the vital energies of the state, I shall rejoice that there are means to nurture them; at ease amid diligent care [?], I shall see the imperial realm secured forever. What reverent care accomplishes is precisely where blessings accumulate; the daily diligence you exert upon yourselves is thus the means by which you render service to your ruler above. Yet could this benefit be confined to me, the one man? These myriad people, fortunate to be born in an enlightened and flourishing age, will all find protection through which to satisfy their desire for safety and security. Delighted to encounter a leader who possesses the Way, all will find support through which they themselves…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遂其生養之情以定其趨賴上剛柔之克也藉
以寡過皞皞焉相安於至治矣以同其風賴上
正直之化也則以自治熈熈焉相忘於大道矣
此其德之所成即民之所賴而君之所為集慶
於上者斯其所以錫福於民者乎吁敬刑所致
其效有如此者爾諸侯可無用勤以自慰哉抑
此化中之會有虞事也今想其太和宇宙邈不
可尚乃穆王以之責成諸侯豈其有志於重華
事業哉顧其本未可以易言也然觀日勤數語
===
猶有哀矜惻怛遺意則文武之澤固在也是故
夫子猶有取云
詩
南山有桑北山有楊樂只君子邦家之光
樂只君子萬壽無疆南山有杞北山有
李樂只君子民之父母樂只君子德音
不已
霍鎮東
同考試官教諭王 批 題長辭簡意亦周密深
punctuated:
遂其生養之情。以定其趨，賴上剛柔之克也，藉以寡過，皞皞焉相安於至治矣；以同其風，賴上正直之化也，則以自治，熈熈焉相忘於大道矣。此其德之所成，即民之所賴，而君之所為集慶於上者，斯其所以錫福於民者乎！吁！敬刑所致，其效有如此者，爾諸侯可無用勤以自慰哉？抑此化中之會，有虞事也。今想其太和宇宙，邈不可尚，乃穆王以之責成諸侯，豈其有志於重華事業哉？顧其本未可以易言也。然觀「日勤」數語，猶有哀矜惻怛遺意，則文武之澤固在也。是故夫子猶有取云。

詩
南山有桑，北山有楊。樂只君子，邦家之光。樂只君子，萬壽無疆。南山有杞，北山有李。樂只君子，民之父母。樂只君子，德音不已。

霍鎮東

同考試官教諭王批：題長辭簡，意亦周密，深
translation_en:
…fulfill their desire to sustain their lives and nurture their families. To give their conduct a settled direction, they depend upon their ruler’s ability to employ firmness and gentleness appropriately; through this they lessen their faults and live contentedly together under consummate government. To bring their customs into accord, they depend upon the transforming influence of their ruler’s uprightness; thus they regulate themselves and, in joyful harmony, forget one another’s presence within the Great Way. What his virtue accomplishes is precisely what the people rely upon. Is not the ruler’s gathering of blessings above the very means by which he bestows good fortune upon the people? Ah! Such are the results of reverent care in administering punishments. Can you, the regional lords, fail to exert yourselves diligently and thereby find peace of mind?

Yet this convergence of transformation and the mean [?] belongs to the age of Youyu, the sage Shun. When we now imagine the supreme harmony that filled his universe, it seems remote beyond surpassing. Nevertheless, King Mu held the regional lords responsible for achieving it. Could it be that he aspired to the achievements of Chonghua, or Shun? Yet its foundations cannot be spoken of lightly. Looking at the few words concerning “daily diligence,” however, we still find a surviving spirit of compassion and heartfelt concern. The beneficent legacy of Kings Wen and Wu was certainly still present. For this reason, the Master, Confucius, still found something here worth preserving.

Book of Odes

On the southern mountain grow mulberries;
on the northern mountain grow poplars.
Joyful is the noble lord,
the glory of the realm and its ruling house.
Joyful is the noble lord:
may he live ten thousand years without end!
On the southern mountain grow wolfberry trees;
on the northern mountain grow plum trees.
Joyful is the noble lord,
the father and mother of the people.
Joyful is the noble lord:
may his virtuous renown never cease!

Huo Zhendong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The topic is long, but the wording is concise; the ideas, too, are comprehensive and closely reasoned, deeply…”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得詩人祝頌之㫖
考試官敎諭萬批辭意溫醇可式
考試官敎授鄒批敷腴
詩人兩卽物以美君子之德而天人與之矣夫
惟德爲足以得壽而永譽也王者以是美諸侯
蓋本其所以致之者與此燕享通用之樂歌謂
夫人臣以祗天惠民爲大節則必以得天獲民
爲順應我君子不有可美者乎彼南山有桑北
山有楊山之生木則然矣我樂只君子以亮采
===
有邦其文炳也以浚明有家其文蔚也寧不載
錫之光哉吾知天之所佑者德也而至和之所
保合元氣爲委順焉其必萬有斯年而與邦家
相爲悠久矣斯謂有德者必得其壽與南山有
杞北山有李地之敏樹則然矣我樂只君子平
易以近民有父之尊也和順以率物有母之親
也豈不爲孔邇者哉吾知民之所與者德也而
篤實之所輝光令名爲無窮焉其必一德允孚
而人之頌父母者不衰矣斯謂有德者必得其
punctuated:
得詩人祝頌之㫖。
考試官敎諭萬批：辭意溫醇，可式。
考試官敎授鄒批：敷腴。
詩人兩卽物以美君子之德，而天人與之矣。夫惟德爲足以得壽而永譽也，王者以是美諸侯，蓋本其所以致之者與？此燕享通用之樂歌，謂夫人臣以祗天惠民爲大節，則必以得天獲民爲順應。我君子不有可美者乎？彼南山有桑，北山有楊，山之生木則然矣。我樂只君子，以亮采有邦，其文炳也；以浚明有家，其文蔚也，寧不載錫之光哉？吾知天之所佑者德也，而至和之所保合，元氣爲委順焉。其必萬有斯年，而與邦家相爲悠久矣。斯謂有德者必得其壽與？南山有杞，北山有李，地之敏樹則然矣。我樂只君子，平易以近民，有父之尊也；和順以率物，有母之親也，豈不爲孔邇者哉？吾知民之所與者德也，而篤實之所輝光，令名爲無窮焉。其必一德允孚，而人之頌父母者不衰矣。斯謂有德者必得其
translation_en:
…captures the purport of the poet’s blessings and praise.

Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning are warm and mellow, worthy of emulation.”

Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: “Ample and rich.”

Twice the poet draws upon things in nature to praise the gentleman’s virtue, and Heaven and the people lend him their support. Only virtue suffices to secure longevity and lasting renown. In praising the feudal lords in this way, does not the king take as his foundation that which brings these blessings about?
