This song, used alike at banquets and ceremonial feasts, conveys that, since a minister’s great obligations are to revere Heaven and benefit the people, gaining Heaven’s favor and the people’s allegiance must be their fitting recompense. Does our gentleman not possess qualities worthy of praise?

“There are mulberry trees on the southern mountain, and poplars on the northern mountain”: such is the way mountains produce trees. Our joyous gentleman brilliantly discharges his duties as lord of a state, and his cultivated excellence shines forth; he displays profound discernment as head of a noble house, and his cultivated excellence flourishes. Does he not thereby bestow glory upon them? I know that what Heaven protects is virtue. Where perfect harmony preserves and unites, primordial vital energy yields and accords with it. Surely he will live for ten thousand years, enduring together with his state and house. Is this what is meant by saying that the virtuous must attain longevity?

“There are qi trees on the southern mountain, and plum trees on the northern mountain”: such is the earth’s readiness to grow trees. Our joyous gentleman approaches the people with simplicity and ease, possessing a father’s dignity; he leads all beings with harmony and gentleness, possessing a mother’s affection. Is he not exceedingly close to them? I know that what the people support is virtue. Where substantial sincerity shines forth, a fine reputation becomes inexhaustible. Surely his single-minded virtue will inspire true trust, and the people’s praise of him as their father and mother will never fade. Is this what is meant by saying that the virtuous must attain their…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
名與吁王者以是而美其臣逮下之仁可想見
矣抑論之上下交而後爲道之泰也周之盛時
臣子之忠愛其君皆頌不忘規今觀南山之詩
君之宣慈惠於其臣尤必先其所以致之者蓋
上下交相爲儆也玆其所以爲成周有道之長
與
方命厥后奄有九有
林應祥
同考試官敎諭王批體裁莊重辭理簡明商
人頌祖之意宛然想見
考試官敎諭萬批成湯誕受帝命當時王
業之盛見於人心土宇如此是作闡揚殆盡
考試官敎授鄒批典雅
商人頌聖祖受命自其王業之盛言之也蓋人
心土宇王業之所係也商王受命而大一統焉
是宜詩人侈之登歌也與此祭祀宗廟之樂歌
也意曰一代之王業成之者人也本之者天也
我武湯之受天命而興何如哉彼四海之諸侯
punctuated:
名與？吁！王者以是而美其臣，逮下之仁可想見矣。抑論之，上下交而後爲道之泰也。周之盛時，臣子之忠愛其君，皆頌不忘規。今觀南山之詩，君之宣慈惠於其臣，尤必先其所以致之者，蓋上下交相爲儆也。玆其所以爲成周有道之長與？
方命厥后，奄有九有。
林應祥
同考試官敎諭王批：體裁莊重，辭理簡明，商人頌祖之意宛然想見。
考試官敎諭萬批：成湯誕受帝命，當時王業之盛見於人心土宇如此，是作闡揚殆盡。
考試官敎授鄒批：典雅。
商人頌聖祖受命，自其王業之盛言之也。蓋人心土宇，王業之所係也。商王受命而大一統焉，是宜詩人侈之登歌也與！此祭祀宗廟之樂歌也。意曰：一代之王業，成之者人也，本之者天也。我武湯之受天命而興何如哉？彼四海之諸侯
translation_en:
…a good name? Ah! In thus praising his ministers, the king makes manifest his benevolence toward those below him. To consider this further: only when those above and below communicate does the Way attain flourishing harmony. In Zhou’s heyday, ministers, loyal to and loving their ruler, never forgot admonition even in their praises. Now, looking at the poem about the southern mountain, we see that the ruler, in extending kindness and favor to his ministers, especially gives precedence to the qualities by which they have earned them. Thus those above and below admonish one another. Is this not why the flourishing Zhou so long possessed the Way?
“He issued commands to their lords everywhere and possessed all nine regions.”
Lin Yingxiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, an Instructor: “The composition is dignified, and its language and reasoning concise and clear. The intent of the people of Shang in praising their ancestor can be vividly imagined.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, an Instructor: “Cheng Tang received the great mandate of the Lord on High. The splendor of his kingly enterprise at that time was thus manifested in the people’s allegiance and the lands he ruled. This composition expounds it almost exhaustively.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, a Professor: “Classical and elegant.”
The people of Shang praise their sage ancestor’s receipt of the mandate by speaking of the greatness of his kingly enterprise. For the people’s allegiance and the lands ruled are what a kingly enterprise depends upon. The king of Shang received the mandate and brought all under one rule. It was fitting that the poet should magnify this in a hymn sung at the ceremonial ascent! This is a musical hymn for sacrifices in the ancestral temple. Its meaning is: the kingly enterprise of a dynasty is accomplished by men, but its foundation lies in Heaven. How did our martial Tang receive Heaven’s mandate and rise? Those feudal lords within the four seas…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皆有夏之臣庶也茲焉智勇天錫旣舉夏正而
爰革之但見六服羣辟莫不欽一人之威命而
奔走之恐後庶邦冢君舉皆仰皇靈之振肅而
歸向之不違禮樂征伐于此焉受也政敎號令
于此焉受也蓋人心之所在卽天命之所在天
旣以命夏者而命商則四海之諸侯得不以戴
夏者而戴商耶九有之土地皆有夏之輿圖也
茲焉聖武布昭旣盡禹績而一統之但見式廓
之增舉覆載之所加者悉入于統馭之內幅隕
===
之廣凡照墜之所及者皆在其疆理之中內而
華夏莫非其地也外而蠻貊莫非其地也蓋土
地之所歸卽天命之所歸天旣以命禹者而命
湯則九有之土地得不以附禹者而附湯耶吁
詩人于登歌之際而追述之其亦不忘所自者
矣雖然基命以裕後前王之所以垂統也脩德
以保業後王之所以承先也商人祭祀而惓惓
以祖宗功德爲言無亦以法祖望其君與撫成
業者尚繹思之
punctuated:
皆有夏之臣庶也。茲焉智勇天錫，旣舉夏正而爰革之，但見六服羣辟，莫不欽一人之威命而奔走之恐後；庶邦冢君，舉皆仰皇靈之振肅而歸向之不違。禮樂征伐，于此焉受也；政敎號令，于此焉受也。蓋人心之所在，卽天命之所在。天旣以命夏者而命商，則四海之諸侯，得不以戴夏者而戴商耶？
九有之土地，皆有夏之輿圖也。茲焉聖武布昭，旣盡禹績而一統之，但見式廓之增，舉覆載之所加者，悉入于統馭之內；幅隕之廣，凡照墜之所及者，皆在其疆理之中。內而華夏，莫非其地也；外而蠻貊，莫非其地也。蓋土地之所歸，卽天命之所歸。天旣以命禹者而命湯，則九有之土地，得不以附禹者而附湯耶？
吁！詩人于登歌之際而追述之，其亦不忘所自者矣。雖然，基命以裕後，前王之所以垂統也；脩德以保業，後王之所以承先也。商人祭祀而惓惓以祖宗功德爲言，無亦以法祖望其君與？撫成業者，尚繹思之。
translation_en:
…were all subjects of the Xia. Now, endowed by Heaven with wisdom and courage, Tang overturned the rule of Xia. The many lords of the six zones of submission all revered the sovereign’s august commands and hurried to serve him, fearing to fall behind. The rulers of the many states all looked up to his awe-inspiring majesty and turned to him in allegiance without dissent. From him they received authority over rites, music, and punitive expeditions; from him they received governmental instruction and commands. For where the people’s hearts incline, there too rests Heaven’s Mandate. Since Heaven had bestowed upon Shang the mandate it had bestowed upon Xia, could the lords within the four seas fail to uphold Shang as they had upheld Xia?
The lands of the nine regions had all belonged to the domain of Xia. Now Tang’s sagely martial might shone abroad, and he unified the entire territory brought to order by Yu. With the expansion of his domain, everything beneath Heaven’s covering and upon Earth’s support came under his rule. Such was the breadth of his territory [?] that everything reached by celestial illumination and earthly support [?] lay within his boundaries. Within, the lands of Huaxia were all his; beyond, the lands of the Man and Mo peoples were all his. For where the lands turn in allegiance, there too rests Heaven’s Mandate. Since Heaven had bestowed upon Tang the mandate it had bestowed upon Yu, could the lands of the nine regions fail to attach themselves to Tang as they had attached themselves to Yu?
Ah! When the poet recalled these deeds in the song performed in the ancestral hall, he surely showed that he had not forgotten their source. Nevertheless, establishing the Mandate so as to enrich posterity was how former kings handed down their rule; cultivating virtue so as to preserve their inheritance was how later kings carried on the work of their predecessors. When the people of Shang offered sacrifices and spoke so earnestly of their ancestors’ achievements and virtue, was it not in the hope that their ruler would emulate those ancestors? Let those who hold an established inheritance ponder this deeply.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
春王三月甲寅齊人伐衛〔莊公二十有八年〕齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕
許岸
同考試官敎諭鄭批是作深得春秋謹嚴家
法錄之
考試官敎諭萬批體裁峻整筆力渾雄
考試官敎授鄒批雅健
伯主始奉命討罪春秋予其正繼專命恤患春
===
秋予其權于以見桓之有功於天下也伐衛則
正城邢不嫌於專春秋兩予之也宜哉衛伐周
而立頹桓公伐之春秋予之以正者何蓋君令
臣共分也正以秩分者也衛可伐也威不可作
也向使專命而行其誰能悅之桓蓋能知正者
有侯伯之賜有召伯之請奉辭問罪一以王命
臨之使衛之得正法者桓之力也昭哉其命討
之公乎是雖衛抗如故也然方侯度無統之日
微桓也起而振之天下將不知有周矣此其義
punctuated:
春秋

春，王三月，甲寅，齊人伐衛。〔莊公二十有八年〕齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。〔僖公元年〕

許岸

同考試官敎諭鄭批：是作深得春秋謹嚴家法，錄之。
考試官敎諭萬批：體裁峻整，筆力渾雄。
考試官敎授鄒批：雅健。

伯主始奉命討罪，春秋予其正；繼專命恤患，春秋予其權。于以見桓之有功於天下也。伐衛則正，城邢不嫌於專，春秋兩予之也，宜哉！衛伐周而立頹，桓公伐之。春秋予之以正者何？蓋君令臣共，分也；正以秩分者也。衛可伐也，威不可作也。向使專命而行，其誰能悅之？桓蓋能知正者。有侯伯之賜，有召伯之請，奉辭問罪，一以王命臨之，使衛之得正法者，桓之力也。昭哉，其命討之公乎！是雖衛抗如故也，然方侯度無統之日，微桓也起而振之，天下將不知有周矣。此其義
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In spring, in the third month by the royal calendar, on the jiayin day, men of Qi attacked Wei.” 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang〕 “The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao fortified Xing.” 〔First year of Duke Xi〕

Xu An

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “This composition thoroughly grasps the exacting and rigorous interpretive discipline of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Admit it to the selection.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The composition is imposing and orderly; the writing is full-bodied and powerful.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Elegant and vigorous.”

The hegemon first obeyed a command to punish wrongdoing, and the Spring and Autumn Annals approves his adherence to proper authority. Later, he acted on his own authority to relieve distress, and the Spring and Autumn Annals approves his exercise of discretion. Here we see Duke Huan’s service to the realm. His attack on Wei accorded with proper authority; his fortification of Xing incurred no reproach for unilateral action. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals approves both!

Wei attacked Zhou and installed Tui, and Duke Huan attacked Wei. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve him for acting in accordance with proper authority? For the ruler to command and the minister to obey is the proper division of roles; adherence to proper authority keeps those roles in order. Wei could rightly be attacked, but coercive authority could not be assumed at will. Had he acted on his own command, who could have accepted it willingly? Duke Huan indeed understood proper authority. There was the grant of authority as chief of the feudal lords, and there was the request of the Earl of Shao. Bearing the royal charge, he called Wei to account for its offenses, confronting it wholly on the authority of the king’s command. It was through Duke Huan’s efforts that Wei was brought under the proper application of the law. How manifest was the public justice of his punitive commission!

Although Wei remained defiant as before, this was a time when the conduct of the feudal lords lacked any unifying authority. Had Duke Huan not risen to restore it, the realm would no longer have recognized the existence of Zhou. The significance of this …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何如也而桓可少乎哉故予之若曰持天下之
名分者不可一日而無正予桓者興常典也邢
避狄而遷邑桓公城之春秋予之以權者何蓋
安內攘外義也權以達義者也邢可城也時不
可後也向使請命而行其疇能聽之桓蓋能知
權者焉狄人之逐焉邢邑之營具器度工一以
便宜從之邢之幸不亡者桓之力也偉哉其綏
定之績乎是雖師出若專也然方小國潰亡之
時微桓也起而存之斯民其不免左衽矣此其
功何如也而桓可沒乎哉故予之若曰濟天下
之事功者亦不可一日而無權予桓者不得已
也是知討罪予之重王道也恤患予之重世道
也何莫非聖人之精義哉雖然伐衛正矣取其
賂則偷城邢美矣待其潰則不仁大抵襲義於
衛觀釁於狄養禍於邢此皆伯者計功謀利之
心為之論桓者當取其功不可略其心
晉人宋人衛人曹人伐鄭〔宣公十年〕馮瑞
punctuated:
何如也，而桓可少乎哉？故予之，若曰：「持天下之名分者，不可一日而無正。」予桓者，興常典也。邢避狄而遷邑，桓公城之，《春秋》予之以權者何？蓋安內攘外，義也；權以達義者也。邢可城也，時不可後也。向使請命而行，其疇能聽之？桓蓋能知權者焉。狄人之逐焉，邢邑之營，具器度工，一以便宜從之。邢之幸不亡者，桓之力也。偉哉，其綏定之績乎！是雖師出若專也，然方小國潰亡之時，微桓也起而存之，斯民其不免左衽矣。此其功何如也，而桓可沒乎哉？故予之，若曰：「濟天下之事功者，亦不可一日而無權。」予桓者，不得已也。是知討罪予之，重王道也；恤患予之，重世道也。何莫非聖人之精義哉！雖然，伐衛正矣，取其賂則偷；城邢美矣，待其潰則不仁。大抵襲義於衛，觀釁於狄，養禍於邢，此皆伯者計功謀利之心為之。論桓者，當取其功，不可略其心。
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人伐鄭。〔宣公十年〕馮瑞
translation_en:
…How great was the righteousness of this deed! Could Duke Huan have been dispensed with? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him, as if to say: “Those who uphold the recognized distinctions of rank and duty throughout the realm cannot for a single day dispense with adherence to proper principles.” Its commendation of Huan serves to revive the established norms.

Xing moved its settlement to escape the Di, and Duke Huan fortified it. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals commend his exercise of expedient judgment? Securing those within and repelling those without is righteousness; expedient judgment is the means of realizing righteousness. Xing needed fortifications, and delay was impossible. Had he first sought authorization before acting, who could have heeded his request? Huan evidently understood expedient judgment. In driving out the Di and constructing Xing’s settlement, supplying equipment and estimating the labor required, he acted throughout as circumstances required. That Xing fortunately escaped destruction was owing to Huan’s efforts. How magnificent his achievement in bringing security and stability! Though his deployment of troops might seem an unauthorized act, at a time when small states were collapsing and perishing, had Huan not risen to preserve Xing, its people could hardly have avoided wearing their robes fastened on the left, in the manner of the non-Chinese peoples. How great was this achievement! Could Huan’s contribution be effaced? Thus the Annals commends him, as if to say: “Those who bring the affairs of the realm to fruition likewise cannot for a single day dispense with expedient judgment.” Its commendation of Huan arose from necessity.

From this we know that commending his punishment of wrongdoing honors the Way of kings, while commending his relief of distress honors the moral order of the world. Which of these judgments does not embody the sage’s finely discerning sense of right? Nevertheless, attacking Wei was proper, but accepting its bribes was base; fortifying Xing was admirable, but waiting until it collapsed was inhumane. In general, assuming the guise of righteousness in dealing with Wei, watching for an opening against the Di, and allowing disaster to develop in Xing—all arose from a hegemon’s disposition to calculate achievements and pursue advantage. Those who judge Huan should acknowledge his achievements, but must not overlook his motives.

“Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao attacked Zheng.” 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan〕 Feng Rui.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭批招攜以德是作發揮明
盡可以式矣
考試官教諭萬批認傳切實措辭雄蔚
考試官教授鄒批嚴正
伯者恃力爭貳春秋深責之焉夫人心不可以
力强也晉爭鄭而失所以感人者伯業其替乎
自柳棼之敗楚之怒鄭益淫鄭之平楚是急玆
四國所爲伐也春秋稱人則責伯之詞也何責
之深乎蓋伯者匪不武之患惟務德之難鄭介
===
大國之間將擇强而求庇焉者今棄而從楚社
稷之故也豈其情哉晉苟反身脩德則楚屈而
鄭自服矣奚事於兵奈何信義罔聞招懷失策
少西有可問之罪也爲之戡定而以德鎮之彼
將帖吾之義而不敢攜矣不伐陳而伐鄭義乎
不義乎鄭有可分之災也爲之安靖而以德撫
之彼將懷吾之仁而不忍貳矣不觀德而觀兵
可乎不可乎夫篳路藍縷吾無望其知德耳矣
晉友邦也楚以兵爭鄭吾亦以兵角楚不知晉
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭批：招攜以德，是作發揮明盡，可以式矣。
考試官教諭萬批：認傳切實，措辭雄蔚。
考試官教授鄒批：嚴正。
伯者恃力爭貳，春秋深責之焉。夫人心不可以力强也。晉爭鄭而失所以感人者，伯業其替乎？自柳棼之敗，楚之怒鄭益淫，鄭之平楚是急，玆四國所爲伐也。春秋稱人，則責伯之詞也。何責之深乎？蓋伯者匪不武之患，惟務德之難。鄭介大國之間，將擇强而求庇焉者。今棄而從楚，社稷之故也，豈其情哉？晉苟反身脩德，則楚屈而鄭自服矣，奚事於兵？奈何信義罔聞，招懷失策？少西有可問之罪也，爲之戡定而以德鎮之，彼將帖吾之義而不敢攜矣。不伐陳而伐鄭，義乎？不義乎？鄭有可分之災也，爲之安靖而以德撫之，彼將懷吾之仁而不忍貳矣。不觀德而觀兵，可乎？不可乎？夫篳路藍縷，吾無望其知德耳矣。晉友邦也，楚以兵爭鄭，吾亦以兵角楚，不知晉
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Winning back the estranged through virtue: this composition develops the point clearly and fully. It may serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “Its understanding of the commentary is precise and sound; its language is powerful and rich.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Rigorous and upright.”
When a hegemon relies on force to contend for a state of divided allegiance, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him severely. For people’s hearts cannot be compelled by force. Jin contended for Zheng but lost the means of moving people’s hearts: was its hegemony not bound to decline? After the defeat at Liufen, Chu’s anger against Zheng grew ever more excessive. Zheng urgently sought peace with Chu, and this was why these four states attacked it. The Spring and Autumn Annals calls their commanders simply “men”: this wording censures the hegemon. Why is its censure so severe? Because a hegemon’s concern is not a lack of military prowess; the difficulty lies in cultivating virtue.
Zheng, situated between great states, would choose the stronger and seek its protection. That it now abandoned Jin and followed Chu was for the sake of preserving its altars of soil and grain. Could this have been its heart’s desire? Had Jin examined itself and cultivated virtue, Chu would have yielded and Zheng would have submitted of its own accord. What need would there have been for arms? Why, then, was nothing heard of good faith and righteousness, and why did its efforts to attract and conciliate go astray? Shaoxi had committed a crime for which he could be called to account [?]. Had Jin pacified the disorder for them and secured them through virtue, they would have submitted to our righteousness and dared not become estranged. Was attacking Zheng instead of Chen righteous or unrighteous? Zheng suffered a calamity whose burden could have been shared. Had Jin restored its peace and comforted it through virtue, it would have cherished our benevolence and been unable to bear divided allegiance. Was displaying arms instead of displaying virtue acceptable or unacceptable?
As for those of the ‘brushwood cart and ragged clothes,’ I have no expectation that they understand virtue. But Jin is a friendly state. Chu contends for Zheng through arms, and we likewise use arms to compete with Chu. I do not understand how Jin …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之所以駕楚者何如也其無乃尤而效之也乎
裔夷異族吾無責其競力耳矣晉宗盟也鄭方
困楚之令吾亦脅鄭之成不知晉之所以信鄭
者何如也其無乃驅而去之也乎自是晉之爭
鄭雖力鄭之從楚益親南北之勢分辰陵之謀
合天下不伯晉而伯楚矣晉也其能得志於鄭
哉吁此春秋所以重責晉也雖然鄭獨無罪與
不擇所從甘心外比下喬而入谷矣楚獨無罪
與謀夏亂華入陳入鄭暴而不戢欲何為哉君
===
子謂逢道之入鄭自貽之戚也邲勝而志驕天
下日擾擾焉楚矣景不桓不文其世道之不幸
夫
禮記
事君以自顯也
陳綯
同考試官學正廖批人君為天下所事故即
自顯以見當事之義此作得之錄以為式
考試官教諭萬批得君而事其亦自顯乎
punctuated:
之所以駕楚者何如也？其無乃尤而效之也乎？裔夷異族，吾無責其競力耳矣。晉宗盟也，鄭方困楚之令，吾亦脅鄭之成，不知晉之所以信鄭者何如也？其無乃驅而去之也乎？自是，晉之爭鄭雖力，鄭之從楚益親。南北之勢分，辰陵之謀合，天下不伯晉而伯楚矣。晉也，其能得志於鄭哉？吁！此《春秋》所以重責晉也。雖然，鄭獨無罪與？不擇所從，甘心外比，下喬而入谷矣。楚獨無罪與？謀夏亂華，入陳入鄭，暴而不戢，欲何為哉？君子謂逢道之入鄭，自貽之戚也。邲勝而志驕，天下日擾擾焉，楚矣。景不桓不文，其世道之不幸夫！

《禮記》
事君以自顯也。
陳綯

同考試官學正廖批：人君為天下所事，故即自顯以見當事之義。此作得之，錄以為式。

考試官教諭萬批：得君而事，其亦自顯乎？
translation_en:
…how Jin was to surpass Chu. Was this not to condemn Chu and yet imitate it? As distant barbarians of a different stock, they could hardly be expected to do otherwise than compete in strength. But Jin presided over the covenant of the kindred states. Just when Zheng was suffering under Chu’s commands, Jin too coerced Zheng into a settlement. How, then, was Jin to win Zheng’s trust? Was this not to drive it away? Thereafter, however vigorously Jin contended for Zheng, Zheng’s allegiance to Chu grew ever closer. The northern and southern powers became divided, and the designs laid at Chenling came together. All under Heaven recognized Chu, rather than Jin, as hegemon. Could Jin then attain its aims in Zheng? Alas! This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals so severely reproaches Jin. Even so, was Zheng alone without fault? Making no careful choice of whom to follow, it willingly attached itself to an outside power: it descended from the tall trees into the valley. Was Chu alone without fault? Plotting against the Xia states and throwing the Hua states into disorder, invading Chen and Zheng, it pursued violence without restraint. What did it intend? The gentleman says that the invasion of Zheng at Fengdao [?] was a calamity Zheng brought upon itself. Victory at Bi made Chu arrogant, and the mounting turmoil throughout the realm was Chu’s doing. Duke Jing was neither a Duke Huan nor a Duke Wen: what a misfortune for the order of the age!

Record of Rites
“By serving his lord, one brings distinction to oneself.”
Chen Tao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: The ruler is served by all under Heaven. Thus the reference to bringing distinction to oneself reveals the duty to serve him. This composition grasps that meaning and has been recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: Having found a lord to serve, does one not thereby bring distinction to oneself? …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
能發明此意知尊君矣
考試官敎授鄒批事君之義明徹
記者論事君之益所以明爲下之分也夫臣以
事君爲分也因以自顯則益矣分之不可不盡
如是夫禮運之意曰天下有大分君臣是已天
下有大義以臣事君是已何則惟辟作福者也
凡畀一命之寄孰非君之所以寵其臣乎惟民
從乂者也凡膺一命之榮孰非臣之所以荷其
君乎故百姓仰大君之在上而策名委質以覲
===
夫耿光慶明君之有作而先資自獻以承其休
德或左右宣力則式昭夫錫予之隆惟賢惟能
其顯於官使者何如也或出入均勞則用彰夫
崇報之典馭貴馭富其顯於爵祿者何如也此
則以道事君以道自顯者也而非有私於身也
人臣靖共之心當如是耳以忠事君以忠自顯
者也而亦非有要於君也人臣敬事之心不容
已耳此之謂盡天下之大義此之謂明天下之
大分百姓事君如此不可以觀人君之所以尊
punctuated:
能發明此意，知尊君矣。
考試官敎授鄒批：事君之義明徹。
記者論事君之益，所以明爲下之分也。夫臣以事君爲分也，因以自顯則益矣。分之不可不盡，如是夫！禮運之意曰：天下有大分，君臣是已；天下有大義，以臣事君是已。何則？惟辟作福者也，凡畀一命之寄，孰非君之所以寵其臣乎？惟民從乂者也，凡膺一命之榮，孰非臣之所以荷其君乎？故百姓仰大君之在上，而策名委質，以覲夫耿光；慶明君之有作，而先資自獻，以承其休德。或左右宣力，則式昭夫錫予之隆，惟賢惟能，其顯於官使者何如也？或出入均勞，則用彰夫崇報之典，馭貴馭富，其顯於爵祿者何如也？此則以道事君，以道自顯者也，而非有私於身也，人臣靖共之心當如是耳；以忠事君，以忠自顯者也，而亦非有要於君也，人臣敬事之心不容已耳。此之謂盡天下之大義，此之謂明天下之大分。百姓事君如此，不可以觀人君之所以尊
translation_en:
…He can elucidate this meaning and understands how to honor the ruler.
Examiner Zou, Instructor, comments: The duty of serving the ruler is explained with thorough clarity.
The author of the Record discusses the benefits of serving the ruler in order to clarify the duty of those below. A minister’s duty is to serve his ruler; if he thereby also attains distinction, that is a benefit. Such is the imperative to fulfill one’s duty! The meaning of “The Conveyance of Rites” (Liyun) is this: the great distinction under Heaven is that between ruler and minister; the great duty under Heaven is that of serving the ruler as a minister. Why is this so? It is the sovereign alone who bestows blessings. Whenever someone is entrusted with an official appointment, is this not how the ruler favors his minister? It is the people who submit to governance. Whenever someone receives the honor of an appointment, is this not how the minister receives his ruler’s beneficence? Thus the people look up to the great ruler above, have their names entered into service, and pledge their allegiance, that they may behold his brilliant radiance. They rejoice that an enlightened ruler has arisen and take the initiative in offering themselves [?], that they may receive his excellent virtue.
Some exert themselves at his side, thereby displaying the abundance of his bestowals. Appointed for their worthiness and ability, how great is the distinction they attain through official service! Others share the toil of service within and outside the court, thereby making manifest the institutions of generous recompense. Governed through the conferral of nobility and wealth, how great is the distinction they attain through rank and emolument! These are people who serve their ruler in accordance with the Way and attain distinction in accordance with the Way. They harbor no selfish concern for themselves: such, and no more, should be a minister’s disposition of devoted reverence. They serve their ruler with loyalty and attain distinction through loyalty. Nor do they seek to exact anything from the ruler: a minister’s impulse to serve reverently simply cannot be restrained. This is what is meant by fulfilling the great duty under Heaven; this is what is meant by clarifying the great distinction under Heaven. When the people serve their ruler in this manner, can we not perceive therein why the ruler is honored…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉大抵上有明聖之君則下必有忠順之臣此
唐虞三代之盛君臣相得而共成正大光明之
業以顯於後世也苟為不然則自卑求幸自小
求用此又富貴利達之心將以稱於天下曰自
顯則未也事君者其思之
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節
熊承諒
同考試官學正廖批禮樂能同天地乃聖人
制作之妙也是篇渾融得旨可錄
===
考試官教諭萬批道出同和同節氣象深
得禮樂之情者
考試官教授鄒批善言禮樂
先王制作之大有以合乎造化焉夫天地有和
節禮樂之原也非聖人制作之妙孰能與之同
哉樂記言此若曰大哉禮樂之道乎制作於聖
人而貫通於天地者也何則天地以一陽之氣
煦育品彙有自然之和焉先王之樂人見其靜
而易也豈知與天地同和乎蓋大樂之與天地
punctuated:
哉！大抵上有明聖之君，則下必有忠順之臣。此唐虞三代之盛，君臣相得，而共成正大光明之業，以顯於後世也。苟為不然，則自卑求幸，自小求用，此又富貴利達之心，將以稱於天下曰自顯，則未也。事君者其思之！

大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。
熊承諒

同考試官學正廖批：禮樂能同天地，乃聖人制作之妙也。是篇渾融得旨，可錄。

考試官教諭萬批：道出同和同節氣象，深得禮樂之情者。

考試官教授鄒批：善言禮樂。

先王制作之大，有以合乎造化焉。夫天地有和節，禮樂之原也。非聖人制作之妙，孰能與之同哉？《樂記》言此，若曰：大哉，禮樂之道乎！制作於聖人，而貫通於天地者也。何則？天地以一陽之氣煦育品彙，有自然之和焉。先王之樂，人見其靜而易也，豈知與天地同和乎？蓋大樂之與天地
translation_en:
… exalted! In general, when an enlightened and sagely ruler stands above, loyal and obedient ministers must serve below. Such was the flourishing age of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties: rulers and ministers found their fitting counterparts and together accomplished upright and illustrious deeds, becoming renowned among later generations. If this is not so, then men abase themselves to seek favor and belittle themselves to seek employment. This, too, springs from a desire for wealth, rank, advantage, and advancement. To claim before the world that this is making oneself illustrious would be unwarranted. Let those who serve a ruler reflect on this!

“Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the measured order of Heaven and Earth.”
By Xiong Chengliang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: That ritual and music can accord with Heaven and Earth is the marvel of the sages’ institutional creations. This essay integrates its ideas smoothly and captures the essential meaning; it merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: It conveys the character of shared harmony and shared measured order, deeply apprehending the true nature of ritual and music.

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: It speaks well of ritual and music.

The greatness of the former kings’ institutional creations lay in their accord with the workings of creation. Heaven and Earth possess harmony and measured order: these are the source of ritual and music. Without the marvelous institutions created by the sages, what could accord with them? The Record of Music speaks of this as if to say: How great is the Way of ritual and music! Established by the sages, it permeates Heaven and Earth. Why is this? Through the single vital force of yang, Heaven and Earth warm and nurture the myriad kinds of beings, possessing a harmony that arises of itself. People see that the music of the former kings is tranquil and easy, but how could they know that it shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth? For great music and Heaven and Earth …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一氣相爲流通耳是故流而不息之機一太和
之洋溢也合同而化之妙一性術之交暢也八
音諧而萬舞奕和之至也而天地之和敦於此
矣至是不知孰爲大樂也孰爲天地之和也有
弗同者與天地以一陰之氣品制羣動有自然
之節焉先王之禮人見其文而簡也豈知與天
地同節乎蓋大禮之與天地一理相爲契合耳
是故尊卑之各定皆截然者與其辨也動靜之
有常皆燦然者與其秩也三綱正而九疇敘節
===
之至也而天地之節別於此矣至是不知孰爲
大禮也孰爲天地之節也有弗同者與吁大人
舉禮樂之妙如此則其贊化育而感人心也固
其所哉雖然至和無聲至敬無文吾心之禮樂
也論聖人之大樂大禮不必求和節於天地而
惟求之吾心焉斯得其本矣不然人而不仁其
如禮樂何然就二者而觀之禮又樂之本也聲
音之道所由生也苟非至治之極則至樂無因
而作矣故曰禮先而樂後
punctuated: 一氣相爲流通耳。是故流而不息之機，一太和之洋溢也；合同而化之妙，一性術之交暢也。八音諧而萬舞奕，和之至也，而天地之和敦於此矣。至是不知孰爲大樂也，孰爲天地之和也，有弗同者與？天地以一陰之氣品制羣動，有自然之節焉。先王之禮，人見其文而簡也，豈知與天地同節乎？蓋大禮之與天地，一理相爲契合耳。是故尊卑之各定，皆截然者與其辨也；動靜之有常，皆燦然者與其秩也。三綱正而九疇敘，節之至也，而天地之節別於此矣。至是不知孰爲大禮也，孰爲天地之節也，有弗同者與？吁！大人舉禮樂之妙如此，則其贊化育而感人心也，固其所哉！雖然，至和無聲，至敬無文，吾心之禮樂也。論聖人之大樂大禮，不必求和節於天地，而惟求之吾心焉，斯得其本矣。不然，人而不仁，其如禮樂何？然就二者而觀之，禮又樂之本也，聲音之道所由生也。苟非至治之極，則至樂無因而作矣。故曰：「禮先而樂後。」
translation_en: …a single vital force simply circulates between them. Thus, the working that flows without ceasing is the overflowing of supreme harmony; the marvel of union and transformation is the mutual unfolding of nature and method [?]. When the eight classes of musical instruments sound in harmony and the wan dance is splendidly performed, harmony reaches its utmost, and the harmony of Heaven and Earth is made abundant therein. At this point, one no longer knows which is great music and which is the harmony of Heaven and Earth. Is there any difference between them? Through the single vital force of yin, Heaven and Earth grade and regulate all moving things, possessing a natural measure. People see that the ritual of the former kings is patterned yet simple; how could they know that it shares the measure of Heaven and Earth? Great ritual and Heaven and Earth simply accord through a single principle. Thus, when the stations of the honored and the lowly are each fixed, their clear separation accords with its distinctions; when movement and stillness have their constant rules, their manifest arrangement accords with its order. When the Three Bonds are rectified and the Nine Categories are ordered, measure reaches its utmost, and the measures of Heaven and Earth are differentiated therein. At this point, one no longer knows which is great ritual and which is the measure of Heaven and Earth. Is there any difference between them? Ah! When the great man brings the subtleties of ritual and music into practice in this way, surely it is fitting that he should assist the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth and move human hearts! Nevertheless, the utmost harmony has no sound, and the utmost reverence has no outward pattern: these are the ritual and music of our own hearts. In discussing the sages’ great music and great ritual, we need not seek harmony and measure in Heaven and Earth, but only in our own hearts; then we grasp their root. Otherwise, if a person lacks benevolence, what can he do with ritual and music? Yet, considering the two together, ritual is also the root of music, that from which the Way of musical sound arises. Unless the highest perfection of good government is attained, the utmost music has no basis upon which to arise. Hence it is said: “Ritual comes first, and music follows.”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
人主制馭臣民之柄
霍鎭東
同考試官敎諭王批意新筆健格古思深佳
作也可以占所蘊矣
考試官敎諭萬批議論切當格調古雅
考試官敎授鄒批辭雅氣昌積學之士也
聖人能以天下運諸心而不以其心徇天下夫
===
聖人一心而天下之臣之民則億萬其心也聖
人豈能日斤斤焉敝精竭神以求與億萬之心
合喜怒而輕重低昂其法哉蓋亦有機焉以執
之矣機運於心以達之天下天下之心一聖人
之心也何也喜怒一人之私也賞罰天下之公
也吾以一人之喜怒而賞罰乎天下天下未有
不以為詩者苟以天下之喜怒為喜怒則賞一
人焉喜以天下也罰一人焉怒以天下也天下
有不心服而勸且懲者乎夫惟其心之勸且懲
punctuated:
第貳場

論

人主制馭臣民之柄

霍鎭東

同考試官敎諭王批：意新筆健，格古思深，佳作也，可以占所蘊矣。

考試官敎諭萬批：議論切當，格調古雅。

考試官敎授鄒批：辭雅氣昌，積學之士也。

聖人能以天下運諸心，而不以其心徇天下。夫聖人一心，而天下之臣之民則億萬其心也。聖人豈能日斤斤焉，敝精竭神，以求與億萬之心合喜怒，而輕重低昂其法哉？蓋亦有機焉，以執之矣。機運於心，以達之天下，天下之心一聖人之心也。何也？喜怒，一人之私也；賞罰，天下之公也。吾以一人之喜怒而賞罰乎天下，天下未有不以為詩者。苟以天下之喜怒為喜怒，則賞一人焉，喜以天下也；罰一人焉，怒以天下也。天下有不心服而勸且懲者乎？夫惟其心之勸且懲，
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse

The Ruler’s Means of Controlling His Officials and People

Huo Zhendong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Fresh ideas, vigorous writing, an antique style, and profound thought: an excellent composition, from which one can discern the learning stored within.”

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The argument is apt and sound; the style is classically elegant.”

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Elegant diction and abundant vigor: this is a man of accumulated learning.”

The sage can direct all under Heaven within his mind without making his mind subservient to all under Heaven. The sage has but one mind, whereas the officials and people throughout the realm have hundreds of millions of minds. How could the sage fuss over matters daily, exhausting his energies and spirit, seeking to make his joy and anger accord with those of hundreds of millions of minds, and accordingly tightening or relaxing, raising or lowering the severity of his laws? There must surely be a pivotal means by which he holds control. This pivotal means operates within his mind and extends throughout the realm, so that the minds of all under Heaven become one with the sage’s mind. Why is this? Joy and anger are the private feelings of one person; rewards and punishments are the public concern of all under Heaven. If I reward and punish all under Heaven according to one person’s joy and anger, none under Heaven will fail to regard this as “poetry” [?]. If, however, I take the joy and anger of all under Heaven as my own, then when I reward one person, I rejoice together with all under Heaven; when I punish one person, I am angry together with all under Heaven. Would anyone in the realm fail to submit wholeheartedly, finding encouragement and taking warning? Now, precisely because their hearts are thus encouraged and deterred…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也則舉天下之人惟聖人所輕重低昂而莫敢
不用其命是法行於天下而不見其迹機執於
一人而不見其勞聖人又何樂乎役其心以徇
天下哉宋儒劉氏以賞罰為人主制馭臣民之
柄請得廣其意而論之今夫聖人作而在上天
下臣民之主也大臣小臣吾股肱也羣黎百姓
吾赤子也故聖人視天下有一臣之不共一民
之不懷是股肱之痿痺而赤子之水火也不為
之所則患愈深起而圖之不得其機則又不勝
===
其自擾聖人曰吾為天下元首待痿痺而後治
之病獨股肱乎哉吾為天下父母待水火而後
急之危獨赤子乎哉是故其圖之也必預執之
也必簡運之也神妙而無方與天下為一體而
無復痿痺水火之足患焉何也聖人之心至明
也至公也明則天下之善惡功罪一無所隱公
則所以善善惡惡功功罪罪者一無所私於是
賞罰行焉聖人非以意為之善與功人心所共
是也惡與罪人心所共非也然人人能是非之
punctuated:
也，則舉天下之人，惟聖人所輕重低昂，而莫敢不用其命。是法行於天下而不見其迹，機執於一人而不見其勞，聖人又何樂乎役其心以徇天下哉？宋儒劉氏以賞罰為人主制馭臣民之柄，請得廣其意而論之。

今夫聖人作而在上，天下臣民之主也。大臣小臣，吾股肱也；羣黎百姓，吾赤子也。故聖人視天下，有一臣之不共、一民之不懷，是股肱之痿痺而赤子之水火也。不為之所，則患愈深；起而圖之，不得其機，則又不勝其自擾。聖人曰：「吾為天下元首，待痿痺而後治之，病獨股肱乎哉？吾為天下父母，待水火而後急之，危獨赤子乎哉？」是故其圖之也必預，執之也必簡，運之也神妙而無方，與天下為一體，而無復痿痺水火之足患焉。何也？聖人之心至明也，至公也。明則天下之善惡功罪一無所隱，公則所以善善惡惡功功罪罪者一無所私。於是賞罰行焉，聖人非以意為之。善與功，人心所共是也；惡與罪，人心所共非也。然人人能是非之
translation_en:
…then all the people under Heaven submit to whatever weight or standing the sage assigns them, and none dare fail to obey his commands. Thus the law operates throughout the realm without its workings being visible, and the pivotal mechanism rests in one man's hands without his exertion being apparent. Why, then, would the sage take pleasure in taxing his mind to accommodate everyone under Heaven? The Song Confucian scholar Master Liu regarded rewards and punishments as the ruler's means of controlling his officials and people. Allow me to expand upon his meaning and discuss it.

When a sage arises and occupies the highest position, he is lord of all officials and people under Heaven. Great and lesser officials are his limbs; the common people are his infant children. Thus, when the sage surveys the realm, a single official who fails in his duty or a single subject who feels no attachment to him is like paralysis in his limbs or an infant caught in flood or fire. If he makes no provision for them, the affliction grows deeper; if he rises to address it but fails to grasp the pivotal mechanism, he merely entangles himself in endless trouble. The sage says: “I am the head of all under Heaven. If I wait for paralysis before treating it, will the illness affect only my limbs? I am father and mother to all under Heaven. If I wait for flood or fire before attending urgently to it, will the danger threaten only my infant children?” Therefore, his planning must be anticipatory, his grasp of the governing mechanism must be simple, and his exercise of it must be wondrously subtle, unrestricted by any fixed method. He forms one body with all under Heaven, and paralysis, flood, and fire no longer give cause for anxiety. Why is this? The sage's mind is supremely discerning and supremely impartial. Through discernment, none of the good and evil, merit and wrongdoing under Heaven remains hidden; through impartiality, there is no private bias in how he commends goodness, condemns evil, credits merit, and punishes wrongdoing. Rewards and punishments are then put into effect: the sage does not administer them according to personal whim. Goodness and merit are what all people's hearts approve; evil and wrongdoing are what all people's hearts condemn. Yet, although everyone can judge these to be right or wrong…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而不皆能賞罰之故聖人先得天下是非之心
以議法賞足為天下勸罰足為天下懲是聖人
以天下治天下其執而運之者固自我也此所
謂制馭之柄非徒以法束縛之馳驟之之謂也
方十六相之未舉而四凶之未去也堯非蔽賢
而容姦也及舜舉而去之非自用也其善惡未
著堯不得以意先之先之固非天下之心也善
惡旣著舜不得以意後之後之尤非天下之心
也其斯為萬世賞罰之準乎甞考周禮以八柄
===
詔王曰爵以馭其貴祿以馭其富予以馭其幸
置以馭其行生以馭其福奪以馭其貧廢以馭
其罪誅以馭其過夫賞之柄五罰之柄三此柄
之所由名而為聖人之所執則一焉故自作威
作福而言則柄懸於君不可移也自命德討罪
而言則柄授於天不可易也自于祖于社而言
則柄制於命不可假也自衆共衆棄而言則柄
公於人不可私也自不費不暴而言則柄止於
節不可過也凡此皆聖人之所以運諸心而一
punctuated:
而不皆能賞罰之，故聖人先得天下是非之心以議法，賞足為天下勸，罰足為天下懲。是聖人以天下治天下，其執而運之者固自我也。此所謂制馭之柄，非徒以法束縛之、馳驟之之謂也。
方十六相之未舉而四凶之未去也，堯非蔽賢而容姦也；及舜舉而去之，非自用也。其善惡未著，堯不得以意先之，先之固非天下之心也；善惡旣著，舜不得以意後之，後之尤非天下之心也。其斯為萬世賞罰之準乎？
甞考《周禮》，以八柄詔王，曰：「爵以馭其貴，祿以馭其富，予以馭其幸，置以馭其行，生以馭其福，奪以馭其貧，廢以馭其罪，誅以馭其過。」夫賞之柄五，罰之柄三，此柄之所由名，而為聖人之所執則一焉。故自作威作福而言，則柄懸於君，不可移也；自命德討罪而言，則柄授於天，不可易也；自于祖于社而言，則柄制於命，不可假也；自衆共衆棄而言，則柄公於人，不可私也；自不費不暴而言，則柄止於節，不可過也。凡此皆聖人之所以運諸心而一
translation_en:
…yet not all can reward and punish them. Thus the sage first grasps the judgments of right and wrong shared by all under Heaven and uses these to deliberate upon laws. His rewards suffice to encourage all under Heaven, and his punishments suffice to admonish them. In this way the sage governs all under Heaven through their own judgments; yet it is he himself who holds and exercises this authority. This is what is meant by the handles of governance and control—not merely restraining people with laws and driving them hither and thither.
When the sixteen ministers had not yet been raised to office and the Four Malefactors had not yet been removed, Yao was not concealing worthy men and tolerating evil ones. When Shun subsequently raised the former and removed the latter, he was not acting on his own arbitrary judgment. Before their goodness and wickedness had become manifest, Yao could not anticipate matters according to his own wishes: to have done so would certainly not have accorded with the common judgment of all under Heaven. Once their goodness and wickedness had become manifest, Shun could not delay matters according to his own wishes: to have done so would still less have accorded with that common judgment. Is this not the standard for rewards and punishments for all ages?
I have examined the Rites of Zhou, which instructs the king through the eight handles of authority, saying: “Ranks control their nobility; emoluments control their wealth; grants control their good fortune; appointments control their conduct; sparing life controls their blessings; deprivation controls their poverty; dismissal controls their offenses; chastisement controls their transgressions.” There are five handles of reward and three of punishment. This is how these handles receive their names, but in the sage’s grasp they form a unity. Thus, in terms of wielding severity and bestowing blessings, these handles rest with the ruler and cannot be transferred. In terms of appointing the virtuous and punishing the guilty, these handles are conferred by Heaven and cannot be altered. In terms of rewards before the ancestral shrine and punishments before the altar of soil, these handles are regulated by the mandate and cannot be lent to others. In terms of honoring those whom the multitude honors and rejecting those whom the multitude rejects, these handles belong impartially to the people and cannot serve private interests. In terms of avoiding wastefulness and cruelty, these handles must remain within due measure and cannot exceed it. All these are the means by which the sage exercises them in his heart and brings into unity…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎天下者也是故賞當功而不僭罰當罪而不
濫天下之心悅服於此矣賞得罰而益恩罰得
賞而益威天下之心鼓舞於此矣由是天下無
不共之臣無不懷之民比屋可封而不仁者遠
焉非臣民之故也以聖人之賞罰素明也聖人
不能保天下之皆善而不惡有功而無罪而惟
恃吾所以生殺予奪乎天下者各當乎天下之
心而使之亹亹而趨鰓鰓而懼莫知誰之所爲
此聖人之世所以德多而刑少以其心運於法
而非法之所能盡也然猶未也昔者先王將賞
爲之加膳蓋喜之也至於罪人則五聽而後刑
三讓而後罰蓋愼之也嗟乎聖人之微意不可
識乎臯陶氏曰功疑惟重罪疑惟輕與其殺不
辜寧失不經左氏亦曰賞以春夏刑以秋冬玆
所謂仁可過義不可過聖人一天道也天道陽
主乎生育陰積於空虛任德而不任刑仲舒蓋
善言天人之際矣然則聖人仁天下之心又何
可以法盡哉後世烹阿封卽墨者不以毀譽撓
punctuated:
乎天下者也。是故賞當功而不僭，罰當罪而不濫，天下之心悅服於此矣；賞得罰而益恩，罰得賞而益威，天下之心鼓舞於此矣。由是天下無不共之臣，無不懷之民，比屋可封，而不仁者遠焉。非臣民之故也，以聖人之賞罰素明也。聖人不能保天下之皆善而不惡，有功而無罪，而惟恃吾所以生殺予奪乎天下者，各當乎天下之心，而使之亹亹而趨，鰓鰓而懼，莫知誰之所爲。此聖人之世所以德多而刑少，以其心運於法，而非法之所能盡也。
然猶未也。昔者先王將賞，爲之加膳，蓋喜之也；至於罪人，則五聽而後刑，三讓而後罰，蓋愼之也。嗟乎！聖人之微意不可識乎？臯陶氏曰：「功疑惟重，罪疑惟輕。與其殺不辜，寧失不經。」左氏亦曰：「賞以春夏，刑以秋冬。」玆所謂仁可過，義不可過，聖人一天道也。天道陽主乎生育，陰積於空虛，任德而不任刑。仲舒蓋善言天人之際矣。然則聖人仁天下之心，又何可以法盡哉？後世烹阿封卽墨者，不以毀譽撓
translation_en:
…and bring unity to all under Heaven. Thus, when rewards match achievements without exceeding what is deserved, and punishments match offenses without being excessive, the hearts of all under Heaven submit gladly. When rewards are complemented by punishments, their graciousness increases; when punishments are complemented by rewards, their authority increases. The hearts of all under Heaven are thereby stirred to action. Consequently, there are no ministers who are not reverent and no common people who are not devoted. Every household has someone worthy of enfeoffment, and the inhumane keep their distance. This is not owing to the ministers and people themselves, but to the sage’s consistently clear administration of rewards and punishments. The sage cannot ensure that everyone under Heaven will do good and never evil, render meritorious service and never commit an offense. He relies only on ensuring that his exercise of the powers to preserve life and put to death, to grant and to take away, accords in every case with the hearts of all under Heaven. He thereby makes them strive diligently and stand anxiously in fear, without knowing who has brought this about. This is why, in the age of a sage, virtue abounds and punishments are few: his heart guides the operation of law, yet law cannot encompass all that is in it.
But there is more. In antiquity, when the former kings were about to bestow a reward, they increased the food at their meals, expressing their joy. When dealing with offenders, however, they imposed corporal punishment only after the five modes of examining testimony, and inflicted penalties only after three admonitions, expressing their caution. Alas! Can we not discern the sage’s subtle intention? Gao Yao said: “When merit is doubtful, make the reward heavier; when guilt is doubtful, make the punishment lighter. Rather than kill the innocent, prefer to err by departing from the established norm.” Master Zuo also said: “Bestow rewards in spring and summer; impose punishments in autumn and winter.” This is what is meant by saying that benevolence may be carried to excess, but righteousness must not be: the sage is at one with the Way of Heaven. In the Way of Heaven, yang presides over generation and nurture, while yin accumulates in emptiness; it relies on virtue rather than punishment. Zhongshu indeed spoke well of the relationship between Heaven and humanity. How, then, could law fully encompass the sage’s heart of benevolence toward all under Heaven? In later times, the ruler who boiled the governor of A and enfeoffed the governor of Jimo did not allow slander or praise to sway…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其柄封雍齒斬丁公者不以恩怨殽其柄雖皆
有意為之然猶庶幾得聖人之遺意焉乃至賞
不必善罰不必惡或奪其所不肖以予其所賢
或殺其所憎以生其所愛使豪傑解體衆庶離
心遂為厲階同一制馭之柄而顧逆施之若此
宜其與聖人遠也可鑒哉
表
擬宋遣使分賑諸州羣臣謝表建隆元年
金節
===
同考試官學正林批場中作表率皆浮蔓此
能敷宣賑民實意深為可嘉
考試官敎諭萬批辭華駢麗音調鏗鏘四
六之隹者
考試官敎授鄒批典則可誦
建隆元年某月某日具官臣某等伏蒙
聖恩遣使分賑諸州稱
謝者伏以
恩詔肅將仰
punctuated:
其柄；封雍齒、斬丁公者，不以恩怨殽其柄。雖皆有意為之，然猶庶幾得聖人之遺意焉。乃至賞不必善，罰不必惡，或奪其所不肖以予其所賢，或殺其所憎以生其所愛，使豪傑解體，衆庶離心，遂為厲階。同一制馭之柄，而顧逆施之若此，宜其與聖人遠也。可鑒哉！
表
擬宋遣使分賑諸州羣臣謝表，建隆元年。
金節
同考試官學正林批：場中作表，率皆浮蔓，此能敷宣賑民實意，深為可嘉。
考試官敎諭萬批：辭華駢麗，音調鏗鏘，四六之隹者。
考試官敎授鄒批：典則可誦。
建隆元年某月某日，具官臣某等伏蒙聖恩，遣使分賑諸州，稱謝者。伏以：恩詔肅將，仰
translation_en:
…his authority; the ruler who enfeoffed Yong Chi and executed Ding Gong did not let gratitude or resentment confuse the exercise of his authority. Though both acted with deliberate intent, they nevertheless came close to preserving something of the sages’ underlying purpose. But when rewards do not necessarily go to the good, nor punishments to the wicked—when a ruler takes from those he considers unworthy to give to those he considers worthy, or kills those he hates to preserve those he loves—he causes outstanding men to lose their allegiance and the common people to become estranged, thereby laying the groundwork for calamity. The authority to govern is the same, yet he exercises it perversely in this fashion. No wonder he is far removed from the sages! Let this serve as a warning!

Memorial

A memorial of thanks composed in the voice of the assembled officials of the Song, upon the dispatch of envoys to distribute relief among the prefectures, in the first year of Jianlong [960].

Jin Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The memorials composed in the examination are generally superficial and prolix. This one expounds the substantive intent of bringing relief to the people and is highly commendable.”

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The diction is ornate, the parallel phrases beautiful, and the cadence sonorous: an excellent example of four-and-six prose.” [The transcription’s 隹 is doubtful; apparently intended as ‘excellent.’]

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Classically proper and worthy of recitation.”

On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Jianlong, your servants, so-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, respectfully offer thanks for having received your sagely favor in dispatching envoys to distribute relief among the prefectures. We humbly submit:

Your gracious edict is reverently carried out; we look up in admiration to …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天地好生之德
惠施均渥知
帝王開國之猷
和氣溢乎兩間懽聲騰於諸路矧濫親民之
責能忘戴
主之忱臣某等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首上言竊惟
天之立君爲民民之立命在食故虞廷受
禪先憂四海困窮而稷穀用登乃致萬邦
作乂餉遺鄰國格天之業斯弘粟散鉅橋
===
卜世之圖益永月令乘時和以布德相命
無私司徒散貨利以救荒政存有備九年
之積足國正以足民三鬴之賙濟衆爲能
得衆但法無舉息而代有汙隆阻饑之念
一疎康食之風鮮奏聞省斂省耕而大戒
齊令偶新以移民移粟爲盡心梁仁未溥
驅人民於蜀道恐多不待之虞給衣食於
縣官似匪可經之策設糜良苦嗟來而食
者幾何貸種徒殷累息而收者必至蓋豐
punctuated:
天地好生之德；惠施均渥，知帝王開國之猷。和氣溢乎兩間，懽聲騰於諸路。矧濫親民之責，能忘戴主之忱？臣某等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言。
竊惟天之立君爲民，民之立命在食。故虞廷受禪，先憂四海困窮，而稷穀用登，乃致萬邦作乂。餉遺鄰國，格天之業斯弘；粟散鉅橋，卜世之圖益永。《月令》乘時和以布德，相命無私；司徒散貨利以救荒，政存有備。九年之積，足國正以足民；三鬴之賙，濟衆爲能得衆。但法無舉息，而代有汙隆。阻饑之念一疎，康食之風鮮奏。聞省斂省耕而大戒，齊令偶新；以移民移粟爲盡心，梁仁未溥。驅人民於蜀道，恐多不待之虞；給衣食於縣官，似匪可經之策。設糜良苦，嗟來而食者幾何？貸種徒殷，累息而收者必至。蓋豐
translation_en:
…the life-loving virtue of Heaven and Earth. Your beneficence is bestowed equally and abundantly, revealing the grand design by which emperors and kings establish their states. Harmonious influence fills the space between Heaven and Earth; joyful acclaim rises throughout the circuits. Since we have undeservedly been entrusted with responsibility for tending the people, how could we forget our heartfelt devotion to our sovereign? Your servants, So-and-so and the others, in utmost joy and delight, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow as we submit this memorial.
We humbly reflect that Heaven establishes rulers for the people, and that the people depend upon food for their lives. Thus, when Shun received the throne by abdication at the court of Yu, his first concern was hardship and destitution throughout the realm. Only when the millet and grain ripened did the myriad states attain good order. By sending provisions to neighboring states, the undertaking that reached Heaven was magnified; by distributing the grain at Juqiao, the design for a dynasty lasting many generations was further secured. The Monthly Ordinances prescribe taking advantage of the season’s harmonious conditions to spread beneficence, with impartial injunctions [?]; the Minister of Education distributes goods and resources to relieve famine, his administration maintaining preparedness. Reserves sufficient for nine years enrich the state precisely by providing sufficiently for the people; relief amounting to three fu of grain assists the multitude and thereby wins their allegiance.
Yet although these principles admit of neither suspension nor abandonment, successive ages have their declines and flourishing periods. Once concern for those beset by hunger slackens, the practice of ensuring that people eat in security seldom produces results. On hearing of inspecting harvests and inspecting cultivation, the ruler of Qi took earnest warning, and his commands briefly assumed a new character [?]; but in regarding the transfer of people and grain as the utmost fulfillment of his duty, the ruler of Liang had yet to extend his benevolence widely. Driving the people onto the roads to Shu risks leaving many unable to survive until relief arrives; supplying clothing and food from government resources seems hardly a sustainable policy. Providing gruel entails much toil, yet how many will eat food offered with the contemptuous cry, “Hey, you, come here!”? Loans of seed may be plentiful to no purpose: collection with accumulated interest is certain to follow. For abundance…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
凶秦自司牧心類亡弓出納持之大農迹
同銷印此膏施難於下究而美意卒為虛
聲非遇
明時曷臻實效玆蓋恭遇
〇〇〇〇
睿謨神授
景運天開
德紹唐虞
功兼覆載紫雲獻彩適符
===
聖作之期赤日重輝允協人歸之兆蓋自
改元御宇惟
思發政施仁慨五季之陵夷兵連禍結閔諸
州之荼毒水溢旱乾鳥面鵠形望之頗無
生氣竹花木酪采之已竭餘根疹癘干天
仰觸
如傷之視哀號徹野彌嬰
若保之懷謂農事係王業之安危而
君心以民隱為休戚北漢之師且緩先
punctuated:
凶秦自司牧，心類亡弓；出納持之大農，迹同銷印。此膏施難於下究，而美意卒為虛聲，非遇明時，曷臻實效？
玆蓋恭遇〇〇〇〇睿謨神授，景運天開，德紹唐虞，功兼覆載。紫雲獻彩，適符聖作之期；赤日重輝，允協人歸之兆。蓋自改元御宇，惟思發政施仁。慨五季之陵夷，兵連禍結；閔諸州之荼毒，水溢旱乾。鳥面鵠形，望之頗無生氣；竹花木酪，采之已竭餘根。疹癘干天，仰觸如傷之視；哀號徹野，彌嬰若保之懷。謂農事係王業之安危，而君心以民隱為休戚。北漢之師且緩，先
translation_en:
…famine is left to the local governors [?], whose attitude resembles that of one who has lost a bow; receipts and disbursements remain under the Minister of Agriculture, whose actions resemble the melting down of seals. Thus beneficence can scarcely reach those below, and good intentions ultimately become empty words. Without an enlightened age, how could tangible results be attained?
Now we respectfully encounter 〇〇〇〇 a sovereign whose sagacious plans are divinely bestowed, whose glorious fortune Heaven has inaugurated, whose virtue continues that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, and whose achievements rival those of Heaven and Earth. Purple clouds display their colors, fittingly marking the advent of the sage sovereign; the red sun shines anew, truly answering the sign that the people turn to him. Ever since changing the reign title and assuming rule over the realm, he has thought only of issuing ordinances and practicing benevolence. He lamented the decline of the Five Dynasties, with warfare unending and calamities intertwined; he pitied the suffering of the various prefectures, afflicted by floods and drought. With faces like birds and bodies like gaunt swans, the people appeared scarcely alive. Gathering bamboo flowers and tree curds [?], they had already exhausted even the remaining roots. Disease and pestilence reached Heaven, moving his compassionate gaze, which regarded the people as though they were wounded; cries of distress resounded across the countryside, all the more stirring his concern to protect them as infants. He held that farming determined the security or peril of the imperial enterprise, and that the ruler’s heart shared in the people’s joys and sorrows through concern for their hardships. He therefore deferred the campaign against the Northern Han, first…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遣使以恤侵中原之略未遑遂分州而賑乏
發金錢於
內帑周賚同符資粟麥於郡倉漢蠲殊轍自
三川以周河北均覃
雨露之恩由兩畿以達淮南盡慰雲霓之望輶
軒所至待哺之息更生
詔令分傳推食之仁普及玆
有道之國天不能災而保民之
君人所共戴者也嵩呼雷應壤擊風從臣等竊
===
祿當官不免素餐之耻視饑由已徒深絶
粒之憂欲厚下而未能雖省躬而莫措惟
玆
駿惠實出
鴻私四方之菜色潜消百辟之葵心愈奮敢不
奉揚
德意保輯生靈夙駕桑田爲三農無逸之勸委
輸囷廩備五榖不升之需伏願
洞悉時艱
punctuated:
遣使以恤侵，中原之略未遑，遂分州而賑乏。發金錢於內帑，周賚同符；資粟麥於郡倉，漢蠲殊轍。自三川以周河北，均覃雨露之恩；由兩畿以達淮南，盡慰雲霓之望。輶軒所至，待哺之息更生；詔令分傳，推食之仁普及。玆有道之國，天不能災，而保民之君，人所共戴者也。嵩呼雷應，壤擊風從。
臣等竊祿當官，不免素餐之耻；視饑由已，徒深絶粒之憂。欲厚下而未能，雖省躬而莫措。惟玆駿惠，實出鴻私。四方之菜色潜消，百辟之葵心愈奮。敢不奉揚德意，保輯生靈，夙駕桑田，爲三農無逸之勸；委輸囷廩，備五榖不升之需。
伏願洞悉時艱，
translation_en:
…sent envoys to relieve those suffering from calamity [?]. Before there was leisure to undertake the conquest of the Central Plain, officials were dispatched to the various prefectures to relieve want. Gold and cash were issued from the palace treasury, matching the munificence of the Zhou; millet and wheat were supplied from prefectural granaries, taking a different course from the Han practice of tax remission. From Sanchuan throughout Hebei, all equally received grace like rain and dew; from the two capital regions as far as Huainan, all had their hopes fulfilled, like those who long for clouds and rainbows in drought. Wherever the envoys’ light carriages arrived, those awaiting nourishment gained a new lease on life. As imperial edicts were transmitted in every direction, the benevolence of sharing one’s own food reached everyone. This is a realm possessed of the Way, which Heaven cannot afflict with disaster, and a sovereign who protects the people, whom all alike uphold. Cries of acclaim, like those at Mount Song, resounded like thunder; people beat upon the earth in contentment and followed like the wind.
We, your servants, draw salaries we have not earned and occupy official posts, unable to escape the shame of eating without rendering service. Regarding the people’s hunger as our own responsibility, we merely deepen our anxiety over their lack of grain. We wish to enrich those below us but cannot; though we examine ourselves, we find no measures to take. This great beneficence comes entirely from your abundant favor. The pallor of hunger throughout the realm quietly fades, while the sunflower-like hearts of all officials turn toward you with ever greater zeal. How could we fail to carry forth your virtuous intentions and safeguard the people, setting out early for the mulberry fields to encourage the farming population to unremitting diligence, and delivering supplies to the granaries to provide against the need arising when the five grains fail to ripen?
We humbly pray that you fully comprehend the hardships of the times…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周諏物力
固已凝之
天命兢業恒存
綏旣定之人心惠鮮益廣拓封疆以恢
帝統萬方臻富庶之休登賢俊以輔
皇圖百代衍靈長之慶臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖恇躍感戴之至謹奉
表稱
===
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
同考試官敎諭王批〔霍鎭東事詳而覈辭典而文且〕
〔忠愛懇切之情具見篇末子其負經世之具者乎〕
〔允宜首薦〕
punctuated:
周諏物力，固已凝之天命，兢業恒存；綏旣定之人心，惠鮮益廣。拓封疆以恢帝統，萬方臻富庶之休；登賢俊以輔皇圖，百代衍靈長之慶。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、恇躍感戴之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策
第一問
同考試官敎諭王批〔霍鎭東：事詳而覈，辭典而文，且〕〔忠愛懇切之情具見篇末。子其負經世之具者乎？〕〔允宜首薦。〕
translation_en:
…inquire thoroughly into material resources; strengthen Heaven’s Mandate, already secured, maintaining constant vigilance and reverence; and reassure the people’s hearts, already settled, extending ever more widely your benevolence toward those in need. Expand the frontiers to enlarge the imperial dominion, so that all regions may enjoy prosperity and abundance; advance worthy and talented men to support the imperial enterprise, so that the blessing of enduring rule may extend through a hundred generations. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty, overwhelmed with trembling joy and grateful devotion. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and bring them to Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Huo Zhendong: His treatment of affairs is detailed and exact; his language is dignified and elegant. Moreover,〕〔his earnest feelings of loyalty and devotion are fully apparent at the essay’s close. Are you not one who possesses the abilities to order the world?〕〔He certainly deserves to be recommended first.〕

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭萬批敷揚我
祖宗燕翼大計詳矣盡矣非素懷芹暴之忱曷能究心如此
考試官敎授鄒批是篇條答明悉足備
皇儲進講之助宜錄之以式多士
人君愛天下必先愛其所親故垂裕之圖
不可以不遠人臣忠其君必先忠其所愛
故輔翼之術不可以不端玆執事策承學
首以古今儲訓爲問蓋善體
皇上愛子愛天下之心而以三代有道之長期
===
願之也意誠忠矣愚生卽委瑣未通於
國體其能默默無一辭之贊乎竊聞左師之
言曰父母愛子則爲之計深遠此在衆庶
且然况天子之子乎故愛之必有以敎之
也又叔孫之言曰太子天下本則天子之
愛其子非愛天下乎故敎之乃所以愛之
也三代盛王享國長久率用是道有典有
則夏之貽也玆啓所由以敬承禹道也三
風十愆殷之訓也玆太甲所由以克終允
punctuated:
考試官敎諭萬批：敷揚我祖宗燕翼大計，詳矣，盡矣！非素懷芹暴之忱，曷能究心如此？

考試官敎授鄒批：是篇條答明悉，足備皇儲進講之助，宜錄之以式多士。

人君愛天下，必先愛其所親，故垂裕之圖不可以不遠；人臣忠其君，必先忠其所愛，故輔翼之術不可以不端。玆執事策承學，首以古今儲訓爲問，蓋善體皇上愛子愛天下之心，而以三代有道之長期願之也，意誠忠矣！愚生卽委瑣，未通於國體，其能默默無一辭之贊乎？竊聞左師之言曰：「父母愛子，則爲之計深遠。」此在衆庶且然，况天子之子乎？故愛之必有以敎之也。又叔孫之言曰：「太子天下本。」則天子之愛其子，非愛天下乎？故敎之乃所以愛之也。三代盛王享國長久，率用是道。「有典有則」，夏之貽也，玆啓所由以敬承禹道也；「三風十愆」，殷之訓也，玆太甲所由以克終允
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: This exposition of our imperial ancestors’ grand plans for securing the welfare of their descendants is detailed and exhaustive! Had the writer not long cherished the sincere wish to offer his humble service—as one might offer celery or the warmth of the sun—how could he have devoted such thought to the matter?

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: This essay’s answers to the individual points are clear and thorough, and could assist in preparing lectures for the imperial heir apparent. It should be recorded as a model for the many scholars.

A ruler who loves all under Heaven must first love his own kin; thus his plans to leave prosperity to his descendants must be far-reaching. A minister loyal to his ruler must first be loyal to those whom his ruler loves; thus his methods of guidance and assistance must be upright. You, the examining officials, have now put policy questions to us students, beginning with the instruction of heirs apparent in ancient and modern times. Surely you understand well His Majesty’s love for his son and for all under Heaven, and wish for him the enduring rule enjoyed by the Three Dynasties when they possessed the Way. Your intention is truly loyal! Though I, an ignorant student, am insignificant and have not mastered the principles of government, could I remain silent without offering a single word in support?

I have heard the Master of the Left say: “When parents love their children, they plan deeply and far ahead for them.” If this is so even among common people, how much more so for the Son of Heaven’s son? Thus, loving him necessarily entails providing for his education. Shusun also said: “The heir apparent is the foundation of all under Heaven.” Is not the Son of Heaven’s love for his son, then, love for all under Heaven? Thus, educating him is the means of loving him.

The flourishing kings of the Three Dynasties enjoyed their realms for a long time because they all followed this Way. “Established institutions and established rules” were the legacy of the Xia: through these, Qi reverently carried on the Way of Yu. The “three pernicious habits and ten faults” were the admonitions of the Yin: through these, Tai Jia was able to remain to the end truly …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
德也文謨武烈周之佑啓也玆成康所由
以祈天永命弘濟艱難也故夏爲天子十
有餘世殷爲天子二十餘世周爲天子三
十餘世三代有道之長其故可知也然周
之卜曆視二代又過之而敎太子之法亦
至於周大備甞讀大戴禮文王世子而能
言其略焉夫自勸膳之禮肇於文嗜鮑之
禁嚴於武抗世子之法行於周公周之所
以固國本而造王業者從來遠矣然猶慮
===
夫天下後世諭敎之無法也則又監二代
而酌爲令典於是有始生之禮負之有司
見之南郊過闕則下過廟則趨是也有禈
褓孩提之訓入則有保出則有師太傅在
前少傅在後保其身體傅其德義導之敎
訓而又選天下之端士孝悌博聞有道術
者以輔翼之使得見正事聞正言行正道
是也及其少長則入於學入東學上親而
貴仁入南學上齒而貴信入西學上賢而
punctuated: 德也。文謨武烈，周之佑啓也，玆成康所由以祈天永命、弘濟艱難也。故夏爲天子十有餘世，殷爲天子二十餘世，周爲天子三十餘世。三代有道之長，其故可知也。然周之卜曆，視二代又過之，而敎太子之法，亦至於周大備。甞讀《大戴禮》、《文王世子》，而能言其略焉。夫自勸膳之禮肇於文，嗜鮑之禁嚴於武，抗世子之法行於周公，周之所以固國本而造王業者，從來遠矣。然猶慮夫天下後世諭敎之無法也，則又監二代而酌爲令典。於是有始生之禮，負之有司，見之南郊，過闕則下，過廟則趨，是也。有禈褓孩提之訓，入則有保，出則有師，太傅在前，少傅在後，保其身體，傅其德義，導之敎訓，而又選天下之端士，孝悌博聞有道術者，以輔翼之，使得見正事、聞正言、行正道，是也。及其少長，則入於學。入東學，上親而貴仁；入南學，上齒而貴信；入西學，上賢而
translation_en:
…virtue. King Wen’s plans and King Wu’s achievements provided the Zhou with support and guidance at its founding. Through these, Kings Cheng and Kang prayed to Heaven for an enduring mandate and successfully overcame great difficulties. Thus the Xia held the position of Son of Heaven for more than ten generations, the Yin for more than twenty, and the Zhou for more than thirty. We can understand why the Three Dynasties maintained their rule in accordance with the Way for so long. Yet the span of rule foretold by divination for the Zhou exceeded those of the preceding two dynasties, and the methods for educating the heir apparent also reached their fullest development under the Zhou. I have read the Elder Dai’s Record of Ritual and “King Wen as Heir Apparent,” and can set out their essentials.

The ritual of encouraging a parent to eat began with King Wen; the prohibition concerning a liking for salted fish was strictly observed by King Wu; and the rules for elevating the heir apparent [?] were put into practice by the Duke of Zhou. The means by which the Zhou secured the foundation of the state and established its royal enterprise thus had a long history. Yet they still feared that later generations throughout the realm would lack standards for instruction. They therefore looked to the preceding two dynasties and, weighing their practices, established exemplary institutions.

There were, accordingly, rites at birth: the responsible official carried the infant on his back, and the infant was presented in the southern suburb; when passing a palace gateway, the bearer dismounted, and when passing an ancestral temple, he quickened his steps. There was instruction in swaddling clothes [?] and early childhood: within, the child had a guardian; outside, he had a teacher. The Grand Preceptor stood before him and the Junior Preceptor behind him. They protected his physical well-being, instructed him in virtue and righteousness, and guided him through teaching. Upright gentlemen from throughout the realm—filial, respectful toward elder brothers, widely learned, and versed in the Way—were also selected to assist him, so that he would see proper deeds, hear proper words, and follow the proper path.

When he had grown a little older, he entered the schools. In the eastern school, he honored kinship and valued benevolence; in the southern school, he honored seniority in age and valued trustworthiness; in the western school, he honored the worthy and…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
貴德入北學上貴而尊爵入大學承師問
道退而考於太傅則德智長而治道得矣
旣冠成人則有紀過之吏徹膳之宰進善
之旌敢諫之鼓大夫進謀士傳民語則化
與心成而中道若性矣猶未也春誦夏絃
秋學禮冬讀書無一時非敎也行以和鸞
步中采齊趨中肆夏無一動非敎也周之
所以久於二代其故又可知也詩書所稱
一人元良萬邦以貞詒厥孫謀以燕翼子
===
其斯之謂乎秦人棄禮義而敎刑獄二世
之蹙寔自貽之此周秦之辨賈誼陳於漢
室者至詳也惜文帝未遑用耳漢唐晉宋
諸君稍稍脩故事無論儲寀更置敎法詳
略卽其身已多不免於風愆者又安望其
典則佑啓如三代哉宜不足以勤執事問
也惟我
太祖高皇帝
順天應人
punctuated:
貴德；入北學，上貴而尊爵；入大學，承師問道，退而考於太傅，則德智長而治道得矣。旣冠成人，則有紀過之吏、徹膳之宰、進善之旌、敢諫之鼓；大夫進謀，士傳民語，則化與心成，而中道若性矣。猶未也，春誦夏絃，秋學禮，冬讀書，無一時非敎也；行以和鸞，步中采齊，趨中肆夏，無一動非敎也。周之所以久於二代，其故又可知也。詩書所稱「一人元良，萬邦以貞」、「詒厥孫謀，以燕翼子」，其斯之謂乎？秦人棄禮義而敎刑獄，二世之蹙，寔自貽之。此周秦之辨，賈誼陳於漢室者至詳也，惜文帝未遑用耳。漢唐晉宋諸君稍稍脩故事，無論儲寀更置、敎法詳略，卽其身已多不免於風愆者，又安望其典則佑啓如三代哉？宜不足以勤執事問也。
惟我太祖高皇帝，順天應人，
translation_en:
…and prizes virtue; entering the northern school, he esteems the noble and honors rank; entering the Great Learning, he receives his teachers’ instruction and inquires into the Way. On withdrawing, he reviews what he has learned with the Grand Preceptor. Thus his virtue and wisdom grow, and he acquires the Way of government. Once capped and come of age, he has an official who records his faults, a steward who withdraws dishes from his meals, a banner inviting good counsel, and a drum inviting forthright remonstrance. Great officers offer plans, and gentlemen relay the people’s words. Thus his transformation develops together with his mind, and conformity to the Way becomes like an inborn disposition. Nor is this all: in spring he recites, in summer he plays the strings, in autumn he studies ritual, and in winter he reads the texts. There is no season without instruction. When traveling, he is guided by the harmonious carriage bells; his measured steps accord with “Cai Qi,” and his quicker steps with “Si Xia.” There is no movement without instruction. We can therefore understand why Zhou endured longer than the two preceding dynasties. Is this not what the Odes and the Documents mean when they say, “When the one man is supremely good, the myriad states are set right,” and “He bequeaths plans to his descendants, thereby bringing peace and aid to his sons”?
The men of Qin abandoned ritual and righteousness and taught punishments and imprisonment instead. Their straitened plight under the Second Emperor was truly of their own making. Jia Yi presented this distinction between Zhou and Qin to the Han court in the greatest detail; regrettably, Emperor Wen found no opportunity to put it into practice. The rulers of Han, Tang, Jin, and Song restored established practices to some extent. Leaving aside changes in the crown prince’s attendants and the degree of detail in their methods of instruction, many of these rulers themselves could not avoid errors and transgressions [?]. How, then, could one expect their standards and rules to provide guidance and enlightenment like those of the Three Dynasties? They surely do not merit troubling you with further inquiry.
Our own Emperor Taizu Gao, following Heaven and responding to the people…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
驅夷宅夏衣冠萬國鞮譯八荒宇宙一再造
矣乃其所以貽諸
聖子神孫者又非獨
崇高之業巳也
文德武威
躬兼三代建
儲置輔略昉成周首闢
大本堂以脩重傅之禮
面諭
===
皇太子以崇敬
天之學巳又博采古今
作昭鑒錄凡歷代善所當法惡所當戒者紀
載旣詳甄别尤審且
命輔導諸臣曰以此進講夫錄以鑒名語有之
矣以銅爲鑒可正衣冠以古爲鑒可知興
替故法善卽典則佑啓也戒惡卽三風十
愆也玆一鑒也上以照千古下以照萬世
大哉王言其終天地而不磨者乎逮我
punctuated: 驅夷宅夏，衣冠萬國，鞮譯八荒，宇宙一再造矣。乃其所以貽諸聖子神孫者，又非獨崇高之業巳也。文德武威，躬兼三代；建儲置輔，略昉成周。首闢大本堂，以脩重傅之禮，面諭皇太子，以崇敬天之學。巳又博采古今，作《昭鑒錄》，凡歷代善所當法、惡所當戒者，紀載旣詳，甄别尤審。且命輔導諸臣曰：「以此進講。」夫錄以鑒名，語有之矣：「以銅爲鑒，可正衣冠；以古爲鑒，可知興替。」故法善卽典則佑啓也，戒惡卽三風十愆也。玆一鑒也，上以照千古，下以照萬世。大哉王言！其終天地而不磨者乎！逮我
translation_en:
… expelled the barbarians and established himself in the Chinese heartland, brought the myriad countries into the civilized order of caps and robes, and received interpreters from the eight distant regions: the universe was made anew. Yet what he bequeathed to his sagely sons and divine grandsons was more than an exalted imperial enterprise alone. In his own person, he united the civil virtue and martial authority of the Three Dynasties; in establishing the heir apparent and appointing his assistants, he broadly followed the precedent of Zhou. He first opened the Hall of the Great Foundation (Dabentang) to uphold the rites of honoring tutors, and personally instructed the imperial heir apparent to esteem the learning of reverence for Heaven. He then drew widely upon ancient and recent history to compile the Record of the Illuminating Mirror (Zhaojian lu). Its accounts of good deeds worthy of emulation and evils to guard against throughout successive dynasties were detailed, and its discrimination between them especially judicious. He further commanded the ministers responsible for guidance and instruction: “Use this in your lectures.”
The record takes its title from the mirror, as the saying has it: “With bronze as a mirror, one can set one's cap and robes straight; with antiquity as a mirror, one can understand rise and decline.” Thus, emulating goodness means using established norms to assist and enlighten; guarding against evil means guarding against the three pernicious habits and ten faults. This single mirror illuminates the millennia of the past and the myriad generations to come. Great indeed are these royal words! Will they not endure, unerased, as long as Heaven and Earth? When it came to our …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝則有
聖學心法之撰綱凡有四君道也臣道也父
道也子道也而君道其大要焉目凡三十
有一有統言者有專言者而學問其急務
焉
宣宗章皇帝則有
御製帝訓為篇二十有五首君德以重神人之
主終馭夷以峻內外之防而脩治之術殆
無所不備焉
===
憲宗純皇帝則有
文華大訓為目有四曰進學曰養德曰厚倫
曰明治而四者之要亦以務學為急焉是
三書也繹自
宸衷而其旨廓閎深遠證諸往跡而其辭體要
簡嚴重
儲教即所以揚
祖德也範
當世即所以登三王也要之皆
punctuated:
成祖文皇帝則有《聖學心法》之撰，綱凡有四：君道也，臣道也，父道也，子道也，而君道其大要焉。目凡三十有一，有統言者，有專言者，而學問其急務焉。
宣宗章皇帝則有《御製帝訓》，為篇二十有五，首君德以重神人之主，終馭夷以峻內外之防，而脩治之術殆無所不備焉。
憲宗純皇帝則有《文華大訓》，為目有四：曰進學，曰養德，曰厚倫，曰明治，而四者之要亦以務學為急焉。是三書也，繹自宸衷，而其旨廓閎深遠；證諸往跡，而其辭體要簡嚴。重儲教，即所以揚祖德也；範當世，即所以登三王也。要之，皆
translation_en:
…Emperor Wen, Chengzu, composed Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). Its overarching categories number four: the way of the ruler, the way of the minister, the way of the father, and the way of the son; among these, the way of the ruler is the chief concern. Its topics number thirty-one, some treating matters comprehensively and others addressing particular subjects; learning and inquiry are its most urgent business.
Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong, produced the Imperially Composed Instructions for Emperors (Yuzhi dixun), in twenty-five chapters. It begins with the ruler’s virtue, emphasizing the importance of the sovereign who presides over spirits and men, and ends with controlling the foreign peoples, making strict the boundaries between the inner and outer realms. It encompasses virtually every method of cultivating oneself and governing.
Emperor Chun, Xianzong, produced the Great Instructions of Wenhua (Wenhua daxun), with four headings: advancing learning, nurturing virtue, strengthening human relationships, and making government enlightened. The essential concern of these four likewise gives priority to diligent learning. These three books issue from the imperial heart, and their purport is expansive, profound, and far-reaching. They are substantiated by the events of the past, and their language embodies essentials with concision and rigor. Giving weight to the education of the heir apparent is precisely the means of exalting ancestral virtue; providing a model for the present age is precisely the means of attaining the stature of the Three Kings. In essence, all …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇祖昭鑒之遺意也曷可以同異論哉恭惟我
皇上
撫運重熙受
天眷命
篤生
聖胤照耀
前星天下臣民莫不頌螽斯歌麟趾爲
社稷靈長慶矣
紀元二年
===
儲位早定此尤
皇上遠覽獨斷神人悅從上以培
仁厚之基下以開
纘承之緒自非
德合三代其能然乎然
垂裕之道在
君輔翼之責在臣故賈生又曰太子之善在於
早諭敎選左右夫心未鑿而先諭敎則化
易成開於道術智誼之指則敎之力也賈
punctuated:
皇祖昭鑒之遺意也，曷可以同異論哉？恭惟我皇上，撫運重熙，受天眷命，篤生聖胤，照耀前星。天下臣民莫不頌《螽斯》、歌《麟趾》，爲社稷靈長慶矣。
紀元二年，儲位早定，此尤皇上遠覽獨斷，神人悅從，上以培仁厚之基，下以開纘承之緒。自非德合三代，其能然乎？然垂裕之道在君，輔翼之責在臣。故賈生又曰：「太子之善，在於早諭敎、選左右。」夫心未鑿而先諭敎，則化易成；開於道術智誼之指，則敎之力也。賈
translation_en:
…the intention bequeathed by the imperial ancestor in his luminous discernment. How could these be judged in terms of sameness or difference? We reverently reflect that our Emperor, presiding over an era of renewed splendor and receiving Heaven’s favor and mandate, has been blessed with a sagely son, bringing radiance to the star of the heir apparent. Throughout the realm, subjects and common people alike recite “The Locusts” and sing “The Qilin’s Feet,” celebrating the enduring good fortune of the altars of soil and grain.
In the second year of the reign, the succession was settled early. This, above all, arose from the Emperor’s far-reaching vision and sole determination, which spirits and men gladly accepted. It strengthened the foundation of benevolence and generosity inherited from above and opened the way for succession below. Had his virtue not matched that of the Three Dynasties, could this have been achieved? Yet the way to bequeath lasting prosperity rests with the ruler, while the responsibility for assisting and guiding rests with his ministers. Thus Master Jia also said: “The goodness of the crown prince depends on instructing him early and selecting those who attend him.” If instruction begins before the mind has been carved by experience, moral transformation is readily accomplished. Enlightenment in the principles of the Way, learning, wisdom, and righteousness is the effect of instruction. Jia…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
生通達國體確乎其言之也今
皇太子
天授睿質
仁孝著聞釋襁褓以親
帷幄養德義以端聖功茲非其時哉蓋天下
臣民之願亦
皇上眞愛之心也
講筵肇舉儲寀環侍啓沃之道將奚先乎曰
三代敎法與
===
祖宗謨訓具在舉而行之則古今無二理誦而
詠之則述作無二心故語不必須使樂聞
也譬不必遠使樂悟也儀不必瀆使樂行
也功不必程使樂化也色溫氣和使易親
也辭嚴義正使知憚也憸夫壬人勿使在
側遠物異寶勿使在前夫然後
志氣清明義理浹洽
游息三王
陟降
punctuated:
生通達國體，確乎其言之也！今皇太子天授睿質，仁孝著聞，釋襁褓以親帷幄，養德義以端聖功，茲非其時哉？蓋天下臣民之願，亦皇上眞愛之心也。

講筵肇舉，儲寀環侍，啓沃之道將奚先乎？曰：三代敎法與祖宗謨訓具在，舉而行之，則古今無二理；誦而詠之，則述作無二心。故語不必須，使樂聞也；譬不必遠，使樂悟也；儀不必瀆，使樂行也；功不必程，使樂化也。色溫氣和，使易親也；辭嚴義正，使知憚也。憸夫壬人勿使在側，遠物異寶勿使在前。夫然後志氣清明，義理浹洽，游息三王，陟降
translation_en:
…Jia Sheng thoroughly understood the essential principles of governing the state: how sound his words were! Now the Imperial Heir Apparent possesses Heaven-bestowed intelligence, and his benevolence and filial devotion are widely known. Having left his swaddling clothes to enter the curtained chamber of instruction, is this not precisely the time to nurture his virtue and righteousness and set his progress toward sagehood on the proper course? This is the wish of all the empire’s officials and people, and also the true loving intention of His Majesty.

As the lectures commence and the heir apparent’s attendants gather around him, what should come first in enlightening and nourishing his mind? The answer is: the educational methods of the Three Dynasties and the plans and instructions of the imperial ancestors are all available. Put them into practice, and the principles of antiquity and the present prove to be one; recite and chant them, and the intentions of those who transmitted teachings and those who originated them prove to be one. Thus, instruction need not be insistent [?], so that he delights in hearing it; illustrations need not be far-fetched, so that he delights in understanding them; ceremonies need not be excessively repeated, so that he delights in performing them; achievements need not be subject to fixed measures, so that he delights in being transformed. A gentle expression and a harmonious manner make it easy for him to draw near; solemn words and upright principles teach him reverence. Let no treacherous or deceitful men remain at his side, and let no exotic objects or rare treasures be placed before him. Only then will his will and spirit be clear and lucid, and moral principles thoroughly penetrate his understanding; he will roam and repose among the Three Kings, ascending and descending…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列祖
太子聖日聖矣
太子聖而
國本固矣書曰若生子罔不在厥初生學記
曰禁於未發之謂豫宋臣程頤氏亦曰輔
養之道非待過而後諫在涵養薰陶而已
夫涵養薰陶正愼初防豫之謂也其得啓
沃之大旨乎舍乎此則智囊之辯不足任
也博望之賓不足賢也稽古之力不足師
===
也宣猷之集不足侈也承華之箴翼善之
記不足鑑也此在吾
君吾相加之意耳若夫卜世悠久矣啻超越成
周而已哉草茅之見如此不識可聞於
廟堂否惟執事幸敎
第二問
金節
同考試官學正林批儉美德也我
聖祖
punctuated:
列祖，太子聖日聖矣。太子聖而國本固矣。《書》曰：「若生子，罔不在厥初生。」《學記》曰：「禁於未發之謂豫。」宋臣程頤氏亦曰：「輔養之道，非待過而後諫，在涵養薰陶而已。」夫涵養薰陶，正愼初防豫之謂也，其得啓沃之大旨乎！舍乎此，則智囊之辯不足任也，博望之賓不足賢也，稽古之力不足師也，宣猷之集不足侈也，承華之箴、翼善之記不足鑑也。此在吾君吾相加之意耳。若夫卜世悠久矣，啻超越成周而已哉？草茅之見如此，不識可聞於廟堂否？惟執事幸敎。

第二問
金節
同考試官學正林批：「儉，美德也。我聖祖
translation_en:
… the successive imperial ancestors, and the crown prince will grow ever more sagely. When the crown prince is sagely, the foundation of the state will be secure. The Book of Documents says: “As with bearing a child, everything depends upon its first beginnings.” The Record of Learning says: “Preventing something before it arises is called anticipation.” Cheng Yi, a minister of the Song, likewise said: “The way to assist and nurture him is not to wait until he errs and then remonstrate; it lies simply in cultivation and formative influence.” Such cultivation and formative influence mean precisely taking care at the outset and preventing faults beforehand. Does this not capture the essential purpose of enlightening and nurturing the ruler’s mind? Abandon this, and the eloquence of the “Bag of Wisdom” cannot be relied upon; the guests of Bowang cannot be esteemed as worthy; efforts to study antiquity cannot serve as a model; the Xuanyou collection cannot be vaunted; and the Admonition for Chenghua and the Record of Supporting Goodness cannot serve as mirrors. These allusions are uncertain [?]. It rests only with our ruler and our chief minister to give this their attention. As for the dynasty’s enduring for generations to come, would it merely surpass the Zhou? Such are the views of this man of humble station. I do not know whether they may be heard at court. I respectfully hope that you will instruct me.

Second Policy Question
Jin Jie
Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor, comments: “Frugality is an admirable virtue. Our sagely founding ancestor …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上惓惓躬行誠萬代所宜誦法者子能揄揚詳悉可嘉可嘉
考試官教諭萬批嶺海操觚之士能敷宣
聖德無遺可謂被化之深者矣錄之
考試官教授鄒批莊雅豐贍識見尤卓
聖人之心無欲故不見天下有可欲不見
可欲斯所以遺於天下者無窮矣夫人君
見可欲而動以其心不能無欲故也心爲
欲所動而勢又足以聚之則將竭天下有
限之力以供吾無益之娛日亦有不足者
===
惟聖人之心冲虛澹泊一無所欲而天下
之物無一足以動之且存心於天下加志
於窮民方兢兢業業焉未遑也又安能恣
欲以私便其身耶故宮室有制乘輿服御
有度不貴異物不陳玩好非故矯焉以天
下儉其身蓋所以謹細微防逸欲爲天下
萬世慮至遠也此聖人之世所以家給人
足穀粟貴而金玉賤道德一而風俗同聖
人之所遺也而寧有窮乎哉此二帝三王
punctuated:
皇上惓惓躬行，誠萬代所宜誦法者。子能揄揚詳悉，可嘉可嘉！
考試官教諭萬批：嶺海操觚之士，能敷宣聖德無遺，可謂被化之深者矣。錄之。
考試官教授鄒批：莊雅豐贍，識見尤卓。
聖人之心無欲，故不見天下有可欲。不見可欲，斯所以遺於天下者無窮矣。夫人君見可欲而動，以其心不能無欲故也。心爲欲所動，而勢又足以聚之，則將竭天下有限之力，以供吾無益之娛，日亦有不足者。惟聖人之心冲虛澹泊，一無所欲，而天下之物無一足以動之。且存心於天下，加志於窮民，方兢兢業業焉未遑也，又安能恣欲以私便其身耶？故宮室有制，乘輿服御有度，不貴異物，不陳玩好，非故矯焉以天下儉其身，蓋所以謹細微、防逸欲，爲天下萬世慮至遠也。此聖人之世所以家給人足，穀粟貴而金玉賤，道德一而風俗同，聖人之所遺也，而寧有窮乎哉？此二帝三王
translation_en:
… His Majesty assiduously puts it into practice himself: truly this deserves to be praised and emulated for ten thousand generations. You have extolled it fully and in detail. Commendable, most commendable!
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: A man of letters from Linghai can expound the sage virtue without omission; he may indeed be said to have been profoundly imbued with its transforming influence. Accept this essay.
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: Dignified, elegant, rich, and ample; its understanding is especially outstanding.
The sage’s mind is free of desire; thus he sees nothing in the world as desirable. Because he sees nothing as desirable, what he bequeaths to the world is inexhaustible. When a ruler sees something desirable and is stirred by it, this is because his mind cannot be free of desire. If his mind is moved by desire, and his power is sufficient to amass the objects of that desire, he will exhaust the world’s limited resources to furnish his own profitless amusements, yet still find each day’s provision insufficient.
Only the sage’s mind is empty, tranquil, and utterly without desire; nothing in the world is sufficient to move it. Moreover, he sets his heart upon the world and directs his concern toward the impoverished people. He is so vigilant and diligent in this that he has no leisure: how could he indulge his desires for his own private comfort? Thus his palaces have prescribed limits, and his carriages, clothing, and personal furnishings have regulated measures. He does not prize exotic objects or display curios for his amusement. This is no deliberate affectation of personal frugality before the world [?]. Rather, by exercising care over the smallest matters and guarding against indulgent desires, he takes the longest possible view for the world through ten thousand generations. This is why, in the sage’s age, every household has sufficient provision and every person has enough; grain is valued and gold and jade held cheap; moral principles are unified and customs are shared. These are the sage’s bequests: how could they ever be exhausted? These were the Two Emperors and Three Kings …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之事惟我
皇太祖暨我
皇上爲能曠千古而符節之請陳其槩傳曰儉
德之共也書曰慎乃儉德惟懷永圖夫儉
以德言不儉則不德矣圖以永言不儉則
不永矣然則儉豈人君之細行也哉且人
君富有天下玉帛萬國處勢既便衆欲易
攻非儉不足以制之然待其攻而後制未
善也吾無所用其制而欲無所用其攻斯
===
善之善者也今夫彤車白馬大輅越席金
銀珠玉不飾錦繡文綺不展大哉堯之爲
君也而萬世心學之源所由啓乎舜得之
則飯糗茹草若將終身茅茨土階不改其
舊而好生之德以溥禹得之則疎儀狄絶
旨酒卑宮室惡衣服而永賴之績無疆不
邇聲色不殖貨利非湯之所以代虐者乎
分同姓以珍玉分異姓以遠方非武王之
所以易暴者乎之數聖人者性反不同而
punctuated: 之事，惟我皇太祖暨我皇上爲能曠千古而符節之。請陳其槩。傳曰：「儉，德之共也。」書曰：「慎乃儉德，惟懷永圖。」夫儉以德言，不儉則不德矣；圖以永言，不儉則不永矣。然則儉豈人君之細行也哉？且人君富有天下，玉帛萬國，處勢既便，衆欲易攻，非儉不足以制之。然待其攻而後制，未善也。吾無所用其制，而欲無所用其攻，斯善之善者也。今夫彤車白馬，大輅越席，金銀珠玉不飾，錦繡文綺不展，大哉堯之爲君也！而萬世心學之源所由啓乎！舜得之，則飯糗茹草，若將終身，茅茨土階，不改其舊，而好生之德以溥。禹得之，則疎儀狄，絶旨酒，卑宮室，惡衣服，而永賴之績無疆。不邇聲色，不殖貨利，非湯之所以代虐者乎？分同姓以珍玉，分異姓以遠方，非武王之所以易暴者乎？之數聖人者，性反不同，而
translation_en:
…the deeds of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Only our Imperial Grand Progenitor and our reigning Emperor have been able, across the gulf of millennia, to match them like the two halves of a tally. Let me set forth the broad outlines. The Commentary says: “Frugality is the common foundation of virtue.” The Book of Documents says: “Be mindful of your virtue of frugality; cherish plans for the enduring future.” Frugality is spoken of in terms of virtue: without frugality, there is no virtue. Planning is spoken of in terms of endurance: without frugality, nothing endures. Can frugality, then, be merely a minor matter of conduct for a ruler? Moreover, a ruler possesses all the wealth under Heaven and receives jade and silk from the myriad states. His position affords every convenience, and manifold desires can readily assail him; only frugality suffices to restrain them. Yet to wait until they attack before restraining them is not good enough. When I have no need to exercise restraint, and desire has no opening through which to attack, that is the best of all.

Consider the red carriage and white horses, the great carriage with its rush mat: no adornments of gold, silver, pearls, or jade, no display of brocade, embroidery, patterned silk, or damask. Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! Was this not where the learning of the mind for all ages had its source? Shun grasped this principle: he ate parched grain and wild plants as though he would do so all his life, retaining the old thatched roof and earthen steps unchanged; thus his life-loving virtue spread far and wide. Yu grasped it: he distanced himself from Yi Di, rejected fine wine, kept his palaces humble and his clothing coarse; thus the achievements on which later generations would forever rely knew no bounds. To shun music and sensual beauty and not accumulate wealth or profit—was this not how Tang supplanted a cruel ruler? To distribute precious jade among those of his own surname and distant territories among those of other surnames—was this not how King Wu replaced a tyrant? These several sages [?] differed in whether they possessed virtue by nature or returned to it through cultivation, yet…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其心之無欲一也先後異代而其澤之無
窮亦一也下逮漢唐晉宋英誼代興雖寡
欲之學未聞而崇儉之風可述漢文衣綈
履革帳無文繡惜費罷露臺之役下詔却
千里之馬此其儉殆性生也孝景承文守
成躬行節儉詔曰雕文刻鏤傷農事也錦
繡纂組害女紅也又曰黃金珠玉饑不可
食寒不可衣其禁勿采此其儉非偽為也
班固所稱文景移風易俗黎民醇厚以為
===
庶幾成康豈溢美哉其次則有身衣大練
色無重綵如漢光武者偉然中興烈也明
帝嗣之身御澣衣食無兼珍承考之道似
矣乃復惑志於沙門奚足以紹勤約之風
乎有令撞碎七寶器命公主不得飾翠繡
如宋太祖者卓然開國意也仁宗述之試
進士以富民在節儉戒嬪御以絲粒皆民
脂繩祖之武似矣廼至失德於宮闈奚足
以延仁厚之脈乎又其次則晉武焚雉頭
punctuated:
其心之無欲一也。先後異代，而其澤之無窮亦一也。下逮漢唐晉宋，英誼代興，雖寡欲之學未聞，而崇儉之風可述。漢文衣綈履革，帳無文繡，惜費罷露臺之役，下詔却千里之馬，此其儉殆性生也。孝景承文守成，躬行節儉。詔曰：「雕文刻鏤，傷農事也；錦繡纂組，害女紅也。」又曰：「黃金珠玉，饑不可食，寒不可衣，其禁勿采。」此其儉非偽為也。班固所稱文景移風易俗，黎民醇厚，以為庶幾成康，豈溢美哉？
其次，則有身衣大練，色無重綵，如漢光武者，偉然中興烈也。明帝嗣之，身御澣衣，食無兼珍，承考之道似矣。乃復惑志於沙門，奚足以紹勤約之風乎？有令撞碎七寶器，命公主不得飾翠繡，如宋太祖者，卓然開國意也。仁宗述之，試進士以富民在節儉，戒嬪御以絲粒皆民脂，繩祖之武似矣。廼至失德於宮闈，奚足以延仁厚之脈乎？又其次，則晉武焚雉頭
translation_en:
…their hearts were alike in being free from desire. Though they lived in different ages, earlier and later, they were also alike in the inexhaustibility of their beneficence. Coming down to the Han, Tang, Jin, and Song, outstanding and righteous rulers [?] arose in successive ages. Although learning devoted to diminishing desires was unheard of, their practices of honoring frugality deserve recounting. Emperor Wen of Han wore coarse silk and leather shoes, and his curtains had no patterned embroidery. Reluctant to incur the expense, he abandoned construction of the Dew Terrace; he also issued an edict rejecting a horse capable of traveling a thousand li. His frugality was surely innate. Emperor Jing succeeded Emperor Wen and preserved his achievements, personally practicing economy and frugality. His edict declared: “Ornamental carving and engraving harm agricultural work; brocades, embroidery, and decorative braiding harm women’s textile work.” He also said: “Gold, pearls, and jade cannot be eaten when one is hungry or worn when one is cold. Let their extraction be prohibited.” His frugality was no pretense. Ban Gu praised Emperors Wen and Jing for transforming customs and making the common people sincere and substantial, judging them nearly the equals of Kings Cheng and Kang. Was this excessive praise?
