Next come rulers such as Emperor Guangwu of Han, who wore coarse plain silk without layers of colored finery: a magnificent achievement in restoring the dynasty. Emperor Ming succeeded him, wearing washed garments and eating without an array of delicacies. He seemed to follow the proper way of carrying on his deceased father’s work. Yet he then allowed Buddhist monks to lead his mind astray. How could he suffice to perpetuate the tradition of diligence and restraint? There were also rulers such as Emperor Taizu of Song, who ordered vessels made of the seven treasures smashed and forbade princesses to adorn themselves with kingfisher feathers and embroidery: an outstanding expression of a dynasty founder’s resolve. Emperor Renzong carried on his example. He examined candidates for the jinshi degree on the proposition that enriching the people depends upon frugality, and admonished his palace consorts that every silk thread and grain came from the people’s toil. He seemed to follow in his ancestor’s footsteps. Yet he went so far as to fail in virtue within the palace women’s quarters. How could he suffice to sustain the tradition of benevolence and generosity? Next below these, Emperor Wu of Jin burned a pheasant-head…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
裘于前殿玄宗焚珠玉錦繡於殿前非不
示人儉也然溺志酣歌卒釀新亭之禍委
權胡孽自貽羯鼓之憂是儉一也而名實
相懸初終異節其優劣固較然矣卽有彼
善於此豈可與帝王之道同日論哉洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝
躬神聖之德
承帝王之統澹然無欲不假虛聲姑自却珍
===
獻一節言之方谷珍以金玉飾馬鞍獻則
却之曰寶玩非所好也江西行省以陳氏鏤
金牀進則
命毁之曰窮奢極欲亡之道也司天監以元氏
水精宮刻漏進則
命碎之曰此謂作無益害有益也其大者類如
此至若香米進於金華蒲萄酒進於太原
則以口腹累民却竹簟進於蘄州則以勞
民傷財罷其細者類如此又
punctuated:
裘于前殿，玄宗焚珠玉錦繡於殿前，非不示人儉也。然溺志酣歌，卒釀新亭之禍；委權胡孽，自貽羯鼓之憂。是儉一也，而名實相懸，初終異節，其優劣固較然矣。卽有彼善於此，豈可與帝王之道同日論哉？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，躬神聖之德，承帝王之統，澹然無欲，不假虛聲。姑自却珍獻一節言之：方谷珍以金玉飾馬鞍獻，則却之曰：「寶玩非所好也。」江西行省以陳氏鏤金牀進，則命毁之曰：「窮奢極欲，亡之道也。」司天監以元氏水精宮刻漏進，則命碎之曰：「此謂作無益害有益也。」其大者類如此。至若香米進於金華，蒲萄酒進於太原，則以口腹累民却；竹簟進於蘄州，則以勞民傷財罷。其細者類如此。又
translation_en:
…robe in the front hall, while Xuanzong burned pearls, jade, brocades, and embroideries before his palace hall: these were certainly displays of frugality. Yet the former abandoned himself to drunken singing and ultimately brought about the calamity lamented at Xinting; the latter entrusted power to a barbarian villain and brought upon himself the sorrows of the Jie drums. Their frugality was alike, yet reputation and reality stood far apart, and their conduct at the end differed from that at the beginning. Their relative merits and failings are surely plain. Even if one was better than another, how could they be discussed on the same footing as the Way of the true emperors and kings?
We reverently consider our Emperor Taizu Gao, who embodied sagely and divine virtue and inherited the succession of emperors and kings. Serene and free of desires, he did not rely on empty renown. Let us speak merely of his rejection of precious offerings. When Fang Guzhen [?; likely Fang Guozhen] offered a saddle ornamented with gold and jade, he rejected it, saying, “Precious curios are not what I delight in.” When the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat presented a bed ornamented with carved gold belonging to the Chen house, he ordered it destroyed, saying, “Exhausting every luxury and indulging every desire is the road to ruin.” When the Directorate of Astronomy presented the Yuan house’s crystal-palace water clock, he ordered it smashed, saying, “This is what is meant by making useless things to the detriment of useful ones.” Such were the more substantial instances. As for fragrant rice offered from Jinhua and grape wine offered from Taiyuan, he rejected them because satisfying his palate would burden the people. When a bamboo sleeping mat was offered from Qizhou, he stopped the offering because it would toil the people and waste their resources. Such were the smaller instances. Furthermore …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
下令曰四方非朝廷所需不得妄獻且
語省臣曰宋太祖家法子孫不得於遠方取珍
異甚得貽謀之道嗟乎我
皇祖節用愛人謹始範後之微意與古帝王何
間然哉頃年以來民風滋侈物力寖匱奢
示以儉文抹以質蓋有待矣賴我
皇上受命而興代
天理物
上思
===
祖德
下憫民窮
身先節約以風示四方愚生伏覩
登極明詔竊為
社稷蒼生稱慶焉夫光祿以司膳也聚天下之
方物以供
玉食燕饗有常數焉常數之外
明詔一裁而省之凡天下之有冗費如光祿者
又何所不釐乎
punctuated:
下令曰：「四方非朝廷所需，不得妄獻。」且語省臣曰：「宋太祖家法，子孫不得於遠方取珍異，甚得貽謀之道。」嗟乎！我皇祖節用愛人，謹始範後之微意，與古帝王何間然哉？頃年以來，民風滋侈，物力寖匱，奢示以儉，文抹以質，蓋有待矣。賴我皇上受命而興，代天理物，上思祖德，下憫民窮，身先節約，以風示四方。愚生伏覩登極明詔，竊為社稷蒼生稱慶焉。
夫光祿以司膳也，聚天下之方物以供玉食，燕饗有常數焉。常數之外，明詔一裁而省之。凡天下之有冗費如光祿者，又何所不釐乎？
translation_en:
…He issued an order saying: “The regions must not presumptuously present offerings of things the court does not require.” He also told the officials of the Secretariat: “The family rules of Emperor Taizu of the Song forbade his descendants to obtain rare treasures from distant places. This admirably embodied the way of providing guidance for posterity.” Ah! In his economy in expenditure and love for the people, and in his subtle intention to exercise care at the beginning and set a pattern for later generations, how could our imperial ancestor be faulted when compared with the ancient sage kings? In recent years, popular customs have grown increasingly extravagant, while material resources have gradually become exhausted. Showing frugality to the extravagant and effacing ornament with simplicity [?] have awaited someone to undertake them. Fortunately, our Emperor has received the Mandate and risen to rule, governing all things on Heaven’s behalf. Above, he reflects on his ancestor’s virtue; below, he pities the people’s poverty. He personally leads in economy and restraint, setting an example throughout the realm. Having reverently read the clear edict issued upon his accession, I, an unworthy student, privately rejoice for the altars of soil and grain and for the common people.
The Court of Imperial Entertainments is responsible for provisioning imperial meals. It gathers the regional products of the realm to supply the imperial table, and there are fixed allowances for banquets and feasts. Whatever exceeded these allowances the clear edict uniformly curtailed and reduced. Wherever throughout the realm there are superfluous expenditures like those of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, what could remain uncorrected?

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
內府以司藏也納四方之職貢以備
匪頒好用有定式焉定式之外
明詔一清而汰之凡天下之有闌出如
內府者又何所不剔乎至於采取金寶珠玉
織造絨葛綺錦與夫芝石香蠟之類旣罷
其役以爲民節力又約其緡以代民輸租
且惓惓
諭部臣曰朕加意節省用自有餘
朝野肅然改觀臣民竝受其福
===
德音所被眞如頌典謨訓誥異文而合旨也
媲美帝王同符
聖祖猗與休哉雖然
皇上儉德誠無以加矣顧愛
君必防其漸愼德必始於微況
一人之好尚萬方之耳目寓焉
一念之敬忽萬姓之休戚關焉古者工瞽獻規
女史紀過刀劒戶牖莫不有銘所以防逸
欲於易萌而不敢以自聖也是故舜無欲
punctuated:
內府以司藏也，納四方之職貢以備匪頒好用，有定式焉。定式之外，明詔一清而汰之。凡天下之有闌出如內府者，又何所不剔乎？至於采取金寶珠玉，織造絨葛綺錦，與夫芝石香蠟之類，旣罷其役以爲民節力，又約其緡以代民輸租。且惓惓諭部臣曰：「朕加意節省，用自有餘。」朝野肅然改觀，臣民竝受其福。
德音所被，眞如頌典謨訓誥，異文而合旨也。媲美帝王，同符聖祖，猗與休哉！雖然，皇上儉德誠無以加矣，顧愛君必防其漸，愼德必始於微。況一人之好尚，萬方之耳目寓焉；一念之敬忽，萬姓之休戚關焉。古者工瞽獻規，女史紀過，刀劒戶牖莫不有銘，所以防逸欲於易萌，而不敢以自聖也。是故舜無欲
translation_en:
The imperial storehouses are responsible for safekeeping: they receive the prescribed tribute from all quarters to provide for distributions and expenditures [?], for which established regulations exist. Whatever exceeded those regulations, the enlightened edict has comprehensively reviewed and eliminated. Wherever in the realm there are unauthorized disbursements like those of the imperial storehouses, what could now escape removal? As for procuring gold, precious objects, pearls, and jade; weaving velvet, kudzu cloth, figured silks, and brocades; and such things as numinous fungi, stones [?], incense, and wax, Your Majesty has abolished the labor services involved to spare the people's strength, and has also reduced the funds allotted to them to offset the people's tax payments. Moreover, you earnestly instructed the ministers: “I am taking particular care to economize; there will naturally be enough for expenses.” Court and country have solemnly taken on a new aspect, and officials and people alike receive the blessings.
Wherever these gracious pronouncements reach, it is truly as though one were reciting the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents: the wording differs, but the meaning accords. Your Majesty rivals the ancient emperors and kings in excellence and accords with the sagely dynastic progenitor. Ah, how splendid! Nevertheless, although Your Majesty's virtue of frugality truly could not be surpassed, one who loves his ruler must guard against the beginnings of decline, and vigilance over virtue must begin with the smallest things. How much more so when the eyes and ears of every region attend to the preferences of the One Man, and the well-being or distress of all the people depends on whether a single thought is attentive or negligent! In antiquity, court musicians and blind music masters offered admonitions, female scribes recorded faults, and knives, swords, doors, and windows all bore inscriptions. These served to guard against indulgence and desire where they could readily sprout, for rulers dared not regard themselves as already sages. Thus Shun was free of desire…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也而有惟危惟微之戒禹無欲也而有罔
遊罔淫之戒湯無欲也而有自滿自用之
戒武無欲也而有玩人玩物之戒此可見
帝王之心虔始以令終謹微以圖大淵默
非靜也臨御非動也深宮非內也大廷非
外也畿甸非邇也要荒非遠也匹夫非寡
也億兆非衆也持一敬以宰之則無欲之
心通於神明樽節之道範乎天地蓋有不
令而行者矣今我
===
===
皇上
儉與帝王同德
敬與帝王一心而顯微初終之義當有不待
戒而常惺者顧愚生所欲自效舍芹暴無
以也儻執事以爲然乎
第三問
徐賛化
同考試官敎諭陳批以觀心爲知人切要確
論也錄之
punctuated:
也，而有惟危惟微之戒；禹無欲也，而有罔遊罔淫之戒；湯無欲也，而有自滿自用之戒；武無欲也，而有玩人玩物之戒。此可見帝王之心，虔始以令終，謹微以圖大。淵默非靜也，臨御非動也；深宮非內也，大廷非外也；畿甸非邇也，要荒非遠也；匹夫非寡也，億兆非衆也。持一敬以宰之，則無欲之心通於神明，樽節之道範乎天地，蓋有不令而行者矣。今我皇上，儉與帝王同德，敬與帝王一心，而顯微初終之義，當有不待戒而常惺者。顧愚生所欲自效，舍芹暴無以也。儻執事以爲然乎？

第三問
徐賛化

同考試官敎諭陳批：「以觀心爲知人切要，確論也，錄之。」
translation_en:
…yet he received the warning that the human mind is precarious and the mind of the Way subtle. Yu was free of desires, yet received warnings against idle roaming and excess. Tang was free of desires, yet received warnings against self-satisfaction and reliance on his own judgment. King Wu was free of desires, yet received warnings against treating people and things as playthings. From this we can see the disposition of the ancient emperors and kings: reverent at the outset to secure a good conclusion, and attentive to small matters to accomplish great things. Profound silence is not stillness; presiding over government is not movement. The secluded palace is not an inner realm; the great court is not an outer realm. The royal domain is not near; the remote borderlands are not far. A single commoner is not few; the countless millions are not many. If one maintains undivided reverence to govern all these, a mind free of desires will communicate with spiritual powers, and the way of restraint and moderation will serve as a model for Heaven and Earth. There will indeed be things accomplished without commands.

Now our Emperor shares the virtue of frugality with the ancient emperors and kings, and is of one mind with them in reverence. Concerning the principles governing the manifest and the subtle, beginnings and endings, he surely remains constantly alert without needing admonition. Yet this foolish student, wishing to offer his service, has nothing beyond humble offerings of cress and the sun’s warmth. Might you, honored examiners, find this acceptable?

Third Policy Question
Xu Zanhua

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He takes observing the mind as the essential means of knowing people. This is a sound argument. Accept it.”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭萬批敷答明盡有養之士也
考試官教授鄒批條答有據
聖人有周天下之智是故以先務爲急聖
人有愛天下之仁是故以知人爲難急於
先務智之所以周天下也而仁之用益廣
難於知人仁之所以愛天下也而智之用
益神仁智相成此隆古聖帝所以致治之
盛也夫有啓運之君必有名世之臣則人
才之得如景從響應理固然矣乃知人則
===
哲古之聖人猶以爲難者何哉蓋聖人之
所謂才者與俗異必其涵養此心精純粹
美凝之弘深靜密出之通變圓神然後可
以受大荷艱綏猷經世惟其所用無不宜
之夫當其用之也固若景星之在天人皆
見之矣方其未用也則若良玉之在璞孰
從而辨之蓋天之生人不數其知而得之
也豈易易乎哉當堯之時羣后德讓豈惟
禹稷皐夔爲賢卽州牧侯伯莫非俊乂之
punctuated:
考試官教諭萬批：敷答明盡，有養之士也。
考試官教授鄒批：條答有據。
聖人有周天下之智，是故以先務爲急；聖人有愛天下之仁，是故以知人爲難。急於先務，智之所以周天下也，而仁之用益廣；難於知人，仁之所以愛天下也，而智之用益神。仁智相成，此隆古聖帝所以致治之盛也。夫有啓運之君，必有名世之臣，則人才之得，如景從響應，理固然矣。乃「知人則哲」，古之聖人猶以爲難者，何哉？蓋聖人之所謂才者與俗異，必其涵養此心，精純粹美，凝之弘深靜密，出之通變圓神，然後可以受大荷艱，綏猷經世，惟其所用無不宜之。夫當其用之也，固若景星之在天，人皆見之矣。方其未用也，則若良玉之在璞，孰從而辨之？蓋天之生人不數，其知而得之也，豈易易乎哉？當堯之時，羣后德讓，豈惟禹稷皐夔爲賢？卽州牧侯伯，莫非俊乂之
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Wan, an Instructor: “His exposition is clear and exhaustive; he is a scholar of cultivated character.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, a Professor: “His answers to the individual points are well supported.”
The sage possesses wisdom encompassing all under Heaven, and therefore regards the most pressing duties as urgent. The sage possesses benevolence that loves all under Heaven, and therefore regards discerning men as difficult. Giving urgency to the most pressing duties is how his wisdom encompasses all under Heaven, while the exercise of his benevolence becomes ever broader. Recognizing the difficulty of discerning men is how his benevolence loves all under Heaven, while the exercise of his wisdom becomes ever more wondrous. Benevolence and wisdom complete one another: this is how the sage emperors of high antiquity achieved such flourishing government.
Where there is a ruler who inaugurates a new era, there must be ministers renowned in their age. That men of talent should be found is thus as natural as a shadow following a form or an echo answering a sound. Yet, as the saying goes, “To discern men is to be wise.” Why did even the sages of antiquity regard this as difficult? It is because what sages mean by talent differs from the common understanding. Such a man must nourish his mind until it is refined, pure, and perfectly good. Inwardly, it must be broad and deep, still and attentive; outwardly, it must respond to change with adaptable and wondrous skill. Only then can he accept great responsibilities and shoulder difficult tasks, bring order to the plans of government, and govern the world, proving suitable for whatever employment he receives.
Once such a man is employed, he is indeed like an auspicious star in the heavens, visible to all. But before he is employed, he is like fine jade within an unworked stone: how can anyone distinguish him? Heaven does not often produce such men [?]; how could recognizing and securing them be an easy matter? In Yao’s time, the many lords were virtuous and deferential. Were Yu, Ji, Gao, and Kui alone worthy? Even the regional governors and the feudal lords were all among the outstanding men selected …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
選也然觀皐陶陳知人安民之謨而禹吁
之曰惟帝其難信斯言也雖聖人亦有歉
焉况逮後世風氣漸漓矯僞日滋則人之
難知不尤甚乎昔晏元獻之判西京也以
人物詢范文正遂舉富文忠張文定對焉
卒之竝薦於朝說者謂一問答而四相萃
矣張忠定之守金陵也以人物詢范延賞
遂舉張希顏對焉卒之竝薦於朝說者謂
一咨詢而二雋得矣何堯得之之難而元
===
獻與忠定得之之易也至若房玄齡杜如
晦二子微時曾靡尺寸之豎高孝基一見
卽以公輔期之若取攜然王勃楊炯盧照
鄰駱賓王四子一時焯有文藝之名裴行
儉一見卽以不終卜之若符券然何堯知
之之難而孝基行儉知之之易也噫是豈
無其故哉蓋堯以安民爲慮自以知人爲
急其鰓鰓然先天下之務者乃其憂天下
之心爲之也彼數子者不過品隲之偶合
punctuated: 選也。然觀皐陶陳知人安民之謨，而禹吁之曰：「惟帝其難。」信斯言也，雖聖人亦有歉焉。况逮後世，風氣漸漓，矯僞日滋，則人之難知不尤甚乎？昔晏元獻之判西京也，以人物詢范文正，遂舉富文忠、張文定對焉，卒之竝薦於朝。說者謂一問答而四相萃矣。張忠定之守金陵也，以人物詢范延賞，遂舉張希顏對焉，卒之竝薦於朝。說者謂一咨詢而二雋得矣。何堯得之之難，而元獻與忠定得之之易也？至若房玄齡、杜如晦二子微時，曾靡尺寸之豎，高孝基一見，卽以公輔期之，若取攜然。王勃、楊炯、盧照鄰、駱賓王四子，一時焯有文藝之名，裴行儉一見，卽以不終卜之，若符券然。何堯知之之難，而孝基、行儉知之之易也？噫！是豈無其故哉？蓋堯以安民爲慮，自以知人爲急，其鰓鰓然先天下之務者，乃其憂天下之心爲之也。彼數子者，不過品隲之偶合
translation_en:
…chosen from among the outstanding and able. Yet consider how, when Gao Yao presented his plans for discerning men and bringing peace to the people, Yu exclaimed: “Even the Emperor finds this difficult.” These words are true: even a sage falls short in this respect. How much more difficult must it have become to discern men in later ages, as prevailing customs grew ever less sincere and pretence and falsehood increased daily?

Formerly, when Yan Yuanxian administered the Western Capital, he asked Fan Wenzheng about men of talent. Fan responded by naming Fu Wenzhong and Zhang Wending, and both were subsequently recommended to the court. Commentators said that a single exchange brought together four chief councillors. When Zhang Zhongding governed Jinling, he asked Fan Yanshang about men of talent. Fan responded by naming Zhang Xiyan, and both were subsequently recommended to the court. Commentators said that a single consultation secured two outstanding men. Why was finding such men difficult for Yao, yet easy for Yuanxian and Zhongding?

Likewise, when Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui were still obscure and had not yet established even the slightest achievement, Gao Xiaoji saw them once and immediately judged that they would become the highest ministers of state, as readily as if taking something into his hand. Wang Bo, Yang Jiong, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang all enjoyed brilliant reputations for literary accomplishment in their day. Yet Pei Xingjian saw them once and immediately predicted that they would not come to a good end, with the certainty of matching the halves of a tally. Why was discerning men difficult for Yao, yet easy for Xiaoji and Xingjian?

Ah! Could there be no reason for this? Because Yao’s concern was to bring peace to the people, he naturally regarded discerning men as urgent. His anxious attention to the affairs of the realm before all else arose from his heart’s concern for the realm. Those other men’s assessments, however, were merely coincidental successes…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
純皭者心也而小廉曲謹見色豆羹者非
矣知難不懼從容順應者心也而戅疎周
章巧於趨避者非矣遇事不苟權度精切
者心也而儇佻脂韋冥行用罔者非矣直
道而行計安社稷者心也而依阿淟涊希
榮邀寵者非矣於此論之則心術攸判人
品較然其可得而欺哉雖然有要焉人君
一心天下之心係之而知人之道則自君
心之明且正者爲之本也眞德秀之衍大
===
學也以辨人才爲格物致知之要凡帝王
知人之事聖賢觀人之法憸壬罔上之情
皆載焉而推原於人君之一心則君心者
庸非天下之心之衡鑑乎故必寡慾以養
此心格物以明此心誠意以實此心親君
子遠小人以維持此心俾惟精惟一上契
帝堯之心法則鑑空衡平羣品莫眩百僚
協師師之風而萬邦成時雍之化矣所以
運天下之仁智者不益廣且神哉
punctuated:
純皭者，心也；而小廉曲謹、見色豆羹者，非矣。知難不懼、從容順應者，心也；而戅疎周章、巧於趨避者，非矣。遇事不苟、權度精切者，心也；而儇佻脂韋、冥行用罔者，非矣。直道而行、計安社稷者，心也；而依阿淟涊、希榮邀寵者，非矣。於此論之，則心術攸判，人品較然，其可得而欺哉？雖然，有要焉。人君一心，天下之心係之，而知人之道，則自君心之明且正者爲之本也。
眞德秀之衍《大學》也，以辨人才爲格物致知之要。凡帝王知人之事、聖賢觀人之法、憸壬罔上之情，皆載焉，而推原於人君之一心。則君心者，庸非天下之心之衡鑑乎？故必寡慾以養此心，格物以明此心，誠意以實此心，親君子、遠小人以維持此心，俾惟精惟一，上契帝堯之心法，則鑑空衡平，羣品莫眩，百僚協師師之風，而萬邦成時雍之化矣。所以運天下之仁智者，不益廣且神哉？
translation_en:
…Purity and unsullied integrity express the heart; petty incorruptibility and scrupulousness over trifles, or showing displeasure over a bowl of bean soup, do not. To recognize difficulties without fear and respond to circumstances calmly and appropriately expresses the heart; obtuse rashness, agitation, and clever maneuvering to advance or evade do not. To handle affairs without carelessness and weigh matters precisely expresses the heart; frivolity, slippery compliance, and blindly proceeding without understanding do not. To follow the straight Way and plan for the security of the state expresses the heart; servile acquiescence, sordid self-abasement, and seeking glory and favor do not. Judged on these grounds, the dispositions of people’s hearts are distinguished and their character becomes clear. How could they succeed in deceiving anyone? Yet there is an essential point. The hearts of all under Heaven depend upon the ruler’s single heart, and the way to understand people has its foundation in the clarity and rectitude of the ruler’s own heart.
In elaborating upon the Great Learning, Zhen Dexiu made discerning human talent essential to investigating things and extending knowledge. He included the deeds by which emperors and kings understood people, the methods by which sages and worthies assessed them, and the actual ways in which treacherous men deceived their superiors, tracing all these back to the ruler’s single heart. Is the ruler’s heart, then, not the balance and mirror for the hearts of all under Heaven? He must therefore diminish desires to nourish this heart, investigate things to enlighten it, make his intentions sincere to give it substance, and draw near to noble men and keep petty men at a distance to sustain it. By making it refined and single-minded, he may accord with the method of governing the heart transmitted by Emperor Yao. Then the mirror will be clear and the balance level, and none among the various kinds of people will confound his judgment. The hundred officials will harmonize in a spirit of mutual emulation, and the myriad states will attain the transforming condition of universal concord. Will not the means by which he puts benevolence and wisdom into effect throughout the world become still more extensive and wondrous?

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第四問
許岸
同考試官教諭鄭批蘊藉宏深議論正大殆
天資之美學力之優者取之
考試官教諭萬批聖賢為學宗旨發揮明
徹皆自得語也非勦說可比
考試官教授鄒批敷腴渾雅錄之
性原於天也則求道者不可無知性之學
學成於人也則盡人者不可無合天之功
===
蓋性道一原也求道而不知性是徇口耳
者也而何以造於自得之真天人一理也
盡人而不能合天是泥形器者也而何以
探其本原之妙此古昔聖賢雖資稟氣習
其始或不能以盡同及其從事於學以求
聞道而知天者則固未始有異也今夫天
不言而四時行百物生者自然而已矣人
之學道者亦惟求其自然者而已矣自然
之道蓋著見於日用彝倫之間而無事於
punctuated:
第四問

許岸

同考試官教諭鄭批：蘊藉宏深，議論正大，殆天資之美、學力之優者，取之。

考試官教諭萬批：聖賢為學宗旨，發揮明徹，皆自得語也，非勦說可比。

考試官教授鄒批：敷腴渾雅，錄之。

性原於天也，則求道者不可無知性之學；學成於人也，則盡人者不可無合天之功。

蓋性道一原也，求道而不知性，是徇口耳者也，而何以造於自得之真？天人一理也，盡人而不能合天，是泥形器者也，而何以探其本原之妙？此古昔聖賢，雖資稟氣習，其始或不能以盡同，及其從事於學，以求聞道而知天者，則固未始有異也。今夫天不言而四時行、百物生者，自然而已矣。人之學道者，亦惟求其自然者而已矣。自然之道，蓋著見於日用彝倫之間，而無事於
translation_en:
Fourth policy question

Xu An

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Rich in substance and profound in scope, with upright and capacious arguments. This is surely someone of excellent natural endowment and superior scholarly attainment. Accept him.”

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The guiding purpose of the sages’ and worthies’ learning is expounded clearly and thoroughly. These are all expressions of understanding attained for oneself, beyond comparison with borrowed explanations.”

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Ample and rich, rounded and elegant. Select him.”

Human nature originates in Heaven; thus those who seek the Way cannot dispense with learning that brings knowledge of human nature. Learning is brought to completion through human effort; thus those who fully realize what is human cannot dispense with the work of attaining accord with Heaven.

Human nature and the Way share a single source. To seek the Way without knowing human nature is merely to follow what passes between ears and mouth: how could one thereby reach the truth of understanding attained for oneself? Heaven and humanity share a single principle. To fulfill what is human without attaining accord with Heaven is to remain confined to material forms: how could one thereby fathom the subtlety of their ultimate source? Thus, although the sages and worthies of antiquity may initially have differed in their innate endowments, temperaments, and habits, when they devoted themselves to learning in order to hear the Way and know Heaven, they never differed in this respect.

Now, Heaven does not speak, yet the four seasons proceed and the myriad things come into being: this is simply spontaneity. Those who study the Way likewise seek only this spontaneity. The Way of spontaneity manifests itself amid daily activities and the enduring human relationships, without any need for…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矜飾矯強之勞者也是故平旦而好惡相
近焉孩提之愛親敬長而不學不慮焉乍
見孺子入井而怵惕惻隱之心生焉皆所
謂天也生知也自然者也而何待於學耶
蓋聖人者順此者也而亦必學焉者戒慎
恐懼以求不失其常而已非有加也賢人
者其自然亦與此同也而苟不學焉則好
惡相近者有時而梏亡之矣愛親敬長者
有不能達之天下者矣見孺子入井而怵
===
惕惻隱焉者有時而內交要譽矣故學也
者所以去其矜飾矯強之勞而歸之於自
然者也此所謂以人合天而其知未始不
一也此聖賢所學之大較也春秋之時有
孔子者出以天縱之聖具上知之資自其
為兒時固已知陳俎豆設禮容大與人異
矣及其長而道益尊四方之士從之游者
蓋三千焉此自古以來未有盛焉者宜若
無俟於學矣而孔子方且好古敏求焉晝
punctuated:
矜飾矯強之勞者也。是故平旦而好惡相近焉，孩提之愛親敬長而不學不慮焉，乍見孺子入井而怵惕惻隱之心生焉，皆所謂天也，生知也，自然者也，而何待於學耶？蓋聖人者順此者也，而亦必學焉者，戒慎恐懼以求不失其常而已，非有加也。賢人者，其自然亦與此同也，而苟不學焉，則好惡相近者，有時而梏亡之矣；愛親敬長者，有不能達之天下者矣；見孺子入井而怵惕惻隱焉者，有時而內交要譽矣。故學也者，所以去其矜飾矯強之勞而歸之於自然者也。此所謂以人合天，而其知未始不一也。此聖賢所學之大較也。
春秋之時，有孔子者出，以天縱之聖，具上知之資，自其為兒時，固已知陳俎豆、設禮容，大與人異矣。及其長而道益尊，四方之士從之游者蓋三千焉，此自古以來未有盛焉者，宜若無俟於學矣。而孔子方且好古敏求焉，晝
translation_en:
…the toil of affected embellishment and forced effort. Thus, at dawn, people’s likes and dislikes are close to one another; little children love their parents and respect their elders without learning or deliberation; and when someone suddenly sees a child falling into a well, alarm and compassion arise in the heart. These are all what is called Heaven, innate knowledge, and spontaneity. What need, then, is there to await learning? Sages follow this, yet they too must learn: through caution and apprehension, they seek merely to preserve its constant norm, adding nothing to it. Worthy people share this same natural endowment. Yet if they do not learn, the likes and dislikes that are so close to those of others may at times be fettered and lost; their love for parents and respect for elders may fail to extend throughout the world; and their alarm and compassion at seeing a child fall into a well may at times become a means of cultivating connections and seeking praise. Learning, therefore, removes the toil of affected embellishment and forced effort and restores spontaneity. This is what is meant by bringing the human into accord with Heaven: the knowledge attained has never been other than one and the same. Such is the broad outline of what sages and worthies learn.
During the Spring and Autumn period, Kongzi appeared. A sage endowed by Heaven, he possessed the capacities of the highest wisdom. Even as a child, he already knew how to arrange sacrificial stands and vessels and assume the proper ritual deportment, differing greatly from others. As he grew older and his Way became ever more revered, scholars from all quarters who associated with him as disciples numbered some three thousand. Such a flourishing had never occurred since antiquity. It would seem that he should have had no need of learning. Yet Kongzi still loved antiquity and diligently sought understanding; by day…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忘食夜忘寢學不厭而誨且不倦焉者何
也蓋誠有見於道之無窮而學不至於知
天者非聞道也故曰下學而上達知我者
其天乎是生知亦未始不學也乃謂孔子
之上而復有所謂生知者非然矣孔門之
徒惟子路爲最勇觀其初見之時佩豭舞
劒而以爲學之無益則其人可知也及聞
孔子忠仁之論括羽鏃礪之譬遂儒服委
質受教焉而卒躋於升堂之列蓋雖未入
===
于室而非學不至是矣孟子生於戰國之
際方其嬉戲爲墓間事踴躍築埋固所謂
閭巷子也及聞母氏斷機之訓遂勤脩不
息而卒願學孔子觀其七篇仁義炳若日
星則自洙泗以後一人而已此非問學之
功而有是乎以至謝顯道之不謁執政羅
仲素之爲南州冠冕固皆所謂載道之器
也然顯道以去矜學仲素以潛思力行學
則亦非無本而然者不然則更經利舉之
punctuated:
忘食，夜忘寢，學不厭而誨且不倦焉者，何也？蓋誠有見於道之無窮，而學不至於知天者，非聞道也。故曰：「下學而上達，知我者其天乎！」是生知亦未始不學也。乃謂孔子之上而復有所謂生知者，非然矣。

孔門之徒，惟子路爲最勇。觀其初見之時，佩豭舞劒，而以爲學之無益，則其人可知也。及聞孔子忠仁之論、括羽鏃礪之譬，遂儒服委質受教焉，而卒躋於升堂之列。蓋雖未入于室，而非學不至是矣。

孟子生於戰國之際，方其嬉戲，爲墓間事，踴躍築埋，固所謂閭巷子也。及聞母氏斷機之訓，遂勤脩不息，而卒願學孔子。觀其七篇，仁義炳若日星，則自洙泗以後一人而已。此非問學之功而有是乎？

以至謝顯道之不謁執政，羅仲素之爲南州冠冕，固皆所謂載道之器也。然顯道以去矜學，仲素以潛思力行學，則亦非無本而然者。不然，則更經利舉之
translation_en:
…forgetting to eat, forgetting to sleep at night, tireless in learning and unwearying in teaching—why was this so? It was surely because he perceived that the Way is inexhaustible, and that learning which does not attain an understanding of Heaven does not amount to hearing the Way. Thus he said: “I learn what is below and attain what is above. Is it not Heaven that understands me?” Even one born with knowledge, then, has never dispensed with learning. To claim that above Confucius there were others who possessed so-called inborn knowledge is mistaken.

Among Confucius’s disciples, Zilu was the boldest. Consider how, at their first meeting, he wore a boar ornament and brandished a sword, believing that learning was useless: this reveals what sort of man he was. When he heard Confucius’s discussion of loyalty and benevolence, and his analogy of fitting feathers to an arrow and sharpening its point, he donned scholarly robes, presented himself as a disciple, and received instruction. In the end he joined the ranks of those who had “ascended the hall.” Though he had not yet “entered the inner chamber,” he could not have reached this point without learning.

Mencius was born during the Warring States period. When, in his childhood games, he imitated activities among the graves, leaping about, building up earth and burying things, he was indeed what one would call an ordinary neighborhood child. But after hearing his mother’s admonition when she cut the weaving from her loom, he cultivated himself diligently without cease, and ultimately aspired to learn from Confucius. In his seven books, benevolence and righteousness shine like the sun and stars. Since the teaching at the Zhu and Si rivers, he alone had attained such stature. Could this have come about without the achievements of inquiry and learning?

Consider also Xie Xiandao, who declined to pay court to those holding power, and Luo Zhongsu, who stood foremost among the men of the southern region. Both were certainly what are called vessels bearing the Way. Yet Xiandao learned by ridding himself of conceit, and Zhongsu by deep reflection and vigorous practice; their attainments, too, were not without a foundation. Otherwise, the habit of changing one’s chosen Classic to gain an advantage in the examinations [?] …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
習卒不免為功名之士而所謂驚汗浹背
者亦不過一時羞惡之良而已其何能以
有成耶他如陸子靜自謂做人不倚師友
載籍楊中立所見一定不須窮索朱仲晦
稱其為天資出人非假學力者若於所謂
生知者似也然子靜之學又自謂不出於
人情事勢物理之外而中立之力學通經
亦非徒恃其天資之美而已者至其禪學
之疑蓋不知者泥於尊德性之一言而晚
===
出一節毀三經闢和議於世教亦有賴焉
豈得以其應時宰之聘而遂詬之耶由是
觀之道不可離也而人卒離道者則不學
之過也可學者人也學至乎純亦不已而
性通焉者則知天之極也此天人之所以
合一也故曰天者自然而已人之學道者
亦惟求其自然者而已嗚呼天豈遠於人
哉人之心固天也人自不知耳今夫人之
日用飲食語默動靜之間一闔一闢一張
punctuated:
習，卒不免為功名之士，而所謂驚汗浹背者，亦不過一時羞惡之良而已，其何能以有成耶？他如陸子靜自謂做人不倚師友載籍，楊中立所見一定，不須窮索，朱仲晦稱其為天資出人，非假學力者，若於所謂生知者似也。然子靜之學，又自謂不出於人情事勢物理之外，而中立之力學通經，亦非徒恃其天資之美而已者。至其禪學之疑，蓋不知者泥於尊德性之一言，而晚出一節，毀三經，闢和議，於世教亦有賴焉，豈得以其應時宰之聘而遂詬之耶？
由是觀之，道不可離也，而人卒離道者，則不學之過也。可學者，人也；學至乎純，亦不已而性通焉者，則知天之極也。此天人之所以合一也。故曰：天者，自然而已；人之學道者，亦惟求其自然者而已。嗚呼！天豈遠於人哉？人之心固天也，人自不知耳。今夫人之日用飲食、語默動靜之間，一闔一闢，一張
translation_en:
…such habits would ultimately leave them mere seekers of achievement and fame. Their much-mentioned alarm, with sweat soaking their backs, would amount to no more than a momentary stirring of their innate sense of shame and aversion to wrong. How could they thereby attain anything? Take other examples: Lu Zijing said that in conducting himself as a person he did not depend upon teachers, friends, or written works; Yang Zhongli, once his understanding was settled, had no need for further exhaustive inquiry. Zhu Zhonghui praised such men as possessing natural endowments surpassing those of others, without relying on the effort of learning. They seem akin to those said to possess knowledge from birth. Yet Zijing himself also said that his learning did not extend beyond human feelings, the circumstances of affairs, and the principles of things. Zhongli, too, studied diligently and mastered the classics, rather than merely relying upon his excellent natural gifts. As for the suspicion that his learning was Chan Buddhist, those who did not understand him were fixated upon the single phrase “honor the moral nature.” Yet the integrity he displayed in his later years [?], his condemnation of the Three Classics, and his opposition to peace negotiations also contributed to the moral teaching of the age. How could one revile him simply because he accepted an invitation from the chief minister of the time?
Seen in this light, the Way cannot be departed from; when people nevertheless depart from it, the fault lies in their failure to learn. It is human beings who are capable of learning. To pursue learning to purity, continuing without cease until one fully comprehends one's nature, is the utmost attainment in knowing Heaven. This is how Heaven and humanity become one. Thus it is said: Heaven is simply what is so of itself; those who study the Way likewise seek only this natural spontaneity. Alas! How could Heaven be distant from human beings? The human heart is itself Heaven; people simply do not recognize this. Now, amid people's everyday eating and drinking, speaking and remaining silent, moving and resting, there is a closing and an opening, a stretching …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一弛所以出之不窮而應之甚裕者蓋自
有天則存焉雖以孔子之聖亦不過默識
乎此耳故意必固我之盡無溫良恭儉讓
之皆備仕止久速之各當其可者蓋已合
乎自然之道而與天爲一矣若孟子固願
學孔子者而氣象巖巖猶不免焉宜乎諸
子之有所未逮也雖然亦存乎其學耳拘
繭滯礙非學不通發楊蹈厲非學不斂簡
伉尊大非學不遜陰幽暗塞非學不暢儇
===
佻捷敏非學不靜盛麗紛華非學不澹汗
漫遺落非學不密學之學之少而習焉長
而安焉老而忘焉則其去聖賢不遠而自
然之道將有與天爲一者矣愚生自束髮
讀書不知學爲何事蓋囿于其習者久之
而後知所以求道也乃者聞執事之敎而
惕乎其有省焉至于所謂自有者則茫乎
其未之有也惟進而敎之使卒有聞焉則
幸矣
punctuated:
一弛，所以出之不窮而應之甚裕者，蓋自有天則存焉。雖以孔子之聖，亦不過默識乎此耳。故意必固我之盡無，溫良恭儉讓之皆備，仕止久速之各當其可者，蓋已合乎自然之道而與天爲一矣。若孟子，固願學孔子者，而氣象巖巖猶不免焉，宜乎諸子之有所未逮也。雖然，亦存乎其學耳。拘繭滯礙，非學不通；發楊蹈厲，非學不斂；簡伉尊大，非學不遜；陰幽暗塞，非學不暢；儇佻捷敏，非學不靜；盛麗紛華，非學不澹；汗漫遺落，非學不密。學之，學之！少而習焉，長而安焉，老而忘焉，則其去聖賢不遠，而自然之道將有與天爲一者矣。

愚生自束髮讀書，不知學爲何事。蓋囿于其習者久之，而後知所以求道也。乃者聞執事之敎，而惕乎其有省焉。至于所謂自有者，則茫乎其未之有也。惟進而敎之，使卒有聞焉，則幸矣。
translation_en:
…and a relaxing: that these issue forth inexhaustibly and respond with such ample ease is because Heaven’s normative order naturally resides within them. Even Confucius, with all his sagehood, did no more than silently apprehend this. Thus he was entirely free of arbitrary notions, insistence, obstinacy, and self-centeredness; he possessed warmth, goodness, respectfulness, frugality, and deference in full; and whether he entered office or withdrew, lingered or departed promptly, he always acted as circumstances required. This was because he had already accorded with the Way of spontaneity and become one with Heaven. As for Mengzi, he certainly aspired to learn from Confucius, yet he could not entirely avoid an imposing severity in his bearing. It is therefore understandable that the other masters fell somewhat short. Nevertheless, this too depends upon their learning. Those confined as though in a cocoon and obstructed [?] cannot become open without learning; those exuberant and fiercely energetic cannot become restrained without learning; those haughty and self-important cannot become deferential without learning; those inwardly obscure and benighted cannot become clear and open without learning; those frivolous and quick-witted cannot become still without learning; those given to splendor and extravagant display cannot become unassuming without learning; those rambling and careless cannot become meticulous without learning. Learn it, learn it! Practice it in youth, become at ease with it in maturity, and in old age forget that one is practicing it. Then one will not be far from the sages and worthies, and through the Way of spontaneity one may come to be one with Heaven.

Ever since I bound up my hair in youth and began reading, I, your humble student, did not understand what learning was for. Only after remaining confined within my accustomed habits for a long time did I come to understand how to seek the Way. Recently, on hearing your instruction, I was stirred to a measure of self-awareness. Yet as for what you call possessing it within oneself, I remain bewildered and have not attained it. I would count it a blessing if you would continue to instruct me, so that I might finally gain some understanding.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
在五嶺之外山川阻深盜賊多有故其種
類有曰猺獞曰黎曰倭曰浪數者蓋自漢
入中國以來而已然矣彌竟山海出沒無
時畫計策者曰勦與撫夫制禦之術豈復
有出於此兩者之外哉顧其人用之有效
不效耳何也蓋勦與撫人人談之也勦而
撫撫而勦闔闢變化神其用於不測者非
有仁人之心運焉不能也今夫官府親民
布德達隱久之情孚漸爾面革此撫也厲
===
兵揚鼓申嚴約束陳師在郊力窮請死然
後責以無禮隨宜安集此勦而撫者也乃
今未諭施惠惠褻不懷方疑示信信反成
詐兼之墨夫利其金帛游徼鼓其熒惑故
納款未幾而嘯聚復熾矣撫之不可於是
乎勦然勦有大征有鵰勦大征者合數道
之師儲竟歲之糧掃穴犁庭期無噍類是
矣然猾酋先遯無辜濫及兵多費侈不可
數也其惟鵰勦乎賊衆俶擾螘聚蜂屯我
punctuated:
在五嶺之外，山川阻深，盜賊多有，故其種類有曰猺獞、曰黎、曰倭、曰浪數者。蓋自漢入中國以來而已然矣。彌竟山海，出沒無時。畫計策者曰勦與撫。夫制禦之術，豈復有出於此兩者之外哉？顧其人用之有效不效耳。何也？蓋勦與撫，人人談之也；勦而撫，撫而勦，闔闢變化，神其用於不測者，非有仁人之心運焉不能也。
今夫官府親民，布德達隱，久之情孚，漸爾面革，此撫也。厲兵揚鼓，申嚴約束，陳師在郊，力窮請死，然後責以無禮，隨宜安集，此勦而撫者也。乃今未諭施惠，惠褻不懷；方疑示信，信反成詐。兼之墨夫利其金帛，游徼鼓其熒惑，故納款未幾，而嘯聚復熾矣。
撫之不可，於是乎勦。然勦有大征，有鵰勦。大征者，合數道之師，儲竟歲之糧，掃穴犁庭，期無噍類，是矣。然猾酋先遯，無辜濫及，兵多費侈，不可數也。其惟鵰勦乎？賊衆俶擾，螘聚蜂屯，我
translation_en:
…beyond the Five Ridges, where mountains and rivers form deep barriers and bandits abound. Thus their several kinds are called Yao and Tong, Li, Wo, and Lang [?]. This has already been so since the Han entered the Central Kingdom [?]. Ranging throughout the mountains and seas, they appear and disappear at unpredictable times. Those who devise strategies speak of suppression and pacification. Can the methods of controlling them really extend beyond these two? It is simply a matter of whether those employing them do so effectively. Why? Everyone talks of suppression and pacification; but to suppress and then pacify, to pacify and then suppress, shifting between restraint and release and employing these methods with unfathomable mastery—this is impossible unless a benevolent heart directs them.
Now, when the authorities draw close to the people, extend beneficence, and acquaint themselves with hidden grievances, mutual trust develops over time, and the people gradually reform their outward conduct: this is pacification. When the authorities ready their weapons and sound their drums, reiterate strict commands, and deploy troops outside the settlements, until the enemy’s strength is exhausted and they submit themselves to death, and then rebuke them for their lack of propriety and settle them as circumstances require: this is suppression followed by pacification. Yet nowadays favors are bestowed before their intent is understood, so those favors are treated lightly and inspire no attachment; trustworthiness is displayed while suspicions persist, so that trustworthiness instead appears deceitful. Moreover, corrupt officials covet their gold and silk, and patrol officers foment their confusion. Thus, scarcely have they pledged submission before their armed gatherings flare up again.
When pacification proves impossible, suppression follows. Suppression, however, takes the form either of a major expedition or of targeted suppression. A major expedition combines the armies of several circuits, stores provisions for an entire year, clears out lairs and razes strongholds, intending to leave not a single survivor. Yet cunning chieftains escape beforehand, the innocent are indiscriminately caught up in the slaughter, and the troops are numerous and the expenses extravagant; such expeditions cannot be undertaken repeatedly. Should one then rely on targeted suppression? When the bandit host stirs up disorder, gathering like ants and swarming like bees, we…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乃攻其不備搴旗梟俊餘衆戢斂束手歸
降或稔惡不悛中情叵測則又陽示弭兵
陰從要擊此撫而勦者也乃今旣獲輯寧
復加掩襲被虜歸還槩行殄戮希功冒賞
冤抑滋多以致向善之念漸微從邪之習
愈錮故鐃歌甫畢而羽檄復馳矣自非仁
人之心神明變化則此兩策者有不倒行
而逆施耶然則制禦之術亦惟明於此兩
者而難易先後自較然矣或謂禦山寇易
===
禦海寇難蓋以雲帆風浪飄忽無定欲擊
而殱之難也然操檣楫則爲海持梃刃則
爲山此何常之有惟得其人則防海者扼
之於海而不能登山防山者蒐之於山而
不能入海矣奚難易之足云耶或謂治賊
如治病當先腹心而後手足蓋以黎岐中
盤猺獞外據其治之宜有先後也然腹心
有病則手足固爲之捍翼手足有病則腹
心亦爲之不寧總之爲病耳惟得其人則
punctuated:
乃攻其不備，搴旗梟俊，餘衆戢斂，束手歸降。或稔惡不悛，中情叵測，則又陽示弭兵，陰從要擊，此撫而勦者也。乃今旣獲輯寧，復加掩襲，被虜歸還，槩行殄戮，希功冒賞，冤抑滋多，以致向善之念漸微，從邪之習愈錮。故鐃歌甫畢，而羽檄復馳矣。自非仁人之心、神明變化，則此兩策者，有不倒行而逆施耶？然則制禦之術，亦惟明於此兩者，而難易先後自較然矣。
或謂禦山寇易，禦海寇難，蓋以雲帆風浪，飄忽無定，欲擊而殱之難也。然操檣楫則爲海，持梃刃則爲山，此何常之有？惟得其人，則防海者扼之於海，而不能登山；防山者蒐之於山，而不能入海矣。奚難易之足云耶？或謂治賊如治病，當先腹心而後手足，蓋以黎岐中盤，猺獞外據，其治之宜有先後也。然腹心有病，則手足固爲之捍翼；手足有病，則腹心亦爲之不寧。總之爲病耳，惟得其人則
translation_en:
…then we attack them unprepared, seize their banners, and behead their leading men. The remaining followers restrain themselves and submit without resistance. If some persist in entrenched wickedness without reforming, and their true intentions cannot be fathomed, we outwardly signal an end to hostilities while secretly moving to intercept and attack them. This is pacification followed by suppression. Yet nowadays, once peace has been secured, surprise attacks are launched again. Those returning from captivity are indiscriminately slaughtered, as men seek credit for victories and fraudulently claim rewards. Injustices multiply, so that the inclination toward goodness gradually wanes, while the habit of following evil becomes ever more entrenched. Thus the victory songs have scarcely ended before urgent military dispatches are again speeding forth. Without a benevolent person's heart and an almost divine capacity to adapt to changing circumstances, how could one avoid perversely misapplying these two policies? The art of control therefore depends simply on understanding these two approaches; their relative difficulty and proper sequence will then become clear of themselves.
Some say that defending against mountain bandits is easy, but defending against sea raiders is difficult, because their towering sails move unpredictably amid wind and waves, making it hard to strike and annihilate them. Yet when they handle masts and oars, they become sea raiders; when they take up clubs and blades, they become mountain bandits. What fixed distinction is there? Provided the right men are appointed, those defending the coast will hold them at sea so that they cannot enter the mountains, while those defending the mountains will hunt them down there so that they cannot take to the sea. What need is there to speak of relative difficulty? Some say that dealing with bandits is like treating illness: one should attend first to the vital organs, and afterward to the hands and feet. They mean that the Li and Qi [?] are entrenched in the interior, while the Yao and Zhuang occupy the outer regions, so there should be a proper sequence in dealing with them. Yet when the vital organs are diseased, the hands and feet naturally serve to defend and support them; when the hands and feet are diseased, the vital organs likewise cannot be at ease. In either case, it is illness. Provided the right men are appointed, then…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
刋山通道之謀自萬全而不必惜其費土
舍招主之設自率訓而無所肆其詭矣又
何先後之可言耶合而言之徭黎者鳥言
夷面荒憬不類然重信約刀耕火種大都
與吾民同也其馴者宜撫黠者宜勦倭醜
者以舟為家以剽掠為糧非言語可化宜
勦不宜撫浪賊者游手游食逃租避罪為
徭黎倭醜作耳目附山則寇山附海則寇
海利則聚害則散撫之在貰罪散黨安生
===
業寬逮繫薄斂省刑勦之在譏偵覵糾舍
匿禁私餉殲渠魁而脅從罔治也然而非
其人不可也蓋撫勦之策固所當講而所
以善用其策於不窮者惟在百執事以仁
存心分任其責耳如填撫百姓興敎化省
繇役聯保伍使守望相助責在守令曉暢
軍事謹尺籍伍符遇敵先登不愛其死責
在將領旬宣勅法簡師庀賦激勸有司賢
不肖責在岳牧監司別功罪明賞罰寬假
punctuated:
刋山通道之謀自萬全，而不必惜其費；土舍招主之設自率訓，而無所肆其詭矣。又何先後之可言耶？合而言之，徭黎者，鳥言夷面，荒憬不類，然重信約，刀耕火種，大都與吾民同也。其馴者宜撫，黠者宜勦。倭醜者，以舟為家，以剽掠為糧，非言語可化，宜勦不宜撫。浪賊者，游手游食，逃租避罪，為徭黎倭醜作耳目，附山則寇山，附海則寇海，利則聚，害則散。撫之在貰罪散黨，安生業，寬逮繫，薄斂省刑；勦之在譏偵覵，糾舍匿，禁私餉，殲渠魁，而脅從罔治也。
然而非其人不可也。蓋撫勦之策固所當講，而所以善用其策於不窮者，惟在百執事以仁存心，分任其責耳。如填撫百姓，興敎化，省繇役，聯保伍，使守望相助，責在守令；曉暢軍事，謹尺籍伍符，遇敵先登，不愛其死，責在將領；旬宣勅法，簡師庀賦，激勸有司賢不肖，責在岳牧監司；別功罪，明賞罰，寬假
translation_en:
…plans to clear the mountains and open roads will naturally be entirely sound, without any need to begrudge the expense; the institution of native chieftains’ heirs and recruiting headmen [?] will naturally secure obedience to instructions, leaving no scope for their deceit. What, then, is there to say about which should come first or last? Taken together, the Yao and Li speak like birds and have the faces of barbarians; remote and uncultivated, they are unlike us. Yet they value good faith and agreements, and practice slash-and-burn cultivation: in most respects they are the same as our own people. The tractable should be pacified, and the crafty suppressed. The Japanese villains make their boats their homes and obtain their provisions by plunder. Words cannot reform them; they should be suppressed, not pacified. The roving bandits live idly without working, evade taxes, and flee punishment. They act as eyes and ears for the Yao, the Li, and the Japanese villains. When attached to the mountains, they raid the mountains; when attached to the sea, they raid the coast. They gather when there is profit and disperse when there is danger. Pacifying them requires pardoning their offenses, dispersing their bands, securing their livelihoods, relaxing arrests and imprisonment, reducing levies, and lessening punishments. Suppressing them requires investigation and reconnaissance [?], bringing those who shelter them to account, prohibiting private provisioning, and destroying the ringleaders, while leaving those compelled to follow unpunished.
Yet none of this is possible without the right men. Policies of pacification and suppression certainly deserve discussion, but employing them effectively amid endless contingencies depends solely on all officials keeping benevolence in their hearts and each taking responsibility for his share. Thus, reassuring and pacifying the common people, promoting moral instruction, reducing labor services, organizing households into mutual-responsibility groups, and ensuring that they assist one another in keeping watch are the responsibilities of prefects and county magistrates. Thoroughly understanding military affairs, carefully maintaining military registers and unit tallies, leading the assault when encountering the enemy, and not begrudging their lives are the responsibilities of military commanders. Spreading imperial authority and enforcing the laws, selecting troops and arranging revenues, and spurring and admonishing officials, both worthy and unworthy, are the responsibilities of regional governors and surveillance commissioners. Distinguishing merit from guilt, making rewards and punishments clear, and allowing latitude…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文法而考其成功責在部使者選將調兵
明節制發縱指示酌緩急而用之責在督
府誠使督府部使者以是行之於上岳牧
監司將領守令以是行之於下上下同心
文武聿力流通實意剔去浮文省簿書期
會之煩而加意民瘼去奔走迎送之苦而
專力兵防蓋所謂以社稷生靈爲一體而
計功謀利之心有不存焉者也如此行之
而盜有不息者否矣苟不得其人而惟日
===
紛紛焉討求制禦之術卽使良平復出將
焉用之頃者仰荷
聖天子憫念海隅蒼生一時布在上下庶位者
皆出
廟堂愼選則愚生前所謂仁人者豈少哉顧
羣孽之航浮箐伏伺釁而動者尚多而嶺
海之間猶未有按堵期也則夫上下同心
舉萬全之策以慰更生之望者宜莫踰於
今日矣愚生第拭目俟之
punctuated: 文法而考其成功，責在部使者；選將調兵，明節制，發縱指示，酌緩急而用之，責在督府。誠使督府、部使者以是行之於上，岳牧、監司、將領、守令以是行之於下，上下同心，文武聿力，流通實意，剔去浮文，省簿書期會之煩而加意民瘼，去奔走迎送之苦而專力兵防，蓋所謂以社稷生靈爲一體而計功謀利之心有不存焉者也。如此行之，而盜有不息者，否矣。苟不得其人而惟日紛紛焉討求制禦之術，卽使良平復出，將焉用之？頃者仰荷聖天子憫念海隅蒼生，一時布在上下庶位者皆出廟堂愼選，則愚生前所謂仁人者豈少哉？顧羣孽之航浮箐伏、伺釁而動者尚多，而嶺海之間猶未有按堵期也，則夫上下同心，舉萬全之策以慰更生之望者，宜莫踰於今日矣。愚生第拭目俟之。
translation_en:
…legal formalities and assessing their actual accomplishments: this is the responsibility of the regional commissioners. Selecting commanders and deploying troops, clarifying the chain of command, directing operations, and employing forces according to the urgency of circumstances: these are the responsibilities of the supreme commander.

If the supreme commander and regional commissioners truly acted upon these principles above, while regional governors, surveillance commissioners, military commanders, prefects, and magistrates acted upon them below, those above and below would share one purpose, and civil and military officials would work together. They would communicate their genuine intentions and eliminate empty formalities, reduce the burdens of paperwork and reporting deadlines and give greater attention to the people’s suffering, and remove the hardship of rushing about to welcome and see off officials so that they could devote their efforts to military defense. This is what is meant by regarding the altars of soil and grain and the living people as one body, without harboring thoughts of calculating personal merit or seeking private advantage. If they acted thus, could banditry fail to cease? Surely not. But if suitable men cannot be found, and all that is done is to bustle about day after day seeking methods of control, then even if Zhang Liang and Chen Ping returned, what use could be made of them?

Recently we have gratefully received the sage Son of Heaven’s compassionate concern for the common people of this coastal region. Those now appointed to the various offices, high and low, have all been carefully selected by the court. Can there therefore be any shortage of the benevolent men of whom this humble student spoke above? Yet many evildoers still sail the waters or lurk in bamboo thickets, watching for an opening to act, and there is still no prospect of peaceful habitation in the region between the mountain ranges and the sea. Surely no time calls more urgently than the present for those above and below to unite in purpose and implement a fully reliable policy, fulfilling the people’s hope for renewed life. This humble student can only wipe his eyes clear and await the result.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
隆慶庚午廣東鄉試錄成濟
川從品藝之後竊系言于末
簡曰嘗讀西漢書陸賈綰方
寸之印銜其主命遨遊南越
爲後使臣所歆豔知五嶺外
爲一大區會也欲攬擷其勝
===
而無繇頃應聘度庾關見矗
巘崇岡不可名狀詢之自玆
山迤邐以南其嶙峋截嶭突
然聳三十二峯於羅陽之界
者羅浮山也比理楫浮淩湞
入三江襟帶灑沈總之望靈
洲以達朝夕之池浩蕩淼茫
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

隆慶庚午，廣東鄉試錄成，濟川從品藝之後，竊系言于末簡曰：嘗讀西漢書，陸賈綰方寸之印，銜其主命，遨遊南越，爲後使臣所歆豔，知五嶺外爲一大區會也。欲攬擷其勝而無繇。頃應聘度庾關，見矗巘崇岡，不可名狀。詢之，自玆山迤邐以南，其嶙峋截嶭，突然聳三十二峯於羅陽之界者，羅浮山也。比理楫浮淩湞，入三江，襟帶灑沈，總之，望靈洲以達朝夕之池，浩蕩淼茫
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

When the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination for the gengwu year of Longqing [1570] was completed, I, Jichuan, having participated in assessing the examination essays, ventured to append these words to its final pages:

I once read in the History of the Western Han how Lu Jia, bearing a seal an inch square and charged with his ruler’s command, journeyed through Nanyue, becoming the envy and admiration of later envoys. From this I knew that beyond the Five Ranges lay a great regional center. I wished to take in its splendid scenery but had no opportunity. Recently, accepting an invitation, I crossed Yuguan Pass and saw towering peaks and lofty ridges beyond description. On making inquiries, I learned that the mountains stretching southward from here, whose rugged, precipitous heights rise abruptly in thirty-two peaks within the bounds of Luoyang, were Mount Luofu.

Then, making ready the oars, I traveled along the Ling and Zhen rivers [?] and entered the Three Rivers, their waters encircling the land like collars and belts and spreading and sinking [?; 灑沈]. Taking it all in, I gazed toward Lingzhou and reached the waters of the morning and evening tides, vast and boundless …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
瀰天浴日濟川乃躊躇四顧
奪目駭心蓋羅浮鎮山渤澥
巨浸大觀具在矣扃鎖元氣
磅礴鬱蟠宜有英能俊乂鍾
於其間爰蒐往牒代有聞人
至於
國朝以德業炳彪一時者後先
===
趾美信造物所鍾不虛也曁
得閱多士之文閎意眇指祖
義本仁昔人評文謂峭拔千
尋波瀾萬頃乃今並見之可
不謂盛與聖門立教德行爲
先茲文藝末耳執是而可悉
多士醞藉固未敢盡必第心
punctuated: 瀰天浴日，濟川乃躊躇四顧，奪目駭心。蓋羅浮鎮山、渤澥巨浸，大觀具在矣。扃鎖元氣，磅礴鬱蟠，宜有英能俊乂鍾於其間。爰蒐往牒，代有聞人。至於國朝，以德業炳彪一時者，後先趾美，信造物所鍾不虛也。曁得閱多士之文，閎意眇指，祖義本仁。昔人評文，謂峭拔千尋、波瀾萬頃，乃今並見之，可不謂盛與？聖門立教，德行爲先，茲文藝末耳。執是而可悉多士醞藉，固未敢盡必，第心
translation_en:
…stretching across the sky and bathing the sun. Crossing the waters, I paused and gazed in all directions, my eyes dazzled and my heart awestruck. Here indeed were magnificent sights in their entirety: Luofu, the region’s guardian mountain, and the vast expanse of the sea. The primordial vital force is held within this landscape, immense, densely gathered, and coiled; surely outstanding and capable men must arise from its concentration here. I therefore searched earlier records and found renowned men in every age. Under our present dynasty, those whose virtue and achievements shone brilliantly in their time have followed one another in excellence. Truly, what the Creator has concentrated here has not been in vain.
When I came to read the examination candidates’ compositions, I found expansive ideas and subtle meanings, taking righteousness as their guiding principle and benevolence as their foundation. Earlier critics described writing as towering a thousand fathoms high and surging in waves across ten thousand qing. Now I have seen both qualities together: could this not be called a flourishing age? In the teachings established by the school of the Sage, virtuous conduct comes first; literary accomplishment is but secondary. I would certainly not venture to insist that these writings alone can fully disclose the candidates’ inner cultivation. Yet the mind…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之精微因言以宣由多士之
文以概其中亦庶乎瞰聖域
之壺奧窺斯道之涯涘者故
陟羅浮必起於谿徑由谿徑
而可躋其巔矣探海必始於
支流由支流而可泝其深矣
文藝者固道德之谿徑支流
也不可以觀人乎哉方今
聖人御極嘉意右文敎化浹於章
縫弓旌徧乎嵒穴多士瞻仰
涵濡己非一日茲得與計偕
縣次續食行將釋短褐據文
軒奉其薄技展采錯事必厚
自培養爭相濯磨攄涓埃之
punctuated: 之精微，因言以宣。由多士之文以概其中，亦庶乎瞰聖域之壺奧、窺斯道之涯涘者。故陟羅浮，必起於谿徑，由谿徑而可躋其巔矣；探海，必始於支流，由支流而可泝其深矣。文藝者，固道德之谿徑支流也，不可以觀人乎哉？方今聖人御極，嘉意右文，敎化浹於章縫，弓旌徧乎嵒穴。多士瞻仰涵濡，己非一日。茲得與計偕，縣次續食，行將釋短褐、據文軒，奉其薄技，展采錯事，必厚自培養，爭相濯磨，攄涓埃之
translation_en:
…the subtle workings of the mind are made manifest through words. By judging the inner character of these scholars from their writings, one may perhaps glimpse the innermost recesses [?] of the sages’ realm and discern the bounds of this Way. Thus, to ascend Luofu, one must begin on paths through the ravines; following these paths, one can reach its summit. To explore the sea, one must begin with its tributaries; following these tributaries, one can trace its depths. Literary accomplishment is indeed the ravine path and tributary of moral virtue. Can it not serve to assess a person?

Now the sage sovereign occupies the throne and, with gracious intent, honors literary learning. His transforming instruction has permeated the ranks of scholars, and the bows and banners summoning worthy men have reached even secluded caves and cliffs. These scholars have long looked up to him and been steeped in his beneficence. Now they have gained the opportunity to travel to the capital with the tribute mission, receiving provisions at successive counties along the way. Soon they will put aside their short garments of coarse cloth and ride in ornamented carriages, offering their modest skills, displaying their abilities, and undertaking official duties. They must cultivate themselves deeply and vie with one another in purification and refinement, contributing something as slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
益以稱塞
主上
高厚之恩
汪濊之澤於萬一俾後稱嶺表
得士惟兹科為最若祇以空
言自綴晪忍以裂膏腴絓牛
鼎於纖枯其何能勝宋人以
===
燕石為璞緹緗十重售鬻於
市發函視之主人掩口竊咲
多士縟文蔑實與玉表石衷
等猶之局於谿徑支流之末
即仰止望洋於羅浮大海胡
可得哉審爾豈直慙吾鄉之
先哲山川且羞之〔濟川〕鰓鰓
punctuated: 益，以稱塞主上高厚之恩、汪濊之澤於萬一，俾後稱嶺表得士，惟兹科為最。若祇以空言自綴晪，忍以裂膏腴、絓牛鼎於纖枯，其何能勝？宋人以燕石為璞，緹緗十重，售鬻於市。發函視之，主人掩口竊咲。多士縟文蔑實，與玉表石衷等，猶之局於谿徑支流之末，即仰止望洋於羅浮大海，胡可得哉？審爾，豈直慙吾鄉之先哲，山川且羞之！〔濟川〕鰓鰓
translation_en: …some slight contribution, thereby repaying even one ten-thousandth of His Majesty’s grace, lofty as Heaven and deep as Earth, and his vast, abundant beneficence. Let later generations say that, for obtaining worthy men in Lingbiao, this examination was unsurpassed. If they merely adorn themselves with empty words [?], presuming thereby to obtain rich lands as fiefs and to hang an ox-sized cauldron upon something slender and withered, how could they bear the weight? A man of Song took a stone from Yan for unworked jade, wrapped it in ten layers of reddish and yellow silk, and offered it for sale in the market. When the case was opened for inspection, the owner covered his mouth and laughed secretly [?]. If you scholars possess elaborate literary ornament but lack substance, you are like something with jade on the outside and mere stone within. You remain confined to the furthest reaches of minor paths and tributary streams. How, then, could you attain the heights of Luofu or the vastness of the great sea, toward which you gaze in awe? If this is indeed so, you would not merely bring shame upon the former worthies of our region: even its mountains and rivers would be ashamed of you! 〔Jichuan〕 anxiously…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然慮多士之一或類是也濟
川學愧為山識侔測蠡然所
以為多士者則忠矣毋併其
言忽之
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教
諭萬濟川謹序
punctuated:
然慮多士之一或類是也。濟川學愧為山，識侔測蠡，然所以為多士者則忠矣，毋併其言忽之。
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭萬濟川謹序。
translation_en:
…anxious lest even one among the many scholars should resemble this. I, Jichuan, am ashamed that my learning falls short of building a mountain, and my understanding is like measuring the sea with a ladle. Yet my intentions toward the many scholars are sincere; do not therefore disregard my words as well.
Respectfully written as a preface by Wan Jichuan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄕試錄序
隆慶庚午爲
皇上御極之四年天下鄕試士凡
再舉矣廣東遠在海隅御史
趙惇蓋自
闕下受
明命萬里馳至而監臨之秦等文
===
===
學官則以前御史楊標禮聘
繼至也闈館旣飭掫扞載嚴
百執事莫不懍懍受御史策
以襄翼
盛典司提調則右布政使莊應
禎右叅政桂嘉孝司監試則
按察使余敬中副使江一麟
punctuated:
廣東鄕試錄序

隆慶庚午，爲皇上御極之四年，天下鄕試士凡再舉矣。廣東遠在海隅，御史趙惇蓋自闕下受明命，萬里馳至而監臨之。秦等文學官則以前御史楊標禮聘，繼至也。闈館旣飭，掫扞載嚴，百執事莫不懍懍受御史策，以襄翼盛典。司提調則右布政使莊應禎、右叅政桂嘉孝；司監試則按察使余敬中、副使江一麟
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The gengwu year of Longqing was the fourth year since His Majesty ascended the throne. By then, the Provincial Examination for scholars throughout the realm had been held twice. Guangdong lies far away on the maritime frontier. Censor Zhao Dun received His Majesty’s illustrious command at court and hastened ten thousand li to serve as Supervising Official. We educational officials, Qin and the others, subsequently arrived, having been formally invited by the former censor Yang Biao.

The examination compound had been put in order, and patrols and defenses were made strict. All the functionaries, without exception, reverently received the Censor’s instructions to assist in this grand ceremony. Serving as Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhuang Yingzhen and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Gui Jiaxiao; overseeing the examination were Surveillance Commissioner Yu Jingzhong and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Jiang Yilin…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以泰與教諭萬濟川爲考試
官學正林大觀廖雲鵬教諭
唐汝禮王世道鄭誨陳然陳
文彬爲同考試官如期進提
學僉事余立所選士二千二
百有奇鎖院三試之得七十
五人錄之遵
===
制也錄且
獻御史謂泰當以職事序首簡謹
拜手言曰職方氏紀南粤爲
揚粤蓋內之也所從來遠矣
夫揚粤負嶺帶海界諸夏以
控制百蠻豈非天下一巨區
乎無論聲曁唐虞功冒成周
punctuated:
以泰與教諭萬濟川爲考試官，學正林大觀、廖雲鵬，教諭唐汝禮、王世道、鄭誨、陳然、陳文彬爲同考試官。如期進提學僉事余立所選士二千二百有奇，鎖院三試之，得七十五人，錄之，遵制也。
錄且獻，御史謂泰當以職事序首簡。謹拜手言曰：職方氏紀南粤爲揚粤，蓋內之也，所從來遠矣。夫揚粤負嶺帶海，界諸夏以控制百蠻，豈非天下一巨區乎？無論聲曁唐虞，功冒成周，
translation_en:
…Tai and Wan Jichuan, Instructor, were appointed Examiners. Lin Daguan and Liao Yunpeng, School Directors, and Tang Ruli, Wang Shidao, Zheng Hui, Chen Ran, and Chen Wenbin, Instructors, were appointed Associate Examiners. On the appointed date, the more than 2,200 candidates selected by Yu Li, Education Intendant and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, were admitted. The examination compound was sealed, and they were examined in three sessions. Seventy-five men were selected and their names recorded, in compliance with imperial regulations.
As the record was about to be presented, the Censor told me, Tai, that my official duties required me to write the preface at its beginning. Respectfully bowing with clasped hands, I say: The Officer of Regions recorded southern Yue as Yang-Yue, thereby including it within the realm. This has a long history. With the mountains at its back and the sea encircling it, Yang-Yue borders the Chinese lands and commands the many non-Chinese peoples. Is it not a great region of the world? Leaving aside its renown reaching back to Tang and Yu, and its achievements extending to the flourishing Zhou, …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
卽楚相傳書以往秦郡其地
而漢藩其王脩貢入侍駸駸
章甫國矣南海衣冠之氣晉
人有能望而測之者彼誠謂
山海靈秀蟠鬱廣旴不當獨
鍾異物必得異才應之顧風
氣之開也以漸而其盛也以
===
時方唐宋盛時張余諸賢相
望崛起功被一世譽流無窮
業已彬彬視鄒魯間至於鴻
筆之士鼎甲之臣則莫盛於
我
祖宗朝秦以其時考之尤宜增盛
於
punctuated: 卽楚相傳書以往，秦郡其地，而漢藩其王，脩貢入侍，駸駸章甫國矣。南海衣冠之氣，晉人有能望而測之者。彼誠謂山海靈秀，蟠鬱廣旴，不當獨鍾異物，必得異才應之。顧風氣之開也以漸，而其盛也以時。方唐宋盛時，張余諸賢，相望崛起，功被一世，譽流無窮，業已彬彬視鄒魯間。至於鴻筆之士、鼎甲之臣，則莫盛於我祖宗朝。秦以其時考之，尤宜增盛於
translation_en:
…From the time when a minister of Chu transmitted writings [?] onward, Qin organized this territory into commanderies, while Han enfeoffed its king as a vassal. Presenting tribute and attending at court, it steadily became a land of ceremonial caps—that is, of cultivated manners. Among the people of the Jin dynasty were those who could discern, from afar, the signs of a cultivated elite in Nanhai. They truly believed that the spiritual excellence of its mountains and seas, gathered densely across its vast expanse, could not be concentrated solely in extraordinary things: extraordinary talents must surely arise in response. Yet the opening of its cultural life proceeded gradually, and its flourishing awaited its proper time.
During the flourishing ages of Tang and Song, worthy men such as Zhang and Yu arose in succession. Their achievements benefited their entire age, and their renown endured without end. The region already possessed a refinement comparable to that of Zou and Lu. As for men of outstanding literary gifts and officials who had attained the top three examination ranks, however, no age surpassed the reigns of our imperial ancestors. I, Qin [?], judging by the times, hold that this flourishing ought to increase still further in…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今日何也應期故也蓋自我
皇祖以及
先帝興教育士垂二百年培養以
待
皇上者至深厚矣我
皇上又以崇儒重道敦本尚實風
之如
===
登極初詔首罷珍異之役表用巖
穴之遺蓋粹乎
帝王盛節賤遠物而寶賢才海邦
黎獻聞風希聲塗歌而邑頌
之矣頃屬窮島巨寇稱釁葦
澤兵連十郡士至無所息踵
我
punctuated: 今日。何也？應期故也。蓋自我皇祖以及先帝，興教育士，垂二百年，培養以待皇上者至深厚矣。我皇上又以崇儒重道、敦本尚實風之。如登極初詔，首罷珍異之役，表用巖穴之遺，蓋粹乎帝王盛節，賤遠物而寶賢才。海邦黎獻聞風希聲，塗歌而邑頌之矣。頃屬窮島巨寇稱釁葦澤，兵連十郡，士至無所息踵。我
translation_en: …in the present day. Why? Because the appointed time has arrived. From our imperial ancestor down to the late emperor, education was promoted and scholars nurtured for nearly two hundred years. Profound indeed was this cultivation in preparation for His Majesty. His Majesty has further guided them by honoring Confucian learning, esteeming the Way, strengthening the fundamentals, and valuing substance. For example, his first edict upon ascending the throne immediately abolished the requisitioning of rare and exotic objects and honored and appointed overlooked worthies living in seclusion. This was the pure expression of the highest imperial virtue: holding goods from afar cheap while treasuring worthy talent. The worthy men of this coastal region heard of his example and sought to echo it, singing his praises along the roads and celebrating him in their towns. Recently, however, great bandits from remote islands stirred up trouble in the reed marshes [?], and warfare spread through ten prefectures, leaving scholars nowhere even to rest their heels. Our…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上南顧憂之爲發
內帑金數萬
詔遣重臣視師平之有司者始得
投戈而講藝焉諸懷鉛刺經
之士遂晏然脫荊棘而就試
于有司此我
皇上之有大造於粵也夫培養厚
===
則掄用有餘資
詔令一則觀聽無異嚮而又出之
鋒刃之衝置諸樽俎之序則
其戴
恩而思報也益奮奮不可遏秦是
以不假洞靈之測而知得士
之必盛於
punctuated: 皇上南顧憂之，爲發內帑金數萬，詔遣重臣視師平之。有司者始得投戈而講藝焉，諸懷鉛刺經之士遂晏然脫荊棘而就試于有司。此我皇上之有大造於粵也。夫培養厚，則掄用有餘資；詔令一，則觀聽無異嚮。而又出之鋒刃之衝，置諸樽俎之序，則其戴恩而思報也益奮，奮不可遏。秦是以不假洞靈之測，而知得士之必盛於
translation_en:
…His Majesty looked south with concern and released tens of thousands in funds from the imperial treasury, issuing an edict to dispatch a high minister to oversee the troops and pacify the unrest. Only then could the responsible officials lay aside their weapons and attend to literary studies. The scholars who carried writing leads and closely studied the Classics could thus peacefully escape the brambles of turmoil and present themselves for examination before the authorities. Such is the immense beneficence His Majesty has bestowed upon Guangdong.

When scholars are generously nurtured, there is an ample pool from which to select men for service; when imperial commands are consistent, those who see and hear them are united in their orientation. Moreover, having been brought out of the clash of blades and placed within the ordered setting of ritual vessels and ceremonial tables, they become still more fervent in gratefully acknowledging imperial favor and seeking to repay it—a fervor that cannot be checked. Thus I, Qin, need not resort to spiritual divination to know that the recruitment of worthy men will surely flourish in…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今夫得士非以文也而文則其
先資之信也今披睹其文類
多明理習事通經術潜乎天
人之際而鏡於得失之林述
性而弗矯其眞譚藝而弗詭
於道圖事揆策而皆度於衷
奏始擊節賞之已而不可勝
===
===
錄則撫卷三歎曰士盛哉古
敷言試功若考德行道藝以
獻賢能何以加此哉雖然奏
又有聞議賢而下之臣之忠
也使士飾其說以自媒而錄
士者又止賢其說而不計其
實則失所爲議賢之道不忠
punctuated: 今。夫得士非以文也，而文則其先資之信也。今披睹其文，類多明理習事，通經術，潜乎天人之際，而鏡於得失之林；述性而弗矯其眞，譚藝而弗詭於道，圖事揆策而皆度於衷。奏始擊節賞之，已而不可勝錄，則撫卷三歎曰：「士盛哉！古敷言試功，若考德行道藝以獻賢能，何以加此哉！」雖然，奏又有聞：議賢而下之，臣之忠也。使士飾其說以自媒，而錄士者又止賢其說而不計其實，則失所爲議賢之道，不忠
translation_en:
…now. Men of worth are not selected for their writing alone, yet their writing provides preliminary evidence of their qualifications. Reading their compositions now, I find that most understand principles and are versed in practical affairs, comprehend the learning of the Classics, probe the relationship between Heaven and humanity, and discern the many instances of success and failure. They expound human nature without distorting its truth, discuss the arts without departing from the Way, and plan affairs and weigh policies in accordance with what is right. Zou [?] at first beat time in admiration; then, finding more worthy passages than could be recorded, he laid his hand upon the papers and sighed repeatedly: “How abundant are men of worth! The ancients examined men’s statements and tested their achievements, or assessed their virtue, conduct, learning, and arts in order to recommend the worthy and capable. How could they surpass this?”
Nevertheless, Zou [?] has also heard this: to assess worthy men and defer to them is a minister’s loyalty. If candidates embellish their arguments to promote themselves, and those who select them merely esteem their arguments without considering their actual qualities, then the proper way of assessing worthy men is lost. Such disloyalty …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孰甚焉昔者伊尹就聘數語
傅說對揚三篇皆先資也卒
之堯舜君民霖雨天下即畎
畝巖穴所自信者以成其信
次則杖策鄴下屏語隆中曾
不移時而定天下大計及其
功烈所就如合左券然由是
===
觀之古人之自獻皆量其能
而後言也辟諸田獵射御貫
則能獲禽不則厭覆是懼何
暇思獲泰不佞敢以忠道自
責而以量入之道望諸士諸
士其爲伊傅乎爲禹亮乎毋
徒沾沾豪舉爲也是役也先
punctuated:
孰甚焉？昔者伊尹就聘數語，傅說對揚三篇，皆先資也。卒之堯舜君民，霖雨天下，即畎畝巖穴所自信者，以成其信。次則杖策鄴下，屏語隆中，曾不移時而定天下大計；及其功烈所就，如合左券然。由是觀之，古人之自獻，皆量其能而後言也。辟諸田獵，射御貫則能獲禽，不則厭覆是懼，何暇思獲？泰不佞，敢以忠道自責，而以量入之道望諸士。諸士其爲伊傅乎？爲禹亮乎？毋徒沾沾豪舉爲也。
是役也，先
translation_en:
…what greater disloyalty could there be? In former times, Yi Yin’s few words upon accepting appointment and Fu Yue’s three chapters in response to the royal charge were both initial credentials [?]. Ultimately, they made their rulers and people like Yao and Shun and brought nourishing rain to all under Heaven. Thus they fulfilled the confidence they had held while still among the fields and caves. Next came the man who arrived at Ye carrying his staff, and the man who spoke privately at Longzhong: in scarcely any time they settled the grand strategy for the realm. When their achievements came to fruition, these matched their words as exactly as the two halves of a contract tally. From this we see that when men of antiquity offered their services, they first assessed their abilities and only then spoke. It is like hunting: those practiced in archery and charioteering can take game; otherwise, they fear being crushed or overturned—what leisure have they to think of taking game? I, Tai, untalented though I am, venture to hold myself accountable to the way of loyalty, and expect these scholars likewise to assess their own capacities. Will you scholars become men like Yi Yin and Fu Yue? Like Deng Yu and Zhuge Liang? Do not merely delight complacently in grand gestures.
In this examination undertaking, the former…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
總督兩廣左都御史兼兵部
左侍郎劉燾夙著勳猷士有
寧宇今提督兩廣巡撫廣東
兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史
李遷奮武揆文譽髦斯士先
巡撫廣東右副都御史熊汝
達飭度綏化士民用章先提
===
督南贛右僉都御史張翀今
提督南贛右僉都御史殷從
儉約法樹防澤流教遠右參
議史嗣元按察使分巡伸威
道張子弘副使許宗鎰史朝
宜僉事楊芷羅向辰防範於
外綜翊惟周右參將羅繼祖
punctuated: 總督兩廣左都御史兼兵部左侍郎劉燾，夙著勳猷，士有寧宇。今提督兩廣巡撫廣東兵部左侍郎兼右僉都御史李遷，奮武揆文，譽髦斯士。先巡撫廣東右副都御史熊汝達，飭度綏化，士民用章。先提督南贛右僉都御史張翀、今提督南贛右僉都御史殷從儉，約法樹防，澤流教遠。右參議史嗣元、按察使分巡伸威道張子弘、副使許宗鎰、史朝宜、僉事楊芷、羅向辰，防範於外，綜翊惟周。右參將羅繼祖，
translation_en:
…Liu Tao, Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Left Censor-in-Chief, and concurrently Left Vice Minister of War, had long distinguished himself through meritorious achievements and wise plans, giving the scholars a peaceful abode. Li Qian, the present Superintendent of Military Affairs in Liangguang and Grand Coordinator of Guangdong, Left Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, promoted military preparedness and directed civil affairs, honoring the outstanding scholars here. Xiong Ruda, the former Grand Coordinator of Guangdong and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, put regulations in order and fostered peaceful moral transformation, through which scholars and commoners manifested their virtues.

Zhang Chong, the former Superintendent of Military Affairs in Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and Yin Congjian, the present holder of those offices, established concise laws and safeguards; their beneficence spread and their instruction reached far. Shi Siyuan, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Zhang Zihong, Surveillance Commissioner assigned to inspect the Shenwei Circuit [?]; Xu Zongyi and Shi Chaoyi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; and Yang Zhi and Luo Xiangchen, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners, maintained safeguards outside and provided comprehensive coordination and support. Luo Jizu, Assistant Regional Commander of the Right, …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遊擊將軍李誠立署都指揮
僉事來熈晏秋元捍禦於外
保綏孔固副使施堯臣左參
議黎德充以入
賀行左參政姚世熈僉事張士
純以遷秩行皆先後賛襄與
有勞焉故事得竝書書之
===
直隸太平府儒學敎授鄒秦
謹序
punctuated:
遊擊將軍李誠立、署都指揮僉事來熈、晏秋元，捍禦於外，保綏孔固。副使施堯臣、左參議黎德充以入賀行，左參政姚世熈、僉事張士純以遷秩行，皆先後賛襄，與有勞焉。故事，得竝書，書之。
直隸太平府儒學敎授鄒秦謹序。
translation_en:
… Mobile Corps Commander Li Chengli and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Lai Xi and Yan Qiuyuan defended against external threats, ensuring firm protection and security. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Shi Yaochen and Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left Li Dechong departed to offer congratulations at court; Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Yao Shixi and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Zhang Shichun departed upon promotion. All, at different times, assisted in the undertaking and shared in its meritorious work. Established precedent permits them to be recorded together, and I therefore record them here.
Preface respectfully composed by Zou Qin, Professor of the Confucian School of Taiping Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史趙惇〔子明山東平原縣人乙丑進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使莊應禎〔希周福建惠安縣人丁未進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司右參政桂嘉孝〔純甫四川成都縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使余敬中〔子星直隸銅陵縣人己未進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司副使江一麟〔仲文直隸婺源縣人癸丑進士〕
===
考試官
直隸太平府儒學教授鄒泰〔景益直隸濬縣人癸卯貢士〕
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭萬濟川〔汝舟江西南昌縣人己酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隸鳳陽府亳州儒學學正林大觀〔朝敬福建莆田縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府潁州儒學學正廖雲鵬〔子翀福建候官縣籍江西新淦縣人壬子貢士〕
直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣儒學教諭唐汝禮〔思敬浙江蘭谿縣人甲子貢士〕
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭王世道〔時鳴江西萬年縣人壬子貢士〕
湖廣荊州府夷陵州遠安縣儒學教諭鄭誨〔忠卿江西浮梁縣人戊午貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年廣東鄉試

監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史趙惇〔子明，山東平原縣人，乙丑進士〕。

廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使莊應禎〔希周，福建惠安縣人，丁未進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司右參政桂嘉孝〔純甫，四川成都縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使余敬中〔子星，直隸銅陵縣人，己未進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司副使江一麟〔仲文，直隸婺源縣人，癸丑進士〕。

考試官
直隸太平府儒學教授鄒泰〔景益，直隸濬縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
湖廣黃州府黃陂縣儒學教諭萬濟川〔汝舟，江西南昌縣人，己酉貢士〕。

同考試官
直隸鳳陽府亳州儒學學正林大觀〔朝敬，福建莆田縣人，壬子貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府潁州儒學學正廖雲鵬〔子翀，福建候官縣籍，江西新淦縣人，壬子貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府宿州靈璧縣儒學教諭唐汝禮〔思敬，浙江蘭谿縣人，甲子貢士〕。
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭王世道〔時鳴，江西萬年縣人，壬子貢士〕。
湖廣荊州府夷陵州遠安縣儒學教諭鄭誨〔忠卿，江西浮梁縣人，戊午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Longqing (1570)

Supervising Official
Zhao Dun, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Ziming and was from Pingyuan County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yichou year.

Proctors
Zhuang Yingzhen, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Xizhou and was from Hui’an County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Gui Jiaxiao, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Chunfu and was from Chengdu County, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Yu Jingzhong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Zixing and was from Tongling County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year.
Jiang Yilin, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Zhongwen and was from Wuyuan County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Examiners
Zou Tai, Professor of the Confucian School of Taiping Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Jingyi and was from Xun County, Zhili. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the guimao year.
Wan Jichuan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Ruzhou and was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute student of the jiyou year.

Associate Examiners
Lin Daguan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Bo Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Chaojing and was from Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute student of the renzi year.
Liao Yunpeng, Instructor of the Confucian School of Ying Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zichong. His registered domicile was Houguan County [?], Fujian, and he was a native of Xingan County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute student of the renzi year.
Tang Ruli, Instructor of the Confucian School of Lingbi County, Su Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Sijing and was from Lanxi County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute student of the jiazi year.
Wang Shidao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Shiming and was from Wannian County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute student of the renzi year.
Zheng Hui, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yuan’an County, Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Zhongqing and was from Fuliang County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute student of the wuwu year.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭陳然〔少白湖廣沅陵縣人戊午貢士〕
浙江嘉興府嘉善縣儒學教諭陳文彬〔仲質廣西陸川縣人甲子貢士〕
印卷官
廣東等處承宣布政使司理問所副理問羅廷芳〔汝桂湖廣安鄉縣人監生〕
廣東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷程玠〔國信直隸休寧縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
南雄府知府林應節〔時卿福建莆田縣人巳未進士〕
潮州府知府侯必登〔叔良雲南廣南衛籍直隸上元縣人巳未進士〕
肇慶府知府熊俸〔德甫江西星子縣人丙辰進士〕
===
高州府知府吳國倫〔明卿湖廣興國州人庚戌進士〕
瓊州府知府周思久〔子徵湖廣麻城縣人癸丑進士〕
受卷官
韶州府同知熊曉〔達夫福建甌寧縣人壬子貢士〕
南雄府推官殷濡〔子霑直隸常熟縣人戊辰進士〕
惠州府長寧縣知縣趙鉞〔可度福建長汀縣人丙午貢士〕
肇慶府德慶州瀧水縣知縣譚文達〔時義廣西賓州人乙卯貢士〕
彌封官
廉州府同知江萬仞〔若度福建晉江縣人癸丑進士〕
punctuated:
江西南昌府南昌縣儒學教諭陳然〔少白，湖廣沅陵縣人，戊午貢士〕。浙江嘉興府嘉善縣儒學教諭陳文彬〔仲質，廣西陸川縣人，甲子貢士〕。

印卷官：廣東等處承宣布政使司理問所副理問羅廷芳〔汝桂，湖廣安鄉縣人，監生〕。廣東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷程玠〔國信，直隸休寧縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：南雄府知府林應節〔時卿，福建莆田縣人，巳未進士〕。潮州府知府侯必登〔叔良，雲南廣南衛籍，直隸上元縣人，巳未進士〕。肇慶府知府熊俸〔德甫，江西星子縣人，丙辰進士〕。高州府知府吳國倫〔明卿，湖廣興國州人，庚戌進士〕。瓊州府知府周思久〔子徵，湖廣麻城縣人，癸丑進士〕。

受卷官：韶州府同知熊曉〔達夫，福建甌寧縣人，壬子貢士〕。南雄府推官殷濡〔子霑，直隸常熟縣人，戊辰進士〕。惠州府長寧縣知縣趙鉞〔可度，福建長汀縣人，丙午貢士〕。肇慶府德慶州瀧水縣知縣譚文達〔時義，廣西賓州人，乙卯貢士〕。

彌封官：廉州府同知江萬仞〔若度，福建晉江縣人，癸丑進士〕。
translation_en:
Chen Ran, Instructor of the Confucian School of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Shaobai. He was from Yuanling County, Huguang, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the wuwu year.
Chen Wenbin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Zhongzhi. He was from Luchuan County, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

Hou Bideng, Prefect of Chaozhou, had the courtesy name Shuliang. He was registered in Guangnan Guard, Yunnan, and was originally from Shangyuan County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jiwei year [?; transcribed as 巳未].
Xiong Feng, Prefect of Zhaoqing, had the courtesy name Defu. He was from Xingzi County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.
Wu Guolun, Prefect of Gaozhou, had the courtesy name Mingqing. He was from Xingguo Subprefecture, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.
Zhou Sijiu, Prefect of Qiongzhou, had the courtesy name Zizheng. He was from Macheng County, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

Officials responsible for receiving examination scripts:
Xiong Xiao, Vice Prefect of Shaozhou, had the courtesy name Dafu. He was from Ouning County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the renzi year.
Yin Ru, Prefectural Judge of Nanxiong, had the courtesy name Zizhan. He was from Changshu County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.
Zhao Yue, Magistrate of Changning County, Huizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Kedu. He was from Changting County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the bingwu year.
Tan Wenda, Magistrate of Longshui County, Deqing Subprefecture, Zhaoqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shiyi. He was from Binzhou Subprefecture, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the yimao year.

Officials responsible for sealing candidates’ identifying information:
Jiang Wanren, Vice Prefect of Lianzhou, had the courtesy name Ruodu. He was from Jinjiang County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣州府連州知州徐美〔中夫福建邵武縣人壬子貢士〕
廣州府增城縣知縣張孔脩〔德成福建福寧州籍浙江餘姚縣人己酉貢士〕
謄錄官
潮州府同知陳學麟〔尚經福建懷安縣人戊午貢士〕
潮州府推官來經濟〔濟時浙江蕭山縣人戊辰進士〕
廣州府南海縣知縣蕭騰鳳〔明仲福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
廣州府東莞縣知縣張鏜〔汝敭江西永豐縣人戊辰進士〕
肇慶府四會縣知縣劉順之〔體信廣西馬平縣籍湖廣善化縣人壬子貢士〕
對讀官
===
廣州府推官王任重〔尹卿福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
肇慶府推官李時春〔元卿福建候官縣人乙卯貢士〕
惠州府博羅縣知縣顏容舒〔日莊福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
潮州府海陽縣知縣秦舜翰〔國宗福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
潮州府潮陽縣知縣黃一龍〔雲卿福建晉江縣人戊辰進士〕
巡綽官
廣州左衛指揮使趙陞〔惟選直隸灤州人〕
廣州右衛指揮同知王暹〔于明直隸無為州人〕
廣州右衛指揮僉事李田龍〔文見湖廣桂東縣人〕
punctuated:
廣州府連州知州徐美〔中夫，福建邵武縣人，壬子貢士〕。廣州府增城縣知縣張孔脩〔德成，福建福寧州籍，浙江餘姚縣人，己酉貢士〕。

謄錄官
潮州府同知陳學麟〔尚經，福建懷安縣人，戊午貢士〕。潮州府推官來經濟〔濟時，浙江蕭山縣人，戊辰進士〕。廣州府南海縣知縣蕭騰鳳〔明仲，福建晉江縣人，戊辰進士〕。廣州府東莞縣知縣張鏜〔汝敭，江西永豐縣人，戊辰進士〕。肇慶府四會縣知縣劉順之〔體信，廣西馬平縣籍，湖廣善化縣人，壬子貢士〕。

對讀官
廣州府推官王任重〔尹卿，福建晉江縣人，戊辰進士〕。肇慶府推官李時春〔元卿，福建候官縣人，乙卯貢士〕。惠州府博羅縣知縣顏容舒〔日莊，福建晉江縣人，戊辰進士〕。潮州府海陽縣知縣秦舜翰〔國宗，福建晉江縣人，戊辰進士〕。潮州府潮陽縣知縣黃一龍〔雲卿，福建晉江縣人，戊辰進士〕。

巡綽官
廣州左衛指揮使趙陞〔惟選，直隸灤州人〕。廣州右衛指揮同知王暹〔于明，直隸無為州人〕。廣州右衛指揮僉事李田龍〔文見，湖廣桂東縣人〕。
translation_en:

text:
