title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰性相近也習相遠也
所求乎子以事父未能也所求乎臣以事
君未能也
中天下而立定四海之民
易
聖人以順動則刑罰清而民服
天地節而四時成節以制度不傷財不害
===
民
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深也
故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成天下
之務唯神也故不疾而速不行而至
震東方也
書
九德咸事俊乂在官百僚師師百工惟時
撫于五辰庶績其凝
導岍及岐至于荊山逾于河壺口雷首至
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「性相近也，習相遠也。」

所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也。

中天下而立，定四海之民。

易

聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。

天地節而四時成；節以制度，不傷財，不害民。

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。

震，東方也。

書

九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

導岍及岐，至于荊山；逾于河，壺口、雷首，至
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “By nature, people are close to one another; through habitual practice, they grow far apart.”

What I require of a son, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my father; what I require of a minister, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my ruler.

To stand at the center of all under Heaven and bring stability to the people within the Four Seas.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

When the sage acts in accordance with what is right, punishments are just and clear, and the people submit.

Heaven and Earth observe their limits, and the four seasons take shape. Establish limits through institutions and regulations, without wasting wealth or harming the people.

The Changes is the means by which the sage plumbs the depths and investigates the first stirrings of events. Because it is profound, it can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven; because it grasps those first stirrings, it can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; because it is numinous, it is swift without haste and arrives without traveling.

Zhen, the Thunder trigram, represents the east.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

When those possessing the nine virtues are all employed and talented, capable men hold office, the many officials take one another as models, and the various officers attend to their duties at the proper times, bringing them into harmony with the five celestial seasons, all undertakings will attain fulfillment.

Trace the mountains from Qian and Qi as far as Mount Jing; cross the Yellow River to Hukou and Leishou, and reach …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于太岳底柱析城至于王屋太行恒山
至于碣石入于海
無偏無黨王道蕩蕩
一人有慶兆民賴之
詩
彼君子兮不素餐兮
南山有桑北山有楊樂只君子邦家之光
樂只君子萬壽無疆南山有杞北山有
李樂只君子民之父母樂只君子德音
===
不已
恒之秬秠是穫是畝恒之縻芑是任是負
方命厥后奄有九有
春秋
晉人敗狄于箕〔僖公三十有三年〕晉欒書
帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕
春王三月甲寅齊人伐衛〔莊公二十有八〕
〔年〕齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕
晉人宋人衛人曹人伐鄭〔宣公十年〕
punctuated:
于太岳、底柱、析城，至于王屋、太行、恒山，至于碣石，入于海。
無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩。
一人有慶，兆民賴之。

詩
彼君子兮，不素餐兮。
南山有桑，北山有楊。樂只君子，邦家之光。樂只君子，萬壽無疆。南山有杞，北山有李。樂只君子，民之父母。樂只君子，德音不已。
恒之秬秠，是穫是畝。恒之縻芑，是任是負。
方命厥后，奄有九有。

春秋
晉人敗狄于箕〔僖公三十有三年〕。晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。
春，王三月，甲寅，齊人伐衛〔莊公二十有八〕〔年〕。齊師、宋師、曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕。
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人伐鄭〔宣公十年〕。
translation_en:
…to Taiyue, Dizhu, and Xicheng, reaching Wangwu, Taihang, and Hengshan; then reaching Jieshi and entering the sea.
Without partiality or faction, the kingly Way is broad and open.
When the One Man enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them.

Book of Odes
That gentleman does not eat without earning his food.
On the southern mountain grow mulberries; on the northern mountain grow poplars. Joyful is the gentleman, the glory of the state and its ruling house. Joyful is the gentleman: may he live ten thousand years without end! On the southern mountain grows boxthorn; on the northern mountain grow plum trees. Joyful is the gentleman, father and mother of the people. Joyful is the gentleman: his virtuous fame never ceases.
The black millet and the double-grained black millet [?]: these are harvested, these are laid in the fields. The mi [?] and the white millet: these are carried in the arms, these are borne on the back.
Then he charged their sovereign to possess all the nine regions.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The men of Jin defeated the Di at Ji. 〔Thirty-third year of Duke Xi.〕 Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕
In spring, in the third month of the royal calendar, on the day jiayin, the men of Qi attacked Wei. 〔Twenty-eighth〕〔year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built walls around Xing. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕
The men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao attacked Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan.〕

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
八月戊辰同盟于馬陵〔成公七年〕
禮記
事君以自顯也
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節
使民有父之尊有母之親如此而后可以
為民父母矣
氣如白虹天也
第貳塲
論
===
人主制馭臣民之柄
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔〔甘〕
〔露三年〕
擬唐加裴度同平章事誥〔長慶四年〕
擬宋遣使分賑諸州羣臣謝表〔建隆元年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
轉解官物
punctuated:
八月戊辰，同盟于馬陵。〔成公七年〕

禮記
事君以自顯也。
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。
使民有父之尊，有母之親，如此而后可以為民父母矣。
氣如白虹，天也。

第貳塲
論
人主制馭臣民之柄。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢詔諸儒講五經異同於石渠閣詔。〔甘〕〔露三年〕
擬唐加裴度同平章事誥。〔長慶四年〕
擬宋遣使分賑諸州羣臣謝表。〔建隆元年〕

判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
轉解官物。
translation_en:
On the wuchen day of the eighth month, they entered into a joint covenant at Maling. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng〕

Book of Rites
“To serve one’s ruler is to make oneself illustrious.”
“Great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares their ordered measures.”
“Let the people find in one the dignity of a father and the affection of a mother; only then can one become the father and mother of the people.”
“Its vital essence resembles a white rainbow: this is Heaven.”

Second Session
Discourse
“The authority by which the ruler controls and governs his ministers and people.”

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question to be set from among these [?]〕
Compose, in the manner of the Han dynasty, an edict summoning the Confucian scholars to discuss similarities and differences among the Five Classics at the Shiqu Pavilion. 〔Third year of Ganlu〕
Compose, in the manner of the Tang dynasty, a proclamation appointing Pei Du as Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. 〔Fourth year of Changqing〕
Compose, in the manner of the Song dynasty, a memorial of thanks from the assembled ministers for the dispatch of envoys to distribute famine relief among the prefectures. 〔First year of Jianlong〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks.
Forwarding government goods.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禁止迎送
優恤軍屬
脩理倉庫
第叁塲
策五道
問書稱元良詩詠燕翼自古帝王所以爲
宗社萬世計至深遠也三代之盛不可
尚已然典則風愆與夫謨烈之垂班班
可考則盛治固有本矣我
===
太祖高皇帝誕膺
天命肇造區宇深惟
國本之重爰作
昭鑒錄以爲萬世
聖子
神孫法其大旨可得聞與嗣我
成祖文皇帝則有
聖學心法
宣宗章皇帝則有
punctuated:
禁止迎送。
優恤軍屬。
脩理倉庫。

第叁塲
策五道

問：書稱元良，詩詠燕翼，自古帝王所以爲宗社萬世計，至深遠也。三代之盛，不可尚已。然典則風愆，與夫謨烈之垂，班班可考，則盛治固有本矣。我太祖高皇帝誕膺天命，肇造區宇，深惟國本之重，爰作《昭鑒錄》，以爲萬世聖子神孫法。其大旨可得聞與？嗣我成祖文皇帝則有《聖學心法》，宣宗章皇帝則有
translation_en:
Prohibiting ceremonial receptions and send-offs.
Providing preferential relief for military dependents.
Repairing granaries and storehouses.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Documents speaks of the supremely worthy heir, and the Book of Odes sings of securing peace for descendants. Since antiquity, emperors and kings have thus planned for their ancestral temples and altars of state through ten thousand generations with the deepest foresight. The flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties cannot be surpassed. Yet their transmitted standards, admonitions against faults [?], counsels, and achievements can still be clearly examined: flourishing government assuredly had its foundations.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s mandate and founded the realm. Reflecting deeply on the importance of the foundation of the state, he thereupon composed the Record of the Illustrious Mirror (Zhaojian lu), to serve as a model for his sagely sons and divine grandsons through ten thousand generations. May we hear its essential meaning? Subsequently, our Emperor Chengzu Wen produced the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang produced …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
御製帝訓
憲宗純皇帝則有
文華大訓三書之旨不知於
昭鑒錄同與否與我
皇上盛德格
天
前星炳耀
東宮正位
睿知夙啓行且進講
===
宮廷述
祖宗之訓以資啓沃副
聖心其將奚先諸士咸懷忠愛之忱願悉陳之
將轉聞于
上
問帝王慎乃儉德非獨爲天下節財其爲
慮蓋遠也稽之唐虞夏商周如史臣所
紀典謨訓誥所載數聖人儉德先後一
揆至漢唐晉宋諸君有衣弋綈履革舄
punctuated:
《御製帝訓》；憲宗純皇帝則有《文華大訓》。三書之旨，不知於《昭鑒錄》同與否與？我皇上盛德格天，前星炳耀，東宮正位，睿知夙啓，行且進講宮廷，述祖宗之訓，以資啓沃，副聖心，其將奚先？諸士咸懷忠愛之忱，願悉陳之，將轉聞于上。
問：帝王慎乃儉德，非獨爲天下節財，其爲慮蓋遠也。稽之唐虞夏商周，如史臣所紀、典謨訓誥所載，數聖人儉德，先後一揆。至漢唐晉宋諸君，有衣弋綈、履革舄
translation_en:
…the Imperially Composed Instructions for Emperors (Yuzhi dixun); Emperor Xianzong Chun, in turn, produced the Grand Instructions of the Hall of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua daxun). Do the central teachings of these three books accord with those of the Record of Illustrious Admonitions (Zhaojian lu), or not? Our reigning emperor’s abundant virtue reaches Heaven. The Foremost Star—the crown prince—shines brightly; he occupies his rightful position in the Eastern Palace, and his sagely understanding has awakened early. Soon lectures will be delivered in the palace, expounding the ancestral emperors’ instructions to nourish his understanding and fulfill His Majesty’s wishes. What should take precedence? You gentlemen all cherish sincere loyalty and devotion. We ask you to set forth your views fully, so that they may be conveyed to His Majesty.
Question: When emperors and kings diligently cultivate the virtue of frugality, they do so not merely to conserve the realm’s wealth: their concerns extend much further. Examining the ages of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, we find that, according to the court historians’ records and the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, these several sages followed one consistent standard in their frugality, early and late alike. As for the rulers of Han, Tang, Jin, and Song, some wore dark, coarse silk [?] and leather shoes…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有詔恐妨農事害女紅者有身衣大練
色無重綵有身御澣服食無兼珍者有
焚裘焚錦於前殿者有碎七寶器有以
節儉試進士以民力戒嬪御者類以儉
名也孰優劣與洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
承帝王之統
敦儉德以爲天下先開
國之初屢卻珍獻鉅若金玉飾馬鞍鏤金牀
===
水晶漏細若香米蘄簟蒲萄酒不但毀
絕不受且
下令以爲戒而又
諭省臣以惜民力法子孫至意此豈與古帝王
有異較耶迨我
皇上中天撫運法
祖愛民
登極一詔行之信如四時諸生嘗伏誦之矣如
裁省光祿供億清汰
punctuated: 有詔恐妨農事、害女紅者，有身衣大練、色無重綵，有身御澣服、食無兼珍者，有焚裘焚錦於前殿者，有碎七寶器，有以節儉試進士、以民力戒嬪御者，類以儉名也。孰優劣與？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，承帝王之統，敦儉德以爲天下先。開國之初，屢卻珍獻，鉅若金玉飾馬鞍、鏤金牀、水晶漏，細若香米、蘄簟、蒲萄酒，不但毀絕不受，且下令以爲戒，而又諭省臣以惜民力、法子孫至意。此豈與古帝王有異較耶？迨我皇上中天撫運，法祖愛民，登極一詔，行之信如四時，諸生嘗伏誦之矣。如裁省光祿供億，清汰
translation_en:
…There were those whose edicts expressed concern lest farming be disrupted and women’s textile work impaired; those who wore coarse silk, with no layers of richly colored fabric; those who wore washed garments and ate without an array of delicacies; those who burned fur robes and brocades before the front hall; those who smashed vessels made of the seven precious substances; and those who examined candidates for metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status on frugality and admonished their consorts and palace women to spare the people’s labor. All were generally renowned for frugality. Which were superior, and which inferior?
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Taizu Gao, who inherited the succession of emperors and kings and cultivated the virtue of frugality as an example to all under Heaven. At the founding of the dynasty, he repeatedly rejected precious offerings: great objects such as saddles ornamented with gold and jade, beds with carved gold decoration, and crystal clepsydras; small things such as fragrant rice, bamboo mats from Qi, and grape wine. He not only destroyed or prohibited these things and refused to accept them, but also issued orders making them a warning. Moreover, he instructed the officials of the Secretariat in his profound intention to spare the people’s labor and set a model for his descendants. Could this admit of any different assessment from that of the ancient emperors and kings [?]?
Now our Emperor has assumed Heaven’s mandate at the meridian of dynastic fortune, emulating his ancestor and cherishing the people. His accession edict has been implemented with the constancy of the four seasons; you students have reverently read it. Examples include reducing the provisions supplied by the Court of Imperial Entertainments and eliminating…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
內府諸需至於珠寶香蠟之役一切罷之以
蘇民困且
諭部臣曰朕加意節省用自有餘猗歟此即典
謨訓誥文也
媲美唐虞同符
聖祖
社稷生靈抑何幸耶諸生博古憲
今其將殫述而榆揚之毋忽
問書曰在知人在安民知人固所以安民
===
===
也又曰知人則哲惟帝其難之則人才
難得亦難知矣然晏元獻之判西京也
與范希文論人一問答而萃四相張忠
定之守金陵也一諮詢而得二子皆當
時之儁則人才之得亦不難與房杜微
時曾靡尺寸之豎而司銓衡者預以公
輔期之盧駱王楊文藝燁燁一時而占
器識者已逆覩其後焉則知人之鑑顧
亦易與彼慨人之難知至有江海浮雲
punctuated:
內府諸需，至於珠寶香蠟之役，一切罷之，以蘇民困。且諭部臣曰：「朕加意節省，用自有餘。」猗歟！此即典謨訓誥文也。媲美唐虞，同符聖祖，社稷生靈抑何幸耶！諸生博古憲今，其將殫述而榆揚之，毋忽！

問：書曰：「在知人，在安民。」知人固所以安民也。又曰：「知人則哲，惟帝其難之。」則人才難得，亦難知矣。然晏元獻之判西京也，與范希文論人，一問答而萃四相；張忠定之守金陵也，一諮詢而得二子，皆當時之儁。則人才之得亦不難與？房杜微時，曾靡尺寸之豎，而司銓衡者預以公輔期之；盧駱王楊，文藝燁燁一時，而占器識者已逆覩其後焉。則知人之鑑，顧亦易與？彼慨人之難知，至有江海浮雲
translation_en:
…the various requirements of the Inner Palace; as for the exactions for pearls, precious stones, incense, and wax, he abolished them all to relieve the people's distress. Moreover, he instructed the ministry officials: “I am giving particular attention to economy; there will naturally be more than enough for expenditure.” Ah! These are words worthy of the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements in the Book of Documents. Matching the beauty of the reigns of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, and conforming to the example of the sagely ancestor—how fortunate are the state and its people! You students, versed in antiquity and taking the present as your model, should set this forth fully and extol it [?]. Do not be remiss!

Question: The Book of Documents says: “It lies in knowing men and in bringing peace to the people.” Knowing men is indeed the means of bringing peace to the people. It also says: “To know men is wisdom; even the emperor found this difficult.” Thus, talented men are hard to obtain and also hard to recognize. Yet when Yan Yuanxian administered the Western Capital, he discussed men with Fan Xiwen, and a single exchange of question and answer brought together four future chief councilors. When Zhang Zhongding governed Jinling, a single inquiry brought him two men, both outstanding talents of their time. Was obtaining talented men therefore not difficult after all? When Fang and Du were still obscure, they had not yet established even the slightest achievement [?], yet the official responsible for personnel selection already expected them to become chief ministers. Lu, Luo, Wang, and Yang shone brilliantly in the literary arts in their day, yet those who assessed their capacity and judgment had already foreseen their subsequent fortunes. Was discerning men's worth, then, actually easy? Why did those who lamented the difficulty of knowing men go so far as to invoke rivers, seas, and floating clouds…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之喻抑又何也方今
聖明御極思得才賢以乂安斯民意甚殷也天
下士懷瑾握瑜雲蒸風會然用輒乏才
至廑
當宁知人之慮何與夫知之眞而後用之不謬
不知知人果有其術與古有所謂五視
九徴之法亦可采而行之與大學衍義
所以辨人才者悉矣可得聞其要與爲
政在人誠切務也故以質之多士
===
問人有恒言聖本生知無事于學乃孔子
大聖人也其自謂曰我非生而知之者
好古敏以求之者也又曰我學不厭豈
孔子之上復有所謂生知者乎抑其學
固與人異也夫學之益人自昔然矣故
佩豭之子解利劒而升堂築埋之兒聞
斷機而學孔不謁執政者固曾欲更經
利舉之人冠冕南州者其進在驚汗浹
背之後藉令此四子者安其故習罔典
punctuated:
之喻，抑又何也？方今聖明御極，思得才賢以乂安斯民，意甚殷也。天下士懷瑾握瑜，雲蒸風會，然用輒乏才，至廑當宁知人之慮，何與？夫知之眞而後用之不謬，不知知人果有其術與？古有所謂五視九徴之法，亦可采而行之與？大學衍義所以辨人才者悉矣，可得聞其要與？爲政在人，誠切務也，故以質之多士。

問：人有恒言，聖本生知，無事于學。乃孔子大聖人也，其自謂曰：「我非生而知之者，好古，敏以求之者也。」又曰：「我學不厭。」豈孔子之上復有所謂生知者乎？抑其學固與人異也？夫學之益人，自昔然矣。故佩豭之子解利劒而升堂，築埋之兒聞斷機而學孔。不謁執政者，固曾欲更經利舉之人；冠冕南州者，其進在驚汗浹背之後。藉令此四子者安其故習，罔典
translation_en:
…the comparison to rivers, seas, and floating clouds—why, then, was this made? Now that our sagely and enlightened sovereign occupies the throne, his desire to obtain talented and worthy men to govern and bring peace to the people is most earnest. Scholars throughout the realm cherish jade-like virtues, gathering like rising clouds and converging winds. Yet whenever men must be employed, talent is lacking, to the point of troubling the sovereign with concern over how to discern men. Why is this? Only after men are truly understood can they be employed without error. Is there indeed a method for discerning men? Might the ancient methods called the Five Observations and Nine Tests also be adopted and put into practice? The Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) treats the discernment of talent comprehensively. May we hear its essentials? Government depends upon obtaining the right men: this is truly an urgent concern. We therefore put these questions to you assembled scholars.

Question: People commonly say that sages are born with knowledge and have no need of learning. Yet Confucius was a great sage, and he said of himself: “I am not one who was born with knowledge; I love antiquity and diligently seek it.” He also said: “I am tireless in learning.” Could there be others above Confucius who possess what is called innate knowledge? Or was his learning fundamentally different from that of others? Learning has benefited people since ancient times. Thus the youth who wore a boar ornament unbuckled his sharp sword and ascended the hall to receive instruction; the child who played at making graves [?], upon hearing the lesson of the severed weaving, studied Confucius. The man who would not pay a visit to those wielding governmental power had once wished to change the Classic he studied to improve his prospects in the examinations; the man preeminent among the scholars of the southern region made his advance only after a shock that drenched his back in sweat. Suppose these four men had remained content with their former habits and paid no heed …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于學其終身所就能至此否耶又有自
謂做人不倚師友載籍者有所見一定
不須窮索人稱其為天資出人非假學
力者皆若於生知似矣而一則不免於
禪學之疑一則坐蒙乎晚出之詬此又
何耶夫學人也不學而知天也天人之
際非知道者孰能一之二三子儻有達
於此者乎其以所自有者商之毋勦昔
人已吐之語
===
問寇賊姦宄蠻夷猾夏古盛世亦不免者
東粵之寇有猺黎倭醜及巢浪諸種類
不一彌竟山海出沒不時其所從來舊
矣畫計者曰勦與撫大都不越此兩者
然鐃歌甫畢而羽檄復馳納款未幾而
嘯聚旋熾豈制禦之術此兩者猶不足
以盡之而別有其說與或謂禦山寇易
禦海寇難蓋謂其雲帆風浪蹤跡飄忽
欲繫而殪之難也乃今舍其檣楫執梃
punctuated:
于學，其終身所就能至此否耶？又有自謂做人不倚師友載籍者，有所見一定不須窮索、人稱其為天資出人非假學力者，皆若於生知似矣。而一則不免於禪學之疑，一則坐蒙乎晚出之詬，此又何耶？夫學，人也；不學而知，天也。天人之際，非知道者孰能一之？二三子儻有達於此者乎？其以所自有者商之，毋勦昔人已吐之語。

問：寇賊姦宄，蠻夷猾夏，古盛世亦不免者。東粵之寇，有猺黎倭醜及巢浪諸種，類不一，彌竟山海，出沒不時，其所從來舊矣。畫計者曰勦與撫，大都不越此兩者。然鐃歌甫畢，而羽檄復馳；納款未幾，而嘯聚旋熾。豈制禦之術，此兩者猶不足以盡之，而別有其說與？或謂禦山寇易，禦海寇難，蓋謂其雲帆風浪，蹤跡飄忽，欲繫而殪之難也。乃今舍其檣楫，執梃
translation_en:
…in learning, could their lifetime accomplishments have reached such heights? There are also those who claim that in conducting themselves they rely on neither teachers and friends nor written works, and those whose views, once fixed, require no further searching, whom people praise as naturally endowed beyond others, without recourse to the effort of learning. All seem to resemble those born with knowledge. Yet one cannot escape the suspicion of practicing Chan learning, while another incurs the reproach of having emerged late. Why is this? Learning belongs to the human; knowing without learning belongs to Heaven. At the juncture of Heaven and humanity, who but one who understands the Way can unite them? Might any of you gentlemen have attained an understanding of this? Discuss it on the basis of your own understanding; do not plagiarize words already uttered by earlier men.

Question: Bandits, robbers, and evildoers, and the disturbance of the Chinese realm by the Man and Yi peoples, were things that even the flourishing ages of antiquity could not avoid. Among the raiders of eastern Yue are the Yao, the Li, the villainous Wo, and the various groups called Chao and Lang [?]. They are of many kinds, ranging throughout the mountains and seas, appearing and disappearing at unpredictable times. Their presence has a long history. Those who devise plans speak of extermination and pacification; their proposals generally go no further than these two approaches. Yet scarcely have the victory songs ended when urgent military dispatches speed forth again; not long after submission has been offered, bands gather once more and their activity intensifies. Could it be that these two approaches do not exhaust the arts of control and defense, and that there is some other doctrine? Some say that defending against mountain bandits is easy, but defending against sea raiders is difficult. Presumably they mean that, with sails towering into the clouds amid wind and waves, their movements are elusive, making it difficult to capture and kill them. But now they abandon their masts and oars and take up clubs…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
刃而與山寇竝訌則山與海何別而計
又將安施耶又謂黎𤢜盤流卒難盡殲
當先拔其苞孽如治病先腹心而後手
足其說似矣然刋山通道之謀費重而
難舉土舍招主之設詭譎而難憑腹心
手足總之為病則所以治之者又當孰
先後也夫士明於當世之務者然後可
與言經濟矧二三子生長海邦恫瘝乆
矣其以嘉謨相告當事者將采而行之
punctuated: 刃而與山寇竝訌，則山與海何別，而計又將安施耶？又謂黎𤢜盤流，卒難盡殲，當先拔其苞孽，如治病先腹心而後手足，其說似矣。然刋山通道之謀，費重而難舉；土舍招主之設，詭譎而難憑。腹心手足，總之為病，則所以治之者，又當孰先後也？夫士明於當世之務者，然後可與言經濟。矧二三子生長海邦，恫瘝乆矣，其以嘉謨相告，當事者將采而行之。
translation_en:
…and blades, joining the mountain bandits in rebellion, then what distinction remains between mountain and maritime bandits, and what strategy should now be applied? It is also said that the Li and other groups [?] cannot, in the end, be wholly annihilated, and that their roots should first be uprooted, just as one treats illness first in the vital organs and afterward in the limbs. This argument seems plausible. Yet the plan to cut through the mountains and open roads is costly and difficult to undertake; the arrangement involving sons of native officials and recruiting headmen [?] is fraught with deception and difficult to rely upon. Whether in the vital organs or the limbs, it is all illness: in treating it, then, which should come first and which afterward?
Only with scholars who understand the affairs of the present age can one discuss statecraft. You gentlemen, moreover, were born and raised in this coastal region and have long felt its suffering. Offer your sound counsels; those responsible for these affairs will adopt and implement them.

punctuated:
中式舉人七十五名。

translation_en:
Seventy-five successful candidates awarded provincial graduate (juren) status.

First: Huo Zhendong, a student of the Nanhai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Second: Jin Jie, an expanded-quota student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Third: Xu Zanhua, an attached student of the Dongguan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Fourth: Xu An, a student of the Chaozhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Fifth: Chen Xuan, an attached student of the Dongguan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.
Sixth: Lin Yingxiang, a student of the Huizhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Seventh: Liang Feng, a student of the Maoming County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Eighth: Zhou Dufei, a student of the Chaozhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Ninth: Xian Guifang, an attached student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Tenth: Wu Yue, an attached student of the Nanhai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Eleventh: Feng Rui, an attached student of the Panyu County School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Twelfth: Huang Guang, an expanded-quota student of the Huizhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Thirteenth: Xian Siqian, an attached student of the Guangzhou Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Fourteenth: Yao Yuexiang, a student of the Huazhou Subprefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Fifteenth: Shen Xijie, a student of the Chenghai County School. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Sixteenth: Xiong Chengliang, an attached student of the Dongguan County School. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰性相近也習相遠也
霍鎮東
同考試官教諭王批性字場中作者率欠體
認是篇發明眞切蓋甞究心性學者
考試官教諭萬批見理精深措辭醇雅
考試官教授鄒批體認精確
聖人原性之初而究其所由異焉夫性之相近
===
者其初也至有相遠則由於習耳而豈性之有
異乎夫子欲人自識其初言此若曰天下之論
性者惟因其所習之異遂以性為相遠矣曷自
其初而觀之夫性也者帝降之衷盡夫人而各
正民秉之彝隨所賦而惟均雖其秉夫氣者有
清濁之不同矣然稟氣之初其天精未汩也蓋
不過統同中之小異耳雖其麗夫質者有厚薄
之不一矣然凝質之初其天粹未漓也蓋不過
合一中之少間耳但形生之後而命於天者不
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「性相近也，習相遠也。」
霍鎮東

同考試官教諭王批：「性字，場中作者率欠體認。是篇發明眞切，蓋甞究心性學者。」
考試官教諭萬批：「見理精深，措辭醇雅。」
考試官教授鄒批：「體認精確。」

聖人原性之初，而究其所由異焉。夫性之相近者，其初也；至有相遠，則由於習耳，而豈性之有異乎？夫子欲人自識其初，言此若曰：「天下之論性者，惟因其所習之異，遂以性為相遠矣。曷自其初而觀之？夫性也者，帝降之衷，盡夫人而各正；民秉之彝，隨所賦而惟均。雖其秉夫氣者有清濁之不同矣，然稟氣之初，其天精未汩也，蓋不過統同中之小異耳。雖其麗夫質者有厚薄之不一矣，然凝質之初，其天粹未漓也，蓋不過合一中之少間耳。但形生之後，而命於天者不
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
The Master said: “By nature, people are close to one another; through habituation, they become far apart.”
Huo Zhendong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “On the word ‘nature,’ writers in this examination generally lack a true understanding. This essay elucidates it truly and precisely; its author has evidently devoted himself to the study of human nature.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “His understanding of principle is refined and profound; his wording, pure and elegant.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “His understanding is precise and accurate.”

The sage traced human nature to its beginnings and investigated how differences arise. That people are close in nature pertains to their beginnings. When they come to be far apart, this results only from habituation: how could it be that their natures differ? The Master wished people to recognize their own original condition. His words were as if to say: “Those throughout the world who discuss human nature see only differences in acquired habits and consequently regard people’s natures as far apart. Why not examine nature from its beginnings? Nature is the inner norm bestowed by the Lord on High, correct in each and every person; it is the constant standard held by the people, equally present in each according to their endowment. Although the vital force they receive differs in clarity and turbidity, at the moment of its reception their heavenly essence has not yet been muddied. These are merely small differences within an overall sameness. Although the physical constitution to which their nature adheres varies in substantiality and thinness, when that constitution first takes shape, its heavenly purity has not yet been diluted. These are merely slight divergences within an underlying unity. Yet after bodily form comes into being, what is ordained by Heaven cannot…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
能不間之以人神發之餘而成於人者不能盡
全乎其天或習於善焉則與善同歸不惟清與
厚者然也即氣質之不美者亦可日進于高明
而其去夫惡也于是乎頓殊矣或習於惡焉則
與惡同歸不惟濁與薄者然也即氣質之美者
亦將日流於汙下而其去夫善也于是乎迥別
矣要之原其始之所賦可以分數言不可以等
級論也于此而善反之則天地之性存焉而容
可以自諉乎究其終之所異乃習之使然非天
===
之降才爾殊也于此而不善反之則所以異於
禽獸者幾希而容可以弗愼乎吁觀于夫子之
言則知人之欲盡性者誠不可不端所習矣抑
聞氣質之用小學問之功大則欲端所習者又
存乎學也奈何後世性學不明而杞柳湍水紛
紛異議非孟子力倡性善之旨辭而闢之則夫
子立言之意湮矣故曰孟氏有功聖門
所求乎子以事父未能也所求乎臣以事
君未能也
punctuated:
能不間之以人，神發之餘，而成於人者不能盡全乎其天。或習於善焉，則與善同歸，不惟清與厚者然也，即氣質之不美者亦可日進于高明，而其去夫惡也，于是乎頓殊矣。或習於惡焉，則與惡同歸，不惟濁與薄者然也，即氣質之美者亦將日流於汙下，而其去夫善也，于是乎迥別矣。要之，原其始之所賦，可以分數言，不可以等級論也。于此而善反之，則天地之性存焉，而容可以自諉乎？究其終之所異，乃習之使然，非天之降才爾殊也。于此而不善反之，則所以異於禽獸者幾希，而容可以弗愼乎？吁！觀于夫子之言，則知人之欲盡性者，誠不可不端所習矣。抑聞氣質之用小，學問之功大，則欲端所習者，又存乎學也。奈何後世性學不明，而杞柳、湍水紛紛異議？非孟子力倡性善之旨，辭而闢之，則夫子立言之意湮矣。故曰：孟氏有功聖門。

所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也。
translation_en:
…cannot remain free from the intrusion of human influences; once the spirit has become active, what takes shape in the human realm cannot wholly preserve its heavenly endowment. If people become accustomed to goodness, they come to accord with goodness. This is true not only of those whose vital force is clear and whose constitution is substantial: even those whose disposition is unfavorable can advance daily toward loftiness and illumination, thereby distancing themselves decisively from evil. If people become accustomed to evil, they come to accord with evil. This is true not only of those whose vital force is turbid and whose constitution is insubstantial: even those whose disposition is favorable will daily sink toward baseness, thereby becoming utterly estranged from goodness.

In essence, if we trace what people were endowed with at the outset, we may speak of differences in proportion, but cannot rank them in grades. If one successfully returns to this original endowment, the nature bestowed by Heaven and Earth is preserved. How, then, could one make excuses for oneself? If we investigate the differences that ultimately arise, it is habituation that produces them; it is not that Heaven bestowed capacities so disparate. If one fails to return to the original endowment, little remains to distinguish one from birds and beasts. How, then, could one fail to be vigilant?

Ah! Considering the Master's words, we understand that those who wish to realize their nature fully must indeed set their habits right. I have also heard that the influence of one's native disposition is small, while the efficacy of learning is great. Thus, setting one's habits right depends in turn upon learning. Why was the study of human nature unclear in later generations, with conflicting arguments about willow wood and swirling water proliferating? Had Mengzi not vigorously championed the teaching that human nature is good, refuting and rejecting those arguments, the intention behind the Master's pronouncement would have been obscured. Thus it is said: Mengzi rendered a great service to the sage's school.

“What I require of a son, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my father; what I require of a minister, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my ruler.”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
金節
同考試官學正林批發揮聖人自責之意最
為婉切宜錄之以式多士
考試官教諭萬批辭不繁而意自縝密
考試官教授鄒批簡潔可嘉
聖人責人以子臣之道而以之自責焉甚矣聖
人人道之極也而自責者不外乎子臣之倫道
之不遠人也可見矣昔中庸引夫子之言以明
道也若曰學以盡倫為先倫以君親為大丘竊
===
有志焉而未之逮也是故子之事父天之性也
吾固謂不可解於其心而求人以為子之翼矣
然而吾之所以事父亦人之所以為子也反之
於已其能如其所求乎蓋親之恩罔極而人子
之孝養為無方苟一毫之未盡即子道之有虧
皇皇焉惟懼其忝爾所生此吾之所以明發有
懷也敢曰能之而姑以自恕哉臣之事君天之
制也吾固謂無所逃於其分而求人以為臣之
共矣然而吾之所以事君亦人之所以為臣也
punctuated:
金節

同考試官學正林批：發揮聖人自責之意，最為婉切，宜錄之以式多士。
考試官教諭萬批：辭不繁而意自縝密。
考試官教授鄒批：簡潔可嘉。

聖人責人以子臣之道，而以之自責焉。甚矣！聖人人道之極也，而自責者不外乎子臣之倫，道之不遠人也可見矣。昔《中庸》引夫子之言以明道也，若曰：「學以盡倫為先，倫以君親為大。丘竊有志焉，而未之逮也。是故子之事父，天之性也。吾固謂不可解於其心，而求人以為子之翼矣。然而吾之所以事父，亦人之所以為子也。反之於已，其能如其所求乎？蓋親之恩罔極，而人子之孝養為無方。苟一毫之未盡，即子道之有虧。皇皇焉，惟懼其忝爾所生，此吾之所以明發有懷也。敢曰能之，而姑以自恕哉？臣之事君，天之制也。吾固謂無所逃於其分，而求人以為臣之共矣。然而吾之所以事君，亦人之所以為臣也。
translation_en:
Jin Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor: His exposition of the sage’s self-reproach is especially tactful and incisive. This should be recorded as a model for the many scholars.
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: The language is economical, yet the thought is meticulous.
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: Commendably concise and clear.

The sage holds others accountable to the Way of the son and the minister, and holds himself accountable by the same standard. How exacting he is! The sage is the highest embodiment of the human Way, yet his self-reproach concerns nothing beyond the relationships of son and minister. We can thus see that the Way is not remote from human beings. The Doctrine of the Mean once quoted the Master’s words to illuminate the Way, as though he were saying: “In learning, fulfilling one’s human relationships comes first; among these relationships, those with ruler and parents are paramount. I, Qiu, privately aspire to this, but have not attained it. Thus, a son’s service to his father is a Heaven-given disposition. I have always maintained that he must not grow lax at heart, and have required of others the attentive care proper to a son. Yet the standard by which I serve my father is also the standard by which others act as sons. Turning back to examine myself, can I measure up to what I demand? A parent’s kindness is boundless, and a son’s filial care knows no fixed limits. If even the slightest part remains unfulfilled, the Way of the son is thereby impaired. Anxiously fearing only that I may disgrace those who gave me birth, I remain full of concern when dawn breaks. How could I dare claim to have fulfilled it and thereby indulge myself with excuses? A minister’s service to his ruler is an ordinance of Heaven. I have always maintained that there is no escaping the obligations of his station, and have required of others the reverence proper to a minister. Yet the standard by which I serve my ruler is also the standard by which others act as ministers. …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
反之於已其能如其所求乎蓋君之尊如天而
人臣之忠愛爲無已茍一毫之未盡卽臣節之
未純皇皇焉惟恐其上負吾君此吾之所以夙
夜匪懈也敢曰能之而容以自諉哉是則子道
也臣道也不遠於人也而以此責人自責夫豈
遠人以爲道哉雖然聖人亦非心以爲能而故
爲是退託也蓋臣子之心無窮雖忠孝之至亦
不過其當爲之分耳自昔稱忠孝莫盛於舜與
周公然一則夔夔齋慄一則公孫碩膚與夫子
===
未能之心一也若自以爲已足則豈聖人之心
哉
中天下而立定四海之民
徐賛化
同考試官教諭唐 批 格局正大辭氣明整可
以觀所養矣敬羨敬美
考試官教諭萬 批 辭健氣渾迥異衆作
考試官教授鄒 批 醇正典雅
觀君子一統之治而道之大行可知矣夫君子
punctuated:
反之於已，其能如其所求乎？蓋君之尊如天，而人臣之忠愛爲無已，茍一毫之未盡，卽臣節之未純，皇皇焉惟恐其上負吾君，此吾之所以夙夜匪懈也。敢曰能之，而容以自諉哉？是則子道也，臣道也，不遠於人也，而以此責人自責，夫豈遠人以爲道哉？雖然，聖人亦非心以爲能，而故爲是退託也。蓋臣子之心無窮，雖忠孝之至，亦不過其當爲之分耳。自昔稱忠孝，莫盛於舜與周公，然一則夔夔齋慄，一則公孫碩膚，與夫子未能之心一也。若自以爲已足，則豈聖人之心哉？

中天下而立，定四海之民。
徐賛化

同考試官教諭唐批：格局正大，辭氣明整，可以觀所養矣。敬羨敬美。
考試官教諭萬批：辭健氣渾，迥異衆作。
考試官教授鄒批：醇正典雅。

觀君子一統之治，而道之大行可知矣。夫君子
translation_en:
…Turning this back upon oneself, can one meet the demands one makes of others? The ruler is as exalted as Heaven, and a subject’s loyalty and love admit of no end. If even the slightest measure remains unfulfilled, the subject’s integrity is not yet pure. Anxiously fearing only that I might fail my ruler above, I remain diligent morning and night. Dare I claim to have achieved this and allow myself an excuse? Thus the way of the son and the way of the subject are not far from human beings. To use these standards to hold both others and oneself accountable—how could this be to seek the Way far from human beings? Nevertheless, the sage does not inwardly consider himself fully capable and then deliberately profess inadequacy out of modesty. The devotion of a subject or a son has no limit: even the utmost loyalty and filial piety do no more than fulfill one’s proper duty. From antiquity, none have been more celebrated for loyalty and filial piety than Shun and the Duke of Zhou. Yet the one was reverently watchful and fearful, and the other humble despite his great achievements. Their disposition was identical to the Master’s sense that he had not yet attained these virtues. If one considered oneself already sufficient, how could that be the mind of a sage?

“To stand at the center of all under Heaven and bring stability to the people within the Four Seas.”
By Xu Zanhua.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor: “The structure is upright and broad in scope; the language and tone are clear and orderly. From these one can discern his cultivation. I respectfully admire and commend it.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The language is vigorous and its spirit full and integrated, markedly different from the other compositions.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Pure and correct, dignified and elegant.”

By observing the gentleman’s unified governance, one can recognize the widespread realization of the Way. Now, the gentleman…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以天下爲度者也中天下而定四海則一統之
治在是矣不可以見道之大行也哉昔孟子論
性而先之以此曰君子之欲行其道者心也而
所賴以得行其道者勢也廣土衆民勢固可資
而不猶有所限乎玆焉體元凝命而居中以君
臨乎萬邦嚮明出治而宅中以宰制乎六合中
國之要樞于是乎握也而又安之澤有以弘敷
而不匱天下之根本于是乎植也而撫綏之仁
有以廣運而無方中天下而爲紀法之宗盡一
===
世而帲冒之而凡四海之待命於我者胥此焉
定其分矣中天下而爲綱常之主盡一世而甄
陶之而凡四海之取則於我者胥此焉定其性
矣斯蓋語其統御之大則極天所覆也極地所
載也而聯屬天下以成其身矣廣土云乎哉語
其德業之隆則覆之如天焉載之如地焉而以
萬物得所爲極致矣衆民云乎哉吁觀於君子
之所樂在此其視夫所欲者誠有間矣雖然所
謂君子之樂之者非徒以是爲榮也蓋一夫不
punctuated: 以天下爲度者也。中天下而定四海，則一統之治在是矣，不可以見道之大行也哉？昔孟子論性而先之以此，曰：「君子之欲行其道者，心也；而所賴以得行其道者，勢也。廣土衆民，勢固可資，而不猶有所限乎？玆焉體元凝命，而居中以君臨乎萬邦；嚮明出治，而宅中以宰制乎六合。中國之要樞于是乎握也，而又安之澤有以弘敷而不匱；天下之根本于是乎植也，而撫綏之仁有以廣運而無方。中天下而爲紀法之宗，盡一世而帲冒之，而凡四海之待命於我者，胥此焉定其分矣。中天下而爲綱常之主，盡一世而甄陶之，而凡四海之取則於我者，胥此焉定其性矣。斯蓋語其統御之大，則極天所覆也，極地所載也，而聯屬天下以成其身矣，廣土云乎哉？語其德業之隆，則覆之如天焉，載之如地焉，而以萬物得所爲極致矣，衆民云乎哉？吁！觀於君子之所樂在此，其視夫所欲者誠有間矣。雖然，所謂君子之樂之者，非徒以是爲榮也。蓋一夫不
translation_en: …takes all under Heaven as his measure. To stand at the center of all under Heaven and bring stability to the people within the Four Seas: herein lies unified government. Does this not reveal the Way being practiced far and wide? Formerly, when Mengzi discussed human nature, he prefaced it with this, saying: “What makes the gentleman wish to put his Way into practice is his heart; what enables him to do so is his position of power. Extensive territory and a numerous people certainly provide power on which he may draw, yet does this not still have its limits? Here, embodying the primal principle and securing Heaven’s mandate, he occupies the center and rules over the myriad states; facing the light and issuing his governance, he dwells at the center and governs the six directions. Thus he grasps the vital pivot of the Central Realm, while the blessings of bringing peace spread abundantly and inexhaustibly. Thus the foundation of all under Heaven is established, while his benevolence in comforting and pacifying extends everywhere without limit. Standing at the center of all under Heaven as the source of order and law, he shelters the entire age; all within the Four Seas who await his commands thereby have their respective stations settled. Standing at the center of all under Heaven as the master of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues, he molds and nurtures the entire age; all within the Four Seas who take him as their model thereby have their natures settled. Speaking of the breadth of his rule, it reaches as far as Heaven covers and Earth supports, joining all under Heaven into a single body. Can this be described merely as extensive territory? Speaking of the grandeur of his virtue and achievements, he shelters like Heaven and supports like Earth, taking as his highest attainment that all things find their proper place. Can this be described merely as a numerous people? Ah! Seeing that this is what the gentleman delights in, there is indeed a distinction between it and what he desires. Nevertheless, when we speak of the gentleman delighting in this, it is not simply that he regards it as an honor. For if even one man does not…”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
獲猶曰時予之辜而道旣大行君子之心始慰
矣不然堯舜事業亦漠然無所與耳寧足以動
其心耶故大行窮居必處之一而後見君子所
性之蘊
易
聖人以順動則刑罰清而民服
徐賛化
同考試官教諭陳批豫道不外順動此作就
豫上發揮精密典雅點民服尤有關鍵宜冠本房
===
考試官教諭萬批發上下和樂意明雅
考試官教授鄒批發豫道明悉
聖人以豫道治天下而大順之化成焉蓋順而
動豫道也聖人以此為治而天下有不順應之
者乎此見豫之道大也且豫以和樂為義而以
順動為德推其極天地旣不能外之以運化矣
聖人之治天下何如哉蓋其心與理涵而本之
為和順之積故其動與理俱而達之為至順之
猷以總萬幾非一無所為也然皆隨感而順應
punctuated:
獲，猶曰「時予之辜」，而道旣大行，君子之心始慰矣。不然，堯舜事業亦漠然無所與耳，寧足以動其心耶？故大行窮居，必處之一，而後見君子所性之蘊。

易
聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。
徐賛化

同考試官教諭陳批：豫道不外順動，此作就豫上發揮，精密典雅，點民服尤有關鍵，宜冠本房。
考試官教諭萬批：發上下和樂意，明雅。
考試官教授鄒批：發豫道明悉。

聖人以豫道治天下，而大順之化成焉。蓋順而動，豫道也。聖人以此為治，而天下有不順應之者乎？此見豫之道大也。且豫以和樂為義，而以順動為德。推其極，天地旣不能外之以運化矣，聖人之治天下何如哉？蓋其心與理涵，而本之為和順之積，故其動與理俱，而達之為至順之猷。以總萬幾，非一無所為也，然皆隨感而順應
translation_en:
…fails to find his proper place, he still says, “This is my fault”; only when the Way prevails widely does the gentleman’s heart find comfort. Otherwise, even the achievements of Yao and Shun would leave him indifferent, as though they had nothing to do with him. How could they suffice to move his heart? Thus, whether his Way prevails widely or he lives in straitened circumstances, he must regard both alike; only then can the depths of what the gentleman possesses by nature be seen.

Book of Changes
“When the sage acts in accordance with what is right, punishments become clear and the people submit.”
Xu Zanhua 徐賛化

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The Way of Yu (Contentment) consists entirely in acting in accordance with what is right. This composition develops its argument from Yu with precision, refinement, and classical elegance. Its treatment of “the people submit” is especially telling. It should rank first in this examining room.
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: It develops the idea of harmony and joy between those above and below with clarity and elegance.
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: It expounds the Way of Yu clearly and fully.

The sage governs All-under-Heaven through the Way of Yu, and thereby brings to fulfillment a transforming influence of perfect accord. For acting in accordance with what is right is the Way of Yu. When the sage governs by this means, is there anyone under Heaven who does not respond in accord? Here we see the greatness of the Way of Yu. Moreover, Yu has harmony and joy as its meaning, and action in accord with what is right as its virtue. Pushed to its fullest extent, even Heaven and Earth cannot operate and transform outside it. How, then, does the sage govern All-under-Heaven? His heart is steeped in principle, establishing an accumulated harmony and accord as its foundation. Thus his actions accompany principle, extending it into plans of perfect accord. In overseeing the myriad affairs of government, he is by no means wholly inactive; rather, in every case he responds in accord to whatever moves him…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之聖人之所爲固人心之所欲爲者也而一毫
私智不存焉以裁庶務非一無所事也然皆因
勢而利導之聖人之有事乃天下之所恃以無
事者也而一毫已意不與焉夫如是吾知順動
之德旣參諸天地而不違則和樂之情自通乎
上下而無間國有五刑將以弼教也玆則教巳
孚於神道之設而民默順乎帝則焉刑不必施
而天下咸以聖人之心爲心矣是謂無爲而治
其治之所以益隆乎刑有五罰將以明法也玆
===
則法巳昭於大道之公而民自格其非心焉罰
不必用而天下皆以聖人之德爲德矣是謂不
言而化其化之所以益神乎夫盡民而服之又
不假刑罰焉順之極也豫之至也而以順動得
之豫之爲義大矣哉嗟乎此堯舜事也精一執
中垂拱無爲而時雍於變堯舜不知焉殆與天
地之順動一道也至於禹則有不然者下車之
泣蓋傷之也而刑罰其可遽措乎雖然禹非不
能順動而民自爲心時也無害其爲服也人君
punctuated: 之。聖人之所爲，固人心之所欲爲者也，而一毫私智不存焉。以裁庶務，非一無所事也，然皆因勢而利導之。聖人之有事，乃天下之所恃以無事者也，而一毫已意不與焉。夫如是，吾知順動之德旣參諸天地而不違，則和樂之情自通乎上下而無間。國有五刑，將以弼教也，玆則教巳孚於神道之設，而民默順乎帝則焉。刑不必施，而天下咸以聖人之心爲心矣。是謂無爲而治，其治之所以益隆乎！刑有五罰，將以明法也，玆則法巳昭於大道之公，而民自格其非心焉。罰不必用，而天下皆以聖人之德爲德矣。是謂不言而化，其化之所以益神乎！夫盡民而服之，又不假刑罰焉，順之極也，豫之至也，而以順動得之。豫之爲義大矣哉！嗟乎！此堯舜事也。精一執中，垂拱無爲，而時雍於變，堯舜不知焉，殆與天地之順動一道也。至於禹，則有不然者。下車之泣，蓋傷之也，而刑罰其可遽措乎？雖然，禹非不能順動，而民自爲心，時也，無害其爲服也。人君
translation_en:
…to them. What the sage does is precisely what the hearts of the people desire to do, and not the slightest private cleverness enters into it. In settling the many affairs of government, he does not remain wholly inactive; rather, he follows the circumstances and guides them toward beneficial ends. The sage’s activity is what all under Heaven rely upon for their freedom from trouble, and not the slightest personal intention intervenes. In this way, I know that, once the virtue of acting in accord joins with Heaven and Earth without diverging from them, feelings of harmony and joy naturally pass between those above and below without obstruction. The state has the five punishments to support moral instruction. Here, however, instruction has already won trust through the establishment of the numinous way, and the people silently accord with the Supreme Lord’s standard. Punishments need not be inflicted, and all under Heaven take the sage’s heart as their own. This is called governing through nonaction: is this not how his governance becomes ever more exalted? The penal system has five fines to make the law clear. Here, however, the law has already been made manifest through the impartiality of the Great Way, and the people themselves correct the wrongful inclinations of their hearts. Fines need not be imposed, and all under Heaven take the sage’s virtue as their own. This is called transforming without words: is this not how his transforming influence becomes ever more wondrous? To bring all the people into willing submission without resorting to punishments or fines is the utmost accord and the highest realization of Yu, or joyful ease; it is attained by acting in accord. Great indeed is the significance of Yu!

Ah! These were the achievements of Yao and Shun. Discerning and single-minded, they held fast to the Mean; with robes hanging down and hands folded, they practiced nonaction. The people were transformed and brought into harmony, without Yao and Shun being conscious of it. This was surely the same way as the movement of Heaven and Earth in accord. With Yu, however, matters were different. His tears upon descending from his carriage surely expressed his sorrow over this; could punishments and fines then be set aside at once? Nevertheless, it was not that Yu was incapable of acting in accord. Rather, the people each followed their own hearts: this was a matter of the times, and did not detract from their submission. A ruler…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
欲法堯舜其惟以順動乎
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也唯深也
故能通天下之志唯幾也故能成天下
之務唯神也故不疾而速不行而至
梁俸
同考試官教諭陳批融會幾深本旨說入通
志成務一神所為意明徹可玩允宜高薦
考試官教諭萬批諸作幾深神類用套堆
積此獨脫去浮辭洞見本真殆邃於易學者
===
考試官教授鄒批歸功聖人得旨
大傳以易道歸聖人而因推其妙用焉甚矣易
非聖人不能作也易作而天下之妙用具是矣
人可不知所尚乎大傳之意若曰易之為道闡
於聖心者甚微而利於天下也甚大是故辭占
象變皆易也而以為聖人之道何哉蓋以吉凶
之理精入無形若是乎深矣聖人以心涵之而
繫之辭焉决之占焉所以洩此理之秘而究極
其深也深極而精有不顯乎老少之端變動莫
punctuated:
欲法堯舜，其惟以順動乎！

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。唯深也，故能通天下之志；唯幾也，故能成天下之務；唯神也，故不疾而速，不行而至。

梁俸

同考試官教諭陳批：融會幾深本旨，說入通志成務，一神所為，意明徹可玩，允宜高薦。

考試官教諭萬批：諸作幾深神，類用套堆積；此獨脫去浮辭，洞見本真，殆邃於易學者。

考試官教授鄒批：歸功聖人，得旨。

大傳以易道歸聖人，而因推其妙用焉。甚矣，易非聖人不能作也！易作而天下之妙用具，是矣。人可不知所尚乎？大傳之意若曰：易之為道，闡於聖心者甚微，而利於天下也甚大。是故辭占象變，皆易也，而以為聖人之道，何哉？蓋以吉凶之理，精入無形，若是乎深矣。聖人以心涵之，而繫之辭焉，决之占焉，所以洩此理之秘，而究極其深也。深極而精有不顯乎？老少之端，變動莫
translation_en:
…If a ruler wishes to emulate Yao and Shun, surely he must act in accordance with the proper order!

“The Changes is that by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient workings of things. Only through depth can they comprehend the intentions of all under Heaven; only through incipient workings can they accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; only through numinous efficacy can they be swift without haste and arrive without travelling.”

Liang Feng 梁俸

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: He integrates the fundamental meaning of incipient workings and depth, bringing his exposition to bear on comprehending intentions and accomplishing affairs, all as the operation of numinous efficacy. His meaning is lucid and merits close appreciation. He certainly deserves a high recommendation.

Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: The other compositions discussing incipient workings, depth, and numinous efficacy mostly pile up stock expressions. This one alone casts off empty language and penetrates to the true essentials. Its author must be deeply versed in the study of the Changes.

Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: By attributing the achievement to the sages, he grasps the purport.

The Great Commentary attributes the Way of the Changes to the sages and thereby elaborates its wondrous operation. How true it is that none but the sages could have composed the Changes! Once the Changes was composed, all the wondrous operations of the world were fully embodied in it: this is indeed so. Can people fail to know what they should esteem? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as though it said: the Way of the Changes, as unfolded in the minds of the sages, is exceedingly subtle, yet its benefits to all under Heaven are exceedingly great. Thus the statements, divinations, images, and transformations all belong to the Changes; why, then, are they regarded as the Way of the sages? It is because the principles of good and ill fortune are so refined that they enter the realm of the formless: such is their depth. The sages embraced these principles in their minds, attached statements to them, and determined them through divination. In this way they disclosed the secrets of these principles and plumbed their depths to the utmost. Once those depths are fully plumbed, could their refined essence fail to become manifest? As for the beginnings of the old and young forms of yin and yang, their transformations cannot…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
測若是乎幾矣聖人以心契之而裁之變焉定
之象焉所以發此端之微而研窮其幾也幾研
而變有不著乎夫惟辭占一深也故能受命知
來示人以失得之報而天下無復有惑志矣惟
象變一幾也故能成文定象鼓人以趨避之方
而天下無復有廢務矣惟深與幾而無思無爲
一天下之至神也故機動於無端而化應於無
迹志之通也若或啓之務之成也若或翼之所
以妙於寂而通於感者又豈待疾而後速行而
===
後至也哉此其精變之用雖達之天下而幾深
之妙實闡於聖人惟聖人妙神道以設教故天
下自鼓舞以盡神易有聖人之道不其然乎雖
然易之作也聖人豈得已哉幾深之理弗彰則
天下無由以寡過因貳以濟民行其慮蓋深矣
故象變立卽不能忘象辭占立卽不能忘言尚
易者又執其象與言而求之聖人之意益遠矣
宋儒有言君子脩之吉小人悖之凶蓋得之言
象之外也其深於易者乎
punctuated:
測，若是乎幾矣！聖人以心契之，而裁之變焉，定之象焉，所以發此端之微而研窮其幾也。幾研而變有不著乎？夫惟辭占一深也，故能受命知來，示人以失得之報，而天下無復有惑志矣。惟象變一幾也，故能成文定象，鼓人以趨避之方，而天下無復有廢務矣。惟深與幾，而無思無爲，一天下之至神也，故機動於無端，而化應於無迹。志之通也，若或啓之；務之成也，若或翼之。所以妙於寂而通於感者，又豈待疾而後速、行而後至也哉？此其精變之用雖達之天下，而幾深之妙實闡於聖人。惟聖人妙神道以設教，故天下自鼓舞以盡神。《易》有聖人之道，不其然乎？
雖然，《易》之作也，聖人豈得已哉？幾深之理弗彰，則天下無由以寡過。因貳以濟民行，其慮蓋深矣。故象變立，卽不能忘象；辭占立，卽不能忘言。尚《易》者又執其象與言而求之，聖人之意益遠矣。宋儒有言：「君子脩之吉，小人悖之凶。」蓋得之言象之外也，其深於《易》者乎！
translation_en:
…beyond fathoming: how subtle these incipient movements are! The sages grasped them in their hearts, regulated them through the changes, and gave them determinate form through the images. Thus they disclosed the subtlety of these beginnings and thoroughly investigated their incipient movements. Once these have been investigated, could the changes fail to become manifest? The statements and divinations are united in their depth; hence they can receive a consultation and reveal what is to come, showing people the consequences of failure and success, so that no perplexity of purpose remains under Heaven. The images and changes are united in their subtle incipience; hence they can form patterns and establish images, stirring people to pursue or avoid as appropriate, so that no undertaking under Heaven is left neglected. Depth and incipient movement, operating without thought or action, together constitute the utmost spiritual efficacy under Heaven. Thus their impulse stirs without any discernible beginning, and their transforming responses leave no trace. When purposes find fulfillment, it is as though something opened the way; when undertakings succeed, it is as though something lent assistance. Wondrous in stillness and responsive when moved, how could this efficacy need haste to be swift, or movement to arrive? Although its operations of refinement and change extend throughout the world, the marvel of its incipience and depth is made manifest through the sages. Only the sages wondrously employed the spiritual Way to establish their teaching; thus all under Heaven were spontaneously stirred and inspired to realize its spiritual efficacy fully. Is it not indeed true that the Changes contains the Way of the sages?
Nevertheless, could the sages have refrained from making the Changes? If the principles of incipience and depth were not made manifest, people under Heaven would have no means of reducing their errors. By addressing doubts, the sages aided the people’s conduct: profound indeed was their concern. Thus, once images and changes were established, the images could not be forgotten; once statements and divinations were established, the words could not be forgotten. Yet when those who esteem the Changes cling to its images and words in seeking its meaning, they move ever farther from the sages’ intent. A Song Confucian said: “For the noble man who cultivates it, good fortune; for the petty man who goes against it, misfortune.” Surely this grasps what lies beyond words and images. Was he not one who understood the Changes profoundly?

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書
九德咸事俊乂在官百僚師師百工惟時
撫于五辰庶績其凝
金節
同考試官學正林批〔近作于九德俊乂百僚百工講多纏繞予獨辭不費而理明悉佳作也〕
考試官教諭萬批〔虞廷得人氣象宛然在目可取可敬〕
考試官教授鄒批〔清脫得旨〕
===
大臣論官人之效羣賢用而治功成也蓋治道
以人而立也羣賢悉效其用而治功其有不成
者哉皐陶陳謨至此若曰天下無不可用之賢
人君貴得善用之道誠於九德之人而翕受敷
施矣吾知德之在人雖有多寡而均為有常之
吉也舉咸自奮於明時而因才以任事人之抱
德雖有大小而均為俊乂之良也茲皆布列於
庶位而隨事以服官以斯人也任斯治也同道
以為朋則見其百僚之師師焉惟善是主孚契
punctuated:
書

九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

金節

同考試官學正林批〔近作于九德、俊乂、百僚、百工，講多纏繞，予獨辭不費而理明悉，佳作也。〕
考試官教諭萬批〔虞廷得人氣象，宛然在目，可取可敬。〕
考試官教授鄒批〔清脫得旨。〕

大臣論官人之效，羣賢用而治功成也。蓋治道以人而立也，羣賢悉效其用，而治功其有不成者哉？皐陶陳謨至此，若曰：天下無不可用之賢，人君貴得善用之道。誠於九德之人而翕受敷施矣，吾知德之在人，雖有多寡，而均為有常之吉也。舉咸自奮於明時，而因才以任事；人之抱德，雖有大小，而均為俊乂之良也。茲皆布列於庶位，而隨事以服官。以斯人也任斯治也，同道以為朋，則見其百僚之師師焉。惟善是主，孚契
translation_en:
Book of Documents

“Those possessing the nine virtues all undertake service; men of outstanding ability hold office. The many officials learn from one another, and all officers attend to the proper timing of their duties. They bring affairs into accord with the five seasons, and the many undertakings are brought to completion.”

Jin Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, School Instructor: “Recent essays discussing the nine virtues, outstanding men, the many officials, and all officers have mostly become entangled in their exposition. Here alone [?], the wording is economical and the principles are explained clearly and fully. An excellent composition.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The atmosphere of the court of Yu, with worthy men in office, appears vividly before one’s eyes. Worthy of selection and respect.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Lucid and unencumbered; it captures the essential meaning.”

The great minister discusses the results of appointing men to office: when the assembled worthies are employed, the work of government is accomplished. For the way of government is established through men. When all the worthies fully contribute their abilities, how could the work of government fail to be accomplished?

At this point in presenting his counsels, Gao Yao seems to say: Among the worthy men of the world, none is incapable of being employed; what matters for the ruler is to grasp the way of employing them well. If he truly receives together those who possess the nine virtues and distributes them among their duties, then I know that, although men possess these virtues in greater or lesser number, they are all good men of constancy. All exert themselves in an enlightened age and are assigned responsibilities according to their abilities. Although the virtue men possess varies in degree, they are all excellent men of outstanding ability. Now they are arrayed throughout the various positions and serve in office according to the business entrusted to them.

With such men entrusted with this government, they form fellowships through their shared Way, and thus one sees the many officials learning from one another. Taking goodness alone as their guiding principle, they are joined in trust and accord …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于人已之交無睽志矣率職以自效則見其百
工之咸勤焉若時是務順播乎節宣之宜無曠
官矣夫衆賢悉致旣有以豫敏政之本羣力畢
宣又足以臻廣業之休庶績之分理於邦家者
不齊也自是其人存則其政舉而治具燦然爲
之弘敷矣放勳之業於今其爲烈乎庶績之分
布於天下者不一也自是有治人斯有治法而
衆功秩然爲之就緒矣煕載之治今茲其考成
乎吁治不自成而成於官之得人人不易得而
===
得於知之有道帝於知人之謨可不加之意哉
雖然官人要矣而君身尤爲取人之本苟少肆
於功成之餘亦未有能盡其用者故君臣相遇
自古爲難此皐陶陳謨必先之以允廸厥德而
無教逸欲之戒尤惓惓於庶績其凝之後也嘉
有虞之治者尚鑒茲哉
一人有慶兆民賴之
周篤棐
同考試官學正林 批 通篇氣格渾融而歸重
punctuated:
于人已之交，無睽志矣。率職以自效，則見其百工之咸勤焉，若時是務，順播乎節宣之宜，無曠官矣。夫衆賢悉致，旣有以豫敏政之本；羣力畢宣，又足以臻廣業之休。庶績之分理於邦家者不齊也，自是其人存則其政舉，而治具燦然爲之弘敷矣。放勳之業，於今其爲烈乎！庶績之分布於天下者不一也，自是有治人斯有治法，而衆功秩然爲之就緒矣。煕載之治，今茲其考成乎！吁！治不自成，而成於官之得人；人不易得，而得於知之有道。帝於知人之謨，可不加之意哉？雖然，官人要矣，而君身尤爲取人之本。苟少肆於功成之餘，亦未有能盡其用者。故君臣相遇，自古爲難。此皐陶陳謨，必先之以允廸厥德，而無教逸欲之戒，尤惓惓於庶績其凝之後也。嘉有虞之治者，尚鑒茲哉！
一人有慶，兆民賴之。
周篤棐
同考試官學正林批：通篇氣格渾融，而歸重
translation_en:
…in relations between oneself and others, there will be no divergence of purpose. When each fulfills his duties and offers his service, all the officials will be seen working diligently. Attending to what the times require, they will appropriately regulate and give scope to their efforts, leaving no office neglected. When all the worthy have been brought into service, the foundation for effective government is already laid; when their combined efforts are fully exerted, the splendid achievement of extending the great enterprise can also be attained. The many undertakings administered separately within the state differ from one another. Henceforth, with the right men present, their policies will be carried out, and the instruments of government will be splendidly deployed far and wide. Will not Fangxun’s achievements now become illustrious? The many undertakings distributed throughout the realm are diverse. Henceforth, with men capable of governing, there will be methods of government, and all endeavors will be brought into orderly operation. Will not the administration that makes every undertaking flourish now attain fulfillment?
Ah! Good government does not come about of itself: it comes about through appointing the right men to office. Such men are not easily found, but they can be found through a proper method of discerning them. Can the emperor fail to give careful attention to this counsel on knowing men? Nevertheless, although appointing officials is essential, the ruler’s own person is especially fundamental to selecting men. If he indulges himself even slightly after success has been achieved, he will never be able to make full use of their abilities. Thus, since antiquity, it has been difficult for ruler and ministers to find one another. This is why Gao Yao, in presenting his counsels, necessarily began with sincerely putting one’s virtue into practice, and why the admonition against encouraging idleness and desire was especially earnest after the many achievements had been firmly established. May those who admire the government of Youyu take this as their mirror!
“When the one man enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them.”
Zhou Dufei
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Throughout the piece, its vigor and style form a harmonious whole, while its principal emphasis rests on…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一人有慶尤見卓識是文之可傳者
考試官教諭萬批規模宏壯辭氣端重得
人君訓諸侯敬刑體
考試官教授鄒批瑩練
賢王言敬刑之福由君而及之民也夫民藉君
以自安也君慶於上而民以賴焉其刑之祥何
如哉穆王訓刑之意若曰人君以一人而臨兆
民有斂福敷錫之道焉而其機則司刑者致之
茲爾能敬刑以成德也將見惟予一人幸剛柔
===
之兼濟而民用不犯垂拱以迓乂安之休樂正
直之無為而化成有象恭己以享平康之盛天
地之和氣慶其有以導迎之也優游於清穆而
帝位其不疚矣國家之元氣慶其有以培植之
也伴奐於密勿而皇圖其永綏矣此蓋敬之所
成即慶之所集而汝之所為日勤於己者斯其
所以上效於君者也然豈專於予一人哉今此
兆民幸生明盛之世莫不獲有所庇以自適其
安全之願欣逢有道之長莫不獲有所依以自
punctuated:
一人有慶，尤見卓識，是文之可傳者。
考試官教諭萬批：規模宏壯，辭氣端重，得人君訓諸侯敬刑體。
考試官教授鄒批：瑩練。
賢王言敬刑之福，由君而及之民也。夫民藉君以自安也，君慶於上，而民以賴焉，其刑之祥何如哉！穆王訓刑之意若曰：人君以一人而臨兆民，有斂福敷錫之道焉，而其機則司刑者致之。茲爾能敬刑以成德也，將見惟予一人，幸剛柔之兼濟，而民用不犯，垂拱以迓乂安之休；樂正直之無為，而化成有象，恭己以享平康之盛。天地之和氣，慶其有以導迎之也，優游於清穆，而帝位其不疚矣；國家之元氣，慶其有以培植之也，伴奐於密勿，而皇圖其永綏矣。此蓋敬之所成，即慶之所集，而汝之所為日勤於己者，斯其所以上效於君者也。然豈專於予一人哉？今此兆民，幸生明盛之世，莫不獲有所庇，以自適其安全之願；欣逢有道之長，莫不獲有所依，以自
translation_en:
…“The one man enjoys blessings”: the emphasis on this especially reveals outstanding insight, making this essay worthy of transmission.
Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: “Grand in scope, with dignified and weighty diction and tone; it captures the manner of a sovereign instructing the feudal lords to exercise reverence in administering punishments.”
Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: “Polished and refined.”
The worthy king speaks of how the blessings of reverence in administering punishments extend from the ruler to the people. The people depend upon their ruler for their security. When the ruler enjoys blessings above and the people benefit thereby, how auspicious are the effects of his punishments! The meaning of King Mu’s instructions concerning punishments is as though he said:
“The ruler, as the one man presiding over the myriad people, has a way to gather blessings and bestow them widely; yet those who administer punishments are the means by which this is accomplished. Now, if you can exercise reverence in administering punishments and thereby perfect your virtue, you will see that I, the one man, am fortunate to have firmness and gentleness complement each other, so that the people commit no offenses. With robes hanging down and hands folded, I shall welcome the blessings of order and peace. I shall delight in the effortless efficacy of uprightness, as its transforming influence takes visible shape, and, maintaining a reverent bearing, enjoy the fullness of peace and well-being. As for the harmonious energies of Heaven and Earth, I rejoice that there is a means to usher them in: dwelling at ease in pure serenity, I shall be free from distress upon the imperial throne. As for the vital energies of the state, I rejoice that there is a means to nurture them: at ease amid diligent exertion, I shall see the imperial enterprise remain forever secure. What reverence accomplishes is precisely where blessings gather; your daily diligence in your own duties is thus the means by which you render service upward to your ruler.
“Yet could this benefit belong exclusively to me, the one man? These myriad people, fortunate to be born into an enlightened and flourishing age, all find protection through which to satisfy their wish for safety and security. Rejoicing to encounter a leader who possesses the Way, all find someone upon whom they may rely, so that they themselves…”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
遂其生養之情以定其趨賴上剛柔之克也藉
以寡過皞皞焉相安於至治矣以同其風賴上
正直之化也則以自治熈熈焉相忘於大道矣
此其德之所成卽民之所賴而君之所爲集慶
於上者斯其所以錫福於民者乎吁敬刑所致
其效有如此者爾諸侯可無用勸以自慰哉抑
此化中之會有虞事也今想其太和宇宙邈不
可尚乃穆王以之責成諸侯豈其有志於重華
事業哉顧其本未可以易言也然觀日勤數語
===
猶有哀矜惻怛遺意則文武之澤固在也是故
夫子猶有取云
詩
南山有桑北山有楊樂只君子邦家之光
樂只君子萬壽無疆南山有杞北山有
李樂只君子民之父母樂只君子德音
不已
霍鎮東
同考試官教諭王 批 題長辭簡意亦周密深
punctuated:
遂其生養之情。以定其趨，賴上剛柔之克也，藉以寡過，皞皞焉相安於至治矣；以同其風，賴上正直之化也，則以自治，熈熈焉相忘於大道矣。此其德之所成，卽民之所賴，而君之所爲集慶於上者，斯其所以錫福於民者乎？吁！敬刑所致，其效有如此者，爾諸侯可無用勸以自慰哉？抑此化中之會，有虞事也。今想其太和宇宙，邈不可尚，乃穆王以之責成諸侯，豈其有志於重華事業哉？顧其本未可以易言也。然觀日勤數語，猶有哀矜惻怛遺意，則文武之澤固在也。是故夫子猶有取云。

詩
南山有桑，北山有楊。樂只君子，邦家之光。樂只君子，萬壽無疆。南山有杞，北山有李。樂只君子，民之父母。樂只君子，德音不已。

霍鎮東

同考試官教諭王批：題長辭簡，意亦周密，深
translation_en:
…fulfill their desire to sustain their lives and nurture their families. To steady their course, they depend on those above being capable of firmness and gentleness; through this they lessen their faults and live together in simple contentment under perfect government. To bring their customs into accord, they depend on the transforming influence of uprightness above; thus they govern themselves and, in joyful harmony, forget one another within the Great Way. What his virtue accomplishes is precisely what the people depend upon. Is not the ruler’s gathering of blessings above thus the means by which he bestows good fortune upon the people? Ah! Such are the effects of reverence in administering punishments. Can you, the feudal lords, fail to take encouragement from this and thereby find reassurance? Yet this convergence within transforming influence [?] belongs to the age of Yu Shun. Today, imagining the supreme harmony of his realm, we find it so remote as to be beyond surpassing. Nevertheless, King Mu held the feudal lords responsible for achieving it. Did he perhaps aspire to the achievements of Chonghua [Shun]? Yet the foundation of this cannot lightly be spoken of. Still, in the few words about daily diligence, there remains something of the spirit of compassion and heartfelt concern: the beneficent legacy of Kings Wen and Wu was indeed still present. For this reason, the Master [Confucius] still found something here worth preserving.

Book of Poetry
“On the southern mountain are mulberry trees; on the northern mountain are poplars. Joyful is the noble lord, the glory of the state. Joyful is the noble lord: may he live ten thousand years without end! On the southern mountain are medlar trees; on the northern mountain are plum trees. Joyful is the noble lord, father and mother to the people. Joyful is the noble lord: may his virtuous renown never cease!”

Huo Zhendong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The topic is long, but the wording is concise; the meaning, too, is comprehensive and carefully developed, profoundly…”

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得詩人祝願之㫖
考試官敎諭萬批辭意溫醇可式
考試官敎授鄒批敷腴
詩人兩卽物以美君子之德而天人與之矣夫
惟德爲足以得壽而永譽也王者以是美諸侯
蓋本其所以致之者與此燕享通用之樂歌謂
夫人臣以祗天惠民爲大節則必以得天獲民
爲順應我君子不有可美者乎彼南山有桑北
山有楊山之生木則然矣我樂只君子以亮采
===
有邦其文炳也以浚明有家其文蔚也寧不載
錫之光哉吾知天之所佑者德也而至和之所
保合元氣爲委順焉其必萬有斯年而與邦家
相爲悠久矣斯謂有德者必得其壽與南山有
杞北山有李地之敏樹則然矣我樂只君子平
易以近民有父之尊也和順以率物有母之親
也豈不爲孔邇者哉吾知民之所與者德也而
篤實之所輝光令名爲無窮焉其必一德允孚
而人之頌父母者不衰矣斯謂有德者必得其
punctuated:
得詩人祝願之㫖。
考試官敎諭萬批：辭意溫醇，可式。
考試官敎授鄒批：敷腴。
詩人兩卽物以美君子之德，而天人與之矣。夫惟德爲足以得壽而永譽也，王者以是美諸侯，蓋本其所以致之者與！此燕享通用之樂歌，謂夫人臣以祗天惠民爲大節，則必以得天獲民爲順應。我君子不有可美者乎？彼南山有桑，北山有楊，山之生木則然矣。我樂只君子，以亮采有邦，其文炳也；以浚明有家，其文蔚也。寧不載錫之光哉？吾知天之所佑者德也，而至和之所保合，元氣爲委順焉。其必萬有斯年，而與邦家相爲悠久矣。斯謂有德者必得其壽與！南山有杞，北山有李，地之敏樹則然矣。我樂只君子，平易以近民，有父之尊也；和順以率物，有母之親也。豈不爲孔邇者哉？吾知民之所與者德也，而篤實之所輝光，令名爲無窮焉。其必一德允孚，而人之頌父母者不衰矣。斯謂有德者必得其
translation_en:
…captures the intent of the poet’s blessings.
Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: “The language and thought are gentle and rich; this may serve as a model.”
Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: “Full and rich.”
The poet twice draws upon things to praise the noble lord’s virtue, and Heaven and the people give him their support. Only virtue suffices to secure longevity and lasting renown. In praising the feudal lords in these terms, the king surely grounds his praise in what brings about these blessings! This song, used alike at banquets and sacrificial feasts, declares that a minister’s cardinal duties are to revere Heaven and benefit the people; accordingly, Heaven’s favor and the people’s allegiance must follow as their fitting response. Does our noble lord not possess qualities worthy of praise? On the southern mountain are mulberry trees; on the northern mountain are poplars: such is the way mountains produce trees. Our joyous noble lord faithfully discharges his duties in possessing a state, and his cultivated excellence shines brightly; he displays profound discernment in possessing a house, and his cultivated excellence flourishes abundantly. Does he not thus bestow glory upon them? I know that what Heaven protects is virtue. Where perfect harmony preserves and unites, the primal vital force yields in accord. Surely he will live for ten thousand years, enduring together with his state and house. Is this not what is meant by saying that the virtuous are certain to attain longevity?
On the southern mountain are qi trees; on the northern mountain are plum trees: such is the earth’s vigor in growing trees. Our joyous noble lord is accessible and unassuming in drawing close to the people, possessing a father’s dignity; harmonious and gentle in guiding all beings, he possesses a mother’s affection. Is he not exceedingly close to them? I know that what the people support is virtue. Where steadfast sincerity shines forth, a good name becomes inexhaustible. Surely his undivided virtue will inspire true trust, and the people’s praise of him as their father and mother will never diminish. Is this not what is meant by saying that the virtuous are certain to attain their…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
名與吁王者以是而美其臣逮下之仁可想見
矣抑論之上下交而後爲道之泰也周之盛時
臣子之忠愛其君皆頌不忘規今觀南山之詩
君之宣慈惠於其臣尤必先其所以致之者蓋
上下交相爲儆也玆其所以爲成周有道之長
與
方命厥后奄有九有
林應祥
同考試官敎諭王批體裁莊重辭理簡明商
===
人頌祖之意宛然想見
考試官敎諭萬批成湯誕受帝命當時王
業之盛見於人心土宇如此是作闡揚殆盡
考試官敎授鄒批典雅
商人頌聖祖受命自其王業之盛言之也蓋人
心土宇王業之所係也商王受命而大一統焉
是宜詩人侈之登歌也與此祭祀宗廟之樂歌
也意曰一代之王業成之者人也本之者天也
我武湯之受天命而興何如哉彼四海之諸侯
punctuated:
名與？吁！王者以是而美其臣，逮下之仁可想見矣。抑論之，上下交而後爲道之泰也。周之盛時，臣子之忠愛其君，皆頌不忘規。今觀南山之詩，君之宣慈惠於其臣，尤必先其所以致之者，蓋上下交相爲儆也。玆其所以爲成周有道之長與？
方命厥后，奄有九有。
林應祥
同考試官敎諭王批：體裁莊重，辭理簡明，商人頌祖之意宛然想見。
考試官敎諭萬批：成湯誕受帝命，當時王業之盛見於人心土宇如此，是作闡揚殆盡。
考試官敎授鄒批：典雅。
商人頌聖祖受命，自其王業之盛言之也。蓋人心土宇，王業之所係也。商王受命而大一統焉，是宜詩人侈之登歌也與！此祭祀宗廟之樂歌也。意曰：一代之王業，成之者人也，本之者天也。我武湯之受天命而興何如哉？彼四海之諸侯，
translation_en:
…reputation? Ah! From the way the king praises his ministers, we can imagine his benevolence extending to those below. To consider this further: only when those above and below communicate does the Way flourish. In Zhou’s flourishing age, ministers and subjects, in their loyalty and love toward their ruler, never forgot admonition amid their praise. Now, looking at the poem on the Southern Mountain, we see that when the ruler extends kindness and favor to his ministers, he especially emphasizes first the qualities by which they have earned these. Thus those above and below admonish one another. Is this not why the accomplished Zhou so long possessed the Way?
“He issued commands to their lords and possessed all the Nine Regions.”
Lin Yingxiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The composition is dignified, its language and reasoning concise and clear. The Shang people’s intention in praising their ancestor can be vividly apprehended.
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: Cheng Tang received the august mandate of the Lord on High. Such was the flourishing of his royal enterprise at that time, manifested in the people’s allegiance and the extent of his territory. This composition expounds it almost exhaustively.
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: Classical and elegant.
The Shang people praise their sage ancestor’s receipt of the mandate by speaking of the flourishing of his royal enterprise. For the people’s allegiance and the realm’s territory are what the royal enterprise depends upon. The Shang king received the mandate and achieved comprehensive unity: surely it was fitting that the poet should magnify this achievement and celebrate it in song! This is a ritual song for sacrifices in the ancestral temple. Its meaning is: the royal enterprise of a dynasty is accomplished by human beings, but has its foundation in Heaven. How did our martial Tang receive Heaven’s mandate and rise to power? Those feudal lords within the Four Seas…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皆有夏之臣庶也茲焉智勇天錫旣舉夏正而
爰革之但見六服羣辟莫不欽一人之威命而
奔走之恐後庶邦冢君舉皆仰皇靈之振肅而
歸向之不違禮樂征伐于此焉受也政敎號令
于此焉受也蓋人心之所在卽天命之所在天
旣以命夏者而命商則四海之諸侯得不以戴
夏者而戴商耶九有之土地皆有夏之輿圖也
茲焉聖武布昭旣盡禹績而一統之但見式廓
之增舉覆載之所加者悉入于統馭之內幅隕
===
之廣凡照墜之所及者皆在其疆理之中內而
華夏莫非其地也外而蠻貊莫非其地也蓋土
地之所歸卽天命之所歸天旣以命禹者而命
湯則九有之土地得不以附禹者而附湯耶吁
詩人于登歌之際而追述之其亦不忘所自者
矣雖然基命以裕後前王之所以垂統也脩德
以保業後王之所以承先也商人祭祀而惓惓
以祖宗功德爲言無亦以法祖望其君與撫成
業者尚繹思之
punctuated: 皆有夏之臣庶也。茲焉智勇天錫，旣舉夏正而爰革之，但見六服羣辟，莫不欽一人之威命而奔走之恐後；庶邦冢君，舉皆仰皇靈之振肅而歸向之不違。禮樂征伐，于此焉受也；政敎號令，于此焉受也。蓋人心之所在，卽天命之所在。天旣以命夏者而命商，則四海之諸侯得不以戴夏者而戴商耶？九有之土地，皆有夏之輿圖也。茲焉聖武布昭，旣盡禹績而一統之，但見式廓之增，舉覆載之所加者，悉入于統馭之內；幅隕之廣，凡照墜之所及者，皆在其疆理之中。內而華夏，莫非其地也；外而蠻貊，莫非其地也。蓋土地之所歸，卽天命之所歸。天旣以命禹者而命湯，則九有之土地得不以附禹者而附湯耶？吁！詩人于登歌之際而追述之，其亦不忘所自者矣。雖然，基命以裕後，前王之所以垂統也；脩德以保業，後王之所以承先也。商人祭祀，而惓惓以祖宗功德爲言，無亦以法祖望其君與？撫成業者，尚繹思之！
translation_en:
…were all subjects of the Xia. Now, endowed by Heaven with wisdom and courage, he overturned the Xia calendar and its rule. All the lords of the six zones of service revered the sovereign’s august commands and hastened to obey, fearing to lag behind; the rulers of the many states looked up to his awe-inspiring majesty and submitted without resistance. From him they received authority over rites, music, and punitive expeditions; from him they received governmental instruction and commands. For where the people’s hearts turn, there too lies Heaven’s mandate. Since Heaven had bestowed upon Shang the mandate formerly bestowed upon Xia, how could the lords within the four seas fail to support Shang as they had supported Xia?

The lands of the nine regions had all belonged to the Xia domain. Now his sagely martial prowess shone forth everywhere, and he unified the whole extent of Yu’s achievement. As his domain expanded, everything beneath Heaven and borne by Earth came under his rule; throughout its vast breadth, wherever celestial light reached [?] lay within his boundaries. Inwardly, all the central Chinese lands were his territory; outwardly, all the lands of the Man and Mo peoples were his territory. For where the lands give their allegiance, there too turns Heaven’s mandate. Since Heaven had bestowed upon Tang the mandate formerly bestowed upon Yu, how could the lands of the nine regions fail to adhere to Tang as they had adhered to Yu?

Ah! In recounting these deeds in the songs sung at the sacrifice, the poets surely showed that they did not forget their origins. Yet establishing the mandate to enrich posterity was how former kings handed down their rule; cultivating virtue to preserve that inheritance was how later kings carried on the work of their predecessors. When the people of Shang offered sacrifices and spoke so earnestly of their ancestors’ achievements and virtue, was it not also their hope that their ruler would emulate those ancestors? May those who hold an established inheritance ponder this deeply!

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
春王三月甲寅齊人伐衛〔莊公二十有八年〕
齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕
許岸
同考試官教諭鄭批〔是作深得春秋謹嚴家法錄之〕
考試官教諭萬批〔體裁峻整筆力渾雄〕
考試官教授鄒批〔雅健〕
伯主始奉命討罪春秋予其正繼專命恤患春
===
秋予其權于以見桓之有功於天下也伐衛則
正城邢不嫌於專春秋兩予之也宜哉衛伐周
而立頹桓公伐之春秋予之以正者何蓋君令
臣共分也正以秩分者也衛可伐也威不可作
也向使專命而行其誰能悅之桓蓋能知正者
有侯伯之賜有召伯之請奉辭問罪一以王命
臨之使衛之得正法者桓之力也昭哉其命討
之公乎是雖衛抗如故也然方侯度無統之日
微桓也起而挋之天下將不知有周矣此其義
punctuated:
《春秋》
春，王三月，甲寅，齊人伐衛。〔莊公二十有八年〕
齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。〔僖公元年〕
許岸
同考試官教諭鄭批〔是作深得春秋謹嚴家法，錄之。〕
考試官教諭萬批〔體裁峻整，筆力渾雄。〕
考試官教授鄒批〔雅健。〕
伯主始奉命討罪，《春秋》予其正；繼專命恤患，《春秋》予其權，于以見桓之有功於天下也。伐衛則正，城邢不嫌於專，《春秋》兩予之也，宜哉！衛伐周而立頹，桓公伐之，《春秋》予之以正者何？蓋君令臣共，分也；正以秩分者也。衛可伐也，威不可作也。向使專命而行，其誰能悅之？桓蓋能知正者。有侯伯之賜，有召伯之請，奉辭問罪，一以王命臨之。使衛之得正法者，桓之力也。昭哉，其命討之公乎！是雖衛抗如故也，然方侯度無統之日，微桓也起而挋之，天下將不知有周矣。此其義
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In spring, in the third month according to the royal calendar, on the jiayin day, men of Qi attacked Wei.” 〔The twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
“The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built walls for Xing.” 〔The first year of Duke Xi.〕
Xu An

Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition profoundly grasps the rigorous and exacting interpretive tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: 〔The composition is tightly structured and orderly; the writing is vigorous and majestic.〕
Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: 〔Elegant and forceful.〕

The hegemon first acted under royal command to punish wrongdoing, and the Spring and Autumn Annals approves his adherence to proper authority. Subsequently, he acted on his own authority to relieve distress, and the Spring and Autumn Annals approves his exercise of discretion. Here we see Duke Huan’s service to all under Heaven. Attacking Wei accorded with proper authority; building walls for Xing incurred no blame for acting independently. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals approves both!

Wei attacked Zhou and installed Tui, and Duke Huan attacked Wei. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve his action as proper? For the ruler to command and the subject to obey is their allotted relationship; proper authority maintains the order of those roles. Wei could rightly be attacked, but coercive authority could not be assumed at will. Had he acted on his own authority, who could have accepted it willingly? Huan indeed understood proper authority. He had received the grant of authority as leader of the regional lords, and he had received the request of the Earl of Shao. Bearing the royal pronouncement, he called Wei to account for its offenses, confronting it wholly on the authority of the king’s command. That Wei was subjected to the proper sanctions was due to Huan’s efforts. How manifest was the impartiality of his royally commanded punitive action!

Although Wei remained defiant as before, this was a time when no unifying authority governed the conduct of the regional lords. Had Huan not risen to restrain it [?], all under Heaven would have ceased to recognize Zhou. The significance of this …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何如也而桓可少乎哉故予之若曰持天下之
名分者不可一日而無正予桓者興常典也邢
避狄而遷邑桓公城之春秋予之以權者何蓋
安內攘外義也權以達義者也邢可城也時不
可後也向使請命而行其疇能聽之桓蓋能知
權者焉狄人之逐焉邢邑之營具器度工一以
便宜從之邢之幸不亡者桓之力也偉哉其綏
定之績乎是雖師出若專也然方小國潰亡之
時微桓也起而存之斯民其不免左衽矣此其
===
功何如也而桓可沒乎哉故予之若曰濟天下
之事功者亦不可一日而無權予桓者不得已
也是知討罪予之重王道也恤患予之重世道
也何莫非聖人之精義哉雖然伐衛正矣取其
賂則偷城邢美矣待其潰則不仁大抵隳義於
衛觀釁於狄養禍於邢此皆伯者計功謀利之
心為之論桓者當取其功不可略其心
晉人宋人衛人曹人伐鄭宣公十年
馮瑞
punctuated:
何如也，而桓可少乎哉？故予之，若曰：持天下之名分者，不可一日而無正。予桓者，興常典也。邢避狄而遷邑，桓公城之，春秋予之以權者何？蓋安內攘外，義也；權以達義者也。邢可城也，時不可後也。向使請命而行，其疇能聽之？桓蓋能知權者焉。狄人之逐焉，邢邑之營，具器度工，一以便宜從之。邢之幸不亡者，桓之力也。偉哉，其綏定之績乎！是雖師出若專也，然方小國潰亡之時，微桓也起而存之，斯民其不免左衽矣。此其功何如也，而桓可沒乎哉？故予之，若曰：濟天下之事功者，亦不可一日而無權。予桓者，不得已也。是知討罪予之，重王道也；恤患予之，重世道也。何莫非聖人之精義哉！雖然，伐衛正矣，取其賂則偷；城邢美矣，待其潰則不仁。大抵隳義於衛，觀釁於狄，養禍於邢，此皆伯者計功謀利之心為之。論桓者當取其功，不可略其心。

晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人伐鄭。宣公十年。
馮瑞。
translation_en:
…What, then, was the significance of this act? Could Duke Huan have been dispensed with? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals approves him, as if to say: those who uphold the distinctions of status and duty throughout the realm cannot go even a single day without adherence to what is right. Its approval of Huan serves to restore the enduring norms.

Xing moved its settlement to escape the Di, and Duke Huan built walls for it. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve him for exercising discretion? Securing those within and repelling those without is righteousness; discretion is the means of realizing righteousness. Xing needed walls, and action could not be delayed. Had he first requested authorization before acting, who could have heeded that request? Huan surely understood discretion. In driving off the Di and constructing Xing’s settlement, procuring equipment and estimating the labor, he acted throughout as circumstances required. That Xing was fortunate enough to escape destruction was due to Huan’s efforts. How great was his achievement in pacifying and securing it! Although his dispatch of troops might seem an unauthorized exercise of power, at a time when small states were collapsing, had Huan not arisen to preserve Xing, its people could hardly have avoided fastening their robes on the left, in the manner of the non-Chinese peoples. What, then, was the magnitude of this achievement? Could Huan’s contribution be effaced? Thus the Annals approves him, as if to say: those who accomplish the affairs of the realm likewise cannot go even a single day without discretion. Its approval of Huan arose from the necessities of the situation.

From this we know that approving his punishment of wrongdoing accords weight to the kingly Way, while approving his relief of distress accords weight to the moral order of the world. How could any of this fail to embody the sage’s subtle principles of righteousness? Nevertheless, attacking Wei was right, but accepting its bribes was ignoble; building walls for Xing was admirable, but waiting until it collapsed was inhumane. In general, abandoning righteousness in his dealings with Wei, watching for an opening against the Di, and allowing disaster to develop in Xing all arose from the hegemon’s disposition to calculate achievements and seek advantage. Those who assess Huan should acknowledge his achievements, but must not overlook his motives.

“Men of Jin, men of Song, men of Wei, and men of Cao attacked Zheng.” Tenth year of Duke Xuan.
Feng Rui.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭批招攜以德是作發揮明
盡可以式矣
考試官教諭萬批認傳切實措辭雄蔚
考試官教授鄒批嚴正
伯者恃力爭貳春秋深責之焉夫人心不可以
力強也晉爭鄭而失所以感人者伯業其替乎
自柳棼之敗楚之怒鄭益淫鄭之平楚是急玆
四國所為伐也春秋稱人則責伯之詞也何責
之深乎蓋伯者匪不武之患惟務德之難鄭介
===
大國之間將擇強而求庇焉者今棄而從楚社
稷之故也豈其情哉晉苟反身脩德則楚屈而
鄭自服矣奚事於兵奈何信義罔聞招懷失策
少西有可問之罪也為之戡定而以德鎮之彼
將帖吾之義而不敢攜矣不伐陳而伐鄭義乎
不義乎鄭有可分之災也為之安靖而以德撫
之彼將懷吾之仁而不忍貳矣不觀德而觀兵
可乎不可乎夫篳路藍縷吾無望其知德耳矣
晉友邦也楚以兵爭鄭吾亦以兵角楚不知晉
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭批：招攜以德，是作發揮明盡，可以式矣。
考試官教諭萬批：認傳切實，措辭雄蔚。
考試官教授鄒批：嚴正。
伯者恃力爭貳，《春秋》深責之焉。夫人心不可以力強也。晉爭鄭而失所以感人者，伯業其替乎？自柳棼之敗，楚之怒鄭益淫，鄭之平楚是急，玆四國所為伐也。《春秋》稱人，則責伯之詞也。何責之深乎？蓋伯者匪不武之患，惟務德之難。鄭介大國之間，將擇強而求庇焉者。今棄而從楚，社稷之故也，豈其情哉？晉苟反身脩德，則楚屈而鄭自服矣，奚事於兵？奈何信義罔聞，招懷失策？少西有可問之罪也，為之戡定而以德鎮之，彼將帖吾之義而不敢攜矣。不伐陳而伐鄭，義乎？不義乎？鄭有可分之災也，為之安靖而以德撫之，彼將懷吾之仁而不忍貳矣。不觀德而觀兵，可乎？不可乎？夫篳路藍縷，吾無望其知德耳矣。晉友邦也，楚以兵爭鄭，吾亦以兵角楚，不知晉
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Win back the estranged through virtue: this composition develops that point clearly and fully. It may serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Wan, Instructor: “The interpretation of the commentary is sound and precise; the language is powerful and rich.”
Comment by Examiner Zou, Professor: “Rigorous and upright.”
The hegemon relies on force to contend for states of divided allegiance, and the Spring and Autumn Annals severely censures him for it. People’s hearts cannot be compelled by force. Jin contended for Zheng but lost the means of winning people over: was its hegemony then declining?
After the defeat at Liufen, Chu’s anger toward Zheng grew increasingly excessive, and Zheng urgently sought peace with Chu. This was why the four states attacked it. The Spring and Autumn Annals calls their leaders simply “men,” thereby censuring the hegemon. Why such severe censure? Because the hegemon’s difficulty lies not in lacking military might, but in devoting himself to virtue. Situated between great states, Zheng would choose the stronger and seek its protection. That it now abandoned Jin and followed Chu was for the sake of preserving its state. Could this have been its true desire? If Jin had examined itself and cultivated virtue, Chu would have yielded and Zheng would naturally have submitted. What need would there have been for arms? Why, then, was nothing heard of good faith and righteousness, while efforts to attract and conciliate went awry?
Shaoxi [?] had committed a crime for which he could be called to account. Had Jin quelled the disorder there and secured the state through virtue, its people would have submitted to our righteousness and dared not turn away. Was attacking Zheng rather than Chen righteous or unrighteous? Zheng suffered calamities whose burden could have been shared. Had Jin restored its peace and comforted it through virtue, its people would have cherished our benevolence and could not have borne to divide their allegiance. Was displaying military force instead of displaying virtue acceptable or unacceptable?
As for those of the brushwood carts and ragged garments, I have no expectation that they should understand virtue. Jin, however, is a friendly state. Chu uses arms to contend for Zheng, and we likewise use arms to challenge Chu. I do not know how Jin …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之所以駕楚者何如也其無乃尤而效之也乎
裔夷異族吾無責其競力耳矣晉宗盟也鄭方
困楚之令吾亦脅鄭之成不知晉之所以信鄭
者何如也其無乃驅而去之也乎自是晉之爭
鄭雖力鄭之從楚益親南北之勢分辰陵之謀
合天下不伯晉而伯楚矣晉也其能得志於鄭
哉吁此春秋所以重責晉也雖然鄭獨無罪與
不擇所從甘心外比下喬而入谷矣楚獨無罪
與謀夏亂華入陳入鄭暴而不戢欲何為哉君
===
子謂逵道之入鄭自貽之慼也邲勝而志驕天
下日擾擾焉楚矣景不桓不文其世道之不幸
夫
禮記
事君以自顯也
陳綯
同考試官學正廖批人君為天下所事故卽
自顯以見當事之義此作得之錄以為式
考試官教諭萬批得君而事可以自顯平
punctuated:
之所以駕楚者何如也？其無乃尤而效之也乎？裔夷異族，吾無責其競力耳矣。晉宗盟也，鄭方困楚之令，吾亦脅鄭之成，不知晉之所以信鄭者何如也？其無乃驅而去之也乎？自是晉之爭鄭雖力，鄭之從楚益親。南北之勢分，辰陵之謀合，天下不伯晉而伯楚矣。晉也，其能得志於鄭哉？吁！此《春秋》所以重責晉也。雖然，鄭獨無罪與？不擇所從，甘心外比，下喬而入谷矣。楚獨無罪與？謀夏亂華，入陳入鄭，暴而不戢，欲何為哉？君子謂逵道之入，鄭自貽之慼也。邲勝而志驕，天下日擾擾焉。楚矣，景不桓不文，其世道之不幸夫！
禮記
事君以自顯也。
陳綯
同考試官學正廖批：人君為天下所事，故卽自顯以見當事之義。此作得之，錄以為式。
考試官教諭萬批：得君而事，可以自顯，平
translation_en:
…how Jin was to surpass Chu? Was it not condemning Chu while imitating it? As for alien peoples of the distant borders, I would not hold them accountable for competing in force alone. But Jin was the leader of the covenant among kindred states. Just as Zheng was suffering under Chu’s commands, Jin too coerced Zheng into a settlement. How, then, was Jin to gain Zheng’s trust? Was this not driving it away? From this time onward, although Jin strove hard to contest possession of Zheng, Zheng’s allegiance to Chu grew ever closer.
