Since His Majesty ascended the throne, he has rewarded ministers who speak with forthright remonstrance and brought distinction to worthy men living in secluded retreat. The scholars of the realm cherish jade-like virtues; gathering like rising clouds and converging winds, they have reached the height of flourishing. Among them there must surely be men who embrace the aspirations of Yu and Gao and share the character of the ancient regional governors and feudal lords. Yet when men are needed for service, talent still proves scarce, and concern over discerning men’s worth remains especially earnest. Is this not Emperor Yao’s own spirit of benevolence toward all under Heaven and urgency about what must come first? The talented men of the realm today are the same as those of antiquity. There is indeed a Way by which to recognize and obtain them, but this does not reside in techniques. Therefore, to put it into practice by means of…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
五視則所謂居視其所親達視其所舉富
視其所與窮視其所不爲貧視其所不取
者非不可也而未足以盡之也行之以九
徵則所謂遠使之而觀其忠近使之而觀
其敬煩使之而觀其能卒然問焉而觀其
智急與之期而觀其信委之財而觀其仁
告之危而觀其節醉之酒而觀其則雜之
處而觀其色者非不可也而亦未足以盡
之也何也知人以術故也以術知人則公
===
===
孫弘猶得售其儉也谷永猶得售其直也
謙恭下士者猶得售其忠也隱居終南者
猶得售其潔也非眞能知人者也夫成天
下之事者才也而所以善其才者心也心
術正矣無論翕張注措皆才也卽才有未
至而其心亦得以自效不害其爲才也苟
險而邪矣無論翕張注措皆非才也卽小
有才焉適足以害乎其心亦何取於才也
知人之道論心焉耳矣故見利不滓始終
punctuated:
五視，則所謂居視其所親，達視其所舉，富視其所與，窮視其所不爲，貧視其所不取者，非不可也，而未足以盡之也。行之以九徵，則所謂遠使之而觀其忠，近使之而觀其敬，煩使之而觀其能，卒然問焉而觀其智，急與之期而觀其信，委之財而觀其仁，告之危而觀其節，醉之酒而觀其則，雜之處而觀其色者，非不可也，而亦未足以盡之也。何也？知人以術故也。以術知人，則公孫弘猶得售其儉也，谷永猶得售其直也，謙恭下士者猶得售其忠也，隱居終南者猶得售其潔也，非眞能知人者也。
夫成天下之事者，才也；而所以善其才者，心也。心術正矣，無論翕張注措，皆才也；卽才有未至，而其心亦得以自效，不害其爲才也。苟險而邪矣，無論翕張注措，皆非才也；卽小有才焉，適足以害乎其心，亦何取於才也？知人之道，論心焉耳矣。故見利不滓，始終
translation_en:
…the five observations: observe whom a man associates with in private life, whom he recommends when he attains prominence, whom he gives to when wealthy, what he refuses to do in adversity, and what he refuses to take when poor. These are certainly usable, but they do not suffice to encompass the matter fully. Apply the nine tests: send him far away and observe his loyalty; employ him nearby and observe his respectfulness; burden him with tasks and observe his ability; question him suddenly and observe his understanding; give him an urgent deadline and observe his trustworthiness; entrust him with wealth and observe his benevolence; tell him of danger and observe his integrity; make him drunk and observe his adherence to proper standards; place him in mixed company and observe his bearing. These too are certainly usable, but they likewise do not suffice to encompass the matter fully. Why? Because they seek to judge men through techniques. If men are judged through techniques, Gongsun Hong can still pass off his frugality as genuine, and Gu Yong his forthrightness; those who humbly and respectfully defer to scholars can still pass off their loyalty as genuine, and those who retire to Mount Zhongnan their purity. This is no true understanding of men.
It is ability that accomplishes the affairs of the world, but the heart makes that ability good. If a man's disposition is upright, whether he draws back or expands his activity, whatever measures he takes, all are expressions of ability. Even if his ability falls short, his heart can still enable him to prove his worth, without detracting from his standing as a man of ability. If he is treacherous and depraved, whether he draws back or expands his activity, whatever measures he takes, none counts as ability. Even if he possesses some small ability, it serves only to injure his heart further. What value, then, is there in such ability? The way to understand men lies simply in judging their hearts. Thus, one who remains untainted at the sight of gain, from beginning to end…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
純皦者心也而小廉曲謹見色豆羹者非
矣知難不懼從容順應者心也而戇竦周
章巧於趨避者非矣遇事不苟權度精切
者心也而儇佻脂韋冥行用罔者非矣直
道而行計安社稷者心也而依阿淟涊希
榮邀寵者非矣於此論之則心術攸判人
品較然其可得而欺哉雖然有要焉人君
一心天下之心係之而知人之道則自君
心之明且正者爲之本也眞德秀之衍大
===
學也以辨人才爲格物致知之要凡帝王
知人之事聖賢觀人之法憸壬罔上之情
皆載焉而推原於人君之一心則君心者
庸非天下之心之衡鑑乎故必寡慾以養
此心格物以明此心誠意以實此心親君
子遠小人以維持此心俾惟精惟一上契
帝堯之心法則鑑空衡平羣品莫眩百僚
協師師之風而萬邦成時雍之化矣所以
運天下之仁智者不益廣且神哉
punctuated:
純皦者，心也；而小廉曲謹、見色豆羹者，非矣。知難不懼、從容順應者，心也；而戇竦周章、巧於趨避者，非矣。遇事不苟、權度精切者，心也；而儇佻脂韋、冥行用罔者，非矣。直道而行、計安社稷者，心也；而依阿淟涊、希榮邀寵者，非矣。於此論之，則心術攸判，人品較然，其可得而欺哉？雖然，有要焉。人君一心，天下之心係之，而知人之道，則自君心之明且正者爲之本也。
眞德秀之衍《大學》也，以辨人才爲格物致知之要。凡帝王知人之事、聖賢觀人之法、憸壬罔上之情，皆載焉。而推原於人君之一心，則君心者，庸非天下之心之衡鑑乎？故必寡慾以養此心，格物以明此心，誠意以實此心，親君子、遠小人以維持此心，俾惟精惟一，上契帝堯之心法，則鑑空衡平，羣品莫眩，百僚協師師之風，而萬邦成時雍之化矣。所以運天下之仁智者，不益廣且神哉？
translation_en:
…remaining pure and unsullied: this manifests the heart. But petty scrupulousness and punctilious caution, with displeasure showing on one’s face over a bowl of bean soup, do not. Recognizing difficulties without fear and responding calmly as circumstances require manifests the heart; being rash, alarmed, and flustered [?], while cleverly choosing what to pursue and what to avoid, does not. Handling affairs conscientiously and weighing them with precision manifests the heart; frivolity, pliant accommodation, and blindly proceeding without discernment do not. Following the upright Way and planning for the security of the state manifests the heart; obsequious compliance and abject acquiescence, seeking glory and courting favor, do not. Judged on these grounds, the orientations of people’s hearts can be distinguished and their character becomes clear. How could deception then succeed? Yet there is an essential point. The hearts of all under Heaven are bound to the single heart of the ruler; the foundation of the way to know people therefore lies in the clarity and rectitude of the ruler’s own heart.
In his Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, Zhen Dexiu made distinguishing men of talent an essential part of investigating things and extending knowledge. He recorded the deeds of emperors and kings in knowing people, the methods of sages and worthies in observing them, and the ways in which crafty villains deceive their superiors. Tracing these matters to their source in the ruler’s single heart, is not that heart the balance and mirror for the hearts of all under Heaven? Thus the ruler must diminish desires to nourish this heart, investigate things to illuminate it, make his intentions sincere to give it substance, and draw near to gentlemen while keeping petty men at a distance to sustain it. By remaining discerning and single-minded, he will accord with the teaching concerning the heart transmitted by Emperor Yao. Then the mirror will be clear and the balance level, and people of every character will be unable to confound his judgment. The hundred officials will unite in a spirit of mutual emulation, and the myriad states will attain the transforming harmony of the age. Will not the means by which benevolence and wisdom are put into practice throughout all under Heaven become still more far-reaching and wondrous?

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第四問
許岸
同考試官教諭鄭批蘊藉宏深議論正大殆
天資之美學力之優者取之
考試官教諭萬批聖賢為學宗旨發揮明
徹皆自得語也非勦說可比
考試官教授鄒批敷腴渾雅錄之
性原於天也則求道者不可無知性之學
學成於人也則盡人者不可無合天之功
===
蓋性道一原也求道而不知性是徇口耳
者也而何以造於自得之眞天人一理也
盡人而不能合天是泥形器者也而何以
探其本原之妙此古昔聖賢雖資稟氣習
其始或不能以盡同及其從事於學以求
聞道而知天者則固未始有異也今夫天
不言而四時行百物生者自然而已矣人
之學道者亦惟求其自然者而已矣自然
之道蓋著見於日用彝倫之間而無事於
punctuated:
第四問
許岸
同考試官教諭鄭批：蘊藉宏深，議論正大，殆天資之美、學力之優者，取之。
考試官教諭萬批：聖賢為學宗旨，發揮明徹，皆自得語也，非勦說可比。
考試官教授鄒批：敷腴渾雅，錄之。
性原於天也，則求道者不可無知性之學；學成於人也，則盡人者不可無合天之功。
蓋性道一原也，求道而不知性，是徇口耳者也，而何以造於自得之眞？天人一理也，盡人而不能合天，是泥形器者也，而何以探其本原之妙？此古昔聖賢，雖資稟氣習，其始或不能以盡同，及其從事於學，以求聞道而知天者，則固未始有異也。今夫天不言而四時行、百物生者，自然而已矣。人之學道者，亦惟求其自然者而已矣。自然之道，蓋著見於日用彝倫之間，而無事於
translation_en:
Fourth Question
Xu An
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Rich in implication and profound in scope, with upright and broad-minded argument. This is surely someone of fine natural endowment and superior scholarly attainment. Accept him.”
Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: “The guiding purpose of the sages’ and worthies’ learning is expounded with clarity and thoroughness. These are all words born of his own understanding, beyond comparison with plagiarized explanations.”
Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: “Ample and rich, harmonious and refined. Select him.”
Human nature originates in Heaven; thus those who seek the Way cannot dispense with learning that brings knowledge of human nature. Learning is brought to completion through human effort; thus those who fulfill their human capacities cannot dispense with the work of uniting with Heaven.
Human nature and the Way share a single source. To seek the Way without knowing human nature is merely to pursue learning that passes from ear to mouth: how could one thereby attain genuine understanding for oneself? Heaven and humanity share a single principle. To fulfill one’s human capacities yet fail to unite with Heaven is to be confined to material forms: how could one thereby fathom the subtle workings of their fundamental source? Thus, although the sages and worthies of antiquity may initially have differed in their endowments, temperaments, and acquired habits, when they devoted themselves to learning in order to hear the Way and know Heaven, they never differed in this respect. Heaven does not speak, yet the four seasons proceed and the myriad things come into being: this is simply spontaneity. Those who study the Way likewise seek only what is spontaneous. The Way of spontaneity is manifest in everyday conduct and the enduring human relationships, without any need for …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矜飾矯强之勞者也是故平旦而好惡相
近焉孩提之愛親敬長而不學不慮焉乍
見孺子入井而怵惕惻隱之心生焉皆所
謂天也生知也自然者也而何待於學耶
蓋聖人者順此者也而亦必學焉者戒慎
恐懼以求不失其常而已非有加也賢人
者其自然亦與此同也而苟不學焉則好
惡相近者有時而牿亡之矣愛親敬長者
有不能達之天下者矣見孺子入井而怵
===
惕惻隱焉者有時而內交要譽矣故學也
者所以去其矜飾矯强之勞而歸之於自
然者也此所謂以人合天而其知未始不
一也此聖賢所學之大較也春秋之時有
孔子者出以天縱之聖具上知之資自其
爲兒時固已知陳俎豆設禮容大與人異
矣及其長而道益尊四方之士從之游者
蓋三千焉此自古以來未有盛焉者宜若
無俟於學矣而孔子方且好古敏求焉晝
punctuated:
矜飾矯强之勞者也。是故平旦而好惡相近焉，孩提之愛親敬長而不學不慮焉，乍見孺子入井而怵惕惻隱之心生焉，皆所謂天也，生知也，自然者也，而何待於學耶？蓋聖人者，順此者也，而亦必學焉者，戒慎恐懼以求不失其常而已，非有加也。賢人者，其自然亦與此同也，而苟不學焉，則好惡相近者，有時而牿亡之矣；愛親敬長者，有不能達之天下者矣；見孺子入井而怵惕惻隱焉者，有時而內交要譽矣。故學也者，所以去其矜飾矯强之勞而歸之於自然者也。此所謂以人合天，而其知未始不一也。此聖賢所學之大較也。
春秋之時，有孔子者出，以天縱之聖，具上知之資。自其爲兒時，固已知陳俎豆、設禮容，大與人異矣。及其長而道益尊，四方之士從之游者，蓋三千焉。此自古以來未有盛焉者，宜若無俟於學矣，而孔子方且好古敏求焉，晝
translation_en:
…the toil of affected embellishment and forced effort. Thus, in the early morning, people’s likes and dislikes approximate those of others; young children love their parents and respect their elders without learning or deliberation; and upon suddenly seeing a child about to fall into a well, a heart of alarm and compassion arises. These are all what we call Heaven, innate knowledge, and spontaneity. What need, then, is there to await learning? Sages follow this, yet they too must learn: through vigilance and apprehension, they seek only to preserve its constant norm, adding nothing to it. Worthy people possess the same spontaneity. But if they do not learn, the likes and dislikes that approximate those of others may at times be fettered and destroyed; their love of parents and respect for elders may fail to extend throughout the world; and their alarm and compassion on seeing a child about to fall into a well may at times turn into attempts to gain the parents’ friendship or win praise. Learning therefore serves to remove the toil of affected embellishment and forced effort and return people to spontaneity. This is what is meant by uniting the human with Heaven: the knowledge involved has never been other than one. Such is the broad outline of the learning of sages and worthies.
During the Spring and Autumn period, Kongzi appeared, a sage endowed by Heaven with the capacity for the highest wisdom. Even as a child, he already knew how to arrange sacrificial stands and vessels and enact ritual deportment, differing greatly from others. As he grew older and his Way became increasingly esteemed, some three thousand scholars from all quarters associated with him as disciples. This flourishing had no precedent since antiquity. It would seem that he should have had no further need of learning, yet Kongzi still loved antiquity and diligently sought knowledge, by day…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忘食夜忘寢學不厭而誨且不倦焉者何
也蓋誠有見於道之無窮而學不至於知
天者非聞道也故曰下學而上達知我者
其天乎是生知亦未始不學也乃謂孔子
之上而復有所謂生知者非然矣孔門之
徒惟子路爲最勇觀其初見之時佩豭舞
劒而以爲學之無益則其人可知也及聞
孔子忠仁之論括羽鏃礪之譬遂儒服委
質受教焉而卒躋於升堂之列蓋雖未入
===
于室而非學不至是矣孟子生於戰國之
際方其嬉戲爲墓間事踴躍築埋固所謂
閭巷子也及聞母氏斷機之訓遂勤脩不
息而卒願學孔子觀其七篇仁義炳若日
星則自洙泗以後一人而已此非問學之
功而有是乎以至謝顯道之不謁執政羅
仲素之爲南州冠冕固皆所謂載道之器
也然顯道以去矜學仲素以潛思力行學
則亦非無本而然者不然則更經利舉之
punctuated:
忘食，夜忘寢，學不厭而誨且不倦焉者，何也？蓋誠有見於道之無窮，而學不至於知天者，非聞道也。故曰：「下學而上達，知我者其天乎！」是生知亦未始不學也。乃謂孔子之上而復有所謂生知者，非然矣。

孔門之徒，惟子路爲最勇。觀其初見之時，佩豭舞劒，而以爲學之無益，則其人可知也。及聞孔子忠仁之論、括羽鏃礪之譬，遂儒服委質受教焉，而卒躋於升堂之列。蓋雖未入于室，而非學不至是矣。

孟子生於戰國之際，方其嬉戲爲墓間事，踴躍築埋，固所謂閭巷子也。及聞母氏斷機之訓，遂勤脩不息，而卒願學孔子。觀其七篇，仁義炳若日星，則自洙泗以後一人而已。此非問學之功而有是乎？

以至謝顯道之不謁執政，羅仲素之爲南州冠冕，固皆所謂載道之器也。然顯道以去矜學，仲素以潛思力行學，則亦非無本而然者。不然，則更經利舉之
translation_en:
…forgetting to eat, forgetting to sleep at night, tireless in learning and unwearied in teaching—why was this? Surely it was because he truly perceived that the Way is inexhaustible, and that anyone whose learning does not reach an understanding of Heaven has not heard the Way. Thus he said: “I learn what is below and attain what is above. Is it not Heaven that understands me?” Even one born with knowledge, then, has never dispensed with learning. To claim that above Confucius there was yet another sort of person supposedly “born with knowledge” is mistaken.

Among Confucius’s disciples, Zilu was the most courageous. Consider how, when he first met Confucius, he wore a boar ornament and brandished a sword, believing learning to be useless: from this we can discern his character. But after hearing Confucius’s discussion of loyalty and benevolence, and his analogy of fitting feathers to an arrow and sharpening its point, he donned scholarly robes, presented an introductory gift, and received instruction. In the end he joined the ranks of those who had “ascended the hall.” Although he had not yet “entered the inner chamber,” without learning he could not have reached this point.

Mengzi was born during the Warring States period. When, at play, he imitated activities among the tombs, leaping about, building graves, and burying things, he was certainly just what one would call an ordinary neighborhood child. After hearing his mother’s admonition when she cut the cloth on her loom, however, he cultivated himself diligently without cease and ultimately aspired to learn from Confucius. In his seven books, benevolence and righteousness shine as brightly as the sun and stars. Since the teaching beside the Zhu and Si rivers, he alone had attained such stature. Could this have come about without the work of inquiry and learning?

Then there were Xie Xiandao, who would not pay a visit to those holding power, and Luo Zhongsu, who stood foremost among the men of the southern region. Both were surely what are called vessels capable of bearing the Way. Yet Xiandao pursued learning by casting off conceit, and Zhongsu by deep reflection and strenuous practice. Their achievements, too, were not without a foundation. Otherwise, through the practices of “reworking the classics for advantage in the examinations” [?]…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
習卒不免為功名之士而所謂驚汗浹背
者亦不過一時羞惡之良而已其何能以
有成耶他如陸子靜自謂做人不倚師友
載籍楊中立所見一定不須窮索朱仲晦
稱其為天資出人非假學力者若於所謂
生知者似也然子靜之學又自謂不出於
人情事勢物理之外而中立之力學通經
亦非徒恃其天資之美而已者至其禪學
之疑蓋不知者泥於尊德性之一言而晚
===
出一節毀三經闢和議於世敎亦有賴焉
豈得以其應時宰之聘而遂詬之耶由是
觀之道不可離也而人卒離道者則不學
之過也可學者人也學至乎純亦不已而
性通焉者則知天之極也此天人之所以
合一也故曰天者自然而已人之學道者
亦惟求其自然者而已嗚呼天豈遠於人
哉人之心固天也人自不知耳今夫人之
日用飲食語默動靜之間一闔一闢一張
punctuated: 習，卒不免為功名之士，而所謂驚汗浹背者，亦不過一時羞惡之良而已，其何能以有成耶？他如陸子靜自謂做人不倚師友載籍，楊中立所見一定，不須窮索，朱仲晦稱其為天資出人、非假學力者，若於所謂生知者似也。然子靜之學，又自謂不出於人情事勢物理之外，而中立之力學通經，亦非徒恃其天資之美而已者。至其禪學之疑，蓋不知者泥於尊德性之一言，而晚出一節，毀三經、闢和議，於世敎亦有賴焉，豈得以其應時宰之聘而遂詬之耶？由是觀之，道不可離也，而人卒離道者，則不學之過也。可學者，人也；學至乎純亦不已，而性通焉者，則知天之極也。此天人之所以合一也。故曰：「天者，自然而已。」人之學道者，亦惟求其自然者而已。嗚呼！天豈遠於人哉？人之心固天也，人自不知耳。今夫人之日用飲食、語默動靜之間，一闔一闢，一張
translation_en:
…such habits, they would ultimately remain men intent on achievement and reputation. Their reputed alarm, which left their backs drenched in sweat, would amount merely to a momentary stirring of their innate sense of shame and aversion to wrongdoing. How could they achieve anything thereby?

Other examples include Lu Zijing, who said that in conducting himself he did not depend on teachers, friends, or written works, and Yang Zhongli, whose understanding, once settled, required no further exhaustive inquiry. Zhu Zhonghui described them as possessing natural endowments surpassing those of others, without relying on the strength of learning. They seem to resemble those said to possess knowledge from birth. Yet Zijing also said that his learning did not go beyond human feelings, the circumstances of affairs, and the principles of things; and Zhongli’s diligent study and mastery of the Classics likewise show that he did not merely rely on his fine natural endowments. As for suspicions that his learning was Chan Buddhism, these arose because those who did not understand seized upon the single phrase “honoring the moral nature.” His conduct on entering office late in life [?]—denouncing the Three Classics and opposing peace negotiations—also served the moral teaching of the age. How could one revile him merely because he accepted an invitation from the chief minister of the time?

Viewed in this light, the Way cannot be departed from; when people nevertheless depart from it, the fault lies in their failure to learn. It is human beings who can learn. When learning reaches purity and still does not cease, so that one’s nature becomes fully penetrated, this is the ultimate attainment in knowing Heaven. This is how Heaven and humanity become one. Thus it is said: “Heaven is simply what is naturally so.” Those who study the Way seek only to attain that natural condition. Alas! How could Heaven be far from humanity? The human heart is itself Heaven; people simply do not recognize it. Now, in people’s daily activities—in eating and drinking, speaking and remaining silent, moving and resting—there is a closing and an opening, a tightening…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一弛所以出之不窮而應之甚裕者蓋自
有天則存焉雖以孔子之聖亦不過默識
乎此耳故意必固我之盡無溫良恭儉讓
之皆備仕止久速之各當其可者蓋已合
乎自然之道而與天爲一矣若孟子固願
學孔子者而氣象巖巖猶不免焉宜乎諸
子之有所未逮也雖然亦存乎其學耳拘
繭滯礙非學不通發揚蹈厲非學不斂簡
伉尊大非學不遜陰幽暗塞非學不暢儇
===
佻捷敏非學不靜盛麗紛華非學不澹汗
漫遺落非學不密學之學之少而習焉長
而安焉老而忘焉則其去聖賢不遠而自
然之道將有與天爲一者矣愚生自束髮
讀書不知學爲何事蓋囿于其習者久之
而後知所以求道也乃者聞執事之教而
惕乎其有省焉至于所謂自有者則茫乎
其未之有也惟進而教之使卒有聞焉則
幸矣
punctuated: 一弛，所以出之不窮而應之甚裕者，蓋自有天則存焉。雖以孔子之聖，亦不過默識乎此耳。故意必固我之盡無，溫良恭儉讓之皆備，仕止久速之各當其可者，蓋已合乎自然之道而與天爲一矣。若孟子，固願學孔子者，而氣象巖巖猶不免焉，宜乎諸子之有所未逮也。雖然，亦存乎其學耳。拘繭滯礙，非學不通；發揚蹈厲，非學不斂；簡伉尊大，非學不遜；陰幽暗塞，非學不暢；儇佻捷敏，非學不靜；盛麗紛華，非學不澹；汗漫遺落，非學不密。學之，學之！少而習焉，長而安焉，老而忘焉，則其去聖賢不遠，而自然之道將有與天爲一者矣。愚生自束髮讀書，不知學爲何事，蓋囿于其習者久之，而後知所以求道也。乃者聞執事之教，而惕乎其有省焉。至于所謂自有者，則茫乎其未之有也。惟進而教之，使卒有聞焉，則幸矣。
translation_en: …and a relaxation: the reason these issue forth inexhaustibly and respond with such ample ease is that Heaven’s principles are inherently present within them. Even Kongzi, for all his sageliness, did no more than silently apprehend this. Thus his complete freedom from preconceptions, insistence on certainty, obstinacy, and egotism; his full possession of gentleness, goodness, reverence, frugality, and deference; and his unfailing appropriateness in taking office or withdrawing, remaining long or departing quickly—all arose because he had already accorded with the Way of natural spontaneity and become one with Heaven. As for Mengzi, he certainly aspired to learn from Kongzi, yet he still could not avoid an air of towering severity. It is therefore understandable that the other masters fell short in some respects. Even so, it all depends upon their learning. Those confined as if in a cocoon [?] and impeded cannot become free-flowing without learning; those exuberant and impetuous cannot become restrained without learning; those disdainful and haughty cannot become deferential without learning; those inwardly obscure and blocked cannot become open without learning; those frivolous and quick-witted cannot become tranquil without learning; those given to splendid display and profuse ornament cannot become simple without learning; those diffuse and careless cannot become meticulous without learning. Learn it, learn it! Practise it in youth, become at ease with it in maturity, and forget it in old age: then one will not be far from the sages and worthies, and through the Way of natural spontaneity one may become one with Heaven. Since first binding up my hair in adolescence and beginning to read, I, your humble student, did not know what learning was for. Only after long confinement within habitual practices did I come to understand how to seek the Way. Recently, hearing your instruction, I was stirred to self-examination and gained some insight. As for what you call that which is inherently present, however, I remain bewildered and have yet to attain it. If you would grant me further instruction, so that I might finally gain understanding, I would count myself fortunate.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第五問
陳絢
同考試官學正廖批議論詳悉區畫措置之
方鑿鑿可行非心思淵邃識見卓越曷能至此
考試官教諭萬批訏謨弘略動合機宜足
占遠器
考試官教授鄒批是能究心時務者錄之
弭盜之術得人為上得策次之夫籌幄之
士一借箸掉舌而能折衝樽俎之上者計
===
策工也乃謂其次於得人何哉計策誠工
矣而苟非其人則如畫餅膠舟何濟於用
故曰弭盜之術在得人得人者得仁人也
仁人者以社稷生靈為一體而計功謀利
之心有不存焉者也誠得是人而布之上
下庶位之間則東粤之寇不足平矣稽古
唐虞之際時雍風動其治盛矣而寇賊姦
宄蠻夷猾夏亦不免焉然有皐以明刑禹
以誓師故卒綏而格之得人故也東粤介
punctuated:
第五問
陳絢
同考試官學正廖批：議論詳悉，區畫措置之方，鑿鑿可行。非心思淵邃、識見卓越，曷能至此？
考試官教諭萬批：訏謨弘略，動合機宜，足占遠器。
考試官教授鄒批：是能究心時務者，錄之。
弭盜之術，得人為上，得策次之。夫籌幄之士，一借箸掉舌，而能折衝樽俎之上者，計策工也。乃謂其次於得人，何哉？計策誠工矣，而苟非其人，則如畫餅膠舟，何濟於用？故曰：弭盜之術，在得人。得人者，得仁人也。仁人者，以社稷生靈為一體，而計功謀利之心有不存焉者也。誠得是人，而布之上下庶位之間，則東粤之寇不足平矣。稽古唐虞之際，時雍風動，其治盛矣，而寇賊姦宄、蠻夷猾夏，亦不免焉。然有皐以明刑，禹以誓師，故卒綏而格之，得人故也。東粤介
translation_en:
Fifth Question
Chen Xuan
Associate Examiner Liao, School Instructor, comments: “The argument is thorough and detailed, and the proposed measures for planning and implementation are demonstrably practicable. Without profound thought and outstanding discernment, how could one attain this?”
Examiner Wan, Instructor, comments: “His grand plans and broad strategies invariably suit the circumstances. These suffice to show his capacity for great future responsibilities.”
Examiner Zou, Professor, comments: “Here is someone capable of applying himself earnestly to current affairs. Accept him.”
In the art of suppressing banditry, securing the right people comes first; securing the right plans comes second. Now, a strategist in the command tent may borrow chopsticks to lay out his plans and deploy his eloquence, thereby repelling aggression over the ceremonial wine vessels and dishes of a diplomatic gathering. This is skill in planning. Why, then, should it be ranked below securing the right people? Plans may indeed be skillful, but without the right person they are like a painted cake or a boat glued fast: what practical use can they serve? Thus I say that the art of suppressing banditry lies in securing the right people. Securing the right people means securing benevolent people. Benevolent people regard the state and its living subjects as one body with themselves, and harbor no thought of calculating personal merit or seeking profit. If such people are truly found and placed throughout the higher and lower offices, then pacifying the bandits of Dongyue would present little difficulty [?]. Looking back to the age of Tang and Yu, harmony prevailed and the people responded to moral influence as to the wind: their government flourished. Yet even then they could not escape bandits, malefactors within and without, and the Man and Yi peoples disturbing the central realm. But Gao clarified the punishments, and Yu exhorted the troops; thus they ultimately pacified these peoples and brought them to submission. This was because they had secured the right people. Dongyue is situated…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
在五嶺之外山川阻深盜賊多有故其種
類有曰猺獞曰黎曰倭曰浪數者蓋自漢
入中國以來而已然矣彌竟山海出沒無
時畫計策者曰勦與撫夫制禦之術豈復
有出於此兩者之外哉顧其人用之有效
不效耳何也蓋勦與撫人人談之也勦而
撫撫而勦闔闢變化神其用於不測者非
有仁人之心運焉不能也今夫官府親民
布德達隱久之情孚漸爾面革此撫也厲
===
兵揚鼓申嚴約束陳師在郊力窮請死然
後責以無禮隨宜安集此勦而撫者也乃
今未諭施惠惠褻不懷方疑示信信反成
詐兼之墨夫利其金帛游徼鼓其熒惑故
納款未幾而嘯聚復熾矣撫之不可於是
乎勦然勦有大征有鵰勦大征者合數道
之師儲竟歲之糧掃穴犁庭期無噍類是
矣然猾酋先遯無辜濫及兵多費侈不可
數也其惟鵰勦乎賊眾俶擾螘聚蜂屯我
punctuated: 在五嶺之外，山川阻深，盜賊多有。故其種類有曰猺獞、曰黎、曰倭、曰浪，數者蓋自漢入中國以來而已然矣。彌竟山海，出沒無時。畫計策者曰勦與撫。夫制禦之術，豈復有出於此兩者之外哉？顧其人用之有效不效耳。何也？蓋勦與撫，人人談之也；勦而撫，撫而勦，闔闢變化，神其用於不測者，非有仁人之心運焉不能也。今夫官府親民，布德達隱，久之情孚，漸爾面革，此撫也。厲兵揚鼓，申嚴約束，陳師在郊，力窮請死，然後責以無禮，隨宜安集，此勦而撫者也。乃今未諭施惠，惠褻不懷；方疑示信，信反成詐。兼之墨夫利其金帛，游徼鼓其熒惑，故納款未幾，而嘯聚復熾矣。撫之不可，於是乎勦。然勦有大征，有鵰勦。大征者，合數道之師，儲竟歲之糧，掃穴犁庭，期無噍類，是矣。然猾酋先遯，無辜濫及，兵多費侈，不可數也。其惟鵰勦乎？賊眾俶擾，螘聚蜂屯，我
translation_en:
…lies beyond the Five Ridges, where the mountains and rivers are rugged and secluded, and bandits abound. Their various kinds are called Yao and Tong, Li, Wo, and Lang [?]. These groups have apparently existed as such ever since the region was incorporated into China under the Han. They range throughout the mountains and coastal waters, appearing and disappearing at unpredictable times. Those who devise strategies speak of suppression and pacification. Indeed, could any means of controlling them lie outside these two? It is simply a matter of whether those employing them achieve results. Why is this? Everyone speaks of suppression and pacification; but to suppress and then pacify, to pacify and then suppress, opening and closing, varying and transforming one’s methods, and deploying them with unfathomable subtlety—none can accomplish this without the guiding heart of a humane person.

When officials draw close to the people, spread benevolence, and learn of hidden suffering, over time their sentiments inspire trust, and gradually the people reform their outward conduct: this is pacification. When officials ready their weapons and sound their drums, reiterate strict commands, and array troops outside the settlements, until the enemy’s strength is exhausted and they submit themselves to death, then rebuke them for their disrespect and settle them as circumstances require: this is suppression followed by pacification.

Nowadays, however, favors are bestowed before understanding has been reached; those favors are treated lightly and win no allegiance. Good faith is displayed while suspicion still prevails, and that good faith instead becomes deception. Moreover, corrupt officials covet their gold and silk, while patrol officers compound their confusion. Thus, scarcely have they submitted before they again gather in armed bands with renewed intensity. When pacification proves impossible, suppression follows.

Suppression, however, comprises both major expeditions and targeted operations. A major expedition combines armies advancing along several routes, stores provisions for an entire year, sweeps out the enemy’s lairs and plows up their courts, intending to leave no survivor. Yet the crafty chieftains escape beforehand, the innocent are indiscriminately caught up in the destruction, and the troops are numerous and the expenditure extravagant. Such expeditions cannot be undertaken repeatedly. Should one then rely on targeted operations? When the bandit host rises in turmoil, gathering like ants and massing like bees, we…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乃攻其不備搴旗梟俊餘衆戢斂束手歸
降或稔惡不悛中情叵測則又陽示弭兵
陰從要擊此撫而勦者也乃今旣獲輯寧
復加掩襲被虜歸還槩行殄戮希功冒賞
冤抑滋多以致向善之念漸微從邪之習
愈錮故鐃歌甫畢而羽檄復馳矣自非仁
人之心神明變化則此兩策者有不倒行
而逆施耶然則制禦之術亦惟明於此兩
者而難易先後自較然矣或謂禦山寇易
===
禦海寇難蓋以雲帆風浪飄忽無定欲擊
而殪之難也然操檣楫則爲海持梃刃則
爲山此何常之有惟得其人則防海者扼
之於海而不能登山防山者蒐之於山而
不能入海矣奚難易之足云耶或謂治賊
如治病當先腹心而後手足蓋以黎岐中
盤傜僮外據其治之宜有先後也然腹心
有病則手足固爲之捍翼手足有病則腹
心亦爲之不寧總之爲病耳惟得其人則
punctuated: 乃攻其不備，搴旗梟俊，餘衆戢斂，束手歸降。或稔惡不悛，中情叵測，則又陽示弭兵，陰從要擊，此撫而勦者也。乃今旣獲輯寧，復加掩襲；被虜歸還，槩行殄戮，希功冒賞，冤抑滋多，以致向善之念漸微，從邪之習愈錮。故鐃歌甫畢，而羽檄復馳矣。自非仁人之心，神明變化，則此兩策者有不倒行而逆施耶？然則制禦之術，亦惟明於此兩者，而難易先後自較然矣。或謂禦山寇易，禦海寇難，蓋以雲帆風浪，飄忽無定，欲擊而殪之難也。然操檣楫則爲海，持梃刃則爲山，此何常之有？惟得其人，則防海者扼之於海，而不能登山；防山者蒐之於山，而不能入海矣。奚難易之足云耶？或謂治賊如治病，當先腹心而後手足，蓋以黎岐中盤，傜僮外據，其治之宜有先後也。然腹心有病，則手足固爲之捍翼；手足有病，則腹心亦爲之不寧。總之爲病耳。惟得其人，則
translation_en:
…then attack them unprepared, seize their banners, and behead their leading men. The remaining followers restrain themselves and submit without resistance. If some persist in evil without reforming, their true intentions unfathomable, we outwardly signal an end to hostilities while secretly moving to intercept and attack them. This is pacification followed by suppression. Yet nowadays, once peace has been secured, surprise attacks are launched again; those returning from captivity are indiscriminately slaughtered. In pursuit of military credit and undeserved rewards, injustices multiply, so that the inclination toward goodness gradually weakens and the habit of following evil becomes ever more entrenched. Thus, scarcely have the victory songs ended before urgent military dispatches speed forth again. Unless one has a benevolent heart and adapts with inspired discernment, how could these two policies fail to be applied perversely and in reverse? The art of control therefore consists simply in understanding these two approaches; their relative difficulty and proper sequence will then become clear of themselves.

Some say that defending against mountain bandits is easy, but defending against sea raiders is difficult. This is presumably because their lofty sails, amid wind and waves, move unpredictably, making it difficult to strike and destroy them. Yet when they handle masts and oars, they are sea raiders; when they wield clubs and blades, they are mountain bandits. What fixed distinction is there? Provided the right men are appointed, those guarding the coast will hold them at sea so that they cannot ascend the mountains, while those guarding the mountains will hunt them down there so that they cannot take to the sea. Why speak of one task as easy and the other as difficult?

Some say that dealing with bandits is like treating an illness: one should attend first to the belly and heart, and afterward to the hands and feet. This is presumably because the Li and Qi occupy the interior, while the Yao and Tong hold the outer regions, so that there ought to be a sequence in dealing with them. Yet when the belly and heart are diseased, the hands and feet naturally serve to protect and support them; when the hands and feet are diseased, the belly and heart are likewise disturbed. In either case, it is illness. Provided the right men are appointed, then…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
刊山通道之謀自萬全而不必惜其費土
舍招主之設自率訓而無所肆其詭矣又
何先後之可言耶合而言之徭黎者鳥言
夷面荒憬不類然重信約刀耕火種大都
與吾民同也其馴者宜撫黠者宜勦倭醜
者以舟爲家以剽掠爲糧非言語可化宜
勦不宜撫浪賊者游手游食逃租避罪爲
徭黎倭醜作耳目附山則冦山附海則冦
海利則聚害則散撫之在貰罪散黨安生
===
業寛逮繋薄斂省刑勦之在譏偵覰糾舍
匿禁私餉殲渠魁而脅從罔治也然而非
其人不可也蓋撫勦之策固所當講而所
以善用其策於不窮者惟在百執事以仁
存心分任其責耳如填撫百姓興敎化省
繇役聯保伍使守望相助責在守令曉暢
軍事謹尺籍伍符遇敵先登不愛其死責
在將領旬宣勅法簡師庀賦激勸有司賢
不肖責在岳牧監司別功罪明賞罰寛假
punctuated:
刊山通道之謀自萬全，而不必惜其費；土舍招主之設自率訓，而無所肆其詭矣。又何先後之可言耶？合而言之，徭黎者，鳥言夷面，荒憬不類，然重信約，刀耕火種，大都與吾民同也。其馴者宜撫，黠者宜勦。倭醜者，以舟爲家，以剽掠爲糧，非言語可化，宜勦不宜撫。浪賊者，游手游食，逃租避罪，爲徭黎倭醜作耳目，附山則冦山，附海則冦海，利則聚，害則散。撫之在貰罪散黨，安生業，寛逮繋，薄斂省刑；勦之在譏偵覰，糾舍匿，禁私餉，殲渠魁，而脅從罔治也。
然而非其人不可也。蓋撫勦之策固所當講，而所以善用其策於不窮者，惟在百執事以仁存心，分任其責耳。如填撫百姓，興敎化，省繇役，聯保伍，使守望相助，責在守令；曉暢軍事，謹尺籍伍符，遇敵先登，不愛其死，責在將領；旬宣勅法，簡師庀賦，激勸有司賢不肖，責在岳牧監司；別功罪，明賞罰，寛假
translation_en:
…plans to clear the mountains and open roads will naturally be fully secure, without any need to begrudge the expense; arrangements for native officers and recruitment headmen [?] will naturally secure obedience to instructions, leaving no scope for their deceit. What, then, is there to say about which should come first or last? Taken together, the Yao and Li speak like birds and have alien faces; remote and uncultivated, they are unlike us. Yet they value good faith and agreements, and practice slash-and-burn cultivation: in most respects they are the same as our common people. Those who are tractable should be pacified; those who are crafty should be suppressed. The Japanese villains make boats their homes and plunder their sustenance. Words cannot reform them: they should be suppressed, not pacified. The roving bandits live in idleness, evade taxes, and flee punishment, serving as eyes and ears for the Yao, Li, and Japanese villains. When they attach themselves to the mountains, they raid the mountains; when they attach themselves to the sea, they raid the sea. They gather when there is profit and scatter when there is danger. Pacifying them consists in pardoning their crimes, dispersing their bands, securing their livelihoods, relaxing arrests and imprisonment, reducing levies, and lessening punishments. Suppressing them consists in investigation, reconnaissance, and surveillance [?], bringing to account those who shelter and conceal them, prohibiting private provisioning, and destroying their ringleaders, while leaving those coerced into joining them unpunished.
Yet none of this can be accomplished without the right men. Policies of pacification and suppression certainly require deliberation, but employing those policies effectively amid inexhaustible contingencies depends solely on all officials keeping benevolence in their hearts and each assuming his share of responsibility. Thus, settling and comforting the common people, promoting moral instruction, reducing labor service, organizing households into mutual-security groups, and ensuring that they help one another keep watch and guard are the responsibilities of prefects and magistrates. Thoroughly understanding military affairs, carefully maintaining troop registers and unit tallies, leading the advance against the enemy, and not begrudging their lives are the responsibilities of military commanders. Spreading imperial beneficence and enforcing the laws, selecting troops and arranging revenues, and spurring and encouraging officials, worthy and unworthy alike, are the responsibilities of regional governors and surveillance officials. Distinguishing merit from wrongdoing, making rewards and punishments clear, and allowing latitude …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文法而考其成功責在部使者選將調兵
明節制發縱指示酌緩急而用之責在督
府誠使督府部使者以是行之於上岳牧
監司將領守令以是行之於下上下同心
文武聿力流通實意剔去浮文省簿書期
會之煩而加意民瘼去奔走迎送之苦而
專力兵防蓋所謂以社稷生靈爲一體而
計功謀利之心有不存焉者也如此行之
而盜有不息者否矣苟不得其人而惟日
===
紛紛焉討求制禦之術卽使良平復出將
焉用之頃者仰荷
聖天子憫念海隅蒼生一時布在上下庶位者
皆出
廟堂愼選則愚生前所謂仁人者豈少哉顧
羣孽之航浮箐伏伺釁而動者尚多而嶺
海之間猶未有按堵期也則夫上下同心
舉萬全之策以慰更生之望者宜莫踰於
今日矣愚生第拭目俟之
punctuated: 文法而考其成功，責在部使者；選將調兵，明節制，發縱指示，酌緩急而用之，責在督府。誠使督府、部使者以是行之於上，岳牧、監司、將領、守令以是行之於下，上下同心，文武聿力，流通實意，剔去浮文，省簿書期會之煩而加意民瘼，去奔走迎送之苦而專力兵防，蓋所謂以社稷生靈爲一體，而計功謀利之心有不存焉者也。如此行之，而盜有不息者，否矣！苟不得其人，而惟日紛紛焉討求制禦之術，卽使良平復出，將焉用之？頃者，仰荷聖天子憫念海隅蒼生，一時布在上下庶位者，皆出廟堂愼選，則愚生前所謂仁人者，豈少哉？顧羣孽之航浮箐伏、伺釁而動者尚多，而嶺海之間猶未有按堵期也。則夫上下同心，舉萬全之策，以慰更生之望者，宜莫踰於今日矣！愚生第拭目俟之。
translation_en:
…procedural rules, and judging their actual achievements: this is the responsibility of the regional commissioners. Selecting generals and deploying troops, making the chain of command clear, directing operations, and employing forces according to the urgency of circumstances: this is the responsibility of the supreme commander. If the supreme commander and regional commissioners truly acted on these principles above, and the provincial and prefectural governors, surveillance commissioners, military commanders, prefects, and magistrates acted on them below, those above and below would be of one mind, and civil and military officials would work together. They would communicate their sincere intentions and eliminate empty formalities, reduce the burdens of paperwork and reporting deadlines while giving greater attention to the people's sufferings, and dispense with the toil of rushing about to welcome and see off officials while concentrating their efforts on military defense. This is what is meant by treating the state and its people as one body, without any thought of seeking personal credit or advantage. If matters were conducted in this way, could banditry fail to cease? Surely not! If the right men are not obtained, and officials merely spend each day busily searching for techniques of control, then even if Zhang Liang and Chen Ping reappeared, what use could be made of them?
Recently, we have gratefully benefited from the sagely Son of Heaven's compassionate concern for the common people of this coastal region. Those now serving in the various higher and lower offices have all been carefully selected by the imperial court. Can there then be any shortage of the benevolent men of whom I, this humble student, spoke earlier? Yet there are still many evildoers who move about in boats or lurk in bamboo thickets, watching for opportunities to act, and there is still no prospect of settled peace in the region of the mountains and sea. Surely there could be no more fitting time than today for those above and below to unite in purpose and put into effect a comprehensive strategy, fulfilling the people's hope of life renewed! I, this humble student, can only wipe my eyes clear and await the result.

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
隆慶庚午廣東鄉試錄成濟
川從品藝之後竊系言于末
簡曰嘗讀西漢書陸賈綰方
寸之印銜其主命遨遊南越
爲後使臣所歆豔知五嶺外
爲一大區會也欲攬擷其勝
===
而無繇頃應聘度庾關見矗
巘崇岡不可名狀詢之自玆
山迤邐以南其嶙峋截嶭突
然聳三十二峯於羅陽之界
者羅浮山也比理楫浮凌湞
入三江襟帶灑沈總之望靈
洲以達朝夕之池浩蕩淼茫
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

隆慶庚午，廣東鄉試錄成。濟川從品藝之後，竊系言于末簡曰：嘗讀《西漢書》，陸賈綰方寸之印，銜其主命，遨遊南越，爲後使臣所歆豔，知五嶺外爲一大區會也。欲攬擷其勝而無繇。頃應聘度庾關，見矗巘崇岡，不可名狀。詢之，自玆山迤邐以南，其嶙峋截嶭、突然聳三十二峯於羅陽之界者，羅浮山也。比理楫浮凌湞，入三江，襟帶灑沈，總之望靈洲，以達朝夕之池，浩蕩淼茫。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the gengwu year of Longqing [1570], the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination was completed. Having participated in evaluating the examination compositions, I, Jichuan, venture to append these words to its closing pages:

I once read in the History of the Former Han how Lu Jia, wearing a seal an inch square and bearing his ruler’s commission, traveled through Nanyue, becoming the envy of later envoys. From this I learned that beyond the Five Ranges lay a great regional center. I wished to take in its splendid sights, but had no opportunity.

Recently, accepting an invitation, I crossed Yu Pass and saw towering peaks and lofty ridges beyond description. Upon inquiry, I learned that, along the mountains stretching southward from here, the rugged, sheer heights that abruptly rise as thirty-two peaks within the territory of Luoyang are Mount Luofu. Then, taking to the oars, I traveled along the Ling and Zhen rivers [?] and entered the Three Rivers. Encircled by waters, amid spray and depths [?], I looked toward Lingzhou and proceeded to the basin of the morning and evening tides, vast and boundless …

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
瀰天浴日濟川乃躊躇四顧
奪目駭心蓋羅浮鎮山渤澥
巨浸大觀具在矣扃鎖元氣
磅礴鬱蟠宜有英能俊乂鍾
於其間爰蒐往牒代有聞人
至於
國朝以德業炳彪一時者後先
===
趾美信造物所鍾不虛也曁
得閱多士之文閎意眇指祖
義本仁昔人評文謂峭拔千
尋波瀾萬頃乃今竝見之可
不謂盛與聖門立教德行為
先玆文藝末耳執是而可悉
多士醞藉固未敢盡必第心
punctuated:
瀰天浴日，濟川乃躊躇四顧，奪目駭心。蓋羅浮鎮山、渤澥巨浸，大觀具在矣。扃鎖元氣，磅礴鬱蟠，宜有英能俊乂鍾於其間。爰蒐往牒，代有聞人。至於國朝，以德業炳彪一時者，後先趾美，信造物所鍾不虛也。
曁得閱多士之文，閎意眇指，祖義本仁。昔人評文，謂峭拔千尋、波瀾萬頃，乃今竝見之，可不謂盛與？聖門立教，德行為先，玆文藝末耳。執是而可悉多士醞藉，固未敢盡必，第心
translation_en:
…stretching across the sky and bathing the sun. Crossing the waters, I paused and gazed in every direction, my eyes dazzled and my heart awestruck. Here indeed were magnificent sights in their fullness: Luofu, the guardian mountain, and the vast expanse of the sea. Holding the primordial vital force within, mighty and densely coiled, this landscape ought surely to concentrate its powers in outstanding and capable men. I therefore searched the records of the past and found men of renown in every age. Under our own dynasty, those whose virtue and achievements shone brilliantly in their day have followed one another in excellence. Truly, what the Creator has concentrated here has not been bestowed in vain.
When I came to read the candidates’ compositions, I found expansive ideas and subtle meanings, taking righteousness as their guide and benevolence as their foundation. Writers of old, appraising literary works, spoke of sheer heights rising a thousand fathoms and billowing waves spreading over ten thousand qing. Now I have seen both together: can this not be called a flourishing age? In the teachings of the Sage’s school, virtuous conduct comes first; literary accomplishment is merely secondary. I certainly would not presume to assert that these writings reveal all the candidates’ cultivated depth. Yet the mind…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之精微因言以宣由多士之
文以概其中亦庶乎瞰聖域
之壺奧窺斯道之涯涘者故
陟羅浮必起於谿徑由谿徑
而可躋其巔矣探海必始於
支流由支流而可泝其深矣
文藝者固道德之谿徑支流
===
也不可以觀人乎哉方今
聖人御極嘉意右文教化浹於章
縫弓旌徧乎嵓穴多士瞻仰
涵濡已非一日茲得與計偕
縣次續食行將釋短褐據文
軒奉其薄技展采錯事必厚
自培養爭相濯磨攄涓埃之
punctuated:
之精微，因言以宣。由多士之文以概其中，亦庶乎瞰聖域之壺奧、窺斯道之涯涘者。故陟羅浮，必起於谿徑，由谿徑而可躋其巔矣；探海，必始於支流，由支流而可泝其深矣。文藝者，固道德之谿徑支流也，不可以觀人乎哉？
方今聖人御極，嘉意右文，教化浹於章縫，弓旌徧乎嵓穴。多士瞻仰涵濡，已非一日。茲得與計偕，縣次續食，行將釋短褐、據文軒，奉其薄技，展采錯事，必厚自培養，爭相濯磨，攄涓埃之
translation_en:
…the subtleties of the mind are expressed through words. By judging the inner character of these many scholars from their writings, one may come close to looking into the innermost recesses [?] of the realm of sagehood and glimpsing the shores of this Way. Thus, to ascend Luofu, one must begin on paths through the ravines; by following these paths, one can reach its summit. To explore the sea, one must begin with its tributaries; by following these tributaries, one can trace its depths. Literary accomplishment is indeed the ravine path and tributary of moral virtue. Can it not serve to reveal a person’s character?
Now the sage sovereign occupies the throne, graciously intent upon honoring literary learning. His transforming instruction permeates the ranks of scholars in their ceremonial caps, while the bows and banners summoning worthy men reach even secluded mountain caves. These many scholars have long looked up to him and been steeped in his beneficent influence. Now they may travel to the capital with the tribute-account delegations, receiving provisions at successive counties along the way. Soon they will cast off their coarse short garments and ride in ornamented carriages, offering their modest abilities, displaying their talents, and undertaking official duties. They must cultivate themselves deeply and vie with one another in cleansing and polishing themselves, so as to render the tiniest measure of…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
益以稱塞
主上
高厚之恩
汪濊之澤於萬一俾後稱嶺表
得士惟茲科爲最若衹以空
言自綴淟涊以裂膏腴結牛
鼎於纖枯其何能勝宋人以
===
燕石爲璞緹縭十重售鬻於
市發函視之主人掩口竊咲
多士縟文蔑實與玉表石衷
等猶之局於谿徑支流之末
卽仰止望洋於羅浮大海胡
可得哉審爾豈直慙恧鄕之
先哲山川且羞之濟川鰓鰓
punctuated: 益，以稱塞主上高厚之恩、汪濊之澤於萬一，俾後稱嶺表得士，惟茲科爲最。若衹以空言自綴，淟涊以裂膏腴，結牛鼎於纖枯，其何能勝？宋人以燕石爲璞，緹縭十重，售鬻於市。發函視之，主人掩口竊咲。多士縟文蔑實，與玉表石衷等，猶之局於谿徑支流之末，卽仰止望洋於羅浮大海，胡可得哉？審爾，豈直慙恧鄕之先哲，山川且羞之。濟川鰓鰓
translation_en:
…benefit, thereby repaying even a ten-thousandth part of His Majesty’s grace, lofty as Heaven and deep as Earth, and his vast beneficence, so that later generations may say that, in obtaining worthy men for Lingbiao, this examination surpassed all others. If you merely adorn yourselves with empty words, debase yourselves to secure portions of fertile land, and suspend an ox-sized cauldron from a slender, withered stalk [?], how can you bear the weight?

A man of Song took a stone from Yan to be unworked jade, wrapped it in ten layers of red silk, and offered it for sale in the marketplace. When the case was opened for inspection, the owner covered his mouth and laughed quietly [?]. If you scholars are elaborate in literary ornament but deficient in substance, you are no different from something with jade outside and ordinary stone within. You would still be confined to the furthest reaches of narrow paths and tributary streams. How, then, could you attain the heights of Luofu or the immensity of the great sea, which you gaze upon in awe? If this were so, you would not merely feel shame before the earlier worthies of your native region: even its mountains and rivers would be ashamed of you. I, Jichuan, am anxiously concerned…

title: 隆慶四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然慮多士之一或類是也濟
川學愧為山識侔測蠡然所
以為多士者則忠矣毋倂其
言忽之
湖廣黄州府黄陂縣儒學教
諭萬濟川謹序
punctuated:
然慮多士之一或類是也。濟川學愧為山，識侔測蠡，然所以為多士者則忠矣，毋倂其言忽之。
湖廣黄州府黄陂縣儒學教諭萬濟川謹序。
translation_en:
…anxiously worries that even one among the many scholars might resemble these examples. I, Jichuan, am ashamed that my learning falls short of building a mountain; my understanding is like measuring the sea with a gourd. Yet my concern for the many scholars is sincere. Do not dismiss my words along with me.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Wan Jichuan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang.
